knowledge_statements.statement_title: Axiomatization of matroid span functions
knowledge_statements.scope_note: Characterizes the set-valued operators on a finite ground set that are exactly matroid span functions.
knowledge_statements.statement_latex: Let \(S\) be finite. A map \(\operatorname{span}:\mathcal P(S)\to\mathcal P(S)\) is the span function of a matroid if and only if: (i) \(T\subseteq\operatorname{span}(T)\) for every \(T\subseteq S\); (ii) for \(T,U\subseteq S\), if \(U\subseteq\operatorname{span}(T)\), then \(\operatorname{span}(U)\subseteq\operatorname{span}(T)\); and (iii) if \(T\subseteq S\), \(t\in S\setminus T\), and \(s\in\operatorname{span}(T\cup\{t\})\setminus\operatorname{span}(T)\), then \(t\in\operatorname{span}(T\cup\{s\})\).
knowledge_statements.statement_plain: On a finite ground set, an operator is a matroid span function exactly when it is extensive, maps every subset of an existing span back into that span, and satisfies the stated exchange law for newly spanned elements.
knowledge_statements.conclusion_latex: \operatorname{span}\text{ is the span function of a matroid}\iff\text{conditions (i)--(iii) hold}.

knowledge_statements.statement_title: Matroid span, spanning sets, and flats
knowledge_statements.scope_note: Defines matroid span from rank and records its basic rank, spanning, flat, and independence characterizations.
knowledge_statements.statement_latex: For a matroid \(M=(S,\mathcal I)\) and \(T\subseteq S\), define \(\operatorname{span}_M(T)=\{s\in S:r_M(T\cup\{s\})=r_M(T)\}\). Then \(T\subseteq\operatorname{span}_M(T)\), \(r_M(\operatorname{span}_M(T))=r_M(T)\), and \(T\) is spanning if and only if \(\operatorname{span}_M(T)=S\). A subset \(F\subseteq S\) is a flat if and only if \(\operatorname{span}_M(F)=F\). Moreover, \(I\subseteq S\) is independent if and only if, for every \(y\in I\), there exists a flat \(F\) such that \(I\setminus\{y\}\subseteq F\) and \(y\notin F\).
knowledge_statements.statement_plain: The span of a set consists of the elements whose addition does not increase its rank. Span contains the original set and has the same rank; a set is spanning exactly when its span is the ground set. Flats are the fixed points of span, and independence is characterized by a flat separating each element from the rest of the set.
knowledge_statements.conclusion_latex: \operatorname{span}_M(T)=\{s\in S:r_M(T\cup\{s\})=r_M(T)\},\quad T\subseteq\operatorname{span}_M(T),\quad r_M(\operatorname{span}_M(T))=r_M(T),\quad [T\text{ spanning}\iff\operatorname{span}_M(T)=S],\quad [F\text{ flat}\iff\operatorname{span}_M(F)=F],\quad [I\in\mathcal I\iff \forall y\in I\;\exists F\text{ flat}:I\setminus\{y\}\subseteq F,\ y\notin F].

knowledge_statements.statement_title: Uniqueness of matroid span
knowledge_statements.scope_note: Uniqueness of the maximal rank-preserving superset used to define matroid span.
knowledge_statements.statement_latex: Let $M=(E,\mathcal I)$ be a matroid and let $A\subseteq E$. There is a unique maximal set $S$ such that $A\subseteq S\subseteq E$ and $r(S)=r(A)$. Consequently, $\operatorname{sp}(A)$ is unique.
knowledge_statements.statement_plain: For every subset of a matroid, the maximal superset having the same rank is unique; hence the subset's span is uniquely determined.
knowledge_statements.conclusion_latex: \operatorname{sp}(A)\text{ is unique.}

knowledge_statements.statement_title: Span-Preserving Ordered Exchange Lemma
knowledge_statements.scope_note: Sufficient ordered-exchange conditions ensuring simultaneous exchanges preserve independence and matroid span.
knowledge_statements.statement_latex:
Let \(M=(S,\mathcal I)\), let \(J\in\mathcal I\), and let \(p_1,q_1,\ldots,p_k,q_k\) be distinct elements satisfying, for \(1\le i\le k\),
\[
p_i\notin J,\quad q_i\in J,\quad J\cup\{p_i\}\notin\mathcal I,\quad (J\cup\{p_i\})\setminus\{q_i\}\in\mathcal I,
\]
and, for \(1\le i<j\le k\),
\[
(J\cup\{p_i\})\setminus\{q_j\}\notin\mathcal I.
\]
If
\[
J'=J\mathbin{\triangle}\{p_1,q_1,\ldots,p_k,q_k\},
\]
then
\[
J'\in\mathcal I\quad\text{and}\quad\operatorname{span}(J')=\operatorname{span}(J).
\]
knowledge_statements.statement_plain: If each outside element p_i can replace its paired element q_i in an independent set J, while no earlier p_i can replace a later q_j, then simultaneously exchanging all pairs produces an independent set with the same span as J.
assumptions_latex: M=(S,\mathcal I)\text{ is a matroid and }J\in\mathcal I.
p_i\notin J\text{ and }q_i\in J\text{ for }1\le i\le k.
J\cup\{p_i\}\notin\mathcal I\text{ and }(J\cup\{p_i\})\setminus\{q_i\}\in\mathcal I\text{ for }1\le i\le k.
knowledge_statements.conclusion_latex: J'=J\triangle\{p_1,q_1,\ldots,p_k,q_k\}\in\mathcal I\quad\text{and}\quad\operatorname{span}(J')=\operatorname{span}(J).

source_refs.locator: Section 5.1, Independence and rank, p. 173

knowledge_statements.statement_latex: Let \(M\) be a finite matroid on \(E\). A subset \(F\subseteq E\) is a flat of \(M\) when \(\operatorname{cl}_M(F)=F\). Equivalently, \(F\) is a flat exactly when every \(e\in E\setminus F\) increases its rank: \[r_M(F\cup\{e\})=r_M(F)+1.\] The intersection of any family of flats of \(M\), including the empty family whose intersection is \(E\), is a flat.
knowledge_statements.statement_plain: A flat is a closed subset, equivalently a subset for which every ground-set element outside it raises its rank by one. Intersections of arbitrary families of flats are flats.

knowledge_statements.statement_title: Meet and Join in the Lattice of Matroid Flats
knowledge_statements.scope_note: Identifies the lattice operations on flats ordered by inclusion.
knowledge_statements.statement_latex: For every matroid \(M\), its inclusion poset of flats \(\mathcal L(M)\) is a lattice. For all flats \(X,Y\) of \(M\), \[X\wedge Y=X\cap Y,\qquad X\vee Y=\operatorname{cl}_M(X\cup Y).\]

knowledge_statements.statement_title: Equivalent criteria for a modular flat
knowledge_statements.scope_note: The three conditions are equivalent for any flat of any matroid.
knowledge_statements.statement_latex: Let \(X\) be a flat of a matroid \(M\). The following are equivalent: (i) \(X\) is modular; (ii) for every flat \(Y\) satisfying \(X\cap Y=\operatorname{cl}_M(\varnothing)\), one has \(r(X)+r(Y)=r(X\cup Y)\); (iii) for every complement \(Y\) of \(X\), one has \(r(X)+r(Y)=r(M)\).
knowledge_statements.statement_plain: A flat is modular exactly when rank is additive with every flat meeting it only in the bottom flat; equivalently, its rank and the rank of each complement sum to the rank of the matroid.
knowledge_statements.conclusion_latex: \begin{aligned}X\text{ is modular}&\iff \forall Y\in\mathcal L(M),\ X\cap Y=\operatorname{cl}_M(\varnothing)\Rightarrow r(X)+r(Y)=r(X\cup Y)\\&\iff \forall Y\text{ complementing }X,\ r(X)+r(Y)=r(M).\end{aligned}

knowledge_statements.statement_title: Modular pairs, modular flats, and modular matroids
knowledge_statements.scope_note: Core definitions from the extraction-grounded source item.
knowledge_statements.statement_latex: Flats \(X,Y\) of a matroid \(M\) form a modular pair if \[r(X)+r(Y)=r(X\cup Y)+r(X\cap Y).\] A flat \(Z\) is modular if \((Z,Y)\) is a modular pair for every flat \(Y\) of \(M\). The matroid \(M\) is modular if every flat of \(M\) is modular.
knowledge_statements.statement_plain: Two flats form a modular pair when equality holds in the rank submodularity relation. A flat is modular when it forms a modular pair with every flat, and a matroid is modular when all of its flats are modular.
knowledge_statements.conclusion_latex: (X,Y)\text{ is a modular pair}\iff r(X)+r(Y)=r(X\cup Y)+r(X\cap Y);\quad Z\text{ is modular}\iff \forall Y\in\mathcal L(M),\ (Z,Y)\text{ is a modular pair}.

knowledge_statements.statement_title: Flat Classification for a Modular-Cut Extension
knowledge_statements.scope_note: Partitions the flats of the extension determined by a modular cut into three disjoint classes.
knowledge_statements.statement_latex: Let \(\mathcal M\) be a modular cut of a matroid \(M\), and let \(M+_{\mathcal M}e\) be the associated single-element extension. Its flats are exactly the following three disjoint classes: (i) flats \(F\) of \(M\) with \(F\notin\mathcal M\); (ii) sets \(F\cup\{e\}\) where \(F\) is a flat of \(M\) with \(F\in\mathcal M\); and (iii) sets \(F\cup\{e\}\) where \(F\) is a flat of \(M\), \(F\notin\mathcal M\), and there is no \(F'\in\mathcal M\) such that \(F\subseteq F'\) and \(r_M(F')=r_M(F)+1\).
knowledge_statements.statement_plain: The flats of a modular-cut extension split disjointly into old flats outside the cut, sets obtained by adjoining e to flats inside the cut, and sets obtained by adjoining e to flats outside the cut that lie in no cut member of rank one greater.
assumptions_latex: \mathcal M\text{ is a modular cut of }M
M+_{\mathcal M}e\text{ is the associated single-element extension}
knowledge_statements.conclusion_latex: \mathcal F(M+_{\mathcal M}e)=\{F\in\mathcal F(M):F\notin\mathcal M\}\,\dot\cup\,\{F\cup\{e\}:F\in\mathcal F(M)\cap\mathcal M\}\,\dot\cup\,\{F\cup\{e\}:F\in\mathcal F(M)\setminus\mathcal M,\ \nexists F'\in\mathcal M\text{ with }F\subseteq F',\ r_M(F')=r_M(F)+1\}.

knowledge_statements.statement_title: Characterization of Simple Rank-at-Most-Three Matroids by Line Families
knowledge_statements.scope_note: Constructs and characterizes simple matroids of rank at most three from prospective nontrivial rank-two flats.
knowledge_statements.statement_latex: Let \(E\) be a set and let \(\Lambda\) be a collection of subsets of \(E\), each having at least three elements, such that \(|L_1\cap L_2|\le 1\) whenever \(L_1,L_2\in\Lambda\) are distinct. Define \(\mathcal I=\{X\subseteq E:|X|\le 3\text{ and no }L\in\Lambda\text{ contains three elements of }X\}\). Then \((E,\mathcal I)\) is a simple matroid of rank at most three. Its rank-one flats are the singletons, and its rank-two flats are the members of \(\Lambda\) together with all two-element subsets \(Y\subseteq E\) contained in no member of \(\Lambda\). Conversely, every simple matroid of rank at most three arises in this way.
knowledge_statements.statement_plain: A family of subsets of size at least three whose distinct members meet in at most one element determines a simple matroid of rank at most three. Its independent sets are the subsets of size at most three that do not contain three elements from one family member. The family members and the pairs lying in no family member are exactly its rank-two flats, and every simple matroid of rank at most three has such a presentation.
knowledge_statements.conclusion_latex: (E,\mathcal I)\text{ is a simple matroid of rank at most }3\text{ with the stated rank-one and rank-two flats, and every simple matroid of rank at most }3\text{ arises this way}.

knowledge_statements.statement_title: Complement of a matroid flat

knowledge_statements.statement_latex: For flats \(X,Y\) of a matroid \(M\), \(Y\) is a complement of \(X\) if \(X\cap Y=\operatorname{cl}_M(\varnothing)\) and \(\operatorname{cl}_M(X\cup Y)=E(M)\). Equivalently, in \(\mathcal L(M)\), \(X\wedge Y=0\) and \(X\vee Y=1\).

knowledge_statements.scope_note: Characterizes collections of subsets that are exactly the flats of a matroid.
knowledge_statements.statement_latex: Let \(S\) be a set and let \(\mathcal F\) be a collection of subsets of \(S\). knowledge_statements.statement_latex:
The poset \(\mathcal L(M)\) is a finite geometric lattice. For flats \(F,G\in\mathcal L(M)\), its operations are
\[
F\wedge G=F\cap G,
\qquad
F\vee G=\operatorname{cl}_M(F\cup G).
\]
Its bottom and top are \(\operatorname{cl}_M(\varnothing)\) and \(E\), respectively; its atoms are the rank-one flats; and its lattice height function is the matroid rank restricted to flats. Semimodularity is expressed by
\[
r(F)+r(G)\ge r(F\cap G)+r(\operatorname{cl}_M(F\cup G)).
\]
knowledge_statements.statement_plain: The flats of a finite matroid form a geometric lattice whose meet is intersection, join is closure of union, and height is matroid rank.

knowledge_statements.statement_title: Cocircuits induced by two disjoint 3-separating triangles
knowledge_statements.scope_note: Structural lemma for 3-connected binary matroids.
knowledge_statements.statement_latex: Let $M$ be a $3$-connected binary matroid with disjoint triangles $T_1,T_2$ such that $T_1\cup T_2$ is $3$-separating. knowledge_statements.statement_title: Non-Separating Cocircuits of 3-Connected Binary Matroids
knowledge_statements.scope_note: Four structural and graphicness properties under the stated connectivity, representability, and size assumptions.
knowledge_statements.statement_latex: Let M be a 3-connected binary matroid with |E(M)|\ge 4. Then: (i) every e\in E(M) belongs to at least two non-separating cocircuits; (ii) M is graphic if and only if every e\in E(M) belongs to at most two non-separating cocircuits; (iii) every cocircuit of M is a symmetric difference of non-separating cocircuits; and (iv) M is graphic if and only if every e\in E(M) avoids exactly r(M)-1 non-separating cocircuits.

knowledge_statements.statement_title: Chains, Semimodular Lattices, and Geometric Lattices
knowledge_statements.scope_note: Collects the finite-poset and finite-lattice definitions needed for the geometric-lattice representation of matroids.
knowledge_statements.statement_latex: Let \(P\) be a finite poset. A chain from \(x_0\) to \(x_n\) is \(x_0<x_1<\cdots<x_n\), has length \(n\), and is maximal when each \(x_i\) covers \(x_{i-1}\). The Jordan--Dedekind condition requires that, for every \(a<b\), all maximal chains from \(a\) to \(b\) have the same length. A zero is an element \(0\le x\) for every \(x\in P\), a one is an element \(1\ge x\) for every \(x\in P\), an atom covers \(0\), and \(h(y)\) is the maximum length of a chain from \(0\) to \(y\). Every finite lattice has a zero and a one; for \(\mathcal L(M)\) they are \(\operatorname{cl}_M(\varnothing)\) and \(E(M)\). A finite lattice \(\mathcal L\) is semimodular when it satisfies Jordan--Dedekind and \[h(x)+h(y)\ge h(x\vee y)+h(x\wedge y)\quad\text{for all }x,y\in\mathcal L.\] It is geometric when it is semimodular and every element is a join of atoms.
knowledge_statements.statement_plain: In a finite poset, maximal chains advance through covering pairs, and the Jordan–Dedekind condition says all maximal chains between fixed comparable endpoints have equal length. A poset may have a least element zero and greatest element one; atoms cover zero, and height is maximum chain length from zero. Every finite lattice has zero and one, with the flat lattice of a matroid having closure of the empty set and the ground set as these elements. A finite lattice is semimodular when it satisfies Jordan–Dedekind and the stated height inequality, and it is geometric when every element is a join of atoms.
assumptions_latex: P\text{ is a finite partially ordered set}
\mathcal L\text{ is a finite lattice for the semimodular and geometric definitions}
M\text{ is a matroid for the identification of the zero and one of }\mathcal L(M)
knowledge_statements.conclusion_latex: \mathcal L\text{ is geometric precisely under the stated finite, semimodular, and atomistic conditions}

knowledge_statements.statement_title: Minty Circuit–Cocircuit Painting Characterization
knowledge_statements.scope_note: Necessary and sufficient conditions for two set families to be the circuit families of a dual pair of matroids.
knowledge_statements.statement_latex: Let $E$ be finite and let $\mathcal C,\mathcal D\subseteq 2^E$. The families $\mathcal C$ and $\mathcal D$ are respectively the circuit families of a dual pair of matroids if and only if: (i) each family is an antichain under proper inclusion; (ii) $|C\cap D|\neq 1$ for every $C\in\mathcal C$ and $D\in\mathcal D$; and (iii) for every red-yellow-green coloring of $E$ having exactly one yellow element, exactly one of the following holds: some $C\in\mathcal C$ contains the yellow element and no red element, or some $D\in\mathcal D$ contains the yellow element and no green element.
knowledge_statements.statement_plain: Two families are the circuit and cocircuit families of a matroid precisely when neither family contains nested members, no circuit and cocircuit meet in exactly one element, and every three-coloring with one distinguished yellow element satisfies exactly one of the stated circuit or cocircuit alternatives.
knowledge_statements.conclusion_latex: \mathcal C\text{ and }\mathcal D\text{ are the circuit families of a dual pair of matroids}\iff\text{conditions (i)--(iii) hold}

knowledge_statements.statement_title: Clones, clonal classes, and fixed or cofixed elements
knowledge_statements.scope_note: Definitions based on automorphisms, single-element extensions, independence, and matroid duality; illustrative claims about Q_6 are excluded.
knowledge_statements.statement_latex: Distinct elements e,f\in E(M) are clones if the permutation interchanging e and f and fixing E(M)\setminus\{e,f\} pointwise is an automorphism of M. A clonal class is a maximal subset X\subseteq E(M) whose distinct members are pairwise clones. An element x\in E(M) is fixed in M if there is no single-element extension M_y of M by y such that x and y are clones in M_y and \{x,y\} is independent in M_y. An element z\in E(M) is cofixed in M if z is fixed in M^*.
knowledge_statements.statement_plain: Two distinct matroid elements are clones when swapping them while fixing every other element is an automorphism. A clonal class is a maximal pairwise-clonal set. An element is fixed when no single-element extension gives it an independent clone, and it is cofixed when it is fixed in the dual matroid.
knowledge_statements.conclusion_latex: \begin{gathered}e,f\text{ are clones}\iff (e\ f)\text{ fixing }E(M)\setminus\{e,f\}\text{ pointwise is an automorphism of }M,\\X\text{ is a clonal class}\iff X\text{ is maximal with all distinct members pairwise clones},\\x\text{ is fixed}\iff \nexists M_y\text{ with }x,y\text{ clones and }\{x,y\}\text{ independent},\\z\text{ is cofixed in }M\iff z\text{ is fixed in }M^*\end{gathered}

knowledge_statements.statement_title: Minors of a tipless r-spike
knowledge_statements.scope_note: Describes spike and tipless-spike minors, a dual isomorphism, the free specialization, and parallel/series replacement representations.
knowledge_statements.statement_latex: Let \(M\) be a tipless \(r\)-spike with legs \(L_i=\{x_i,y_i\}\), \(1\le i\le r\). (i) If \(r\ge4\), then for every \(i\), both \(M/x_i\) and \((M\setminus x_i)^*\) are \((r-1)\)-spikes with tip \(y_i\) and legs \(L_j\cup\{y_i\}\) for \(j\ne i\); moreover, \(M/x_i\cong(M\setminus y_i)^*\). (ii) If \(r\ge4\), then for every \(i\), both \(M/x_i\setminus y_i\) and \(M/y_i\setminus x_i\) are tipless \((r-1)\)-spikes with legs \(L_j\), \(j\ne i\). If \(M\) is a tipless free \(r\)-spike, these minors are equal and are tipless free \((r-1)\)-spikes. (iii) For every \(i\), \(M/L_i\) is obtained from an \((r-1)\)-element circuit by replacing every element with two parallel elements; dually, \(M\setminus L_i\) is obtained from an \((r-1)\)-element cocircuit by replacing every element with two series elements.
knowledge_statements.statement_plain: Let M be a tipless r-spike with two-element legs Li={xi,yi}. For r at least 4, contracting xi and dualizing after deleting xi each produce an (r−1)-spike with tip yi, and M/xi is isomorphic to the dual of M\yi. Contracting one leg element and deleting the other produces a tipless (r−1)-spike; in the tipless free case the two choices coincide and remain free. Contracting an entire leg gives a circuit whose elements are each replaced by a parallel pair, while deleting the leg gives the dual series-pair construction from a cocircuit.
knowledge_statements.conclusion_latex: \begin{gathered}M/x_i,\ (M\setminus x_i)^*\text{ are }(r-1)\text{-spikes with tip }y_i,\quad M/x_i\cong(M\setminus y_i)^*;\\ M/x_i\setminus y_i,\ M/y_i\setminus x_i\text{ are tipless }(r-1)\text{-spikes};\\ M\text{ tipless free}\Rightarrow M/x_i\setminus y_i=M/y_i\setminus x_i\text{ and both remain tipless free};\\ M/L_i\text{ is a parallel-pair replacement of an }(r-1)\text{-circuit, and }M\setminus L_i\text{ is the dual series-pair replacement of an }(r-1)\text{-cocircuit.}\end{gathered}

knowledge_statements.statement_title: Minors of an r-spike
knowledge_statements.scope_note: Describes spike-preserving minors, the free-spike specialization, and the parallel-extension representation after contracting the tip.
knowledge_statements.statement_latex: Let \(M\) be an \(r\)-spike with tip \(t\) and legs \(L_i=\{x_i,y_i,t\}\), \(1\le i\le r\). (i) If \(r\ge4\), then for every \(i\), both \(M/x_i\setminus y_i\) and \(M/y_i\setminus x_i\) are \((r-1)\)-spikes with tip \(t\) and legs \(L_j\) for \(j\ne i\). If \(M\) is a free \(r\)-spike, these two minors are equal and are free \((r-1)\)-spikes. (ii) If \(r\ge4\), then for every \(i\), both \(M\setminus t/x_i\) and \((M\setminus t\setminus x_i)^*\) are \((r-1)\)-spikes with tip \(y_i\). (iii) The matroid \(M/t\) is obtained from an \(r\)-element circuit by adjoining one element parallel to each circuit element.
knowledge_statements.statement_plain: Let M be an r-spike with tip t and legs Li={xi,yi,t}. For r at least 4, contracting one nontip element of a leg and deleting the other produces an (r−1)-spike on the remaining legs; in the free case the two choices give the same free spike. Deleting the tip and contracting xi, or dualizing after deleting the tip and xi, also produces an (r−1)-spike with tip yi. Contracting the tip yields an r-element circuit with one new parallel mate for every circuit element.
knowledge_statements.conclusion_latex: \begin{gathered}M/x_i\setminus y_i,\ M/y_i\setminus x_i\text{ are }(r-1)\text{-spikes for every }i;\\ M\text{ free}\Rightarrow M/x_i\setminus y_i=M/y_i\setminus x_i\text{ and both are free};\\ M\setminus t/x_i,\ (M\setminus t\setminus x_i)^*\text{ are }(r-1)\text{-spikes with tip }y_i;\\ M/t\text{ is an }r\text{-circuit with one parallel mate added to each element.}\end{gathered}

knowledge_statements.statement_title: Circuit-family characterization of paving matroids
knowledge_statements.scope_note: Characterizes exactly which nonempty set families are circuit collections of paving matroids.
knowledge_statements.statement_latex: Let \(\mathcal D\) be a collection of nonempty subsets of a set \(E\). Then \(\mathcal D\) is the circuit set of a paving matroid on \(E\) if and only if there exist an integer \(k\) with \(1\le k\le |E|\) and \(\mathcal D'\subseteq\mathcal D\) such that: (i) every member of \(\mathcal D'\) has cardinality \(k\), and whenever distinct \(D_1,D_2\in\mathcal D'\) satisfy \(|D_1\cap D_2|=k-1\), every \(k\)-element subset of \(D_1\cup D_2\) belongs to \(\mathcal D'\); and (ii) \(\mathcal D\setminus\mathcal D'\) is exactly the family of all \((k+1)\)-element subsets of \(E\) containing no member of \(\mathcal D'\).
knowledge_statements.statement_plain: A collection D of nonempty subsets of E is exactly the circuit family of a paving matroid if and only if, for some integer k between 1 and |E|, it consists of a family D' of k-element sets satisfying the stated closure condition for pairs intersecting in k−1 elements, together with precisely those (k+1)-element subsets of E that contain no member of D'.
knowledge_statements.conclusion_latex: \mathcal D\text{ is the circuit set of a paving matroid on }E\iff \exists k,\mathcal D'\text{ satisfying (i) and (ii).}

knowledge_statements.statement_title: Simplification of a Matroid
knowledge_statements.scope_note: Defines simplification intrinsically through nonloop parallel classes and equivalently through rank-one flats.
knowledge_statements.statement_latex: For a matroid $M$, the simplification $\operatorname{si}(M)$ is obtained, up to isomorphism, by deleting all loops and retaining one representative from each nonloop parallel class. Intrinsically, its ground set may be taken to be the nonloop parallel classes of $M$, with $\{X_1,\ldots,X_k\}$ independent if and only if $r_M(X_1\cup\cdots\cup X_k)=k$. Equivalently, its ground set may be taken to be the rank-one flats of $M$ with the same rank criterion. If $\widetilde G$ is the simple graph associated with a graph $G$, then $\operatorname{si}(M(G))=M(\widetilde G)$.
knowledge_statements.statement_plain: The simplification of a matroid deletes its loops and retains one representative from each nonloop parallel class, producing a matroid determined up to isomorphism. Its elements can equivalently be represented by the nonloop parallel classes or by the rank-one flats, with independence determined by the rank of their union. For graphic matroids, simplification agrees with simplifying the graph.
knowledge_statements.conclusion_latex: \{X_1,\ldots,X_k\}\in\mathcal I(\operatorname{si}(M))\iff r_M\!\left(\bigcup_{i=1}^kX_i\right)=k

knowledge_statements.statement_title: Matroid by Independent-Set Axioms
knowledge_statements.scope_note: Finite matroids in their independence-system representation.
knowledge_statements.statement_latex: A matroid is a pair \(M=(E,\mathcal I)\), where \(E\) is finite and \(\mathcal I\subseteq 2^E\) satisfies \(\varnothing\in\mathcal I\); if \(T\in\mathcal I\) and \(S\subseteq T\), then \(S\in\mathcal I\); and if \(S,T\in\mathcal I\) with \(|T|>|S|\), then some \(t\in T\setminus S\) satisfies \(S\cup\{t\}\in\mathcal I\). knowledge_statements.statement_title: Matroid Bonds and Bridges
knowledge_statements.scope_note: Basis-hitting and circuit characterizations of bonds and bridges, including the subset-relative notion.
knowledge_statements.statement_latex: Let \(M=(S,\mathcal I)\) be a matroid. A bond (cut or cocycle) is an inclusion-minimal set \(B\subseteq S\) that intersects every basis of \(M\). A singleton bond \(\{t\}\) makes \(t\) a cut-element or bridge; equivalently, \(t\) belongs to no circuit of \(M\). More generally, for \(X\subseteq S\) and \(t\in X\), \(t\) is a bridge of \(X\) if it belongs to every maximal independent subset of \(X\). If \(t\) is a bridge of \(X\), then it is a bridge of every \(Y\subseteq X\) with \(t\in Y\).
knowledge_statements.statement_plain: A bond, also called a cut or cocycle, is a minimal subset meeting every basis. An element is a bridge when its singleton is a bond, equivalently when it lies in no circuit. Relative to a subset X, a bridge is an element contained in every maximal independent subset of X; this property persists in every smaller subset containing the element.
knowledge_statements.conclusion_latex: B\text{ is a bond}\iff B\text{ is inclusion-minimal subject to }B\cap Q\ne\varnothing\text{ for every basis }Q;\quad \{t\}\text{ is a bond}\iff t\text{ lies in no circuit};\quad t\text{ bridge of }X\Rightarrow t\text{ bridge of }Y.

knowledge_statements.statement_latex:
The element \(e\) is a loop of \(M\) when the singleton \(\{e\}\) is dependent. Equivalently, each of the following holds:
\[
r(\{e\})=0,
\qquad
e\in\operatorname{cl}_M(\varnothing),
\qquad
\{e\}\text{ is a circuit},
\qquad
e\notin B\text{ for every }B\in\mathcal B(M).
\]
Thus adding a loop to any subset does not increase rank: \(r(X\cup\{e\})=r(X)\) for every \(X\subseteq E\).
knowledge_statements.statement_plain: A loop is an element of rank zero; it forms a singleton circuit and belongs to no basis.

knowledge_statements.statement_latex:
For \(e,f\in E\setminus L\), define \(e\sim f\) when \(\operatorname{cl}_M(\{e\})=\operatorname{cl}_M(\{f\})\). This is an equivalence relation, and its equivalence classes are the parallel classes of \(M\). For distinct nonloops \(e\) and \(f\),
\[
e\sim f
\quad\Longleftrightarrow\quad
r(\{e,f\})=1
\quad\Longleftrightarrow\quad
\{e,f\}\text{ is a circuit}.
\]
A nontrivial parallel class is one containing at least two elements.
knowledge_statements.statement_plain: Parallel classes group nonloops having the same singleton closure; two distinct nonloops are parallel exactly when together they form a circuit.

knowledge_statements.statement_title: Geometric Representation Diagram for a Matroid
knowledge_statements.scope_note: Defines the interpretation conventions for informal geometric diagrams of low-rank matroids.
knowledge_statements.statement_latex: A geometric representation diagram places all loops in one inset, depicts each nontrivial parallel class by touching points or one multiply labeled point, and gives every other nonloop element a distinct isolated point. Points corresponding to a three-element circuit are collinear, and those corresponding to a four-element circuit are coplanar. Depicted lines need not be straight and planes may be twisted; lines and planes may be listed rather than drawn, and short construction lines may be shown. Such a diagram is a matroid representation convention, not a graph diagram.
knowledge_statements.statement_plain: In a geometric matroid diagram, loops share an inset, parallel elements are shown by touching or jointly labeled points, and other nonloop elements have separate points. Three-element circuits are shown on a line and four-element circuits in a plane. Lines and planes may be schematic, listed instead of drawn, or supplemented by construction lines. The diagram is not a graph diagram.
assumptions_latex: M\text{ is represented by a geometric diagram using the stated conventions}
knowledge_statements.conclusion_latex: \text{loops, parallel classes, 3-circuits, and 4-circuits are encoded respectively by the prescribed inset, point, line, and plane conventions}.

knowledge_statements.statement_title: Parallel multiplication and its bipartite realization
knowledge_statements.scope_note: Defines parallel multiplication, its zero-copy boundary case, graphic interpretation, and the induced edge-set matroid construction.
knowledge_statements.statement_latex: Let $M$ be a matroid on $S$, let $s\in S$ be a nonloop, and let $k\ge 0$. Replace $s$ by a disjoint set $S'=\{s_1,\ldots,s_k\}$. A set $X\subseteq(S\setminus\{s\})\cup S'$ is independent exactly when either $X\subseteq S\setminus\{s\}$ is independent in $M$, or $|X\cap S'|=1$ and $(X\setminus S')\cup\{s\}$ is independent in $M$. This defines a matroid; every two distinct elements of $S'$ form a circuit. For $k=0$ the operation is deletion, and for a graphic matroid it replaces an edge by $k$ parallel copies. More generally, if $G=(S,T;E)$ is bipartite and $M$ is loopless on $S$, the sets $F\subseteq E$ whose $S$-endpoints are distinct and independent in $M$ form a matroid isomorphic to that obtained by parallel-multiplying each $s\in S$ by $d_G(s)$.
knowledge_statements.statement_plain: Replace a nonloop element by k new copies. A set is independent when it either avoids all copies and was independent before, or contains exactly one copy and becomes independent after replacing that copy by the original element. The result is a matroid whose new elements are pairwise parallel; zero copies means deletion, and graphic matroids realize the operation by parallel edges. Placing a loopless matroid on the left vertices of a bipartite graph similarly produces the parallel multiplication determined by their degrees.
knowledge_statements.conclusion_latex: \mathcal I'\text{ as defined is the independent-set family of a matroid, and }\{s_i,s_j\}\text{ is a circuit for }i\ne j.

knowledge_statements.statement_title: Loops, parallel classes, and simple matroids
knowledge_statements.scope_note: Circuit-based definitions of loops and parallel elements, the maximality condition for parallel classes, and the resulting definition of simplicity.
knowledge_statements.statement_latex: Let \(M\) be a matroid. An element \(e\in E(M)\) is a loop if and only if \(\{e\}\) is a circuit of \(M\). Distinct elements \(f,g\in E(M)\) are parallel if \(\{f,g\}\) is a circuit. A parallel class is a maximal subset \(X\subseteq E(M)\) whose members are nonloops and whose distinct pairs are parallel; it is trivial if \(|X|=1\). The matroid \(M\) is simple if and only if it has no loops and no nontrivial parallel classes.
knowledge_statements.statement_plain: In a matroid, a loop is an element forming a one-element circuit, and two distinct elements are parallel when they form a two-element circuit. A parallel class is a maximal set of nonloops whose distinct pairs are parallel; it is trivial when it has one element. A matroid is simple exactly when it has no loops and no nontrivial parallel classes.
knowledge_statements.conclusion_latex: M\text{ is simple}\iff M\text{ has no loops and no nontrivial parallel classes}.

knowledge_statements.scope_note: The required coloring update depends on whether the tip is colored.

children.top_down_role: Dual correspondence between the two exceptional element types.

assumptions_latex: \(M\) is a finite matroid on ground set \(E\).
knowledge_statements.conclusion_latex: An element is a loop of \(M\) if and only if it is a coloop of \(M^*\), and conversely.

knowledge_statements.statement_latex:
For every \(e\in E\),
\[
e\in L(M)
\quad\Longleftrightarrow\quad
e\in C(M^*),
\qquad
e\in C(M)
\quad\Longleftrightarrow\quad
e\in L(M^*).
\]
Equivalently, singleton circuits of \(M\) are singleton cocircuits of \(M^*\), while singleton cocircuits of \(M\) are singleton circuits of \(M^*\). Since \((M^*)^*=M\), the two correspondences are mutually inverse.
knowledge_statements.statement_plain: Duality exchanges loops and coloops: each loop becomes a coloop in the dual, and each coloop becomes a loop.

knowledge_statements.statement_title: Series and Parallel Extensions of Graphs
knowledge_statements.scope_note: Defines the extension operations for arbitrary graphs and records boundaries of the series-extension notion.
knowledge_statements.statement_latex: For a graph G, G' is a parallel extension of G (equivalently, G is a parallel deletion of G') if G' has a two-edge cycle \{e,f\} and G'\setminus f=G. It is a series extension of G (equivalently, G is a series contraction of G') if \{e,f\} is a two-edge bond of G' and G'/f=G. Replacing a cut-edge by a path of length two is not a series extension, and a series extension need not arise by replacing an edge with a length-two path.
knowledge_statements.statement_plain: A parallel extension adds an edge belonging with an existing edge to a two-edge cycle and recovers the original graph by deletion. A series extension has a two-edge bond and recovers the original graph by contraction. Subdividing a cut-edge is not a series extension, and not every series extension is an edge subdivision.
knowledge_statements.conclusion_latex: \bigl(\{e,f\}\text{ is a 2-cycle and }G'\setminus f=G\bigr)\Rightarrow G'\text{ is a parallel extension of }G;\quad \bigl(\{e,f\}\text{ is a 2-bond and }G'/f=G\bigr)\Rightarrow G'\text{ is a series extension of }G.

knowledge_statements.statement_title: Ranks and Minors of Binary Series and Parallel Connections
knowledge_statements.scope_note: Structural identities for two matroids whose ground sets meet only at the connection element.
knowledge_statements.statement_latex:
Let E(M_1)\cap E(M_2)=\{p\}. Then
\[
r(S(M_1,M_2))=\begin{cases}r(M_1)+r(M_2)-1,&p\text{ is a coloop of both},\\r(M_1)+r(M_2),&\text{otherwise},\end{cases}
\]
\[
r(P(M_1,M_2))=\begin{cases}r(M_1)+r(M_2),&p\text{ is a loop of both},\\r(M_1)+r(M_2)-1,&\text{otherwise}.
\end{cases}
\]
Moreover,
\[
M_1=S(M_1,M_2)/(E(M_2)-\{p\})
\]
unless p is a loop of M_1 and a coloop of M_2, and
\[
M_1=P(M_1,M_2)\setminus(E(M_2)-\{p\})
\]
unless p is a coloop of M_1 and a loop of M_2. Also
\[
S(M_1,M_2)\setminus p=(M_1\setminus p)\oplus(M_2\setminus p),\quad P(M_1,M_2)/p=(M_1/p)\oplus(M_2/p),
\]
\[
S(M_1,M_2)/p=P(M_1,M_2)\setminus p.
\]
For every e\in E(M_1)-\{p\}, deletion and contraction commute with either connection in the first argument:
\[
S(M_1,M_2)\setminus e=S(M_1\setminus e,M_2),\quad S(M_1,M_2)/e=S(M_1/e,M_2),
\]
\[
P(M_1,M_2)\setminus e=P(M_1\setminus e,M_2),\quad P(M_1,M_2)/e=P(M_1/e,M_2).
\]
knowledge_statements.statement_plain: For two matroids meeting only at p, the ranks of their series and parallel connections have the stated loop–coloop exceptional cases. Each factor can ordinarily be recovered by contracting or deleting the other factor away, deleting or contracting p produces the indicated direct sums and common interface minor, and deletion or contraction of a noninterface element commutes with either connection.
knowledge_statements.conclusion_latex: \text{The displayed rank, factor-recovery, interface-minor, and deletion–contraction identities hold, with the stated exceptions.}

knowledge_statements.statement_title: Matroid Series and Parallel Extensions
knowledge_statements.scope_note: Defines series and parallel extensions and their inverses, then records the duality and series-class characterizations.
knowledge_statements.statement_latex: Let M and N be matroids and let f\in E(M). If M\setminus f=N and f belongs to a 2-circuit of M, then M is a parallel extension of N and N is a parallel deletion of M. If M/f=N and f belongs to a 2-cocircuit of M, then M is a series extension of N and N is a series contraction of M. Moreover, M is a parallel extension of N if and only if M^* is a series extension of N^*. A series class of M is a parallel class of M^* and is nontrivial when it contains at least two elements; two elements are in series in M if and only if they belong to a common nontrivial series class of M.
knowledge_statements.statement_plain: Deleting an element in a two-element circuit defines a parallel extension, while contracting an element in a two-element cocircuit defines a series extension. Duality interchanges these extensions. Series classes are parallel classes of the dual, and two elements are in series exactly when they share a nontrivial series class.
knowledge_statements.conclusion_latex: \bigl(M\setminus f=N\land f\text{ belongs to a 2-circuit of }M\bigr)\Rightarrow M\text{ is a parallel extension of }N;\quad \bigl(M/f=N\land f\text{ belongs to a 2-cocircuit of }M\bigr)\Rightarrow M\text{ is a series extension of }N;\quad M\text{ parallel-extends }N\iff M^*\text{ series-extends }N^*.

A set of arcs is parallel, respectively series, if its arcs are pairwise parallel, respectively pairwise series.

children.title: Matroid Simplification
children.top_down_role: Reduction removing loop and parallel redundancy.

assumptions_latex: \(M\) is a finite matroid with loop set \(L\).
\(P_1,\ldots,P_k\) are its parallel classes on \(E\setminus L\).
knowledge_statements.conclusion_latex: Choosing \(p_i\in P_i\) and \(S=\{p_1,\ldots,p_k\}\), the restriction \(M|S\) is a simplification of \(M\).
knowledge_statements.scope_note: Simplification by deletion and representative selection.

source_refs.locator: Chapter 5. Elements of matroid theory p. 172

knowledge_statements.statement_latex:
Choose one representative \(p_i\in P_i\) from each parallel class and set \(S=\{p_1,\ldots,p_k\}\). A simplification of \(M\) is
\[
\operatorname{si}(M)=M|S.
\]
Equivalently, it is obtained by deleting every loop and deleting all but one element from each nontrivial parallel class. The resulting matroid has no loops and no two-element circuits. Different choices of representatives yield isomorphic matroids, although no canonical labeled simplification is determined in general.
knowledge_statements.statement_plain: A simplification deletes all loops and retains one representative from each parallel class; its isomorphism type is independent of the choices.
knowledge_statements.title: Matroid Simplification

source_witnesses.locator: Chapter 5. Elements of matroid theory p. 172

children.title: Matroid Cosimplification
children.top_down_role: Dual reduction removing coloop and series redundancy.

assumptions_latex: \(M\) is a finite matroid with coloop set \(C\).
\(Q_1,\ldots,Q_k\) are its series classes on \(E\setminus C\).
knowledge_statements.conclusion_latex: Choosing \(q_i\in Q_i\) and \(T=\{q_1,\ldots,q_k\}\), the contraction \(M/(E\setminus T)\) is a cosimplification of \(M\).
knowledge_statements.scope_note: Cosimplification as the dual operation to simplification.

source_refs.locator: Section 13. Duality Theory p. 53

knowledge_statements.statement_latex:
Choose one representative \(q_i\in Q_i\) from each series class and set \(T=\{q_1,\ldots,q_k\}\). A cosimplification of \(M\) is
\[
\operatorname{co}(M)=M/(E\setminus T).
\]
Equivalently,
\[
\operatorname{co}(M)=\bigl(\operatorname{si}(M^*)\bigr)^*.
\]
Operationally, one contracts every coloop and all but one element from each nontrivial series class. The result has no coloops and no two-element cocircuits, and its isomorphism type is independent of the representatives.
knowledge_statements.statement_plain: A cosimplification contracts all coloops and all but one member of each series class; equivalently, it dualizes simplification of the dual.
knowledge_statements.title: Matroid Cosimplification

source_witnesses.locator: Section 13. Duality Theory p. 53

knowledge_statements.statement_title: Cosimplicity and matroid cosimplification
knowledge_statements.scope_note: Defines cosimplicity and gives both the dual and operational representations of cosimplification.
knowledge_statements.statement_latex: A matroid is cosimple if its dual is simple. For any matroid $N$, its cosimplification is $\operatorname{co}(N)=(\operatorname{si}(N^*))^*$. Equivalently, $\operatorname{co}(N)$ is obtained from $N$ by contracting every coloop and all but one element of each nontrivial series class.
knowledge_statements.statement_plain: A matroid is cosimple when its dual is simple. Its cosimplification is the dual of the simplification of its dual, equivalently the result of contracting all coloops and all but one element from every nontrivial series class.
knowledge_statements.conclusion_latex: N\text{ is cosimple}\iff N^*\text{ is simple},\qquad \operatorname{co}(N)=(\operatorname{si}(N^*))^*

children.title: Simple Matroid Core
children.top_down_role: Structural information retained by simplification.

knowledge_statements.conclusion_latex: \(N\) is simple, \(r_N(S)=r_M(E)\), and its flat lattice is isomorphic to that of \(M\).

notation.meaning: A simplification of the original matroid.
Representative ground set of the simplification.

knowledge_statements.scope_note: Rank and flat-lattice invariants of the simple core.

source_refs.locator: Chapter 5. Elements of matroid theory p. 172

knowledge_statements.statement_latex:
The matroid \(N\) is simple: it has neither loops nor two-element circuits. It preserves total rank,
\[
r_N(S)=r_M(E).
\]
Moreover, its flats encode exactly the flat geometry of \(M\). The maps
\[
F\longmapsto\operatorname{cl}_M(F)
\quad\text{and}\quad
G\longmapsto G\cap S
\]
are mutually inverse, inclusion-preserving bijections between the flats \(F\) of \(N\) and the flats \(G\) of \(M\). Thus every simplification realizes the same simple matroid core up to isomorphism.
knowledge_statements.statement_plain: A simplification is a simple, rank-preserving core whose lattice of flats is naturally isomorphic to the original matroid's flat lattice.
knowledge_statements.title: Simple Matroid Core

source_witnesses.locator: Chapter 5. Elements of matroid theory p. 172

children.title: Cosimple Matroid Core
children.top_down_role: Structural information retained by cosimplification.

knowledge_statements.conclusion_latex: \(N\) is cosimple, and \(N^*=\operatorname{si}(M^*)\) up to representative choice and isomorphism.

notation.meaning: A cosimplification of the original matroid.

knowledge_statements.scope_note: Dual rank and flat-geometry invariants of the cosimple core.

source_refs.locator: Section 13. Duality Theory p. 53

knowledge_statements.statement_latex:
The matroid \(N\) is cosimple: it has neither coloops nor two-element cocircuits. Its dual is a simplification of the dual of \(M\), namely
\[
N^*\cong\operatorname{si}(M^*).
\]
Hence the dual rank is preserved:
\[
r_{N^*}(E(N))=r_{M^*}(E).
\]
The flat lattice of \(N^*\) is isomorphic to the flat lattice of \(M^*\). Therefore every cosimplification realizes the same cosimple matroid core up to isomorphism.
knowledge_statements.statement_plain: A cosimplification is a cosimple core; its dual is the simple core of the dual matroid, preserving dual rank and dual flat geometry.
knowledge_statements.title: Cosimple Matroid Core

children.title: Simplification–Cosimplification Duality
children.top_down_role: Dual relationship between the two redundancy reductions.

assumptions_latex: \(M\) is a finite matroid on ground set \(E\).
Simplification retains one representative from each nonloop parallel class; cosimplification is defined dually.
knowledge_statements.conclusion_latex: \(\operatorname{co}(M)=(\operatorname{si}(M^{*}))^{*}\) and \(\operatorname{si}(M)=(\operatorname{co}(M^{*}))^{*}\), up to the canonical choices of retained representatives.
knowledge_statements.scope_note: Finite-matroid duality, with representative choices understood up to isomorphism.

source_refs.locator: Chapter 5. Elements of matroid theory p. 172

knowledge_statements.statement_latex: Let \(M\) be a finite matroid. Deleting its loops and retaining one element from each nonloop parallel class produces \(\operatorname{si}(M)\). Define cosimplification by \(\operatorname{co}(M):=(\operatorname{si}(M^{*}))^{*}\). Consequently, simplification and cosimplification are exchanged by duality: \[\operatorname{co}(M)=(\operatorname{si}(M^{*}))^{*},\qquad \operatorname{si}(M)=(\operatorname{co}(M^{*}))^{*}.\] Equivalently, series classes of \(M\) are parallel classes of \(M^{*}\), while coloops of \(M\) are loops of \(M^{*}\). The identities are canonical up to the choices of class representatives and the resulting matroid isomorphisms.
knowledge_statements.statement_plain: Duality exchanges loops with coloops and parallel classes with series classes, so simplifying the dual and dualizing back gives cosimplification.
knowledge_statements.title: Simplification–Cosimplification Duality

knowledge_statements.statement_title: Elongation of a matroid
knowledge_statements.scope_note: Defines the independent sets and rank function of the finite elongation construction.
knowledge_statements.statement_latex: Let $M=(S,\mathcal F)$ be a matroid with rank function $r$, and let $f\in\mathbb Z_{\ge0}$. Its $f$-elongation $M^f$ declares $X\subseteq S$ independent when $X$ can be obtained from some $I\in\mathcal F$ by adding at most $f$ elements of $S$. This defines a matroid whose rank function is $r^f(X)=\min\{r(X)+f,|X|\}$ for every $X\subseteq S$.
knowledge_statements.statement_plain: The f-elongation makes a set independent when it differs from an original independent set by at most f added elements. The result is a matroid, and its rank on X is the smaller of the size of X and the original rank of X plus f.
assumptions_latex: M=(S,\mathcal F)\text{ is a matroid with rank function }r
knowledge_statements.conclusion_latex: M^f\text{ is a matroid with }r^f(X)=\min\{r(X)+f,|X|\}\quad\forall X\subseteq S.

knowledge_statements.statement_title: Relaxation under Deletion and Contraction
knowledge_statements.scope_note: Interaction of circuit-hyperplane relaxation with single-element minors, including loop and coloop exceptions.
knowledge_statements.statement_latex: Let \(X\) be a circuit-hyperplane of a matroid \(M\), and let \(M'\) be obtained by relaxing \(X\). If \(e\in E(M)\setminus X\), then \(M/e=M'/e\); unless \(e\) is a coloop of \(M\), \(M'\setminus e\) is obtained from \(M\setminus e\) by relaxing its circuit-hyperplane \(X\). Dually, if \(f\in X\), then \(M\setminus f=M'\setminus f\); unless \(f\) is a loop of \(M\), \(M'/f\) is obtained from \(M/f\) by relaxing its circuit-hyperplane \(X\setminus\{f\}\).
knowledge_statements.statement_plain: Relaxing a circuit-hyperplane commutes exactly with contraction outside it and deletion inside it. The complementary deletion or contraction also preserves the relaxation relation, except when the selected element is respectively a coloop or a loop.
knowledge_statements.conclusion_latex: \(e\in E(M)\setminus X\Rightarrow M/e=M'/e\), and if \(e\) is not a coloop then \(M'\setminus e\) relaxes \(X\) in \(M\setminus e\); dually, \(f\in X\Rightarrow M\setminus f=M'\setminus f\), and if \(f\) is not a loop then \(M'/f\) relaxes \(X\setminus\{f\}\) in \(M/f\).

knowledge_statements.statement_title: Matroid Duality and the Dual Rank Formula
knowledge_statements.scope_note: Characterizes preservation of the matroid property under independence-system duality and, under the matroid hypothesis, gives the dual rank function.
knowledge_statements.statement_latex:
Let $(E,\mathcal F)$ be an independence system, let $(E,\mathcal F^*)$ be its dual, and let $r$ and $r^*$ be their rank functions. Then
\[
(E,\mathcal F)\text{ is a matroid}\iff(E,\mathcal F^*)\text{ is a matroid}.
\]
If $(E,\mathcal F)$ is a matroid, then for every $F\subseteq E$,
\[
r^*(F)=|F|+r(E\setminus F)-r(E).
\]
knowledge_statements.statement_plain: An independence system is a matroid exactly when its dual is a matroid. When it is a matroid, the dual rank of a set equals its cardinality plus the primal rank of its complement minus the rank of the ground set.
assumptions_latex: r\text{ and }r^*\text{ are the corresponding rank functions}
knowledge_statements.conclusion_latex: \bigl((E,\mathcal F)\text{ is a matroid}\iff(E,\mathcal F^*)\text{ is a matroid}\bigr)\ \land\ \bigl((E,\mathcal F)\text{ is a matroid}\Rightarrow \forall F\subseteq E,\ r^*(F)=|F|+r(E\setminus F)-r(E)\bigr)

knowledge_statements.statement_title: Graphic–cographic trichotomy for the Shannon Switching Game
knowledge_statements.scope_note: Characterizes short, cut, and neutral games by mutually exclusive cospanning tree and cotree configurations relative to the nonplayable edge.
knowledge_statements.statement_latex: Let $G$ be the graph of a Shannon Switching Game, with distinguished nonplayable edge $e$. Exactly one of the following holds: (i) $G$ contains two disjoint trees that are cospanning in the graphic matroid, span $e$, and do not contain $e$; equivalently, the game is short. (ii) $G$ contains two disjoint cotrees that are cospanning in the cographic matroid, span $e$, and do not contain $e$; equivalently, the game is cut. (iii) $G$ contains two disjoint trees that are cospanning in the graphic matroid, with $e$ belonging to one of them, and also two disjoint cotrees that are cospanning in the cographic matroid, with $e$ belonging to one of them; equivalently, the game is neutral.
knowledge_statements.statement_plain: For a Shannon switching graph with nonplayable edge e, exactly one of three cases occurs. A pair of disjoint graphic-matroid cospanning trees that span but omit e characterizes a short game. The analogous cographic-matroid cotree condition characterizes a cut game. Cospanning tree and cotree pairs in which e belongs to one member of each pair characterize a neutral game.
assumptions_latex: G\text{ is the graph of a Shannon Switching Game.}
e\in E(G)\text{ is the distinguished nonplayable edge.}
knowledge_statements.conclusion_latex: \text{Exactly one of the short, cut, and neutral configurations holds, and each configuration is equivalent to its stated game class.}

knowledge_statements.statement_title: r-spikes and tipless r-spikes
knowledge_statements.scope_note: Defines an r-spike by its distinguished tip, legs, and complete circuit family; incidental historical and example prose is omitted.
knowledge_statements.statement_latex: Let \(r\ge3\). A matroid \(M\) with tip \(t\) and legs \(L_i=\{t,x_i,y_i\}\) for \(1\le i\le r\) is an \(r\)-spike if \(E(M)=\bigcup_{i=1}^rL_i\) and its circuits are: (i) the sets \(L_i\); (ii) every \(\{x_i,y_i,x_j,y_j\}\) with \(1\le i<j\le r\); (iii) a family \(\mathcal C_3\subseteq\{\{z_1,\ldots,z_r\}:z_i\in\{x_i,y_i\}\}\) in which distinct members intersect in at most \(r-2\) elements; and (iv) every \((r+1)\)-subset of \(E(M)\) containing no circuit from (i)--(iii). The deletion \(M\setminus t\) is the associated tipless \(r\)-spike; the spike is free when \(\mathcal C_3=\varnothing\).
knowledge_statements.statement_plain: For r at least three, an r-spike consists of r three-element legs sharing a tip. Its circuits are the legs, every four-element union of two leg pairs without the tip, a suitably sparse family of transversals choosing one element from each pair, and the remaining minimal (r+1)-element circuits. Deleting the tip gives a tipless spike, and the spike is free when the transversal-circuit family is empty.
knowledge_statements.conclusion_latex: \mathcal C(M)=\{L_i	o_string\}_{i=1}^r\cup\{\{x_i,y_i,x_j,y_j\}:i<j\}\cup\mathcal C_3\cup\{X\subseteq E(M):|X|=r+1,\ X\text{ contains no member of the preceding families}\},\quad M\setminus t\text{ is a tipless }r\text{-spike}.

knowledge_statements.statement_latex: For a finite matroid \(M=(E,\mathcal B)\), the dual matroid \(M^{*}\) has the same ground set and basis family \[\mathcal B(M^{*})=\{E\setminus B:B\in\mathcal B\}.\] Thus \(B^{*}\subseteq E\) is a basis of \(M^{*}\) if and only if \(E\setminus B^{*}\) is a basis of \(M\). knowledge_statements.scope_note: An if-and-only-if basis-family characterization using nonemptiness and the reverse-oriented exchange condition.

knowledge_statements.statement_title: Circuit–Cocircuit Characterization of Tipless Spikes
knowledge_statements.scope_note: Characterizes rank-r tipless spikes through a partition into pairs whose pairwise unions are simultaneously circuits and cocircuits.
knowledge_statements.statement_latex: For every integer \(r\ge 3\), a rank-\(r\) matroid \(M\) on a ground set \(E\) with \(|E|=2r\) is a tipless spike if and only if \(E\) can be partitioned as \(E=P_1\mathbin{\dot\cup}\cdots\mathbin{\dot\cup}P_r\), where \(|P_i|=2\), such that \(P_i\cup P_j\) is both a circuit and a cocircuit of \(M\) for every \(1\le i<j\le r\).
knowledge_statements.statement_plain: For r at least 3, a rank-r matroid on 2r elements is a tipless spike exactly when its ground set can be partitioned into r pairs such that the union of every two distinct pairs is both a circuit and a cocircuit.
knowledge_statements.conclusion_latex: M\text{ is a tipless spike}\iff \exists\,E(M)=P_1\mathbin{\dot\cup}\cdots\mathbin{\dot\cup}P_r:\ |P_i|=2\ \land\ \forall i<j,\ P_i\cup P_j\in\mathcal C(M)\cap\mathcal C^*(M).

knowledge_statements.statement_title: Deletion–Contraction Greedy Classification
knowledge_statements.scope_note: This is presented as a substitution for the circuit and cocircuit steps of the preceding greedy variant.
knowledge_statements.statement_latex: Maintain disjoint sets \(A,A',B\), initially \(A=A'=\varnothing\) and \(B=E\), together with the current matroid minor. Repeatedly perform either operation: (i) if \(B\) contains a circuit \(C\), move its smallest element from \(B\) to \(A'\) and delete that element from the current matroid; otherwise move all remaining elements of \(B\) to \(A\) and stop; (ii) if \(B\) contains a cocircuit \(D\), move its largest element from \(B\) to \(A\) and contract that element in the current matroid; otherwise move all remaining elements of \(B\) to \(A'\) and stop.
knowledge_statements.statement_plain: In the current matroid minor, reject and delete the smallest element of a circuit, or accept and contract the largest element of a cocircuit. If the requested circuit or cocircuit does not exist, classify all remaining elements and stop.
assumptions_latex: M\text{ is a matroid on a finite totally ordered ground set }E.
\text{Circuit and cocircuit tests are made in the current matroid minor}.
knowledge_statements.conclusion_latex: B=\varnothing\quad\text{and}\quad E=A\mathbin{\dot\cup}A'\text{ upon termination}.

knowledge_statements.statement_title: Serial multiplication by circuit replacement
knowledge_statements.scope_note: Defines the resulting circuit family and records the graphic realization.
knowledge_statements.statement_latex: Let $M$ be a matroid on $S$, replace $s\in S$ by a disjoint set $S'=\{s_1,\ldots,s_k\}$, and use ground set $(S\setminus\{s\})\cup S'$. Declare $X$ to be a circuit exactly when either $X\subseteq S\setminus\{s\}$ is a circuit of $M$, or $S'\subseteq X$ and $(X\setminus S')\cup\{s\}$ is a circuit of $M$. This circuit family defines a matroid. In a graphic matroid, for $k\ge1$, it corresponds to replacing an edge by a path of length $k$, equivalently subdividing it with $k-1$ new vertices.
knowledge_statements.statement_plain: Serial multiplication replaces an element by k new elements and defines the new circuits as the old circuits avoiding the replaced element together with circuits obtained by replacing that element by the entire new set. These circuits form a matroid. For graphic matroids and positive k, the operation replaces an edge by a path of length k.
knowledge_statements.conclusion_latex: \mathcal C'=\{X\in\mathcal C(M):s\notin X\}\cup\{(C\setminus\{s\})\cup S':C\in\mathcal C(M),\ s\in C\}\text{ is the circuit family of a matroid.

knowledge_statements.statement_title: Unique Tipped-Spike Extension
knowledge_statements.scope_note: Establishes existence and uniqueness of a tipped-spike extension from prescribed paired circuit–cocircuit data.
knowledge_statements.statement_latex: Let \(r\ge 3\), let \(E=\{x_1,y_1,\ldots,x_r,y_r\}\), and let \(M\) be a rank-\(r\) matroid on \(E\). Suppose that \(\{x_i,y_i,x_j,y_j\}\) is both a circuit and a cocircuit of \(M\) for every \(1\le i<j\le r\). Then there is a unique rank-\(r\) spike \(N\) with tip \(t\) and legs \(\{t,x_i,y_i\}\), \(i=1,\ldots,r\), such that \(N\setminus t=M\). Consequently, \(M\) is a tipless spike.
knowledge_statements.statement_plain: Let r be at least 3 and let a rank-r matroid have ground set partitioned into the displayed pairs. If every union of two distinct pairs is both a circuit and a cocircuit, then there is a unique rank-r spike obtained by adjoining a tip whose legs contain those pairs, and deleting the tip recovers the original matroid. Hence the original matroid is a tipless spike.
knowledge_statements.conclusion_latex: \exists!\,N:\ N\text{ is a rank-}r\text{ spike with tip }t,\ L_i=\{t,x_i,y_i\},\ N\setminus t=M;\quad M\text{ is a tipless spike}.

knowledge_statements.conclusion_latex: \(H\) is a hyperplane of \(M\) iff \(E\setminus H\) is a circuit of \(M^{*}\); \(F\) is a flat iff \(E\setminus F\) is a union of cocircuits of \(M\).

knowledge_statements.statement_latex: For \(H\subseteq E\), \(H\) is a hyperplane of \(M\) if and only if \(E\setminus H\) is a cocircuit of \(M\), equivalently a circuit of \(M^{*}\). More generally, \(F\subseteq E\) is a flat of \(M\) if and only if, for every \(e\in E\setminus F\), there exists a cocircuit \(C^{*}\) of \(M\) satisfying \(e\in C^{*}\subseteq E\setminus F\). Thus \(E\setminus F\) is a union of cocircuits; the hyperplane case is exactly when this complement is one cocircuit.
knowledge_statements.statement_plain: A hyperplane's complement is a cocircuit, hence a dual circuit; more generally, the complement of any flat is a union of cocircuits.

knowledge_statements.statement_title: Incidence characterization of modular lines and hyperplanes
knowledge_statements.scope_note: The loopless hypothesis applies to both universally quantified equivalences.
knowledge_statements.statement_latex: Let \(M\) be loopless. Every hyperplane \(H\) of \(M\) is modular if and only if \(H\) intersects every line of \(M\), considered separately for each \(H\). Every line \(L\) of \(M\) is modular if and only if \(L\) intersects every hyperplane of \(M\), considered separately for each \(L\).
knowledge_statements.statement_plain: In a loopless matroid, a hyperplane is modular exactly when it meets every line, and a line is modular exactly when it meets every hyperplane.
knowledge_statements.conclusion_latex: \forall H\text{ a hyperplane of }M,\ H\text{ is modular}\iff \forall L\text{ a line of }M,\ H\cap L\ne\varnothing;\qquad \forall L\text{ a line of }M,\ L\text{ is modular}\iff \forall H\text{ a hyperplane of }M,\ L\cap H\ne\varnothing.

knowledge_statements.statement_latex: Let \(G\) be a finite connected graph with a fixed plane embedding, and let \(G^{\dagger}\) be its geometric dual, using the natural bijection between primal and dual edges. Then \[M(G)^{*}=M(G^{\dagger}).\] Under this correspondence, cycles of \(G^{\dagger}\) are bonds of \(G\), and complements of spanning trees of \(G\) are spanning trees of \(G^{\dagger}\). Thus the dual of a graphic matroid is always cographic, and in the plane case it is represented graphically by the geometric dual.
knowledge_statements.statement_plain: For a connected plane graph, the dual of its cycle matroid is the cycle matroid of the geometric dual graph.

knowledge_statements.statement_latex: The class of finite transversal matroids is not closed under matroid duality. More precisely, if \(M\) is transversal, then \(M^{*}\) is a strict gammoid; conversely, the dual of every strict gammoid is transversal. Hence \[\{M^{*}:M\text{ is transversal}\}=\{N:N\text{ is a strict gammoid}\}.\] Since strict gammoids and transversal matroids are not the same class, one cannot infer that \(M^{*}\) is transversal merely from the transversality of \(M\).
knowledge_statements.statement_plain: Duals of transversal matroids are exactly strict gammoids, so the transversal class itself is not closed under duality.
knowledge_statements.title: Transversal Duality

knowledge_statements.statement_title: Directed linkage and its associated bipartite graph
knowledge_statements.scope_note: Defines directed linkage, linkage into a target set, the linkable-set family, and the bipartite construction used in transversal duality.
knowledge_statements.statement_latex: Let \(G\) be a directed graph with vertex set \(V\). Sets \(X,Y\subseteq V\) are linked if \(|X|=|Y|\) and there are \(|X|\) pairwise vertex-disjoint directed paths whose initial vertices lie in \(X\) and whose final vertices lie in \(Y\); a path may consist of one vertex. The set \(X\) is linked into \(Z\subseteq V\) if it is linked to some subset of \(Z\), and \(L(G,B_0)=\{X\subseteq V:X\text{ is linked into }B_0\}\). For a disjoint copy \(\widehat V\) of \(V\), the associated bipartite graph \(\widehat G\) has vertex set \(V\cup\widehat V\) and edge set \(\{v\widehat v:v\in V\}\cup\{v\widehat u:(u,v)\in E(G)\}\).
knowledge_statements.statement_plain: Equally sized vertex sets are linked when pairwise vertex-disjoint directed paths join them, with one-vertex paths allowed. A set is linked into a target when it is linked to a subset of that target. The associated bipartite graph joins each vertex to its copy and joins v to the copy of u for every arc from u to v.
assumptions_latex: G\text{ is a directed graph with vertex set }V
\widehat V\text{ is a disjoint copy of }V
knowledge_statements.conclusion_latex: L(G,B_0)=\{X\subseteq V:X\text{ is linked into }B_0\},\qquad E(\widehat G)=\{v\widehat v:v\in V\}\cup\{v\widehat u:(u,v)\in E(G)\}.

knowledge_statements.statement_latex: Let \(M\) be represented over \(\mathbb F\) by a full-row-rank matrix whose columns are indexed by \(E\). After choosing a basis and permuting columns, write \(A=[I_r\ D]\). Then the matrix \[A^{*}=[-D^{\mathsf T}\ I_{|E|-r}]\] represents \(M^{*}\) over the same field, with columns in the corresponding complementary order. Indeed, the row spaces of \(A\) and \(A^{*}\) are orthogonal. Consequently, the class of matroids representable over any fixed field \(\mathbb F\) is closed under duality.
knowledge_statements.statement_plain: A standard-form matrix representation yields a transposed complementary matrix for the dual, so fixed-field representability is dual-closed.

knowledge_statements.statement_title: Orthogonality, Orthogonal Complements, and Row Spaces
knowledge_statements.scope_note: Foundational definitions used to express duality for represented matroids.
knowledge_statements.statement_latex: For \(v=(v_1,\ldots,v_n)\) and \(w=(w_1,\ldots,w_n)\) in \(V(n,\mathbb F)\), define \(v\cdot w=\sum_{i=1}^n v_iw_i\); the vectors are orthogonal when \(v\cdot w=0\). For \(W\le V(n,\mathbb F)\), define \(W^\perp=\{v\in V(n,\mathbb F):v\cdot w=0\text{ for every }w\in W\}\). Then \(W^\perp\) is a subspace and \(W\subseteq(W^\perp)^\perp\). For \(A\in\mathbb F^{m\times n}\), \(\mathcal R(A)\) is the span of the rows of \(A\). If \(\mathbb F=\operatorname{GF}(q)\), then \(\mathcal R(A)\) is a linear \(q\)-ary code of length \(n\).
knowledge_statements.statement_plain: The dot product defines orthogonality. The orthogonal complement of a subspace consists of the vectors orthogonal to all its members; it is a subspace, and its double orthogonal complement contains the original subspace. A matrix row space is the span of its rows and, over GF(q), is a linear q-ary code of length equal to the number of columns.
knowledge_statements.conclusion_latex: W^\perp\le V(n,\mathbb F),\quad W\subseteq(W^\perp)^\perp,\quad \mathcal R(A)=\operatorname{span}\{\text{rows of }A\},\quad \mathbb F=\operatorname{GF}(q)\Rightarrow\mathcal R(A)\text{ is a linear }q\text{-ary code of length }n

children.title: Dual-Closure Boundaries
children.top_down_role: Class boundaries governing preservation or departure under dualization.

assumptions_latex: \(\mathcal K\) is a class of finite matroids closed under isomorphism.
Duality is taken on the same ground set.
knowledge_statements.conclusion_latex: \(\mathcal K\) is dual-closed iff \(M\in\mathcal K\Rightarrow M^{*}\in\mathcal K\); fixed-field representable classes satisfy this, while graphic and transversal classes generally do not.
knowledge_statements.scope_note: Closure boundaries for common finite-matroid representation classes.

source_refs.locator: Chapter 5. Elements of matroid theory p. 172
Section 13. Duality Theory p. 53

knowledge_statements.statement_latex: A matroid class \(\mathcal K\) is dual-closed precisely when \(M\in\mathcal K\) implies \(M^{*}\in\mathcal K\). Matroids representable over a fixed field \(\mathbb F\) satisfy this condition. Graphic matroids do not satisfy it in general: their duals are cographic, becoming graphic in the planar regime. Transversal matroids also fail general dual closure: their duals are strict gammoids. Thus closure under duality must be established for the specified representation class and cannot be inferred merely from the existence of a primal representation.
knowledge_statements.statement_plain: Fixed-field representable matroids are dual-closed, whereas graphic and transversal matroids require larger dual partner classes except in special regimes.
knowledge_statements.title: Dual-Closure Boundaries

knowledge_statements.statement_title: Delta and Nabla Exchanges Are Mutual Inverses
knowledge_statements.scope_note: Two inverse identities under the respective coindependence/triangle and independence/triad hypotheses.
knowledge_statements.statement_latex:
Let M be a matroid. (i) If X is coindependent in M and every three-element subset of X is a triangle, then 
abla_X(\Delta_X(M)) is well-defined and 
abla_X(\Delta_X(M))=M. (ii) If X is independent in M and every three-element subset of X is a triad, then \Delta_X(
abla_X(M)) is well-defined and \Delta_X(
abla_X(M))=M.
knowledge_statements.statement_plain: For a coindependent set whose three-element subsets are triangles, generalized delta exchange followed by generalized nabla exchange is well-defined and recovers the original matroid. knowledge_statements.statement_title: Circuit characterization of excluding a uniform minor
knowledge_statements.scope_note: Characterizes exclusion of a specified uniform minor by a bound on circuits through qualifying series classes.
knowledge_statements.statement_latex: Let \(k>1\) be an integer. knowledge_statements.statement_title: Graph Minors and Cycle-Matroid Minors
knowledge_statements.scope_note: Defines graph minors, gives the connected-graph deletion–contraction characterization, and preserves the failure of the converse implication for cycle matroids.
knowledge_statements.statement_latex: A graph \(H\) is a minor of a graph \(G\) if it is a contraction of a subgraph of \(G\); equivalently, \(H\) can be obtained from \(G\) by edge deletions, edge contractions, and deletions of isolated vertices. If \(G\) is connected, then \(H\) is a minor of \(G\) if and only if \(H=G\setminus X/Y\) for some disjoint \(X,Y\subseteq E(G)\). Moreover, if \(H\) is a minor of \(G\), then \(M(H)\) is a minor of \(M(G)\), but the converse need not hold.
knowledge_statements.statement_plain: A graph minor is a contraction of a subgraph, equivalently a graph obtained through edge deletions, edge contractions, and removal of isolated vertices. When G is connected, H is a minor exactly when it can be written as G with one edge set deleted and a disjoint edge set contracted. Graph minors induce cycle-matroid minors, but cycle-matroid minors need not arise from graph minors.
assumptions_latex: G\text{ is connected only for the characterization }H=G\setminus X/Y
knowledge_statements.conclusion_latex: H\preceq G\iff H\text{ is obtainable by edge deletions, edge contractions, and isolated-vertex deletions};\quad G\text{ connected}\Rightarrow\bigl[H\preceq G\iff \exists X,Y\subseteq E(G),\ X\cap Y=\varnothing,\ H=G\setminus X/Y\bigr];\quad H\preceq G\Rightarrow M(H)\preceq M(G),\text{ with no converse in general.}

knowledge_statements.statement_title: Named and Family Matroid Minors
knowledge_statements.scope_note: Defines minors by isomorphism type relative to one matroid or a set of matroids.

knowledge_statements.title: Matroid Deletion
knowledge_statements.scope_note: Deletion of an arbitrary subset from a finite matroid.
knowledge_statements.statement_latex:
Let \(M=(E,\mathcal I)\) be a finite matroid and let \(D\subseteq E\). The deletion of \(D\) from \(M\), denoted \(M\setminus D\), is the matroid on \(E\setminus D\) whose independent sets are
\[\mathcal I(M\setminus D)=\{I\in\mathcal I:I\subseteq E\setminus D\}.\]
Equivalently, for every \(X\subseteq E\setminus D\), its rank satisfies \(r_{M\setminus D}(X)=r_M(X)\).
knowledge_statements.statement_plain: Deleting a subset removes its elements while retaining exactly the original independent sets supported on the remaining ground set.
knowledge_statements.conclusion_latex: \(\mathcal I(M\setminus D)=\{I\in\mathcal I:I\subseteq E\setminus D\}\).

knowledge_statements.statement_title: Two-element witness for increased connectivity after minor reconstruction
knowledge_statements.scope_note: Matroid connectivity criterion for a deletion-contraction minor and compatible ground-set partitions.
knowledge_statements.statement_latex: Let $N=M\setminus D/C$, where $D$ is coindependent and $C$ is independent in $M$. Let $(X,Y)$ and $(X',Y')$ be partitions of $E(N)$ and $E(M)$, respectively, with $X\subseteq X'$ and $Y\subseteq Y'$. Then $\lambda_M(X')>\lambda_N(X)$ if and only if there exist $x\in X'$ and $y\in Y'$ such that $\lambda_{M[D,C;\{x,y\}]}(X\cup\{x\})>\lambda_N(X)$. The witnesses may satisfy $x\in X$ and $y\in Y$.
knowledge_statements.statement_plain: For a minor obtained by deleting a coindependent set and contracting an independent set, a compatible enlarged partition has greater connectivity exactly when two elements, one from each enlarged side, already witness the increase in the corresponding two-element reconstruction. The witnesses may already belong to the original sides.
knowledge_statements.conclusion_latex: \lambda_M(X')>\lambda_N(X)\iff \exists x\in X'\,\exists y\in Y':\ \lambda_{M[D,C;\{x,y\}]}(X\cup\{x\})>\lambda_N(X)

knowledge_statements.title: Matroid Restriction
knowledge_statements.scope_note: Restriction of a finite matroid to a specified ground-set subset.
knowledge_statements.statement_latex:
Let \(M=(E,\mathcal I)\) be a finite matroid and let \(S\subseteq E\). The restriction of \(M\) to \(S\), denoted \(M|S\), is the matroid on \(S\) with
\[\mathcal I(M|S)=\{I\in\mathcal I:I\subseteq S\}.\]
Thus, for every \(X\subseteq S\), one has \(r_{M|S}(X)=r_M(X)\).
knowledge_statements.statement_plain: Restriction retains a chosen subset and exactly those original independent sets contained in it.
knowledge_statements.conclusion_latex: \(\mathcal I(M|S)=\{I\in\mathcal I:I\subseteq S\}\).

knowledge_statements.statement_latex: Let M=(S,\mathcal F) be a matroid and S'\subseteq S. Define \mathcal F'=\{F\subseteq S':F\in\mathcal F\}. Then M'=(S',\mathcal F') is a matroid, called the restriction of M to S'. With Z=S\setminus S', it is also obtained by deleting Z, and is denoted M'=M\mid S'=M-Z.
knowledge_statements.statement_plain: Restricting a matroid to a subset of its ground set retains exactly the independent sets contained in that subset and produces another matroid. Equivalently, this operation deletes the complementary elements.
knowledge_statements.conclusion_latex: M\mid S'=(S',\{F\subseteq S':F\in\mathcal F\})=M-Z\text{ is a matroid.}

knowledge_statements.title: Matroid Contraction
knowledge_statements.scope_note: Contraction characterized by its rank function.
knowledge_statements.statement_latex:
Let \(M\) be a finite matroid on \(E\) with rank function \(r_M\), and let \(C\subseteq E\). The contraction \(M/C\) is the matroid on \(E\setminus C\) whose rank function is
\[r_{M/C}(X)=r_M(X\cup C)-r_M(C)\qquad(X\subseteq E\setminus C).\]
Equivalently, if \(B_C\) is any basis of \(M|C\), then \(I\subseteq E\setminus C\) is independent in \(M/C\) exactly when \(I\cup B_C\) is independent in \(M\).
knowledge_statements.statement_plain: Contraction removes a subset after accounting for its rank; adjoining a basis of the contracted subset tests independence in the contraction.
knowledge_statements.conclusion_latex: \(r_{M/C}(X)=r_M(X\cup C)-r_M(C)\) for every \(X\subseteq E\setminus C\).

notation.meaning: a basis of the restriction to C

knowledge_statements.statement_latex: Let \(M\) be a matroid on \(E\) and let \(T\subseteq E\). The contraction of \(T\) from \(M\) is \[M/T=(M^*\setminus T)^*,\] with ground set \(E\setminus T\). It may also be denoted \(M.(E\setminus T)\), the contraction of \(M\) onto \(E\setminus T\).

knowledge_statements.conclusion_latex: M/T=(M^*\setminus T)^*,\qquad E(M/T)=E\setminus T

knowledge_statements.statement_title: Composition and Commutation Laws for Deletion and Contraction
knowledge_statements.scope_note: States the minor-operation identities for two disjoint subsets of a matroid ground set.
knowledge_statements.statement_latex: Let \(M\) be a matroid, and let \(T_1,T_2\subseteq E(M)\) be disjoint. Then \[(M\setminus T_1)\setminus T_2=M\setminus(T_1\cup T_2)=(M\setminus T_2)\setminus T_1,\] \[(M/T_1)/T_2=M/(T_1\cup T_2)=(M/T_2)/T_1,\] and \[(M\setminus T_1)/T_2=(M/T_2)\setminus T_1.\]
knowledge_statements.statement_plain: For disjoint sets T1 and T2, successive deletions compose as deletion of their union, successive contractions compose as contraction of their union, and deletion of T1 commutes with contraction of T2.
knowledge_statements.conclusion_latex: (M\setminus T_1)\setminus T_2=M\setminus(T_1\cup T_2)=(M\setminus T_2)\setminus T_1,\quad (M/T_1)/T_2=M/(T_1\cup T_2)=(M/T_2)/T_1,\quad (M\setminus T_1)/T_2=(M/T_2)\setminus T_1

knowledge_statements.statement_title: Matroid contraction formulas
knowledge_statements.scope_note: Dual, rank, independence, and circuit descriptions of contraction.
knowledge_statements.statement_latex: Let \(M=(S,\mathcal I)\) be a matroid and \(Z\subseteq S\). Contraction is defined by \(M/Z=(M^*\setminus Z)^*\). For every \(X\subseteq S\setminus Z\), \[r_{M/Z}(X)=r_M(X\cup Z)-r_M(Z).\] If \(B_Z\) is a base of \(Z\), then \(I\subseteq S\setminus Z\) is independent in \(M/Z\) if and only if \(I\cup B_Z\) is independent in \(M\). If \(Y=S\setminus Z\), the circuits of \(M/Z=M\cdot Y\) are precisely the inclusion-minimal nonempty sets among \(\{C\cap Y:C\in\mathcal C(M)\}\).
knowledge_statements.statement_plain: Contraction is deletion in the dual followed by dualization. Its rank is obtained by adjoining the contracted set and subtracting its rank. Independence can be tested by adjoining a base of the contracted set, and its circuits are the minimal nonempty intersections of original circuits with the retained ground set.

knowledge_statements.title: Deletion–Restriction Correspondence
knowledge_statements.scope_note: Canonical equality between deletion and restriction.
knowledge_statements.statement_latex:
Let \(M\) be a finite matroid on \(E\), and let \(D\subseteq E\). Deleting \(D\) is identical to restricting \(M\) to its complementary ground set:
\[M\setminus D=M|(E\setminus D).\]
The equality is literal as matroids on \(E\setminus D\): both sides have precisely the independent sets \(I\in\mathcal I(M)\) satisfying \(I\subseteq E\setminus D\).
knowledge_statements.statement_plain: Deleting a subset is exactly the same operation as restricting the matroid to the subset's complement.
knowledge_statements.conclusion_latex: \(M\setminus D=M|(E\setminus D)\).

children.top_down_role: Dual interchange between deletion and contraction.

knowledge_statements.conclusion_latex: \((M\setminus D)^*=M^*/D\) and \((M/C)^*=M^*\setminus C\).

knowledge_statements.statement_latex:
Let \(M\) be a finite matroid on \(E\), let \(D,C\subseteq E\), and write \(M^*\) for its dual. Deletion and contraction are interchanged by duality:
\[(M\setminus D)^*=M^*/D,\qquad (M/C)^*=M^*\setminus C.\]
Each equality is between matroids on the corresponding complementary ground set. In particular, either minor operation can be defined from the other together with matroid duality.
knowledge_statements.statement_plain: Taking the dual converts deletion into contraction and contraction into deletion on the same removed subset.

knowledge_statements.statement_title: Matroid Deletion, Contraction, and Dual Correspondence
knowledge_statements.scope_note: Rank-based definitions of deletion and contraction, followed by their interchange under dualization.
knowledge_statements.statement_latex: Let $M=(E,\mathcal I)$ have rank function $r$, and let $S\subseteq E$. The independent sets of $M\operatorname{del}S$ are the sets $I'\subseteq E\setminus S$ such that $r(I')=|I'|$. The independent sets of $M\operatorname{ctr}S$ are the sets $I''\subseteq E\setminus S$ such that $r(I''\cup S)=|I''|+r(S)$. Under matroid duality, deletion corresponds to contraction and contraction corresponds to deletion.
knowledge_statements.statement_plain: Deletion retains the independent sets disjoint from S. In the contraction by S, a disjoint set is independent exactly when adjoining it to S increases rank by the size of that set. Duality interchanges deletion and contraction.
assumptions_latex: M=(E,\mathcal I)\text{ is a matroid with rank function }r
knowledge_statements.conclusion_latex: \mathcal I(M\operatorname{del}S)=\{I'\subseteq E\setminus S:r(I')=|I'|\},\quad \mathcal I(M\operatorname{ctr}S)=\{I''\subseteq E\setminus S:r(I''\cup S)=|I''|+r(S)\},\quad \text{duality interchanges deletion and contraction}

knowledge_statements.scope_note: The bound depends on rank parity and includes a recursive characterization of all equality cases.

knowledge_statements.statement_latex:
Let \(M\) be a finite matroid on \(E\), and let \(C,D\subseteq E\) be disjoint. For the minor \(N=(M\setminus D)/C\), duality exchanges deletion and contraction:
\[N^*=(M^*/D)\setminus C.\]
Consequently, the dual of every minor of \(M\) is a minor of \(M^*\), with the deleted and contracted sets exchanged.
