knowledge_statements.statement_title: Duality of Matroid Minors
knowledge_statements.scope_note: States invariance of the minor relation under matroid duality and the associated interchange of deletion and contraction.
knowledge_statements.statement_latex: For matroids $M$ and $N$, $N$ is a minor of $M$ if and only if $N^*$ is a minor of $M^*$. More particularly, for disjoint $X,Y\subseteq E(M)$, $$N=M\setminus X/Y\quad\Longleftrightarrow\quad N^*=M^*/X\setminus Y.$$
knowledge_statements.statement_plain: N is a minor of M if and only if its dual is a minor of the dual of M. More particularly, duality changes deletion of X into contraction of X and contraction of Y into deletion of Y.
knowledge_statements.conclusion_latex: N\preccurlyeq M\iff N^*\preccurlyeq M^*,\qquad N=M\setminus X/Y\iff N^*=M^*/X\setminus Y.

knowledge_statements.title: Minor Projection
knowledge_statements.scope_note: Contraction represented as projection of the rank and closure operators.
knowledge_statements.statement_latex:
Let \(M\) be a finite matroid on \(E\), contract \(C\subseteq E\), and put \(N=M/C\). For every \(X\subseteq E\setminus C\), the rank and closure in the projected matroid are
\[r_N(X)=r_M(X\cup C)-r_M(C),\qquad \operatorname{cl}_N(X)=\operatorname{cl}_M(X\cup C)\setminus C.\]
Thus contraction projects the dependence geometry of \(M\) along \(C\) onto the residual ground set \(E\setminus C\).
knowledge_statements.statement_plain: Contracting a subset projects rank and closure onto the remaining ground set by adjoining the contracted subset before evaluating them.
knowledge_statements.conclusion_latex: \(r_N(X)=r_M(X\cup C)-r_M(C)\) and \(\operatorname{cl}_N(X)=\operatorname{cl}_M(X\cup C)\setminus C\).

knowledge_statements.statement_title: Scum Theorem
knowledge_statements.scope_note: Contraction–restriction representation of an arbitrary matroid minor, with a flat contraction set when the minor is loopless.
knowledge_statements.statement_latex: Let \(N\) be a minor of a matroid \(M\). Then there exists \(Z\subseteq E(M)\setminus E(N)\) such that \(M/Z\) and \(N\) have the same rank and \(N\) is a restriction of \(M/Z\). Moreover, if \(N\) has no loops, then \(Z\) can be chosen to be a flat of \(M\).
knowledge_statements.statement_plain: Every minor N of M is a restriction of a contraction M/Z having the same rank as N. If N is loopless, Z may be chosen as a flat of M.
knowledge_statements.conclusion_latex: \(\exists Z\subseteq E(M)\setminus E(N)\) such that \(r(M/Z)=r(N)\) and \(N\) is a restriction of \(M/Z\); if \(N\) is loopless, \(Z\) may be chosen flat in \(M\).

knowledge_statements.title: Flat Transport through Minors
knowledge_statements.scope_note: Characterization of flats under restriction and contraction.
knowledge_statements.statement_latex: Let \(M\) be a finite matroid on \(E\). If \(S\subseteq E\), then the flats of \(M|S\) are exactly the sets \(F\cap S\), where \(F\) ranges over flats of \(M\). If \(C\subseteq E\), then a set \(G\subseteq E\setminus C\) is a flat of \(M/C\) exactly when \(G\cup C\) is a flat of \(M\). Hence restriction transports flats by intersection, while contraction transports them through flats containing the contracted set.
knowledge_statements.statement_plain: Restriction flats arise by intersection with the retained set; contraction flats correspond to original flats containing the contracted set.
knowledge_statements.conclusion_latex: \(\mathcal F(M|S)=\{F\cap S:F\in\mathcal F(M)\}\) and \(G\in\mathcal F(M/C)\iff G\cup C\in\mathcal F(M)\).

knowledge_statements.statement_title: Flats under Contraction and Deletion
knowledge_statements.scope_note: Exact transport laws for flats through contraction and deletion.
knowledge_statements.statement_latex: Let \(T\subseteq E(M)\) and \(F\subseteq E(M)\setminus T\). Then (i) \(F\) is a flat of \(M/T\) if and only if \(F\cup T\) is a flat of \(M\); and (ii) \(F\) is a flat of \(M\setminus T\) if and only if there exists a flat \(F'\) of \(M\) such that \(F=F'\setminus T\).
knowledge_statements.statement_plain: A set F disjoint from T is a flat after contracting T exactly when F union T is a flat of M. It is a flat after deleting T exactly when it is the part outside T of some flat of M.
knowledge_statements.conclusion_latex: \(F\in\mathcal L(M/T)\iff F\cup T\in\mathcal L(M)\), and \(F\in\mathcal L(M\setminus T)\iff \exists F'\in\mathcal L(M):F=F'\setminus T\).

knowledge_statements.title: Projection–Flat Correspondence
knowledge_statements.scope_note: Order correspondence between contraction flats and ambient flats above the contracted set.
knowledge_statements.statement_latex:
Let \(M\) be a finite matroid on \(E\), let \(C\subseteq E\), and set \(N=M/C\). The maps
\[\Phi(G)=G\cup C,\qquad \Psi(F)=F\setminus C\]
are mutually inverse, inclusion-preserving bijections between the flats \(G\) of \(N\) and the flats \(F\) of \(M\) satisfying \(C\subseteq F\). Under this correspondence, the projected closure obeys \(\operatorname{cl}_N(X)=\operatorname{cl}_M(X\cup C)\setminus C\).
knowledge_statements.statement_plain: Flats of a contraction correspond bijectively, by adjoining or removing the contracted set, to original flats containing that set.
knowledge_statements.conclusion_latex: \(\mathcal F(N)\cong\{F\in\mathcal F(M):C\subseteq F\}\) via \(G\mapsto G\cup C\).

knowledge_statements.statement_title: Flat-cover propagation at maximal rank difference
knowledge_statements.scope_note: Uses the ranks and flat lattices of the two matroids in the surrounding quotient setup.
knowledge_statements.statement_latex: Let \(X\) be a flat of \(M_2\) satisfying \(r_1(X)-r_2(X)=r_1(M_1)-r_2(M_2)\), and let \(Y\) be a flat of \(M_1\) covering \(X\) in \(\mathcal L(M_1)\). Then \(Y\) is a flat of \(M_2\) covering \(X\) in \(\mathcal L(M_2)\), and \(r_1(Y)-r_2(Y)=r_1(M_1)-r_2(M_2)\).
knowledge_statements.statement_plain: If a flat X attains the total rank difference and a flat Y of M1 covers X, then Y is also a flat of M2 covering X and attains the same rank difference.

knowledge_statements.title: Minor-Closed Matroid Classes
knowledge_statements.scope_note: Closure of a matroid class under all finite minor operations.
knowledge_statements.statement_latex:
A class \(\mathcal C\) of finite matroids is minor-closed if, for every \(M\in\mathcal C\) on ground set \(E\) and every pair of disjoint subsets \(C,D\subseteq E\),
\[(M\setminus D)/C\in\mathcal C.\]
Equivalently, \(\mathcal C\) is closed separately under deletion and contraction. Since sequences of deletions and contractions can be reordered on disjoint sets, this condition contains every matroid minor of each member of \(\mathcal C\).
knowledge_statements.statement_plain: A matroid class is minor-closed when every deletion-contraction minor of each member remains in the class.
assumptions_latex: \(\mathcal C\) is a class of finite matroids.
knowledge_statements.conclusion_latex: \(M\in\mathcal C\) and \(C\cap D=\varnothing\) imply \((M\setminus D)/C\in\mathcal C\).

notation.meaning: minor obtained by deleting D and contracting C

knowledge_statements.statement_title: Sharp size bounds for cographic, graphic, and finite-field-representable matroids
knowledge_statements.scope_note: States three cardinality bounds for simple rank-r matroids and preserves their equality characterizations.
knowledge_statements.statement_latex: Let \(M\) be a simple rank-\(r\) matroid. (i) If \(M\) is cographic and \(r\ge 2\), then \(\lvert E(M)\rvert\le 3(r-1)\), with equality if and only if \(M\cong M^*(G)\) for a cubic, 3-edge-connected graph \(G\). (ii) If \(M\) is graphic, then \(\lvert E(M)\rvert\le \binom{r+1}{2}\), with equality if and only if \(M\cong M(K_{r+1})\). (iii) If \(M\) is \(GF(q)\)-representable, then \(\lvert E(M)\rvert\le (q^r-1)/(q-1)\), with equality if and only if \(M\cong PG(r-1,q)\).
knowledge_statements.statement_plain: A simple cographic rank-r matroid has at most 3(r−1) elements when r is at least two, with equality exactly for the bond matroid of a cubic 3-edge-connected graph. The corresponding sharp graphic bound is binomial(r+1,2), attained exactly by the cycle matroid of K_{r+1}; the GF(q)-representable bound is (q^r−1)/(q−1), attained exactly by PG(r−1,q).
assumptions_latex: \(M\) is a simple matroid of rank \(r\).
knowledge_statements.conclusion_latex: \begin{aligned}&\text{(i)}\quad \lvert E(M)\rvert\le 3(r-1),\quad \lvert E(M)\rvert=3(r-1)\iff M\cong M^*(G)\text{ for cubic 3-edge-connected }G;\\&\text{(ii)}\quad \lvert E(M)\rvert\le\binom{r+1}{2},\quad \lvert E(M)\rvert=\binom{r+1}{2}\iff M\cong M(K_{r+1});\\&\text{(iii)}\quad \lvert E(M)\rvert\le\frac{q^r-1}{q-1},\quad \lvert E(M)\rvert=\frac{q^r-1}{q-1}\iff M\cong PG(r-1,q).\end{aligned}

knowledge_statements.statement_title: Extremal matroid in a minor-closed class
knowledge_statements.scope_note: Defines fixed-rank extension maximality and records that it is weaker than maximum cardinality.
knowledge_statements.statement_latex: A simple matroid \(M\) is extremal in a minor-closed class \(\mathcal M\) if \(M\in\mathcal M\) and \(\mathcal M\) contains no simple single-element extension of \(M\) having the same rank as \(M\). Every maximum-sized simple rank-\(r\) member of \(\mathcal M\) is extremal, but the converse is false. In particular, \(M^*(K_{3,3})\) is an extremal rank-4 regular matroid with nine elements, whereas the unique maximum-sized simple rank-4 regular matroid is \(M(K_5)\), with ten elements.

knowledge_statements.statement_title: Local extension–coextension test for a class stabilizer
knowledge_statements.scope_note: Characterizes stabilization of a minor-closed, dual-closed representable class using three local configurations.
knowledge_statements.statement_latex: Let $\mathbb F$ be a field, let $\mathcal M$ be a minor-closed class of $\mathbb F$-representable matroids that is closed under duality, and let $N\in\mathcal M$ be $3$-connected. Then $N$ stabilizes $\mathcal M$ if and only if $N$ stabilizes every $3$-connected $M\in\mathcal M$ of at least one of the following types: (i) $M\setminus x=N$ for some element $x$; (ii) $M/y=N$ for some element $y$; or (iii) $M\setminus x/y=N$ for some elements $x,y$, with both $M\setminus x$ and $M/y$ $3$-connected.
knowledge_statements.statement_plain: A 3-connected matroid stabilizes the whole minor-closed, dual-closed representable class exactly when it stabilizes every qualifying 3-connected one-element extension, one-element coextension, and two-element extension–coextension whose two intermediate minors remain 3-connected.

knowledge_statements.conclusion_latex: N\text{ stabilizes }\mathcal M\iff N\text{ stabilizes every qualifying }3\text{-connected }M\in\mathcal M\text{ of types (i)--(iii).}

knowledge_statements.statement_title: Duality, transitivity, and inheritance of matroid stabilizers
knowledge_statements.scope_note: States four structural properties of representation stabilizers.
knowledge_statements.statement_latex: Let $\mathbb F$ be a field, let $N$ be a $3$-connected $\mathbb F$-representable matroid, and let $\mathcal M$ be a minor-closed class of $\mathbb F$-representable matroids containing $N$ and closed under duality. Then: (i) if an $\mathbb F$-representable matroid $M$ has an $N$-minor, then $N$ stabilizes $M$ over $\mathbb F$ if and only if $N^*$ stabilizes $M^*$ over $\mathbb F$; (ii) $N$ stabilizes $\mathcal M$ over $\mathbb F$ if and only if $N^*$ stabilizes $\mathcal M$ over $\mathbb F$; (iii) if $N,N_1,N_2$ are $\mathbb F$-representable, $N$ is a minor of $N_1$, $N_1$ is a minor of $N_2$, and $N$ stabilizes $N_1$, then $N$ stabilizes $N_2$ if and only if $N_1$ stabilizes $N_2$; and (iv) if $N$ is an $\mathbb F$-stabilizer for $\mathcal M$ and $N'\in\mathcal M$ is $3$-connected and has an $N$-minor, then $N'$ is an $\mathbb F$-stabilizer for $\mathcal M$.
knowledge_statements.statement_plain: Stabilization is invariant under matroid duality, satisfies a transitivity law along a nested minor chain, and passes from a class stabilizer to every 3-connected class member containing it as a minor.
assumptions_latex: \mathcal M\text{ is minor-closed, dual-closed, consists of }\mathbb F\text{-representable matroids, and contains }N
knowledge_statements.conclusion_latex: \operatorname{Stab}_{\mathbb F}(N,M)\iff\operatorname{Stab}_{\mathbb F}(N^*,M^*),\quad \operatorname{Stab}_{\mathbb F}(N,\mathcal M)\iff\operatorname{Stab}_{\mathbb F}(N^*,\mathcal M),\quad\text{together with the stated minor-chain equivalence and inheritance property.}

knowledge_statements.statement_title: Free spikes, circuit-hyperplane relaxation, and clones
knowledge_statements.scope_note: Collects the definitions and structural consequences stated for free spikes and clone elements.
knowledge_statements.statement_latex: A rank-r spike from the standard construction is free when \mathcal C_3=\varnothing. In any spike, every C\in\mathcal C_3 is both a circuit and a hyperplane; relaxing such circuit-hyperplanes preserves the spike class, and relaxing all of them produces the free spike. Distinct e,f\in E(M) are clones precisely when the transposition exchanging e and f and fixing E(M)\setminus\{e,f\} is an automorphism of M. In a free spike, x_i and y_i are clones for every i. Parallel elements are clones, as are loops. Every spike of rank at least four has a unique possible tip; among the cited rank-three cases, the free spike and P_7 have unique tips, whereas F_7 and F_7^- admit multiple tips.
knowledge_statements.statement_plain: A spike is free when its selected transversal-circuit family is empty. Its selected transversal circuits are circuit-hyperplanes, and relaxing all of them yields the free spike. Two elements are clones when swapping only those elements is a matroid automorphism; each pair x_i,y_i in a free spike consists of clones. Spikes of rank at least four have a unique tip, while some rank-three spikes have multiple possible tips.
assumptions_latex: M\text{ is a spike arising from the standard circuit construction}
knowledge_statements.conclusion_latex: \mathcal C_3=\varnothing\Rightarrow M\text{ is free};\quad C\in\mathcal C_3\Rightarrow C\text{ is a circuit-hyperplane};\quad e,f\text{ are clones}\iff(e\ f)\in\operatorname{Aut}(M);\quad r(M)\ge4\Rightarrow M\text{ has a unique tip.}

knowledge_statements.scope_note: The ground sets may overlap; the direct sum is the disjoint-ground-set specialization.
knowledge_statements.statement_latex: Let \(M_1=(E_1,\mathcal I_1)\) and \(M_2=(E_2,\mathcal I_2)\) be matroids, let \(E=E_1\cup E_2\), and define \[\mathcal I=\{I\subseteq E:I=I_1\cup I_2\text{ for some }I_1\in\mathcal I_1,\ I_2\in\mathcal I_2\}.\] Then \(M=(E,\mathcal I)\) is a matroid.
knowledge_statements.statement_plain: The unions of one independent set from each of two matroids form the independent-set family of a matroid on the union of their ground sets.
assumptions_latex: M_1=(E_1,\mathcal I_1)\text{ and }M_2=(E_2,\mathcal I_2)\text{ are matroids}.

knowledge_statements.statement_title: Circuit-hyperplane relaxation construction
knowledge_statements.scope_note: Existence and circuit characterization of the matroid obtained by relaxing a circuit-hyperplane.
knowledge_statements.statement_latex:
Let $M$ be a matroid and let $X\subseteq E(M)$ be both a circuit and a hyperplane. Define $\mathcal B'=\mathcal B(M)\cup\{X\}$. Then $\mathcal B'$ is the set of bases of a matroid $M'$ on $E(M)$, and
\[\mathcal C(M')=(\mathcal C(M)\setminus\{X\})\cup\{X\cup\{e\}:e\in E(M)\setminus X\}.\]
knowledge_statements.statement_plain: If X is both a circuit and a hyperplane of M, adjoining X to the bases of M produces the bases of a matroid M' on the same ground set. Its circuits are the circuits of M other than X, together with X plus each element outside X.
knowledge_statements.conclusion_latex: \mathcal B'\text{ is the basis family of a matroid }M'\text{ on }E(M),\quad \mathcal C(M')=(\mathcal C(M)\setminus\{X\})\cup\{X\cup\{e\}:e\in E(M)\setminus X\}

knowledge_statements.statement_title: Matroid relaxation and the non-Fano matroid
knowledge_statements.scope_note: Definition of relaxation by a circuit-hyperplane and its standard Fano-matroid specialization.
knowledge_statements.statement_latex: Let $X$ be a circuit-hyperplane of a matroid $M$, and let $M'$ be the matroid with $\mathcal B(M')=\mathcal B(M)\cup\{X\}$. knowledge_statements.statement_title: Rank Formula for a Matroid Homomorphic Image
knowledge_statements.scope_note: Expresses the rank of a homomorphic image through the original matroid rank and an uncovered-element defect term.
knowledge_statements.statement_latex: Let \(M=(S,r)\) be a matroid and let \(\varphi(M)=(T,r_\varphi)\) be its homomorphic image under \(\varphi:S\to T\). For every \(Z\subseteq T\), \[r_\varphi(Z)=\min_{X\subseteq Z}\left\{r(\varphi^{-1}(X))+|Z\setminus X|\right\}.\]
knowledge_statements.statement_plain: For every subset Z of the image ground set, its rank in the homomorphic image is the minimum over X contained in Z of the original rank of the inverse image of X plus the number of elements of Z outside X.
knowledge_statements.conclusion_latex: (\forall Z\subseteq T)\quad r_\varphi(Z)=\min_{X\subseteq Z}\{r(\varphi^{-1}(X))+|Z\setminus X|\}

knowledge_statements.statement_title: Criterion for k Disjoint Bases of a Matroid
knowledge_statements.scope_note: Equivalent closed-set rank-deficit and open-set corank conditions.
knowledge_statements.statement_latex: A matroid \(M=(S,r)\) has \(k\) pairwise disjoint bases if and only if \(k\bigl(r(S)-r(Y)\bigr)\le |S\setminus Y|\) for every closed set \(Y\subseteq S\). Equivalently, \(k\,t(X)\le |X|\) for every open set \(X\subseteq S\), where \(t\) is the corank function.
knowledge_statements.statement_plain: A matroid contains k disjoint bases exactly when every closed set's aggregate rank deficit fits in its complement, equivalently when k times the corank of every open set does not exceed its size.
knowledge_statements.conclusion_latex: \(M\text{ has }k\text{ pairwise disjoint bases}\iff \forall\text{ closed }Y\subseteq S,\ k(r(S)-r(Y))\le |S\setminus Y|\iff \forall\text{ open }X\subseteq S,\ k\,t(X)\le |X|\)

knowledge_statements.statement_title: Criterion for Bases with Prescribed Element Multiplicities
knowledge_statements.scope_note: Exact degree prescription across bases of multiple matroids on a common ground set.
knowledge_statements.statement_latex: Let \(M_i\) be \(k\) matroids on a common ground set \(S\), with rank functions \(r_i\), and let \(m:S\to\mathbf Z_{+}\). Write \(\widetilde m(X)=\sum_{s\in X}m(s)\). There exist bases \(B_i\) of \(M_i\) such that every \(s\in S\) belongs to exactly \(m(s)\) of the bases if and only if \(\widetilde m(S)=\sum_{i=1}^k r_i(S)\) and \(\sum_{i=1}^k r_i(X)\ge\widetilde m(X)\) for every \(X\subseteq S\).
knowledge_statements.statement_plain: Bases with exactly prescribed element-occurrence counts exist precisely when total prescribed multiplicity equals total base size and every subset's prescribed multiplicity is at most its aggregate rank.
assumptions_latex: \(M_i\text{ is a matroid on the common ground set }S\quad(i=1,\ldots,k)\)
knowledge_statements.conclusion_latex: \(\exists B_i\text{ bases of }M_i\text{ with }|\{i:s\in B_i\}|=m(s)\ \forall s\in S\iff \widetilde m(S)=\sum_i r_i(S)\text{ and }\forall X\subseteq S,\ \sum_i r_i(X)\ge\widetilde m(X)\)

knowledge_statements.statement_title: Rank criterion for covering a matroid by k bases
knowledge_statements.scope_note: Equivalent global and reduced families of rank inequalities for base covering.
knowledge_statements.statement_latex: Let M=(S,r) be a matroid and let k be a positive integer. The following are equivalent: (A) S can be covered by k bases of M; (B1) k\,r(X)\ge |X| for every X\subseteq S; (B2) k\,r(X)\ge |X| for every subset X\subseteq S that is both closed and nonseparable.
knowledge_statements.statement_plain: A matroid's ground set is coverable by k bases exactly when k times the rank of every subset dominates its size. It is sufficient and necessary to check this inequality only on closed, nonseparable subsets.
knowledge_statements.conclusion_latex: S\text{ is covered by }k\text{ bases}\iff\forall X\subseteq S,\ kr(X)\ge|X|\iff\forall X\subseteq S\text{ closed and nonseparable},\ kr(X)\ge|X|.

knowledge_statements.statement_title: Disjoint Bases Criterion for Several Matroids
knowledge_statements.scope_note: Base-packing characterization for multiple matroids on one ground set.
knowledge_statements.statement_latex: Let \(M_i\) be \(k\) matroids on a common ground set \(S\), with rank functions \(r_i\) and corank functions \(t_i\). Pairwise disjoint bases \(B_i\) of the \(M_i\) exist if and only if \(\sum_{i=1}^k t_i(X)\le |X|\) for every \(X\subseteq S\). Equivalently, they exist if and only if \(\sum_{i=1}^k\bigl(r_i(S)-r_i(Y)\bigr)\le |S\setminus Y|\) for every \(Y\subseteq S\).
knowledge_statements.statement_plain: Several matroids on the same ground set have pairwise disjoint bases exactly when every subset can accommodate the total corank demand; equivalently, every complement can accommodate the aggregate rank deficit.
assumptions_latex: \(r_i\text{ and }t_i\text{ are respectively the rank and corank functions of }M_i\)

knowledge_statements.statement_title: Exact 3-separations and binary-matroid 3-sums
knowledge_statements.scope_note: Extension, decomposition, uniqueness, converse separation, and rank characterization.
knowledge_statements.statement_latex: Let $(X_1,X_2)$ be an exact 3-separation of a binary matroid $M$ with $|X_1|,|X_2|\geq4$, and let $Z$ be a three-element set disjoint from $E(M)$. There exists a binary matroid $N$ on $E(M)\cup Z$ such that $N|E(M)=M$, $Z$ is a circuit of $N$, and $r_N(X_i\cup Z)=r_M(X_i)$ for $i=1,2$. With $N_i=N|(X_i\cup Z)$, one has $M=N_1\oplus_3N_2$, and $N$ is unique up to a permutation of the labels of $Z$. Conversely, if $M=M_1\oplus_3M_2$, then $(E(M_1)-E(M_2),E(M_2)-E(M_1))$ is an exact 3-separation, both displayed parts have more than three elements, and $r(M)=r(M_1)+r(M_2)-2$.
knowledge_statements.statement_plain: Every exact 3-separation of a binary matroid with sides of size at least four can be completed by a new triangle to give a 3-sum decomposition, uniquely up to relabeling that triangle. Conversely, every binary-matroid 3-sum induces the corresponding exact 3-separation and has rank equal to the sum of the component ranks minus two.
knowledge_statements.conclusion_latex: \exists N:\ N|E(M)=M,\ Z\in\mathcal C(N),\ r_N(X_i\cup Z)=r_M(X_i),\ M=N_1\oplus_3N_2;\quad N\text{ is unique up to relabeling }Z,\text{ with the stated converse separation, part-size bounds, and rank formula.}

knowledge_statements.statement_title: Subset criteria for cardinality-bounded matroid covering and partition
knowledge_statements.scope_note: Necessary and sufficient rank inequalities for bounded covering, disjoint independent-set selection, and bounded partition across several matroids.
knowledge_statements.statement_latex: Let $M_i=(S,r_i)$ be matroids and let $0\le f_i\le g_i$ be integers for $i=1,\ldots,k$. Independent sets $I_i\in\mathcal I(M_i)$ can cover $S$ with $|I_i|\le g_i$ if and only if $|X|\le\sum_{i=1}^k\min\{r_i(X),g_i\}$ for every $X\subseteq S$. They can be pairwise disjoint with $|I_i|\ge f_i$ if and only if $|X|\ge\sum_{i=1}^k\bigl(f_i-r_i(S\setminus X)\bigr)^+$ for every $X\subseteq S$. They can partition $S$ with $f_i\le|I_i|\le g_i$ for every $i$ if and only if both families of inequalities hold.
knowledge_statements.statement_plain: Independent sets from several matroids cover the ground set under upper cardinality bounds exactly when the truncated rank inequalities hold. Pairwise disjoint independent sets meet lower cardinality bounds exactly when the complementary-rank inequalities hold. A bounded partition exists exactly when both systems hold.
knowledge_statements.conclusion_latex: \begin{aligned}&\exists I_i\in\mathcal I(M_i):\ S=\bigcup_i I_i,\ |I_i|\le g_i\iff \forall X\subseteq S:\ |X|\le\sum_i\min\{r_i(X),g_i\},\\&\exists\text{ pairwise disjoint }I_i\in\mathcal I(M_i):\ |I_i|\ge f_i\iff \forall X\subseteq S:\ |X|\ge\sum_i(f_i-r_i(S\setminus X))^+,\\&\exists I_i\in\mathcal I(M_i):\ S=\mathbin{\dot\bigcup}_i I_i,\ f_i\le|I_i|\le g_i\iff\text{ both inequality systems hold.}\end{aligned}

knowledge_statements.statement_title: Minimizer characterization after matroid-partition termination
knowledge_statements.scope_note: Characterizes all minimizer sets and the unique extremal minimizers using the terminal exchange digraph.
knowledge_statements.statement_latex: Let M_{\sum} be the sum of matroids M_1,\ldots,M_k. Suppose the matroid-partition algorithm terminates with digraph D and independent sets F_1,\ldots,F_k. Let X_0 be the elements of S reachable from R in D, and let X_1 be the elements from which T is not reachable. A set X\subseteq S is a minimizer for M_{\sum} if and only if R\subseteq X and \delta_D(X)=0. Moreover, X_0 and X_1 are respectively the unique smallest and unique largest minimizers. Every minimizer X contains pairwise disjoint bases of M_1|X,\ldots,M_k|X, while S\setminus X partitions into independent sets of M_1/X,\ldots,M_k/X. For every s\in X_0, X_0\setminus\{s\} contains such disjoint bases. For every s\in S\setminus X_1, after adjoining a parallel copy s' of s to each M_i to form M_i', (S\setminus X_1)\cup\{s'\} partitions into independent sets of M_1'/X_1,\ldots,M_k'/X_1.
knowledge_statements.statement_plain: At termination of the matroid-partition algorithm, the minimizers are exactly the sets containing R with no outgoing arc in the terminal digraph. The reachable and non-reachable constructions give the unique smallest and largest minimizers, together with basis and contracted-independent-set certificates and the stated deletion and parallel-copy strengthenings.
knowledge_statements.conclusion_latex: X\text{ minimizes }M_{\sum}\iff R\subseteq X\text{ and }\delta_D(X)=0,\text{ with the stated extremal and decomposition properties.}

knowledge_statements.statement_latex:
Let \(M_1=(E_1,\mathcal I_1)\) and \(M_2=(E_2,\mathcal I_2)\) be finite matroids with \(E_1\cap E_2=\varnothing\). Their direct sum \(M_1\oplus M_2\) is the matroid on \(E_1\cup E_2\) with
\[\mathcal I(M_1\oplus M_2)=\{I_1\cup I_2:I_i\in\mathcal I_i\}.\]
Equivalently, for every \(X\subseteq E_1\cup E_2\),
\[r_{M_1\oplus M_2}(X)=r_{M_1}(X\cap E_1)+r_{M_2}(X\cap E_2).\]
knowledge_statements.statement_plain: The direct sum combines disjoint matroids independently, so independent sets and ranks decompose componentwise.
knowledge_statements.conclusion_latex: \(\mathcal I(M_1\oplus M_2)=\{I_1\cup I_2:I_i\in\mathcal I_i\}\).

knowledge_statements.statement_title: Direct sum of submodular functions
knowledge_statements.scope_note: Defines the operation on disjoint ground sets and records its closure consequences for associated polyhedral classes.
knowledge_statements.statement_latex: Let b_i:2^{S_i}\to\overline{\mathbb R} be submodular for i=1,2, where S_1\cap S_2=\varnothing. Their direct sum b=b_1\oplus b_2 on S=S_1\cup S_2 is defined by b(X)=b_1(X\cap S_1)+b_2(X\cap S_2). Then b is submodular. The associated submodular polyhedron is the direct sum of S(b_1) and S(b_2); the analogous operation is defined for generalized polymatroids, and a direct sum of base polyhedra is again a base polyhedron. The definition extends to finitely many summands.
knowledge_statements.statement_plain: For submodular functions on disjoint ground sets, the direct sum evaluates a set by adding the two functions on its respective components. This produces another submodular function, induces the corresponding direct-sum construction for submodular polyhedra and generalized polymatroids, and preserves the class of base polyhedra. The construction extends to finitely many summands.
assumptions_latex: b_1\text{ and }b_2\text{ are submodular on }S_1\text{ and }S_2
knowledge_statements.conclusion_latex: b_1\oplus b_2\text{ is submodular, and direct sums preserve base polyhedra (and are defined analogously for g-polymatroids).}

knowledge_statements.statement_title: Circuit Representations of Multiway Series and Parallel Connections
knowledge_statements.scope_note: Existence and circuit descriptions for n matroids sharing exactly one common element.
knowledge_statements.statement_latex:
Let n>1 and let M_1,\ldots,M_n be matroids such that E(M_i)\cap E(M_j)=\{p\} for all i\ne j, and suppose \{p\} is not a separator of any M_k. There exist matroids P(M_1,\ldots,M_n) and S(M_1,\ldots,M_n), each on \bigcup_{i=1}^nE(M_i), with circuit collections
\[
\mathcal C_P=\bigcup_{i=1}^n\mathcal C(M_i)\;\cup\;\{(C_i\cup C_j)-\{p\}:1\le i<j\le n,\ p\in C_i\in\mathcal C(M_i),\ p\in C_j\in\mathcal C(M_j)\},
\]
and
\[
\mathcal C_S=\bigcup_{i=1}^n\mathcal C(M_i\setminus p)\;\cup\;\left\{\bigcup_{i=1}^n C_i:p\in C_i\in\mathcal C(M_i)\text{ for every }i\right\}.
\]
knowledge_statements.statement_plain: For more than one matroid whose pairwise intersection is the common element p, provided p is not a singleton separator in any factor, multiway parallel and series connections exist on the union of the ground sets. Their circuits are respectively the factor circuits together with pairwise circuits joined through p, and the circuits avoiding p together with unions of one p-containing circuit from every factor.
knowledge_statements.conclusion_latex: P(M_1,\ldots,M_n)\text{ and }S(M_1,\ldots,M_n)\text{ exist on }\bigcup_{i=1}^nE(M_i)\text{ with circuit sets }\mathcal C_P\text{ and }\mathcal C_S\text{ as displayed.}

knowledge_statements.statement_title: Direct sum of matroids

knowledge_statements.statement_latex: Let \(n\geq 1\), and let \(M_1,\ldots,M_n\) be matroids on pairwise disjoint ground sets \(E_1,\ldots,E_n\). knowledge_statements.statement_title: Independent Sets of a Matroid Free Product
knowledge_statements.scope_note: Characterizes free-product independence through independence in the first factor and a rank-nullity balance across the factors.
knowledge_statements.statement_latex:
Let $M_1$ and $M_2$ be matroids on disjoint ground sets $E_1$ and $E_2$, with rank functions $r_1$ and $r_2$. For every $I\subseteq E_1\cup E_2$,
\[
I\text{ is independent in }M_1\square M_2
\iff
\left[
I\cap E_1\text{ is independent in }M_1
\ \text{and}\ 
r(M_1)-r_1(I\cap E_1)\ge |I\cap E_2|-r_2(I\cap E_2)
\right].
\]
knowledge_statements.statement_plain: A subset is independent in the free product exactly when its first-ground-set part is independent in the first matroid and the unused rank of that factor is at least the nullity of its second-ground-set part in the second matroid.
assumptions_latex: M_1\text{ and }M_2\text{ are matroids on disjoint ground sets }E_1\text{ and }E_2.
r_1\text{ and }r_2\text{ are the respective rank functions}.
knowledge_statements.conclusion_latex: I\in\mathcal I(M_1\square M_2)\iff \left(I\cap E_1\in\mathcal I(M_1)\ \land\ r(M_1)-r_1(I\cap E_1)\ge |I\cap E_2|-r_2(I\cap E_2)\right).

knowledge_statements.statement_title: Basis Construction for the Matroid Free Product
knowledge_statements.scope_note: Characterizes the bases that define the free product of two matroids on disjoint ground sets.

knowledge_statements.conclusion_latex: \mathcal B\text{ is the set of bases of a matroid }M_1\square M_2\text{ on }E_1\cup E_2.

knowledge_statements.statement_title: Matroid series and parallel connections, including exceptional basepoints
knowledge_statements.scope_note: Extraction-grounded definition preserving the ordinary and exceptional basepoint regimes.
knowledge_statements.statement_latex: Let \(E(M_1)\cap E(M_2)=\{p\}\) and \(E=E(M_1)\cup E(M_2)\). When \(p\) is neither a loop nor a coloop of either matroid, \(S(M_1,M_2)\) and \(P(M_1,M_2)\) are the matroids on \(E\) with the prescribed series- and parallel-connection circuit collections. If \(p\) is a loop of \(M_1\), define \(P(M_1,M_2)=M_1\oplus(M_2/p)\) and \(S(M_1,M_2)=(M_1/p)\oplus M_2\). If \(p\) is a coloop of \(M_1\), define \(P(M_1,M_2)=(M_1\setminus p)\oplus M_2\) and \(S(M_1,M_2)=M_1\oplus(M_2\setminus p)\). These definitions are symmetric in \(M_1,M_2\). If \(\{p\}\) is a separator of both matroids, the loop- and coloop-based formulas agree because \(N\setminus p=N/p\) for such a separator.
knowledge_statements.statement_plain: Two matroids meeting only at a basepoint p have series and parallel connections defined by their prescribed circuit collections in the ordinary case. If p is a loop or coloop, the connections are instead defined by the stated direct sums with contraction or deletion. The definitions are symmetric in the two matroids, and overlapping exceptional definitions agree when p is a singleton separator of both.
knowledge_statements.conclusion_latex: S(M_1,M_2)=S(M_2,M_1),\qquad P(M_1,M_2)=P(M_2,M_1),\text{ with the stated ordinary and exceptional definitions.}

knowledge_statements.statement_title: Direct sums and separability of matroids
knowledge_statements.scope_note: Definition and basic circuit, rank, and separability properties of finite direct sums.
knowledge_statements.statement_latex: Let $M_i=(S_i,\mathcal F_i)$ for $i=1,\ldots,k$ be matroids on pairwise disjoint ground sets. Set $S=\bigcup_{i=1}^k S_i$ and $\mathcal F=\{F_1\cup\cdots\cup F_k:F_i\in\mathcal F_i\}$. Then $(S,\mathcal F)$ is the direct sum $M_1\oplus\cdots\oplus M_k$. Every circuit of the direct sum is a circuit of one of the summands, and for every $X\subseteq S$, $r(X)=\sum_{i=1}^k r_i(X\cap S_i)$. A matroid is separable if it is a direct sum of smaller submatroids and non-separable otherwise; a subset $X\subseteq S$ is non-separable when the restriction $M\mid X$ is non-separable.
knowledge_statements.statement_plain: The direct sum of matroids on disjoint ground sets has independent sets formed by unions of independent sets from the summands. Its circuits lie in individual summands and its rank is the sum of the component ranks. Separability means admitting a decomposition into smaller direct summands, and a subset is non-separable when its restriction is non-separable.
assumptions_latex: $M_i=(S_i,\mathcal F_i)$ is a matroid for each $i=1,\ldots,k$.
knowledge_statements.conclusion_latex: (S,\mathcal F)=\bigoplus_{i=1}^kM_i,\quad C\in\mathcal C(S,\mathcal F)\Rightarrow\exists i\;C\in\mathcal C(M_i),\quad r(X)=\sum_{i=1}^k r_i(X\cap S_i),\quad X\text{ non-separable}\iff M\mid X\text{ non-separable.}

\bigl(r(M_1)=r(M_2)=0\bigr)\ \lor\ \bigl(r(M_1^*)=r(M_2^*)=0\bigr).

knowledge_statements.title: Two-Sums
knowledge_statements.scope_note: Circuit definition of the binary gluing operation along one ordinary element.
knowledge_statements.statement_latex:
Let \(M_i\) be finite matroids on \(E_i\) with \(E_1\cap E_2=\{p\}\), where \(p\) is neither a loop nor a coloop of either matroid. The two-sum \(M_1\oplus_2 M_2\) has ground set \((E_1\cup E_2)\setminus\{p\}\). Its circuits are the circuits of each \(M_i\) avoiding \(p\), together with all sets
\[(C_1\cup C_2)\setminus\{p\},\]
where \(C_i\) is a circuit of \(M_i\) containing \(p\).
knowledge_statements.statement_plain: A two-sum glues two matroids along one nonloop, noncoloop element and then removes it, joining circuits that used the shared element.
assumptions_latex: \(p\) is neither a loop nor a coloop of either \(M_i\).
knowledge_statements.conclusion_latex: \(\mathcal C(M_1\oplus_2M_2)=\mathcal C_1^{\neg p}\cup\mathcal C_2^{\neg p}\cup\{(C_1\cup C_2)\setminus\{p\}:p\in C_i\in\mathcal C(M_i)\}\).

knowledge_statements.statement_title: Matroid two-sum
knowledge_statements.scope_note: Defines the matroid two-sum through series or parallel connection, including its hypotheses, symmetry, terminology, and minimum-size convention.
knowledge_statements.statement_latex: Let M and N be matroids such that |E(M)|,|E(N)|\ge 2, E(M)\cap E(N)=\{p\}, and \{p\} is not a separator of either M or N. The two-sum is M\oplus_2N:=S(M,N)/p=P(M,N)\setminus p. Moreover, N\oplus_2M=M\oplus_2N; p is the basepoint, and M and N are the parts. No requirement that each part have at least three elements is imposed.
knowledge_statements.statement_plain: Two matroids with at least two elements that share exactly one element p, where p is not a one-element separator of either matroid, have a two-sum obtained by contracting p from their series connection, equivalently deleting p from their parallel connection. The operation is commutative, p is the basepoint, and the inputs are its parts. Parts need not have three elements.
assumptions_latex: \{p\}\text{ is not a separator of }M\text{ or }N
knowledge_statements.conclusion_latex: M\oplus_2N=S(M,N)/p=P(M,N)\setminus p=N\oplus_2M

knowledge_statements.statement_title: Duality and connectivity of matroid two-sums
knowledge_statements.scope_note: Records compatibility of two-sums with duality and the exact connectivity criterion for the deleted parallel connection and the resulting two-sum.
knowledge_statements.statement_latex: For a valid two-sum M\oplus_2N, (M\oplus_2N)^*=M^*\oplus_2N^*. If |E(M)|,|E(N)|\ge 2, then P(M,N)\setminus p is connected if and only if both M and N are connected. In particular, M\oplus_2N is connected if and only if both M and N are connected.

knowledge_statements.scope_note: Characterizes the ground set and all circuits of a two-sum from its two parts.

knowledge_statements.statement_title: Recovery of two-sum parts as minors
knowledge_statements.scope_note: States minor containment of both parts, an explicit recovery condition for M, and the sufficient size condition for properness.
knowledge_statements.statement_latex: Let M\oplus_2N be a valid two-sum with basepoint p. Both M and N are isomorphic to minors of M\oplus_2N. If an element p′ of N lies in the same component as the basepoint, an appropriate minor becomes M after p′ is relabelled as p. If N has at least three elements, M is isomorphic to a proper minor.

knowledge_statements.statement_latex: For a finite matroid \(M\), a partition \(E(M)=X\mathbin{\dot\cup}Y\) is a direct-sum separation exactly when \(\lambda_M(X)=0\), equivalently \(M=M|X\oplus M|Y\). If \(M_1\) and \(M_2\) satisfy the assumptions, their two-sum has ground set \((E(M_1)\cup E(M_2))\setminus\{p\}\) and bases \((B_1\cup B_2)\setminus\{p\}\), where each \(B_i\) is a basis of \(M_i\) and exactly one of \(B_1,B_2\) contains \(p\). The resulting two-sum is connected.
knowledge_statements.statement_plain: Direct sums are exactly zero-connectivity separations. Gluing two connected matroids across a common nonloop, noncoloop and then deleting it produces a connected two-sum.

knowledge_statements.statement_title: Inseparable sets and redundancy of separable rank inequalities
knowledge_statements.scope_note: Defines rank-inseparability for an independence system and records the associated redundancy criterion.
knowledge_statements.statement_latex: For an independence system $M$, a set $T\subseteq E(M)$ is inseparable if $r_M(T)=r_M(U)+r_M(T\setminus U)$ implies $U\in\{\varnothing,T\}$. If $T$ is not inseparable, then for some nonempty proper $U\subset T$ equality holds, and the inequality $x(T)\le r_M(T)$ is the sum of $x(U)\le r_M(U)$ and $x(T\setminus U)\le r_M(T\setminus U)$; hence it is redundant.
knowledge_statements.statement_plain: A set is inseparable when its rank cannot be additively decomposed across a nontrivial partition. Whenever such a decomposition exists, the set's rank inequality follows by adding the two inequalities for the partition blocks and is redundant.
knowledge_statements.conclusion_latex: T\text{ inseparable}\iff\bigl[r_M(T)=r_M(U)+r_M(T\setminus U)\Rightarrow U\in\{\varnothing,T\}\bigr];\quad T\text{ not inseparable}\Rightarrow x(T)\le r_M(T)\text{ is redundant}

knowledge_statements.statement_title: Subpartition characterization of terminal-set edge-connectivity augmentation
knowledge_statements.scope_note: Necessary and sufficient cut-deficiency inequalities for augmentation using at most gamma new arcs whose endpoints lie in the terminal set.
knowledge_statements.statement_latex: Let $D=(V,A)$ be a digraph and let $\varnothing\ne T\subseteq V$. The digraph can be made $k$-edge-connected within $T$ by adding at most $\gamma$ arcs with both endpoints in $T$ if and only if, for every set-system $\{X_1,\ldots,X_t\}$ such that $\varnothing\subset X_i\cap T\subset T$ and $\{X_1\cap T,\ldots,X_t\cap T\}$ is a subpartition of $T$, one has $\gamma\ge\sum_i[k-\varrho_D(X_i)]$ and $\gamma\ge\sum_i[k-\delta_D(X_i)]$.
knowledge_statements.statement_plain: At most gamma new arcs between terminals suffice to make a digraph k-edge-connected within a nonempty terminal set T exactly when every terminal subpartition satisfies both the total in-cut-deficiency and total out-cut-deficiency bounds by gamma.
assumptions_latex: \forall\{X_1,\ldots,X_t\}:\ \varnothing\subset X_i\cap T\subset T\text{ and }\{X_i\cap T\}_{i=1}^t\text{ is a subpartition}
knowledge_statements.conclusion_latex: D\text{ is augmentable to }k\text{-edge-connectivity within }T\text{ using at most }\gamma\text{ arcs in }T\iff\gamma\ge\sum_i(k-\varrho_D(X_i))\text{ and }\gamma\ge\sum_i(k-\delta_D(X_i))\text{ for every such set-system}.

knowledge_statements.statement_latex: The parallel connection \(P(M_1,M_2)\) with basepoint \(p\) is the matroid on \(E_1\cup E_2\) whose circuits are the inclusion-minimal nonempty members of \[\mathcal C(M_1)\cup\mathcal C(M_2)\cup\{(C_1\cup C_2)\setminus\{p\}: C_i\in\mathcal C(M_i),\ p\in C_1\cap C_2\}.\] In particular, \(P(M_1,M_2)|E_i=M_i\) for \(i\in\{1,2\}\), and the common element \(p\) remains in the ground set.
knowledge_statements.statement_plain: The parallel connection retains both matroids and adds circuits formed by joining one circuit from each side through their common nonloop basepoint.

knowledge_statements.statement_title: Series and parallel connections of graphs
knowledge_statements.scope_note: Extraction-grounded graph construction, including the exceptional loop boundary.
knowledge_statements.statement_latex: For \(i\in\{1,2\}\), let \(p_i=u_iv_i\) be an arbitrarily oriented edge of a graph \(G_i\). Delete \(p_1,p_2\) and identify \(u_1,u_2\) as \(u\). The series connection is obtained by adding a new edge \(p\) joining \(v_1\) to \(v_2\). The parallel connection is obtained by additionally identifying \(v_1,v_2\) as \(v\) and adding a new edge \(p\) joining \(u\) to \(v\). Unless exactly one of \(p_1,p_2\) is a loop, the parallel connection is equivalently obtained by identifying \(p_1\) and \(p_2\) with agreeing orientations.
knowledge_statements.statement_plain: Orient a distinguished edge in each of two graphs, delete those edges, and identify their tails. Adding an edge between the two remaining heads gives the series connection; identifying the heads and adding an edge between the identified tail and head gives the parallel connection. Except when exactly one distinguished edge is a loop, the parallel construction simply identifies the two edges with agreeing directions.
knowledge_statements.conclusion_latex: \text{The stated deletion, identification, and edge-addition operations define the series and parallel graph connections.}

knowledge_statements.statement_title: Matroid Amalgams and Free Amalgams
knowledge_statements.scope_note: Defines amalgams of two matroids agreeing on their overlapping ground set and the maximal-independence notion of a free amalgam.
knowledge_statements.statement_latex: Let M_1 and M_2 have ground sets E_1 and E_2, let E=E_1\cup E_2 and T=E_1\cap E_2, and suppose M_1|T=M_2|T=N. A matroid M on E is an amalgam of M_1 and M_2 if M|E_1=M_1 and M|E_2=M_2. An amalgam M_0 is the free amalgam if, for every amalgam M of M_1 and M_2, every independent set of M is independent in M_0.
knowledge_statements.statement_plain: If two matroids have the same restriction to their common ground set, an amalgam is a matroid on the union whose restrictions recover both matroids. A free amalgam is an amalgam containing every independent set occurring in any other amalgam.
knowledge_statements.conclusion_latex: M\text{ is an amalgam}\iff M|E_1=M_1\text{ and }M|E_2=M_2;\quad M_0\text{ is free}\iff \forall M\,\bigl(M\text{ amalgam}\Rightarrow \mathcal I(M)\subseteq\mathcal I(M_0)\bigr).

knowledge_statements.scope_note: Constituent recovery, conditional symmetry, modularity, deletion, contraction, and interface-contraction laws.
knowledge_statements.statement_latex: Let \(P=P_N(M_1,M_2)\). Then: (i) \(P\mid E_1=M_1\) and \(P\mid E_2=M_2\); (ii) if \(\operatorname{si}(T)\) is a modular flat in both \(\operatorname{si}(M_1)\) and \(\operatorname{si}(M_2)\), then \(P_N(M_2,M_1)=P_N(M_1,M_2)\); (iii) \(E(\operatorname{si}(M_2))\) is a modular flat of \(\operatorname{si}(P)\); (iv) if \(e\in E_1\setminus T\), then \(P\setminus e=P_N(M_1\setminus e,M_2)\); (v) if \(e\in E_1\setminus\operatorname{cl}_{M_1}(T)\), then \(P/e=P_N(M_1/e,M_2)\); (vi) if \(e\in E_2\setminus T\), then \(P\setminus e=P_N(M_1,M_2\setminus e)\); (vii) if \(e\in E_2\setminus\operatorname{cl}_{M_2}(T)\), then \(P/e=P_N(M_1,M_2/e)\); (viii) if \(e\in T\), then \(P/e=P_{N/e}(M_1/e,M_2/e)\); and (ix) \(P/T=(M_1/T)\oplus(M_2/T)\).
knowledge_statements.statement_plain: A generalized parallel connection recovers both constituents by restriction, is symmetric under the stated two-sided modularity condition, has the stated modular-flat property, commutes with deletion and the specified contractions, and becomes a direct sum after contracting the whole interface.
knowledge_statements.conclusion_latex: \(P\text{ satisfies properties (i)--(ix), with the stated clause-specific hypotheses.}\)

knowledge_statements.statement_title: Generalized parallel connection across a modular common restriction
knowledge_statements.scope_note: Defines the construction and records the accompanying rank formula for its flats.
knowledge_statements.statement_latex: Let \(N=M_1\mid T=M_2\mid T\), define \(\operatorname{si}(T)=\operatorname{si}(M_1\mid T)\), and suppose \(\operatorname{si}(T)\) is a modular flat of \(\operatorname{si}(M_1)\). The proper amalgam of \(M_1\) and \(M_2\) is called their generalized parallel connection across \(T\), denoted \(P_N(M_1,M_2)\) or \(P_T(M_1,M_2)\). For every flat \(F\) of this matroid, \[r(F)=r(F\cap E_1)+r(F\cap E_2)-r(F\cap T).\]
knowledge_statements.statement_plain: When the simplified common restriction is a modular flat of the simplification of M1, the proper amalgam is called the generalized parallel connection across T. The rank of each of its flats is the sum of the two constituent ranks minus the rank on the common restriction.
knowledge_statements.conclusion_latex: \(P_N(M_1,M_2)=P_T(M_1,M_2)\text{ denotes the generalized parallel connection, and every flat }F\text{ satisfies }r(F)=r(F\cap E_1)+r(F\cap E_2)-r(F\cap T).\)

knowledge_statements.scope_note: An interface criterion in the common-restriction setup for amalgamating matroids across T.

knowledge_statements.statement_title: Modular defect and fully embedded subsets
knowledge_statements.scope_note: Definitions of modular defect and the fully embedded interface condition; the accompanying example is excluded.
knowledge_statements.statement_latex: Let \(M\) be a matroid with rank function \(r\). For \(X,Y\subseteq E(M)\), define \(\delta(X,Y)=r(X)+r(Y)-r(X\cup Y)-r(X\cap Y)\). A subset \(Z\subseteq E(M)\) is fully embedded in \(M\) if \(\delta(F_1\cap Z,F_2\cap Z)\leq\delta(F_1,F_2)\) for all flats \(F_1,F_2\) of \(M\).
knowledge_statements.statement_plain: The modular defect measures the slack in the rank submodularity inequality. A subset is fully embedded when intersecting any two flats with it does not increase their modular defect.
assumptions_latex: \(M\text{ is a matroid with rank function }r\)
knowledge_statements.conclusion_latex: \(\delta(X,Y):=r(X)+r(Y)-r(X\cup Y)-r(X\cap Y),\qquad Z\text{ is fully embedded}\iff \forall F_1,F_2,\ \delta(F_1\cap Z,F_2\cap Z)\leq\delta(F_1,F_2).\)

knowledge_statements.statement_title: Reconstruction from a Disconnected Deletion or Contraction
knowledge_statements.scope_note: Series and parallel connection representations induced by a nontrivial direct-sum minor at one element.
knowledge_statements.statement_latex:
Let p\in E(M), where M is connected. If M\setminus p=M_1\oplus M_2 with M_1 and M_2 nonempty, then
\[
M=S\bigl(M/E(M_1),M/E(M_2)\bigr).
\]
Dually, if M/p=M_1\oplus M_2 with M_1 and M_2 nonempty, then
\[
M=P\bigl(M\setminus E(M_1),M\setminus E(M_2)\bigr).
\]
knowledge_statements.statement_plain: If deleting an element of a connected matroid separates the remainder into two nonempty direct-sum factors, the matroid is the series connection of the contractions complementary to those factors. Dually, a disconnected contraction gives the corresponding parallel-connection representation by deletions.
assumptions_latex: M\setminus p=M_1\oplus M_2\text{ with }M_1,M_2\neq\varnothing\quad\text{or}\quad M/p=M_1\oplus M_2\text{ with }M_1,M_2\neq\varnothing
knowledge_statements.conclusion_latex: M=S(M/E(M_1),M/E(M_2))\quad\text{or, respectively,}\quad M=P(M\setminus E(M_1),M\setminus E(M_2)).

children.title: Single-Element Extensions
children.top_down_role: Matroid enlargement by one new element.

assumptions_latex: \(M\) is a finite matroid on \(E\), and \(e\notin E\).
knowledge_statements.conclusion_latex: A single-element extension is exactly a matroid \(M'\) on \(E\cup\{e\}\) satisfying \(M'\setminus e=M\).
knowledge_statements.scope_note: Finite single-element extension, including loop and coloop cases.

source_refs.locator: Chapter 5. Elements of matroid theory p. 172

knowledge_statements.statement_latex: A single-element extension of \(M\) by \(e\) is a matroid \(M'\) on \(E\cup\{e\}\) such that \(M'\setminus e=M\). Equivalently, \(r_{M'}(X)=r_M(X)\) for every \(X\subseteq E\), while for each \(X\subseteq E\), \(r_{M'}(X\cup\{e\})\) is either \(r_M(X)\) or \(r_M(X)+1\), consistently with the matroid rank axioms. The extension is a loop extension when \(e\in\operatorname{cl}_{M'}(\varnothing)\) and a coloop extension when \(r(M')=r(M)+1\).
knowledge_statements.statement_plain: A single-element extension adds one element whose deletion recovers the original matroid; its rank contribution over each old subset is zero or one.

knowledge_statements.statement_title: Independent sets of a principal extension
knowledge_statements.scope_note: Characterizes independence after freely adjoining one element to a flat.
knowledge_statements.statement_latex:
Let \(F\) be a flat of a matroid \(M\), let \(e\notin E(M)\), and let \(N=M+_F e\). Then
\[
\mathcal I(N)=\mathcal I(M)\cup\bigl\{I\cup\{e\}:I\in\mathcal I(M)\text{ and }\operatorname{cl}_M(I)\not\supseteq F\bigr\}.
\]
knowledge_statements.statement_plain: The independent sets of the principal extension are the old independent sets together with sets obtained by adjoining e to an independent set I of M whose closure does not contain F.
knowledge_statements.conclusion_latex: \mathcal I(N)=\mathcal I(M)\cup\{I\cup\{e\}:I\in\mathcal I(M),\ \operatorname{cl}_M(I)\not\supseteq F\}.

knowledge_statements.statement_title: Adjoint single-element extension along a subset
knowledge_statements.scope_note: Defines a particular single-element extension, including its singleton parallel-duplication specialization and affine interpretation.
knowledge_statements.statement_latex: Let $M=(S,\mathcal F)$ be a matroid, let $Z\subseteq S$, and let $z\notin S$. In the adjoint of $z$ along $Z$, a set $X\subseteq S\cup\{z\}$ is independent exactly when either $X\in\mathcal F$, or $z\in X$ and there exists $z'\in Z\setminus X$ such that $(X\setminus\{z\})\cup\{z'\}\in\mathcal F$. If $Z=\{z'\}$, this is parallel duplication. For an affine matroid it adds a point in the flat spanned by $Z$ and otherwise in general position.

A set containing z is independent precisely when z can be exchanged for some omitted element of Z to obtain an independent set of the original matroid; old independent sets remain independent. A singleton Z gives parallel duplication, while in an affine representation the new point lies generically in the flat spanned by Z.

knowledge_statements.statement_title: Principal modular cuts and principal extensions
knowledge_statements.scope_note: Defines freely adjoining a new element to an arbitrary flat and identifies the free-extension special case.
knowledge_statements.statement_latex: Let \(F\) be a flat of a matroid \(M\). The family \(\mathcal M_F=\{X:X\text{ is a flat of }M,\ F\subseteq X\}\) is a modular cut, called the principal modular cut determined by \(F\). The corresponding single-element extension is the principal extension \(M+_F e\), in which \(e\) is freely added to \(F\). The only new circuits are those forced by placing \(e\) on \(F\), and every such circuit spans \(F\). If \(F=E(M)\), then \(M+_{E(M)}e\) is the free extension of \(M\).
knowledge_statements.statement_plain: The flats containing a flat F form its principal modular cut. The corresponding principal extension freely adds a new element to F, creating only circuits forced by that placement, each spanning F. Choosing the whole ground set as F gives the free extension.
knowledge_statements.conclusion_latex: \mathcal M_F=\{X\in\mathcal F(M):F\subseteq X\}\text{ is a modular cut defining }M+_F e;\qquad F=E(M)\Rightarrow M+_F e\text{ is the free extension of }M.

knowledge_statements.statement_title: Free coextension and its dual characterization
knowledge_statements.scope_note: Defines a free coextension using dependent-flat incidence and records its equivalence under matroid duality.
knowledge_statements.statement_latex: Let \(N\) be a coextension of a matroid \(M\) by an element \(e\), where \(e\) is not a loop of \(N\). children.title: Modular-Cut Encoding
children.top_down_role: Encoding of extension choices through modular cuts in the flat lattice.

knowledge_statements.conclusion_latex: Modular cuts of \(M\) are in bijection with single-element extensions of \(M\) on a fixed new element.
knowledge_statements.scope_note: Classical modular-cut encoding of finite one-element extensions.

source_refs.locator: Chapter 5. Elements of matroid theory p. 172

knowledge_statements.statement_latex: A modular cut is a collection \(\mathcal C\subseteq\mathcal F(M)\) that is upward closed among flats and satisfies: if \(F_1,F_2\in\mathcal C\) and \(r(F_1)+r(F_2)=r(F_1\cap F_2)+r(F_1\cup F_2)\), then \(F_1\cap F_2\in\mathcal C\). For an extension \(M'\) by \(e\), its cut is \(\mathcal C_e=\{F\in\mathcal F(M):e\in\operatorname{cl}_{M'}(F)\}\). Conversely, \(\mathcal C\) determines the extension through \[r_{M'}(X\cup\{e\})=\begin{cases}r_M(X),&\operatorname{cl}_M(X)\in\mathcal C,\\r_M(X)+1,&\operatorname{cl}_M(X)\notin\mathcal C.\end{cases}\]
knowledge_statements.statement_plain: A modular cut records exactly which old flats span the new element, and this data uniquely determines the single-element extension rank function.
knowledge_statements.title: Modular-Cut Encoding

knowledge_statements.statement_title: Modular Cut of a Matroid
knowledge_statements.scope_note: Defines a modular cut and records the modular cuts induced by the loop and coloop extensions.
knowledge_statements.statement_latex: A family \(\mathcal M\) of flats of a matroid \(M\) is a modular cut if: (i) whenever \(F\in\mathcal M\) and \(F'\) is a flat of \(M\) containing \(F\), then \(F'\in\mathcal M\); and (ii) whenever \(F_1,F_2\in\mathcal M\) form a modular pair, then \(F_1\cap F_2\in\mathcal M\). Every single-element extension induces a modular cut. The extensions \(M\oplus U_{0,1}\) and \(M\oplus U_{1,1}\) induce, respectively, the family of all flats of \(M\) and the empty family.
knowledge_statements.statement_plain: A modular cut is an upward-closed family of flats closed under intersections of modular pairs. Every single-element extension induces one; adding a loop yields all flats, while adding a coloop yields the empty family.
knowledge_statements.conclusion_latex: \mathcal M\text{ is a modular cut}\iff\left[\begin{array}{l}F\in\mathcal M,\ F\subseteq F',\ F'\in\mathcal F(M)\Rightarrow F'\in\mathcal M,\\F_1,F_2\in\mathcal M\text{ form a modular pair}\Rightarrow F_1\cap F_2\in\mathcal M\end{array}\right].

knowledge_statements.statement_title: Unique Single-Element Extension Represented by a Modular Cut
knowledge_statements.scope_note: Characterizes the unique extension represented by a modular cut and gives its rank function.
knowledge_statements.statement_latex: Let \(M\) be a matroid on \(E\), let \(\mathcal M\) be a modular cut of \(M\), and let \(e\notin E\). There is a unique extension \(N\) of \(M\) on \(E\dot\cup\{e\}\) such that \(\mathcal M\) is exactly the set of flats \(F\) of \(M\) for which \(F\cup\{e\}\) is a flat of \(N\) having rank \(r_M(F)\). For every \(X\subseteq E\), \(r_N(X)=r_M(X)\) and \[r_N(X\cup\{e\})=\begin{cases}r_M(X),&\operatorname{cl}_M(X)\in\mathcal M,\\r_M(X)+1,&\operatorname{cl}_M(X)\notin\mathcal M.\end{cases}\]
knowledge_statements.statement_plain: Every modular cut determines a unique single-element extension. Old subsets retain their ranks; adjoining the new element preserves rank exactly when the old subset's closure belongs to the modular cut, and otherwise raises rank by one.
assumptions_latex: \mathcal M\text{ is a modular cut of }M
knowledge_statements.conclusion_latex: \exists!N\text{ on }E\dot\cup\{e\}\text{ with }N\setminus e=M,\quad r_N(X)=r_M(X),\quad r_N(X\cup\{e\})=\begin{cases}r_M(X),&\operatorname{cl}_M(X)\in\mathcal M,\\r_M(X)+1,&\operatorname{cl}_M(X)\notin\mathcal M\end{cases}\ \forall X\subseteq E.

knowledge_statements.statement_title: Modular-Cut Properties Induced by a Single-Element Extension
knowledge_statements.scope_note: Gives the upward-closure and modular-pair intersection properties of the flat family induced by an extension element.
knowledge_statements.statement_latex: Let \(N\setminus e=M\), and let \(\mathcal M\) be the set of flats \(F\) of \(M\) such that \(F\cup\{e\}\) is a flat of \(N\) and \(r_N(F\cup\{e\})=r_M(F)\). knowledge_statements.statement_title: Modular cut generated by prescribed flats
knowledge_statements.scope_note: Defines the least modular cut containing specified flats and records the loop boundary for the associated extension.
knowledge_statements.statement_latex:
Let \(F_1,\ldots,F_m\) be flats of a matroid M. Intersections of modular cuts are modular cuts, so
\[
\langle F_1,\ldots,F_m\rangle_{\mathrm{mc}}:=\bigcap\{\mathcal C:\mathcal C\text{ is a modular cut of }M,\ \{F_1,\ldots,F_m\}\subseteq\mathcal C\}
\]
is the smallest modular cut containing \(F_1,\ldots,F_m\), called the modular cut they generate. Any single-element extension placing e on every \(F_i\) must correspond to a modular cut containing this generated cut. If the generated cut is the set of all flats of M, then e can be placed on every \(F_i\) only as a loop.
knowledge_statements.statement_plain: The modular cut generated by prescribed flats is the intersection of all modular cuts containing them, hence the smallest such modular cut. An extension that places a new element on all prescribed flats must use a modular cut containing it. If it consists of every flat, the new element must be a loop.
knowledge_statements.conclusion_latex: \langle F_1,\ldots,F_m\rangle_{\mathrm{mc}}=\bigcap_{\substack{\mathcal C\text{ modular cut}\ F_1,\ldots,F_m\in\mathcal C}}\mathcal C;\quad \langle F_1,\ldots,F_m\rangle_{\mathrm{mc}}=\mathcal F(M)\Rightarrow e\text{ must be a loop}.

children.title: Extension–Coextension Duality
children.top_down_role: Dual correspondence between extension and coextension regimes.

assumptions_latex: \(M\) is a finite matroid on \(E\), and \(e\notin E\).
knowledge_statements.conclusion_latex: \(N\setminus e=M\) if and only if \(N^*/e=M^*\), and \(N/e=M\) if and only if \(N^*\setminus e=M^*\).
knowledge_statements.scope_note: Deletion–contraction duality for one-element constructions.

source_refs.locator: Section 13. Duality Theory p. 53

knowledge_statements.statement_latex: Matroid duality exchanges deletion and contraction: \((N\setminus e)^*=N^*/e\) and \((N/e)^*=N^*\setminus e\). Consequently, \(N\) is a single-element extension of \(M\) exactly when \(N^*\) is a single-element coextension of \(M^*\), and \(N\) is a single-element coextension of \(M\) exactly when \(N^*\) is a single-element extension of \(M^*\). The correspondence is involutive because \((M^*)^*=M\).
knowledge_statements.statement_plain: Duality exchanges single-element extensions with coextensions because it exchanges deletion with contraction.

children.title: Extension Realizability Boundaries
children.top_down_role: Structural limits on admissible extension data.

assumptions_latex: \(A=(a_x)_{x\in E}\) represents \(M\) over a field \(\mathbb F\) in a vector space \(V\).
\(W\) is a vector space containing \(V\), and \(v\in W\) represents a proposed new element \(e\).
knowledge_statements.conclusion_latex: An extension preserving the fixed representation is realizable exactly when its modular cut equals \(\{F:v\in\operatorname{span}_{\mathbb F}\{a_x:x\in F\}\}\) for some \(W\supseteq V\) and \(v\in W\).

notation.meaning: Linear span over the representation field

knowledge_statements.scope_note: Representability relative to a fixed linear representation and field.

source_refs.locator: Chapter 5. Elements of matroid theory p. 172

knowledge_statements.statement_latex: Appending \(v\) to \(A\) produces a represented extension whose modular cut is \[\mathcal C_v=\{F\in\mathcal F(M):v\in\operatorname{span}_{\mathbb F}\{a_x:x\in F\}\}.\] Conversely, every extension that extends this fixed representation arises from such a vector in some ambient \(W\supseteq V\). Therefore an abstract modular cut need not be realizable over \(\mathbb F\) relative to \(A\): realizability fails precisely when no vector has the prescribed incidences with the spans of all flats. Allowing \(v\notin V\) includes the coloop extension.
knowledge_statements.statement_plain: For a fixed linear representation, realizable extensions are exactly modular cuts induced by one vector’s membership in flat spans; other modular cuts are unrealizable there.

assumptions_latex: \(M\) and \(Q\) are finite matroids on the same ground set \(E\).

notation.meaning: Deletion and contraction of an auxiliary set

source_refs.locator: Chapter 5. Elements of matroid theory p. 172

knowledge_statements.statement_latex: The matroid \(Q\) is a quotient of \(M\) when the identity map on \(E\) is a strong map from \(M\) to \(Q\), equivalently when \(\mathcal F(Q)\subseteq\mathcal F(M)\). For finite matroids this is also equivalent to the existence of a matroid \(L\) on \(E\mathbin{\dot\cup}X\), for some finite auxiliary set \(X\), such that \(M=L\setminus X\) and \(Q=L/X\). Thus contraction of the auxiliary elements modifies rank while retaining the same displayed ground set \(E\).
knowledge_statements.statement_plain: A quotient has no flats beyond those of the original matroid; equivalently, both arise as deletion and contraction of the same auxiliary elements.

knowledge_statements.statement_title: Weak order and freer matroids
knowledge_statements.scope_note: Weak order on all matroids sharing a fixed ground set, with its greatest and least elements and the behavior of relaxations.
knowledge_statements.statement_latex: For the collection $\mathcal E$ of matroids on a fixed set $E$, define $M_1\ge M_2$ exactly when $\operatorname{id}_E$ is a weak map from $M_1$ to $M_2$. This relation is a partial order, called the weak order. Its greatest element is the free matroid on $E$, and its least element is the rank-zero matroid on $E$. When $M_1\ge M_2$, $M_1$ is said to be freer than $M_2$; in particular, every relaxation of a matroid $M$ is freer than $M$. Passing to a freer matroid corresponds to destroying circuits whose size is less than the rank.
knowledge_statements.statement_plain: On matroids with a common ground set, the weak order declares one matroid at least another when the identity is a weak map between them. The free matroid is greatest, the rank-zero matroid is least, and a relaxation is freer than the original matroid. Increasing freeness corresponds to destroying circuits smaller than the rank.
assumptions_latex: $\mathcal E$ is the collection of all matroids on $E$.
knowledge_statements.conclusion_latex: M_1\ge M_2\iff \operatorname{id}_E:M_1\to M_2\text{ is a weak map};\quad \mathbf 1_{\mathcal E}=M_{\mathrm{free}}(E),\quad \mathbf 0_{\mathcal E}=M_{r=0}(E),\quad \operatorname{Relax}(M)\ge M.

knowledge_statements.statement_title: Matroid quotients and elementary quotients
knowledge_statements.scope_note: Defines general and elementary matroid quotients and records the excluded trivial modular-cut cases.
knowledge_statements.statement_latex: Let \(M\) be a matroid and let \(\mathcal M\) be a nonempty proper modular cut of \(M\). The elementary quotient of \(M\) with respect to \(\mathcal M\) is \((M+_{\mathcal M}e)/e\); it has ground set \(E(M)\) and rank \(r(M)-1\). More generally, \(Q\) is a quotient of \(M\) if there exist a matroid \(N\) and a set \(X\subseteq E(N)\) such that \(M=N\setminus X\) and \(Q=N/X\). Consequently, \(E(Q)=E(M)\). If \(\mathcal M\) is empty or is the set of all flats of \(M\), the elementary construction instead returns \(M\).
knowledge_statements.statement_plain: An elementary quotient is obtained by extending a matroid using a nonempty proper modular cut and then contracting the new element; it preserves the ground set and lowers rank by one. In general, Q is a quotient of M when deleting a set X from some matroid N gives M while contracting X gives Q. Empty or nonproper modular cuts produce only the trivial result M.
assumptions_latex: \mathcal M\text{ is a nonempty proper modular cut of }M
\text{For the general definition, }N\text{ is a matroid and }X\subseteq E(N)
knowledge_statements.conclusion_latex: (M+_{\mathcal M}e)/e\text{ is an elementary quotient of rank }r(M)-1;\quad Q\text{ is a quotient of }M\iff \exists N,X:\ M=N\setminus X,\ Q=N/X.

knowledge_statements.statement_title: Equivalent characterizations of matroid quotients
knowledge_statements.scope_note: Characterizes the quotient relation on a common ground set through flats, rank increments, circuits, and closures.
knowledge_statements.statement_latex: Let \(M_1,M_2\) be matroids on a common ground set \(E\), with rank functions \(r_1,r_2\) and closure operators \(\operatorname{cl}_1,\operatorname{cl}_2\). The following are equivalent: (i) \(M_2\) is a quotient of \(M_1\); (ii) every flat of \(M_2\) is a flat of \(M_1\); (iii) for all \(X\subseteq Y\subseteq E\), \(r_1(Y)-r_1(X)\ge r_2(Y)-r_2(X)\); (iv) every circuit of \(M_1\) is a union of circuits of \(M_2\); and (v) for every \(X\subseteq E\), \(\operatorname{cl}_1(X)\subseteq\operatorname{cl}_2(X)\).
knowledge_statements.statement_plain: For two matroids on the same ground set, M2 is a quotient of M1 exactly when each of four equivalent structural conditions holds: every flat of M2 is a flat of M1; rank increments in M1 dominate those in M2 for every nested pair of sets; every circuit of M1 is a union of circuits of M2; and the M1-closure of every set is contained in its M2-closure.
assumptions_latex: M_1\text{ and }M_2\text{ are matroids on the common ground set }E
knowledge_statements.conclusion_latex: \begin{aligned}M_2\text{ is a quotient of }M_1&\iff \operatorname{Flats}(M_2)\subseteq\operatorname{Flats}(M_1)\\&\iff \forall X\subseteq Y\subseteq E,\ r_1(Y)-r_1(X)\ge r_2(Y)-r_2(X)\\&\iff \text{every circuit of }M_1\text{ is a union of circuits of }M_2\\&\iff \forall X\subseteq E,\ \operatorname{cl}_1(X)\subseteq\operatorname{cl}_2(X).\end{aligned}

knowledge_statements.statement_title: Factorization of a quotient into elementary quotients
knowledge_statements.scope_note: Characterizes a quotient of rank difference k as a chain of exactly k elementary quotients.
knowledge_statements.statement_latex: Let \(M\) and \(Q\) be matroids and let \(k=r(M)-r(Q)\). Then \(Q\) is a quotient of \(M\) if and only if there exist matroids \(M_0,M_1,\ldots,M_k\) such that \(M_0=M\), \(M_k=Q\), and, for every \(i\in\{1,\ldots,k\}\), \(M_i\) is an elementary quotient of \(M_{i-1}\).
knowledge_statements.statement_plain: If the rank difference between M and Q is k, then Q is a quotient of M exactly when M can be transformed into Q through a chain of k elementary quotients.
knowledge_statements.conclusion_latex: Q\text{ is a quotient of }M\iff \exists(M_i)_{i=0}^k:\ M_0=M,\ M_k=Q,\ \forall i\in\{1,\ldots,k\},\ M_i\text{ is an elementary quotient of }M_{i-1}.

knowledge_statements.statement_title: Strong and weak bijective maps of matroids
knowledge_statements.scope_note: Defines strong and weak maps for a bijection and identifies identity strong maps with matroid quotients.
knowledge_statements.statement_latex: Let $M_1$ and $M_2$ be matroids on $E_1$ and $E_2$, and let $\varphi:E_1\to E_2$ be a bijection. The map $\varphi$ is strong if $\varphi^{-1}(F)$ is a flat of $M_1$ for every flat $F$ of $M_2$. It is weak if $\varphi^{-1}(I)$ is independent in $M_1$ for every independent set $I$ of $M_2$; in this case $M_2$ is a weak-map image of $M_1$. If $E_1=E_2$, the identity map is strong from $M_1$ to $M_2$ if and only if $M_2$ is a quotient of $M_1$.
knowledge_statements.statement_plain: A bijection between matroid ground sets is strong when inverse images of target flats are source flats, and weak when inverse images of target independent sets are source independent. On a common ground set, the identity is strong exactly when the target matroid is a quotient of the source.
knowledge_statements.conclusion_latex: \varphi\text{ strong}\iff(\forall F\in\mathcal L(M_2))\ \varphi^{-1}(F)\in\mathcal L(M_1),\quad \varphi\text{ weak}\iff(\forall I\in\mathcal I(M_2))\ \varphi^{-1}(I)\in\mathcal I(M_1);\quad E_1=E_2\Rightarrow[\iota\text{ strong}\iff M_2\text{ is a quotient of }M_1]

knowledge_statements.statement_title: Equivalent characterizations of a weak matroid map
knowledge_statements.scope_note: Applies to bijections between arbitrary matroid ground sets.
knowledge_statements.statement_latex:
Let $M_1$ and $M_2$ be matroids on $E_1$ and $E_2$ with rank functions $r_1$ and $r_2$, and let $\varphi:E_1\to E_2$ be a bijection. The following are equivalent: (i) $\varphi$ is a weak map from $M_1$ to $M_2$; (ii) for every set $D\subseteq E_1$ dependent in $M_1$, $\varphi(D)$ is dependent in $M_2$; (iii) for every circuit $C$ of $M_1$, $\varphi(C)$ contains a circuit of $M_2$; and (iv) for every $X\subseteq E_1$,
\[
r_1(X)\ge r_2(\varphi(X)).
\]
knowledge_statements.statement_plain: For a bijection between two matroid ground sets, being a weak map is equivalent to preserving dependence forward, sending every source circuit to a set containing a target circuit, and never increasing rank under the image map.
assumptions_latex: M_j\text{ is a matroid on }E_j\text{ with rank function }r_j\ (j=1,2)
knowledge_statements.conclusion_latex: \varphi\text{ is weak}\iff[\forall D\subseteq E_1,\ D\text{ dependent in }M_1\Rightarrow\varphi(D)\text{ dependent in }M_2]\iff[\forall C\in\mathcal C(M_1),\ \exists C'\in\mathcal C(M_2):C'\subseteq\varphi(C)]\iff[\forall X\subseteq E_1,\ r_1(X)\ge r_2(\varphi(X))]

knowledge_statements.statement_latex: The matroid \(L\) is a lift of \(M\) if \(M\) is a quotient of \(L\). Equivalently, there exist a finite set \(X\) disjoint from \(E\) and a matroid \(K\) on \(E\mathbin{\dot\cup}X\) such that \(L=K\setminus X\) and \(M=K/X\). By deletion–contraction duality, this holds if and only if \(L^*\) is a quotient of \(M^*\). In flat language, the quotient relation gives \(\mathcal F(M)\subseteq\mathcal F(L)\).
knowledge_statements.statement_plain: A lift reverses the quotient relation: deleting auxiliary elements gives the lift, while contracting them gives the original matroid; duality converts lifts back to quotients.

knowledge_statements.statement_title: Matroid lifts, their representation, and dual characterization
knowledge_statements.scope_note: Defines lifts and elementary lifts, represents a lift by deletion and contraction from a common matroid, and gives the dual quotient equivalence.
knowledge_statements.statement_latex: A matroid \(M_1\) is a lift of \(M_2\) when \(M_2\) is a quotient of \(M_1\); if \(M_2\) is an elementary quotient of \(M_1\), then \(M_1\) is an elementary lift of \(M_2\). Moreover, \(M_1\) is a lift of \(M_2\) if and only if there exist a matroid \(N\) and \(Y\subseteq E(N)\) such that \(N\setminus Y=M_1\) and \(N/Y=M_2\). Equivalently, \(M_1\) is a lift of \(M_2\) if and only if \(M_1^*\) is a quotient of \(M_2^*\).
knowledge_statements.statement_plain: A lift reverses the quotient relation. The two matroids can be obtained from a common matroid by deleting and contracting the same set, and dualizing converts the lift relation into a quotient relation.
knowledge_statements.conclusion_latex: M_1\text{ is a lift of }M_2\iff \exists N\,\exists Y\subseteq E(N):\ N\setminus Y=M_1\ \land\ N/Y=M_2\iff M_1^*\text{ is a quotient of }M_2^*

children.title: Matroid Truncations
children.top_down_role: Rank-lowering construction preserving lower-cardinality independence.

knowledge_statements.title: Matroid Truncations
knowledge_statements.scope_note: Defines rank truncation of a finite matroid by an integer threshold.
knowledge_statements.statement_latex:
Let \(M=(E,\mathcal I)\) be a finite matroid with rank function \(r_M\), and let \(k\) satisfy \(0\le k\le r_M(E)\). The rank-\(k\) truncation \(T_k(M)\) is the matroid on \(E\) whose independent sets and rank function are
\[\mathcal I(T_k(M))=\{I\in\mathcal I:|I|\le k\},\qquad r_{T_k(M)}(X)=\min\{r_M(X),k\}\quad(X\subseteq E).\]
Its bases are exactly the independent \(k\)-subsets of \(M\). The ordinary truncation is \(T_{r_M(E)-1}(M)\) when \(r_M(E)>0\).
knowledge_statements.statement_plain: Truncation caps every set's rank at k; its independent sets are precisely the original independent sets having at most k elements.
knowledge_statements.conclusion_latex: \(r_{T_k(M)}(X)=\min\{r_M(X),k\}\) for every \(X\subseteq E\).

knowledge_statements.title: Free Extensions
knowledge_statements.scope_note: Defines the one-element free extension, including the rank-zero convention.
knowledge_statements.statement_latex:
Let \(M=(E,\mathcal I)\) be a finite matroid of rank \(r\), and let \(e\notin E\). The free extension \(M+e\) is the matroid on \(E\cup\{e\}\) with independent sets
\[\mathcal I(M+e)=\mathcal I\cup\{J\cup\{e\}:J\in\mathcal I,\ |J|<r\}.\]
Thus deletion of \(e\) returns \(M\), while \(e\) lies in the closure of \(E\) but in the closure of no nonspanning subset of \(E\). If \(r=0\), the new element is a loop under this convention.
knowledge_statements.statement_plain: A free extension adds an element that can augment every nonspanning independent set but does not increase the matroid's total rank.
assumptions_latex: \(M\) is a finite matroid of rank \(r\).
knowledge_statements.conclusion_latex: \((M+e)\setminus e=M\) and \(r(M+e)=r(M)\).

notation.meaning: free extension of M by e

knowledge_statements.statement_title: Structure of minor-minimal totally free matroids
knowledge_statements.scope_note: Describes the clonal and connectivity structure when no single-element deletion or contraction remains totally free.
knowledge_statements.statement_latex: Let M be a totally free matroid with |E(M)|\ge 5, and suppose that for every x\in E(M), neither M\setminus x nor M/x is totally free. Then E(M) is a union of two-element clonal classes. Moreover, for every a\in E(M), both M\setminus a and M/a are 3-connected; if a' is the unique clone of a in M, then M\setminus a/a' is totally free.
knowledge_statements.statement_plain: If a totally free matroid has at least five elements and no deletion or contraction of a single element is totally free, its ground set is partitioned into two-element clonal classes. Every single-element deletion and contraction is 3-connected, and deleting an element and contracting its unique clone produces a totally free matroid.

knowledge_statements.conclusion_latex: E(M)\text{ is a union of two-element clonal classes, and }\forall a\in E(M),\;M\setminus a\text{ and }M/a\text{ are 3-connected and }M\setminus a/a'\text{ is totally free, where }a'\text{ is the unique clone of }a.

children.title: Quotient–Lift Duality
children.top_down_role: Dual correspondence between quotient and lift constructions.

knowledge_statements.title: Quotient–Lift Duality
knowledge_statements.scope_note: States deletion–contraction duality for quotient and lift relations on a common ground set.
knowledge_statements.statement_latex:
Let \(M\) and \(N\) be finite matroids on the same ground set \(E\). Say that \(N\) is a quotient of \(M\) if there exist a finite set \(X\) disjoint from \(E\) and a matroid \(L\) on \(E\cup X\) such that \(M=L\setminus X\) and \(N=L/X\); equivalently, \(M\) is a lift of \(N\). Since duality interchanges deletion and contraction,
\[N\text{ is a quotient of }M\quad\Longleftrightarrow\quad N^*\text{ is a lift of }M^*.\]
knowledge_statements.statement_plain: Duality reverses the quotient relation: N is a quotient of M exactly when the dual of N is a lift of the dual of M.
assumptions_latex: \(M\) and \(N\) are finite matroids on the same ground set \(E\).
knowledge_statements.conclusion_latex: \(N\) is a quotient of \(M\) if and only if \(N^*\) is a lift of \(M^*\).

knowledge_statements.statement_title: q-lift construction and its basic properties
knowledge_statements.scope_note: Gives the projective-geometric construction, polynomial identity, and tangential-block preservation law.
knowledge_statements.statement_latex: Let \(M\) be a simple rank-\(r\) \(\mathrm{GF}(q)\)-representable matroid. Choose \(X\subseteq PG(r,q)\) with \(PG(r,q)|X\cong M\), let \(H\) be the hyperplane spanned by \(X\), and choose \(e\in PG(r,q)\setminus H\). If \(M'\) is the restriction of \(PG(r,q)\) to the union of all lines containing \(e\) and a point of \(X\), then \(M'\) is a \(q\)-lift of \(M\) and \[p(M';\lambda)=(\lambda-1)q^r p\!\left(M;\frac{\lambda}{q}\right).\] Moreover, if \(M\) is a tangential \(k\)-block over \(\mathrm{GF}(q)\), then every such \(q\)-lift \(M'\) is a tangential \((k+1)\)-block over \(\mathrm{GF}(q)\).
knowledge_statements.statement_plain: Embed a simple rank-r GF(q)-representable matroid as a restriction X spanning a hyperplane of PG(r,q), select a point e outside that hyperplane, and restrict to the union of the lines joining e to X. The resulting q-lift has polynomial p(M';lambda)=(lambda-1)q^r p(M;lambda/q), and a q-lift of a tangential k-block is a tangential (k+1)-block.
assumptions_latex: M\text{ is a simple rank-}r\text{ matroid representable over }\mathrm{GF}(q)
knowledge_statements.conclusion_latex: p(M';\lambda)=(\lambda-1)q^r p\!\left(M;\lambda/q\right),\qquad M\text{ tangential }k\text{-block}\Rightarrow M'\text{ tangential }(k+1)\text{-block}.
