knowledge_statements.title: Truncation–Free-Extension Relation
knowledge_statements.scope_note: Represents ordinary truncation as contraction of a freely added element.
knowledge_statements.statement_latex:
Let \(M\) be a finite matroid on \(E\) with rank \(r>0\), and let \(M+e\) be its free extension by an element \(e\notin E\). Then
\[(M+e)/e=T_{r-1}(M).\]
Equivalently, its rank function satisfies
\[r_{(M+e)/e}(X)=\min\{r_M(X),r-1\}\qquad(X\subseteq E).\]
Thus every ordinary truncation of a positive-rank matroid has a free-extension-and-contraction representation.
knowledge_statements.statement_plain: Freely adding one element to a positive-rank matroid and then contracting it produces the original matroid truncated by one rank.
assumptions_latex: \(M\) is a finite matroid on \(E\) with rank \(r>0\).

notation.meaning: free extension of M by e

knowledge_statements.statement_title: Matroid truncation and iterated truncation
knowledge_statements.scope_note: Defines truncation via free extension and contraction, including the rank-zero convention, rank change, iteration, and a uniform-matroid instance.
knowledge_statements.statement_latex: For a matroid \(M\) with \(r(M)>0\), define its truncation by \(T(M)=(M+_{E(M)}e)/e\), where \(e\) is added freely. If \(r(M)=0\), set \(T(M)=M\). Thus \(r(T(M))=r(M)-1\) when \(r(M)>0\), and \(r(T(M))=0\) when \(r(M)=0\). For every positive integer \(i\), define \(T^0(M)=M\) and \(T^i(M)=T(T^{i-1}(M))\). In particular, if \(k\le n\), then \(T^k(U_{n,n})=U_{n-k,n}\).
knowledge_statements.statement_plain: Positive-rank matroid truncation freely adds one element and then contracts it, lowering rank by one. A rank-zero matroid is unchanged. Iterated truncation is defined recursively, and k truncations of the rank-n uniform matroid give the rank-(n-k) uniform matroid on the same n elements.
assumptions_latex: 0\le k\le n\text{ for the uniform-matroid instance}
knowledge_statements.conclusion_latex: T(M)=\begin{cases}(M+_{E(M)}e)/e,&r(M)>0,\quad e\text{ added freely},\\M,&r(M)=0,\end{cases}\quad r(T(M))=\max\{r(M)-1,0\},\quad T^0(M)=M,\quad T^i(M)=T(T^{i-1}(M)),\quad T^k(U_{n,n})=U_{n-k,n}

knowledge_statements.statement_title: Local Rank-Axiom Characterization of Matroids
knowledge_statements.scope_note: Characterizes matroid rank functions by normalization, unit-increment monotonicity, and a local closure condition.
knowledge_statements.statement_latex: Let E be a set and r:2^E\to\mathbb{Z}_{\ge 0}. Then r is the rank function of a matroid on E if and only if: (i) r(\varnothing)=0; (ii) for every X\subseteq E and x\in E, r(X)\le r(X\cup\{x\})\le r(X)+1; and (iii) for every X\subseteq E and x,y\in E, if r(X\cup\{x\})=r(X\cup\{y\})=r(X), then r(X\cup\{x,y\})=r(X).
knowledge_statements.statement_plain: A nonnegative integer-valued set function is a matroid rank function exactly when it is zero on the empty set, adjoining one element increases rank by either zero or one, and two elements that individually do not increase rank also do not increase it when adjoined together.

knowledge_statements.statement_title: Jointed free swirls and free swirls
knowledge_statements.scope_note: Construction from a rank-r whirl together with the stated clone and self-duality properties of the resulting free swirl.
knowledge_statements.statement_latex: For r\ge 3, begin with a rank-r whirl having cyclically ordered spokes s_1,\ldots,s_r and nontrivial lines \{s_i,a_i,s_{i+1}\}, where s_{r+1}=s_1. For each i\in\{1,\ldots,r\}, freely add a point b_i on \{s_i,a_i,s_{i+1}\}; the resulting matroid is the rank-r jointed free swirl \Psi_r^+. The rank-r free swirl is \Psi_r=\Psi_r^+\setminus\{s_1,\ldots,s_r\}. In \Psi_r, a_i and b_i are clones for every i, and \Psi_r\cong\Psi_r^*.
knowledge_statements.statement_plain: For rank at least three, form the jointed free swirl by starting with a rank-r whirl and freely adding one point to each specified cyclic line. Deleting all spokes produces the rank-r free swirl. Each pair a_i and b_i consists of clones in the free swirl, and the free swirl is self-dual.
assumptions_latex: s_1,\ldots,s_r\text{ are the cyclically ordered spokes of a rank-}r\text{ whirl}
knowledge_statements.conclusion_latex: \Psi_r^+\text{ and }\Psi_r\text{ are defined by the stated extensions and deletion};\quad a_i,b_i\text{ are clones in }\Psi_r\ (1\le i\le r),\quad \Psi_r\cong\Psi_r^*.

knowledge_statements.statement_title: Binary matroids, regular matroids, and total unimodularity
knowledge_statements.scope_note: Comparative definitions of two representable-matroid classes and the matrix property used to define regularity.
knowledge_statements.statement_latex: A matroid is binary if it is representable over $\operatorname{GF}(2)$. A real matrix is totally unimodular if every square submatrix has determinant in $\{0,1,-1\}$. A matroid is regular if it can be represented by a totally unimodular matrix; such matroids are also called unimodular matroids by some authors.

knowledge_statements.conclusion_latex: M\text{ is binary}\iff M\text{ is representable over }\operatorname{GF}(2),\qquad M\text{ is regular}\iff M\text{ has a totally unimodular matrix representation}.

knowledge_statements.title: Uniform Matroids
knowledge_statements.scope_note: Defines the finite uniform matroid by a single global cardinality capacity.
knowledge_statements.statement_latex:
For a finite set \(E\) of cardinality \(n\) and an integer \(r\) with \(0\le r\le n\), the uniform matroid \(U_{r,n}\) has independent sets
\[\mathcal I(U_{r,n})=\{I\subseteq E:|I|\le r\}.\]
Consequently every \(r\)-subset is a basis, every subset of size at most \(r\) is independent, and its rank function is
\[r_{U_{r,n}}(X)=\min\{|X|,r\}\qquad(X\subseteq E).\]
knowledge_statements.statement_plain: The uniform matroid of rank r declares every subset of at most r elements independent and every larger subset dependent.
knowledge_statements.conclusion_latex: \(\mathcal I(U_{r,n})=\{I\subseteq E:|I|\le r\}\).

notation.meaning: uniform matroid of rank r on n elements

knowledge_statements.statement_title: Paving matroids and uniform matroids
knowledge_statements.scope_note: Defines paving matroids by circuit size and records their relationship to uniform matroids.
knowledge_statements.statement_latex: Let \(M\) be a matroid of rank \(r(M)\). Every circuit of \(M\) has size at most \(r(M)+1\). The matroid \(M\) is uniform if and only if it has no circuit of size less than \(r(M)+1\), and it is paving if and only if it has no circuit of size less than \(r(M)\). Consequently every uniform matroid is paving, but the converse fails; for example, \(M(K_4)\) is paving but not uniform.
knowledge_statements.statement_plain: For a matroid M, every circuit has at most rank(M)+1 elements. M is uniform exactly when it has no circuit smaller than rank(M)+1, while M is paving exactly when it has no circuit smaller than rank(M). Thus every uniform matroid is paving, but not every paving matroid is uniform; the cycle matroid of K4 is a counterexample.
knowledge_statements.conclusion_latex: M\text{ is paving}\iff \nexists C\in\mathcal C(M):|C|<r(M),\qquad \{\text{uniform matroids}\}\subsetneq\{\text{paving matroids}\}.

knowledge_statements.statement_title: General circuit–cocircuit lower bound on ground-set size
knowledge_statements.scope_note: The bound applies without a connectivity assumption and is sharp for uniform matroids of positive rank and corank.
knowledge_statements.statement_latex: Let \(M\) be a matroid with \(r(M)>0\) and \(r^*(M)>0\). If \(c\) and \(c^*\) are respectively the maximum sizes of a circuit and a cocircuit of \(M\), then \[c+c^*-2\le |E(M)|.\] The bound is attained by every uniform matroid having positive rank and corank.
knowledge_statements.statement_plain: For any matroid of positive rank and positive corank, the largest circuit size plus the largest cocircuit size minus two does not exceed the ground-set size. Every uniform matroid of positive rank and corank attains equality.
knowledge_statements.conclusion_latex: c+c^*-2\le |E(M)|,\quad \text{with equality for every positive-rank, positive-corank uniform matroid}

knowledge_statements.statement_title: Properties of the uniform matroid U_{2,4}
knowledge_statements.scope_note: Class, representability, duality, connectivity, roundedness, and algebraicity properties of the four-point line.
knowledge_statements.statement_latex: The uniform matroid $U_{2,4}$ is the four-point line and is isomorphic to the rank-two whirl $\mathcal W^2$. It is the unique excluded minor for binary matroids and an excluded minor for graphic, cographic, and regular matroids. It is $\mathbb F$-representable if and only if $|\mathbb F|\ge 3$, and it is near-regular. It is transversal, a strict gammoid, a gammoid, identically self-dual, and algebraic over every field, and its automorphism group is the symmetric group. It is also the unique three-connected nonbinary matroid $M$ having an element $e$ such that both $M\setminus e$ and $M/e$ are binary, and the unique matroid $M$ with at least four elements such that $\{M\}$ is 2-rounded.
knowledge_statements.statement_plain: U(2,4), the four-point line, is the rank-two whirl. It has the stated excluded-minor, field-representability, class-membership, duality, automorphism, connectivity, roundedness, and algebraicity properties.
knowledge_statements.conclusion_latex: U_{2,4}\cong\mathcal W^2\text{ and has all the stated properties.}

knowledge_statements.statement_title: Truncation of a Matroid
knowledge_statements.scope_note: Definition of rank-$k$ truncation and its rank formula.
knowledge_statements.statement_latex: Let $M=(S,\mathcal I)$ be a matroid and let $k\in\mathbb Z_{\ge0}$. Set $\mathcal I'=\{J\in\mathcal I:|J|\le k\}$. knowledge_statements.conclusion_latex: M'=(S,\{J\in\mathcal I:|J|\le k\})\text{ is a matroid and }(\forall A\subseteq S)\ r'(A)=\min\{r(A),k\}

children.title: Partition Matroids
children.top_down_role: Block-capacity matroids induced by a ground-set partition.

knowledge_statements.title: Partition Matroids
knowledge_statements.scope_note: Defines partition matroids through disjoint block-capacity constraints.
knowledge_statements.statement_latex:
Let \(E=E_1\mathbin{\dot\cup}\cdots\mathbin{\dot\cup}E_m\) be a partition of a finite set, and choose integer capacities \(0\le b_i\le |E_i|\). The associated partition matroid has independent sets
\[\mathcal I=\{I\subseteq E:|I\cap E_i|\le b_i\text{ for every }i=1,\ldots,m\}.\]
Its rank function is
\[r(X)=\sum_{i=1}^{m}\min\{|X\cap E_i|,b_i\}\qquad(X\subseteq E).\]
Thus feasibility is determined independently within each block.
knowledge_statements.statement_plain: A partition matroid permits at most a prescribed number of selected elements from each block of a partition.
knowledge_statements.conclusion_latex: \(I\) is independent exactly when \(|I\cap E_i|\le b_i\) for every \(i\).

knowledge_statements.statement_title: Generalized partition matroid
knowledge_statements.scope_note: Definition by a bounded block-count basis family, including its reduction to partition matroids.
knowledge_statements.statement_latex: Let $\{S_1,\ldots,S_t\}$ partition $S$, let $0\le f_i\le g_i\le |S_i|$ be integers, and let $k$ be a positive integer satisfying $\sum_i f_i\le k\le\sum_i g_i$. Then $\mathcal B=\{X\subseteq S:|X|=k,\ f_i\le |S_i\cap X|\le g_i\text{ for }i=1,\ldots,t\}$ satisfies the basis axioms and defines a generalized partition matroid. When $f_i=0$ for all $i$ and $k=\sum_i\min\{g_i,|S_i|\}$, this construction reduces to a partition matroid.
knowledge_statements.statement_plain: Partition the ground set into blocks S1 through St, impose integral lower and upper bounds fi and gi on the number selected from each block, and fix a feasible positive total size k. The feasible k-element sets form the bases of a generalized partition matroid. With all lower bounds zero and k equal to the sum of the block capacities, the construction reduces to a partition matroid.
assumptions_latex: $f_i,g_i\in\mathbb Z_{\ge0}$ and $0\le f_i\le g_i\le |S_i|$ for every $i$.
knowledge_statements.conclusion_latex: $\mathcal B$ satisfies the basis axioms; if $f_i=0$ for all $i$ and $k=\sum_i\min\{g_i,|S_i|\}$, the resulting matroid is a partition matroid.

knowledge_statements.statement_title: Rank characterization of matroid-partition feasibility
knowledge_statements.scope_note: Necessary and sufficient condition for partitioning a common ground set into sets independent in respective matroids.
knowledge_statements.statement_latex: Let \(M_i=(S,r_i)\), \(i=1,\ldots,k\), be matroids on the same ground set \(S\). There exists a partition \(S=F_1\mathbin{\dot\cup}\cdots\mathbin{\dot\cup}F_k\) such that \(F_i\) is independent in \(M_i\) for every \(i\) if and only if \[\sum_{i=1}^{k}r_i(X)\ge |X|\qquad\text{for every }X\subseteq S.\]
knowledge_statements.statement_plain: A common ground set can be partitioned into one independent set for each of the given matroids exactly when, for every subset of the ground set, the sum of its ranks in those matroids is at least its cardinality.

knowledge_statements.statement_title: Partition-Capacity Sets Form a Matroid
knowledge_statements.scope_note: Block-capacity construction of a partition matroid.
knowledge_statements.statement_latex: Let \(E\) be finite, let \(\pi=\{B_1,\ldots,B_m\}\) be a partition of \(E\), and let \(d_i\in\mathbb Z_{\ge 0}\) for \(i=1,\ldots,m\). Define \(\mathcal I=\{I\subseteq E:|I\cap B_i|\le d_i\text{ for all }i=1,\ldots,m\}\). Then \((E,\mathcal I)\) is a matroid.
knowledge_statements.statement_plain: For a finite set partitioned into disjoint blocks with nonnegative integer capacities, the subsets satisfying every block capacity form the independent sets of a matroid.

knowledge_statements.statement_title: Partition Matroid
knowledge_statements.scope_note: Defines partition matroids by block-capacity constraints and records the common unit-capacity convention.
knowledge_statements.statement_latex: Let $E=E_1\mathbin{\dot\cup}\cdots\mathbin{\dot\cup}E_m$ be a partition of a ground set and let $d_i$ be nonnegative capacity bounds. The partition matroid on $E$ has independent sets $\mathcal I=\{I\subseteq E: |I\cap E_i|\le d_i\text{ for every }i=1,\ldots,m\}$. A common special case, often left implicit, is $d_i=1$ for every $i$.
knowledge_statements.statement_plain: Given a ground set partitioned into blocks, a partition matroid declares a set independent exactly when it contains at most the prescribed capacity d_i from each block E_i. A common convention is that every capacity equals one, even when this is not stated explicitly.
knowledge_statements.conclusion_latex: \mathcal I=\{I\subseteq E: |I\cap E_i|\le d_i\ \forall i=1,\ldots,m\}\text{ defines a partition matroid; commonly }d_i=1\ \forall i.

children.title: Laminar Matroids
children.top_down_role: Capacity matroids induced by a laminar set family.

knowledge_statements.title: Laminar Matroids
knowledge_statements.scope_note: Defines finite laminar matroids using capacities on nested-or-disjoint subsets.
knowledge_statements.statement_latex:
Let \(E\) be finite and let \(\mathcal L\subseteq 2^E\) be laminar: for all \(A,B\in\mathcal L\), either \(A\subseteq B\), \(B\subseteq A\), or \(A\cap B=\varnothing\). Assign each \(A\in\mathcal L\) an integer capacity \(0\le b(A)\le |A|\). The laminar matroid determined by \((\mathcal L,b)\) has independent sets
\[\mathcal I=\{I\subseteq E:|I\cap A|\le b(A)\text{ for every }A\in\mathcal L\}.\]
The laminar nesting condition is what guarantees the matroid exchange axiom for these simultaneous capacities.
knowledge_statements.statement_plain: A laminar matroid imposes cardinality capacities on a family of subsets in which every two sets are nested or disjoint.
knowledge_statements.conclusion_latex: \(\{I\subseteq E:|I\cap A|\le b(A)\ \forall A\in\mathcal L\}\) is a matroid independence system.

children.title: Capacity-Class Specializations
children.top_down_role: Containment and specialization relationships among uniform, partition, and laminar classes.

knowledge_statements.title: Capacity-Class Specializations
knowledge_statements.scope_note: Records the nesting of global, partition, and laminar capacity matroid classes.
knowledge_statements.statement_latex:
Finite cardinality-capacity matroids admit the specialization chain
\[\{\text{uniform matroids}\}\subseteq\{\text{partition matroids}\}\subseteq\{\text{laminar matroids}\}.\]
Specifically, \(U_{r,n}\) is the partition matroid with the single block \(E\) and capacity \(r\). A partition matroid with blocks \(E_1,\ldots,E_m\) and capacities \(b_1,\ldots,b_m\) is the laminar matroid with \(\mathcal L=\{E_1,\ldots,E_m\}\) and \(b(E_i)=b_i\). Adding nested sets to \(\mathcal L\) yields capacities shared across several descendant blocks.
knowledge_statements.statement_plain: Uniform matroids are one-block partition matroids, and partition matroids are laminar matroids whose constrained sets are pairwise disjoint.
assumptions_latex: All ground sets and capacity families are finite.
knowledge_statements.conclusion_latex: \(\mathrm{Uniform}\subseteq\mathrm{Partition}\subseteq\mathrm{Laminar}\).

knowledge_statements.statement_title: Matroid Induced by an Integral Polymatroid Function
knowledge_statements.scope_note: Construction of a constraint-generated matroid from a polymatroid function and the resulting rank formula.
knowledge_statements.statement_latex: Let $b$ be an integral polymatroid function on $S$ and define $\mathcal I(b)=\{I\subseteq S:|I\cap X|\le b(X)\ \text{for every }X\subseteq S\}$. Then $\mathcal I(b)$ satisfies the matroid independence axioms. For the matroid $M_b=(S,\mathcal I(b))$, its rank function is $r_b(Z)=\min_{X\subseteq Z}\bigl(b(X)+|Z\setminus X|\bigr)$ for every $Z\subseteq S$.
knowledge_statements.statement_plain: The subsets whose incidence vectors satisfy all inequalities of an integral polymatroid form a matroid. Its rank on a set is the minimum, over subsets of that set, of the polymatroid value plus the number of omitted elements.
assumptions_latex: b:2^S\to\mathbb Z\text{ is a polymatroid function}
\mathcal I(b)=\{I\subseteq S:|I\cap X|\le b(X)\ \forall X\subseteq S\}
knowledge_statements.conclusion_latex: (S,\mathcal I(b))\text{ is a matroid and }r_b(Z)=\min_{X\subseteq Z}\{b(X)+|Z\setminus X|\}\quad\forall Z\subseteq S

knowledge_statements.statement_title: Sparse forbidden-set construction of a matroid
knowledge_statements.scope_note: A basis-family construction associated with paving matroids.
knowledge_statements.statement_latex: Let $r\ge2$, let $|S|\ge r$, and let $\mathcal H=\{H_1,\ldots,H_t\}$ be a possibly empty family of proper subsets of $S$ such that $|H_i|\ge r$ for every $i$ and $|H_i\cap H_j|\le r-2$ whenever $i\ne j$. Then $\mathcal B_{\mathcal H}=\{B\subseteq S:|B|=r\text{ and }B\nsubseteq H_i\text{ for every }i\}$ satisfies the basis axioms.
knowledge_statements.statement_plain: Let r be at least 2 and let S have at least r elements. If a possibly empty family of proper subsets of S has each member of size at least r and every two distinct members intersect in at most r minus 2 elements, then the r-subsets not contained in any family member satisfy the matroid basis axioms.
assumptions_latex: $\mathcal H=\{H_1,\ldots,H_t\}$ is possibly empty and every $H_i$ is a proper subset of $S$.
knowledge_statements.conclusion_latex: $\mathcal B_{\mathcal H}=\{B\subseteq S:|B|=r,\ B\nsubseteq H_i\ \forall i\}$ satisfies the basis axioms.

knowledge_statements.statement_title: Basis description of the Theta matroid
knowledge_statements.scope_note: Existence and complete basis characterization of \(\Theta_n\).
knowledge_statements.statement_latex: Let \(n\ge 2\), \(X=\{x_1,\ldots,x_n\}\), and \(Y=\{y_1,\ldots,y_n\}\) be disjoint. There is a matroid \(\Theta_n\) on \(X\cup Y\) whose bases are exactly \[\mathcal B=\{Y\}\cup\{(Y\setminus\{y_i\})\cup\{x_j\}:i,j\in[n],\ i\ne j\}\cup\{(Y\setminus Y')\cup X':X'\subseteq X,\ Y'\subseteq Y,\ |X'|=|Y'|=2\}.\]
knowledge_statements.statement_plain: For two disjoint n-element sets X and Y with n at least two, there exists a matroid Theta_n whose bases are precisely Y, every set obtained by replacing y_i with x_j for distinct indices i and j, and every set obtained by replacing two elements of Y by any two elements of X.
knowledge_statements.conclusion_latex: \exists\,\Theta_n\text{ on }X\cup Y\text{ with the stated set }\mathcal B\text{ of bases.}

children.title: Scheduling Matroids

knowledge_statements.title: Scheduling Matroids
knowledge_statements.scope_note: Uses the unit-time, single-machine deadline-feasibility version of a scheduling matroid.
knowledge_statements.statement_latex:
Let \(E\) be a finite set of unit-processing-time jobs, each with an integer deadline \(d_j\ge1\), to be scheduled without idle-time restrictions on one machine starting at time zero. Define
\[\mathcal I=\left\{I\subseteq E:\left|\{j\in I:d_j\le t\}\right|\le t\text{ for every integer }t\ge1\right\}.\]
Then \((E,\mathcal I)\) is a matroid. Its independent sets are exactly the job subsets admitting an ordering in which every job completes no later than its deadline; earliest-deadline-first provides such an ordering whenever the inequalities hold.
knowledge_statements.statement_plain: Unit-time jobs with deadlines form a matroid: a subset is independent exactly when it can be scheduled on one machine without missing a deadline.
assumptions_latex: \(E\) is a finite collection of unit-time jobs.
Each deadline \(d_j\) is a positive integer.
knowledge_statements.conclusion_latex: \(I\) is schedulable by its deadlines if and only if \(|\{j\in I:d_j\le t\}|\le t\) for all integers \(t\ge1\).

knowledge_statements.title: Count Matroids
knowledge_statements.scope_note: Uses the standard vertex-weighted graphical count-matroid construction.
knowledge_statements.statement_latex:
Let \(G=(V,E)\) be a finite loopless graph, let \(m:V\to\mathbb Z_{\ge0}\), and let \(\ell\in\mathbb Z_{\ge0}\) satisfy \(m(u)+m(v)\ge\ell+1\) for every edge \(uv\in E\). For \(F\subseteq E\), write \(V(F)\) for its incident vertices. The count matroid has independent sets
\[\mathcal I=\{F\subseteq E:|F'|\le m(V(F'))-\ell\text{ for every nonempty }F'\subseteq F\},\]
where \(m(X)=\sum_{v\in X}m(v)\). Under the stated edge condition, this system satisfies the matroid axioms.
knowledge_statements.statement_plain: A graphical count matroid bounds every nonempty edge subset by the total weights of its incident vertices minus a fixed offset.
knowledge_statements.conclusion_latex: \(\mathcal I=\{F\subseteq E:|F'|\le m(V(F'))-\ell\ \forall\varnothing\ne F'\subseteq F\}\) is a matroid independence system.

knowledge_statements.statement_title: Matroid-Intersection Characterization of k-Foliages

knowledge_statements.statement_latex: Let \(D=(V,A)\), let \(n=|V|\), and let \(M_1,M_2\) be the associated matroids on \(A\). A subgraph \(D_B=(V,B)\) is a \(k\)-foliage if and only if \(B\) is independent in both \(M_1\) and \(M_2\) and \(|B|=k(n-1)\).

knowledge_statements.conclusion_latex: D_B\text{ is a }k\text{-foliage}\iff B\in\mathcal I(M_1)\cap\mathcal I(M_2)\text{ and }|B|=k(n-1).

knowledge_statements.statement_title: Hypergraph count constraints define a matroid
knowledge_statements.scope_note: Matroid construction on the hyperedge set of a hypergraph closure system.
knowledge_statements.statement_latex: Let \(\mathcal K_H\) be the closure system defined by a hypergraph \(H=(V,\mathcal E)\). Suppose \(h:2^V\to\mathbb R\) satisfies \(h(Z)\ge 0\) for every \(Z\in\mathcal E\), and \(h(X)+h(Y)\ge h(X\cap Y)+h(X\cup Y)\) whenever \(X\cap Y\) induces a hyperedge of \(H\). Then \(\mathcal I^*:=\{\mathcal I\subseteq\mathcal E: i_{\mathcal I}(Z)\le h(Z)\text{ for every }Z\subseteq V\text{ with }i_H(Z)\ge1\}\) satisfies the matroid independence axioms.
knowledge_statements.statement_plain: For a hypergraph closure system, a set function that is nonnegative on hyperedges and submodular for every pair whose intersection induces a hyperedge yields a matroid on the hyperedges: the independent families are exactly those satisfying every induced-subhypergraph count bound.
assumptions_latex: H=(V,\mathcal E)\text{ is a hypergraph defining the closure system }\mathcal K_H.
h(X)+h(Y)\ge h(X\cap Y)+h(X\cup Y)\quad\forall X,Y\subseteq V\text{ such that }X\cap Y\text{ induces a hyperedge of }H.
knowledge_statements.conclusion_latex: \mathcal I^*=\{\mathcal I\subseteq\mathcal E:i_{\mathcal I}(Z)\le h(Z)\ \forall Z\subseteq V\text{ with }i_H(Z)\ge1\}\text{ is the independent-set family of a matroid on }\mathcal E.

knowledge_statements.scope_note: Uses the contextual count matroid \(M^\#\) and vertex-capacity function \(g\).
knowledge_statements.statement_latex: Let \(F'\subseteq E\) be independent in \(M^\#\), let \(f=sz\in E\setminus F'\), and set \(F:=F'\cup\{f\}\). Then \(F\) is independent in \(M^\#\) if and only if \(H=(V,F)\) admits an orientation in which the in-degree of every vertex \(v\) is at most \(g(v)\).
knowledge_statements.statement_plain: Adding f to the independent set preserves independence in the count matroid exactly when the graph formed by the enlarged edge set has an orientation respecting every vertex's in-degree bound.
knowledge_statements.conclusion_latex: F\in\mathcal I(M^\#)\iff \exists\text{ an orientation of }H\text{ such that }\varrho_H(v)\le g(v)\ \forall v\in V.

knowledge_statements.statement_title: Bounded Edge Deletion for In-Degree-Constrained Orientation
knowledge_statements.scope_note: Characterizes when at most γ edges can be removed before orienting the remainder under vertexwise in-degree caps.
knowledge_statements.statement_latex: Let \(H=(V,F)\) be an undirected graph, let \(g':V\to\mathbb Z_+\), and let \(\gamma\in\mathbb Z_+\). At most \(\gamma\) edges can be removed so that the remaining graph \(H'\) admits an orientation with in-degree function \(\varrho'\) satisfying \(\varrho'(v)\le g'(v)\) for every \(v\in V\) if and only if \(g'(X)+\gamma\ge i_H(X)\) for every \(X\subseteq V\).
knowledge_statements.statement_plain: One can delete at most γ edges and orient the remaining graph within all vertex in-degree upper bounds exactly when, for every vertex subset X, its total bound plus γ is at least the number of edges induced by X.
knowledge_statements.conclusion_latex: \exists R\subseteq F,\ |R|\le\gamma,\ \exists\text{ an orientation of }H-R\text{ with }\varrho'(v)\le g'(v)\ \forall v\in V\iff g'(X)+\gamma\ge i_H(X)\ \forall X\subseteq V.

children.top_down_role: Matroids arising from sparsity constraints on combinatorial structures.

knowledge_statements.title: Sparsity Matroids
knowledge_statements.scope_note: Defines finite graphical sparsity matroids in the standard integer parameter range.
knowledge_statements.statement_latex:
Let \(G=(V,E)\) be a finite loopless graph, let \(k\ge1\), and let \(0\le\ell\le2k-1\) be integers. An edge set \(F\subseteq E\) is \((k,\ell)\)-sparse when every nonempty \(F'\subseteq F\) satisfies
\[|F'|\le k|V(F')|-\ell.\]
The family of all \((k,\ell)\)-sparse subsets of \(E\) is the independent-set family of the \((k,\ell)\)-sparsity matroid of \(G\). A spanning set is \((k,\ell)\)-tight when it is sparse and has \(|F|=k|V|-\ell\).
knowledge_statements.statement_plain: A sparsity matroid declares an edge set independent when every nonempty subcollection has at most k times its incident-vertex count minus l edges.
knowledge_statements.conclusion_latex: \(\{F\subseteq E:|F'|\le k|V(F')|-\ell\ \forall\varnothing\ne F'\subseteq F\}\) is a matroid independence system.

knowledge_statements.statement_title: Rigidity rank, partition criterion, and augmentation deficiency
knowledge_statements.scope_note: For a graph on n vertices, characterizes rigidity through the rigidity-matroid rank and an edge-partition inequality, and gives the exact number of edges needed to attain rigidity.
knowledge_statements.statement_latex: Let G=(V,E) have n=|V| and define b^*(F)=2|V(F)|-3. Then G is rigid if and only if r(M_G)=2n-3, equivalently if and only if \sum_{i=1}^k b^*(E_i)\ge 2n-3 for every partition \{E_1,\ldots,E_k\} of E. If G is not rigid, the minimum number of edges whose addition makes G rigid is 2n-3-\min\{\sum_{i=1}^k b^*(E_i):\{E_1,\ldots,E_k\}\text{ partitions }E\}. Moreover, for every minimizing partition, |V(E_i)\cap V(E_j)|\le 1 whenever 1\le i<j\le k.
knowledge_statements.statement_plain: A graph on n vertices is rigid exactly when its rigidity matroid has rank 2n−3, equivalently when every partition of its edge set has total value sum_i(2|V(E_i)|−3) at least 2n−3. If it is not rigid, its minimum rigidifying edge augmentation equals 2n−3 minus the minimum such partition value. In any minimizing partition, two distinct parts involve at most one common vertex.
knowledge_statements.conclusion_latex: G\text{ rigid}\iff r(M_G)=2n-3\iff \forall\{E_i\}_{i=1}^k\text{ partition of }E,\ \sum_i b^*(E_i)\ge 2n-3

children.title: Constraint-Generation Boundaries
children.top_down_role: Conditions separating matroidal constraint systems from nonmatroidal ones.

knowledge_statements.title: Constraint-Generation Boundaries
knowledge_statements.scope_note: Shows that arbitrary overlapping cardinality constraints need not define a matroid.
knowledge_statements.statement_latex:
Let \(E=\{1,2,3\}\) and impose the two capacities
\[|I\cap\{1,2\}|\le1,\qquad |I\cap\{2,3\}|\le1.\]
The resulting hereditary family contains \(A=\{2\}\) and \(B=\{1,3\}\), with \(|A|<|B|\). However, neither \(A\cup\{1\}\) nor \(A\cup\{3\}\) is feasible. Hence the augmentation axiom fails, so arbitrary overlapping capacity sets do not necessarily generate a matroid. Structural hypotheses such as disjointness, laminarity, or an appropriate submodular count construction are therefore essential.
knowledge_statements.statement_plain: Two crossing capacity constraints on three elements yield a hereditary system that violates augmentation, proving that arbitrary constraint families need not define matroids.
assumptions_latex: Feasibility means satisfying both displayed cardinality inequalities.
knowledge_statements.conclusion_latex: \(A=\{2\}\) and \(B=\{1,3\}\) violate matroid augmentation; therefore the feasible family is not a matroid.

knowledge_statements.statement_latex: Define \(\mathcal I_G=\{F\subseteq E:(V,F)\text{ contains no cycle}\}\). Then \(\mathcal I_G\) is the independent-set family of a matroid \(M(G)\) on \(E\), called the graphic matroid of \(G\). Its circuits are precisely the edge sets of graph-theoretic cycles, including a loop as a one-element cycle and two parallel edges as a two-element cycle. Its bases are the maximal forests of \(G\); if \(G\) is connected, these are exactly its spanning trees.
knowledge_statements.statement_plain: A graphic matroid has graph edges as elements and forests as independent sets; its circuits are graph cycles and its bases are maximal forests.

knowledge_statements.statement_title: Graphic Matroid Structure and Representation
knowledge_statements.scope_note: Defines cycle matroids and records their circuits, bases, rank, minor operations, regularity, and excluded-minor characterization among regular matroids.
knowledge_statements.statement_latex: For a graph \(G=(V,E)\), the forests form the independent sets of a matroid \(M(G)\). Its circuits are the graph cycles, its bases are the maximal forests, and for every \(F\subseteq E\), \(r_{M(G)}(F)=|V|-\kappa(V,F)\). Matroid deletion and contraction correspond to edge deletion and contraction. An oriented incidence matrix represents \(M(G)\) over every field, so every graphic matroid is regular. A regular matroid is graphic if and only if it has neither \(M(K_5)^*\) nor \(M(K_{3,3})^*\) as a minor.
knowledge_statements.statement_plain: The forests of a graph form its cycle matroid. Its circuits are graph cycles, its bases are maximal forests, and an edge set has rank equal to the number of vertices minus the number of induced components. Edge deletion and contraction agree with matroid deletion and contraction. Graphic matroids are regular, and among regular matroids they are characterized by excluding the dual cycle matroids of K5 and K3,3.
knowledge_statements.conclusion_latex: M(G)\text{ is a regular matroid},\quad r_{M(G)}(F)=|V|-\kappa(V,F)

knowledge_statements.statement_title: Generalized Cycle with Prescribed Parts
knowledge_statements.scope_note: Defines a cyclic assembly of connected edge-bearing subgraphs through pairs of contact vertices.
knowledge_statements.statement_latex: For k\ge 2, a connected graph G is a generalized cycle with parts G_1,\ldots,G_k if: (i) every G_i is connected and E(G_i)\ne\varnothing, and when k=2 each G_i has at least three vertices; (ii) E(G_1),\ldots,E(G_k) partition E(G), and every G_i shares exactly two contact vertices with \bigcup_{j\ne i}G_j; and (iii) replacing every G_i by an edge joining its contact vertices produces a cycle.
knowledge_statements.statement_plain: A generalized cycle is a connected graph assembled from at least two connected, nonempty-edge parts. Their edge sets partition the graph, each part meets all the others in exactly two contact vertices, and contracting each part conceptually to an edge between its contacts yields a cycle. With two parts, each must have at least three vertices.
knowledge_statements.conclusion_latex: G\text{ is a generalized cycle with parts }G_1,\ldots,G_k\text{ exactly when conditions (i)--(iii) hold}

knowledge_statements.statement_title: Well-definedness and rank formula for matroid contraction
knowledge_statements.scope_note: States that contraction is independent of the chosen basis of the contracted subset and gives its rank.
knowledge_statements.statement_latex: Let M=(S,\mathcal I) have rank function r, let B\subseteq S, and construct M' on S\setminus B by choosing any basis J of B and setting \mathcal I'=\{J'\subseteq S\setminus B:J'\cup J\in\mathcal I\}. Then M' is a matroid independent of the choice of J, and its rank function satisfies r'(A)=r(A\cup B)-r(B) for every A\subseteq S\setminus B.
knowledge_statements.statement_plain: The contraction construction produces the same matroid regardless of which basis of the contracted subset is chosen. Its rank on A equals the original rank of A together with the contracted subset, minus the rank of that subset.
assumptions_latex: M=(S,\mathcal I)\text{ is a matroid with rank function }r
knowledge_statements.conclusion_latex: M'\text{ is a well-defined matroid and }r'(A)=r(A\cup B)-r(B)\quad\forall A\subseteq S\setminus B.

knowledge_statements.statement_title: Graph 2-Isomorphism and Its Cycle-Matroid Invariance
knowledge_statements.scope_note: Graphs are considered without isolated vertices. The statement defines vertex identification, vertex cleaving, Whitney twisting, and the equivalence relation they generate.
knowledge_statements.statement_latex: Vertex identification merges vertices belonging to distinct components. Vertex cleaving is its inverse and is possible only at a cut vertex or a vertex incident with a loop. If G is formed from disjoint G_1,G_2 by identifying u_1 with u_2 and v_1 with v_2, a Whitney twist instead identifies u_1 with v_2 and v_1 with u_2. Graphs G and H are 2-isomorphic when H can be transformed into a graph isomorphic to G by a sequence of these operations. This is an equivalence relation, and G\sim_2 H\Rightarrow M(G)\cong M(H).
knowledge_statements.statement_plain: Vertex identification merges vertices from distinct components; vertex cleaving reverses that operation and can occur only at a cut vertex or a loop-incident vertex. A Whitney twist interchanges the two pairings by which two disjoint graph pieces are joined at two vertices. Two graphs are 2-isomorphic when these operations transform one into a graph isomorphic to the other. This relation is an equivalence relation and preserves the cycle matroid.
assumptions_latex: G\text{ and }H\text{ have no isolated vertices}
knowledge_statements.conclusion_latex: G\sim_2 H\Longrightarrow M(G)\cong M(H)

knowledge_statements.statement_title: Vector, Representable, Graphic, and Uniform Matroids
knowledge_statements.scope_note: Introduces several standard matroid classes and notes that field representability is not universal.
knowledge_statements.statement_latex: For a matrix $A$ over a field $F$, the matroid whose independent sets are the linearly independent subsets of columns of $A$ is the vector matroid of $A$. A matroid is representable over $F$ if it is the vector matroid of some matrix over $F$, and some matroids are not representable over any field. For a graph $G$, the matroid whose independent edge sets are forests is its cycle matroid $\mathcal M(G)$; a matroid is graphic if it is the cycle matroid of some graph, possibly with loops. Matroids with independent sets $\{X\subseteq E:|X|\le k\}$ are uniform matroids.
knowledge_statements.statement_plain: Column independence defines a vector matroid, and a matroid is representable over a field when it has such a matrix representation. Not every matroid is representable over a field. Forest edge sets define the cycle matroid of a graph; graphic matroids are cycle matroids of graphs, including graphs with loops. Cardinality-bounded independence systems are uniform matroids.
assumptions_latex: A\text{ is a matrix over a field }F\text{ for the vector-matroid definition}
G\text{ is a graph, possibly with loops, for the graphic-matroid definition}
E\text{ is finite and }k\in\mathbb Z_{\ge0}\text{ for the uniform-matroid family}
knowledge_statements.conclusion_latex: \mathcal M\text{ is representable over }F\iff \mathcal M\text{ is the vector matroid of a matrix over }F;\quad \exists\mathcal M\ \forall F,\ \mathcal M\text{ is not representable over }F,\quad\text{with graphic and uniform matroids defined as stated.}

knowledge_statements.statement_title: Circuit Axioms for Matroids
knowledge_statements.scope_note: Necessary and sufficient conditions for a family of subsets to be the circuit family of a matroid.
knowledge_statements.statement_latex: A family $\mathcal C\subseteq 2^S$ is the set of circuits of a matroid on $S$ if and only if: (i) $\varnothing\notin\mathcal C$; (ii) for $C_1,C_2\in\mathcal C$, $C_1\subseteq C_2$ implies $C_1=C_2$; and (iii) for distinct $C_1,C_2\in\mathcal C$ and every $e\in C_1\cup C_2$, there exists $C\in\mathcal C$ such that $C\subseteq(C_1\cup C_2)\setminus\{e\}$.
knowledge_statements.statement_plain: A family is the circuit family of a matroid exactly when it excludes the empty set, has no circuit properly containing another, and satisfies the stated circuit-elimination condition for every element of the union of two distinct circuits.
knowledge_statements.conclusion_latex: \mathcal C\text{ is a matroid circuit family}\iff\text{conditions (i)--(iii) hold}

knowledge_statements.statement_title: Deletion of Elements from a Matroid
knowledge_statements.scope_note: Definition and basic closure property of matroid deletion, with graphic and linear specializations.
knowledge_statements.statement_latex: Let $M=(S,\mathcal I)$ be a matroid and $B\subseteq S$. Define $M\setminus B=(S\setminus B,\mathcal I')$, where $\mathcal I'=\{J\subseteq S\setminus B:J\in\mathcal I\}$. Then $M\setminus B$ is a matroid. knowledge_statements.conclusion_latex: M\setminus B=\left(S\setminus B,\{J\subseteq S\setminus B:J\in\mathcal I\}\right)\text{ is a matroid}

knowledge_statements.statement_latex: The cographic matroid of \(G\), also called its bond matroid, is \(M^*(G):=M(G)^*\). Thus \(B\subseteq E\) is a basis of \(M^*(G)\) exactly when \(E\setminus B\) is a maximal forest of \(G\). The circuits of \(M^*(G)\) are precisely the bonds: the inclusion-minimal nonempty edge cuts whose deletion increases \(c(G)\). Consequently, \(X\subseteq E\) is independent in \(M^*(G)\) exactly when \(X\) contains no bond of \(G\).
knowledge_statements.statement_plain: A cographic matroid is the dual of a graph's cycle matroid. Its circuits are the graph's inclusion-minimal nonempty edge cuts, called bonds.

knowledge_statements.statement_title: Cographic Matroids and Graph-Cut Structure
knowledge_statements.scope_note: Defines cographic matroids as dual cycle matroids and describes their bases, independent sets, circuits, rank, and planar duality.
knowledge_statements.statement_latex: For a graph \(G=(V,E)\), the cographic matroid is \(M^*(G)=M(G)^*\). Its bases are the complements of maximal forests; \(F\subseteq E\) is independent exactly when \((V,E\setminus F)\) has the same number of components as \(G\); and its circuits are the inclusionwise minimal nonempty cuts of \(G\). For every \(F\subseteq E\), \(r_{M^*(G)}(F)=|F|-\kappa(V,E\setminus F)+\kappa(V,E)\). If \(G\) is planar with planar dual \(G^*\), then \(M(G^*)\cong M^*(G)\). A matroid is both graphic and cographic if and only if it is isomorphic to the cycle matroid of a planar graph.
knowledge_statements.statement_plain: The cographic matroid of a graph is the dual of its cycle matroid. Its bases complement maximal forests, its circuits are minimal nonempty cuts, and its rank is determined by the component count after deleting selected edges. For a planar graph it is the cycle matroid of the planar dual. A matroid is both graphic and cographic exactly when it is the cycle matroid of a planar graph.
knowledge_statements.conclusion_latex: M^*(G)=M(G)^*,\quad r_{M^*(G)}(F)=|F|-\kappa(V,E\setminus F)+\kappa(V,E);\quad G\text{ planar}\Rightarrow M(G^*)\cong M^*(G)

knowledge_statements.statement_title: Bond Matroids, Cographic Matroids, and Bonds
knowledge_statements.scope_note: Defines the bond matroid and cographic class together with the underlying edge-cut terminology.
knowledge_statements.statement_latex: For a graph \(G\), the dual \(M^*(G)\) of its cycle matroid is called the bond matroid, or cocycle matroid, of \(G\). A matroid \(M\) is cographic if \(M\cong M^*(G)\) for some graph \(G\). For \(X\subseteq E(G)\), \(X\) is an edge cut if \(G\setminus X\) has more connected components than \(G\); an edge \(e\) is a cut-edge if \(\{e\}\) is an edge cut, and an inclusion-minimal edge cut is a bond or cocycle.
knowledge_statements.statement_plain: The dual of a graph's cycle matroid is its bond or cocycle matroid, and a matroid is cographic when it is isomorphic to such a dual. An edge cut is a set whose deletion increases the number of connected components; singleton edge cuts are cut-edges, and minimal edge cuts are bonds or cocycles.
knowledge_statements.conclusion_latex: M\text{ is cographic}\iff \exists G\;\bigl(M\cong M^*(G)\bigr),\qquad X\text{ is a bond}\iff X\text{ is an inclusion-minimal edge cut of }G.

knowledge_statements.statement_latex: Define \(\mathcal I_B=\{F\subseteq E:\text{every connected component of }(V,F)\text{ contains at most one cycle}\}\). Equivalently, \(F\in\mathcal I_B\) if and only if every nonempty subgraph \(H\) of \((V,F)\) satisfies \(|E(H)|\le |V(H)|\). The family \(\mathcal I_B\) is the independent-set family of a matroid on \(E\), called the bicircular matroid \(B(G)\). Its circuits are the inclusion-minimal edge sets inducing a connected subgraph with two cycles.

knowledge_statements.scope_note: Abstract finite-matroid definition using a framing basis.
knowledge_statements.statement_latex: The matroid \(M\) is a frame matroid if there exists a basis \(B\) of \(M\) such that, for every \(e\in E\), some subset \(X_e\subseteq B\) with \(|X_e|\le 2\) satisfies \(e\in\operatorname{cl}_M(X_e)\). Equivalently, after deleting loops, every element \(e\in E\setminus B\) has a fundamental circuit \(C(e,B)\) with \(|C(e,B)|\le 3\). Such a basis \(B\) is called a frame for \(M\).
knowledge_statements.statement_plain: A frame matroid has a basis such that every element is spanned by at most two basis elements; equivalently, each fundamental circuit has at most three elements.

children.title: Graphic–Cographic Duality
children.top_down_role: Dual relationship between cycle and bond matroids.

assumptions_latex: \(G\) is a finite connected plane graph and \(G^*\) is its geometric dual.
knowledge_statements.conclusion_latex: \(M(G)^*=M(G^*)\) under the natural edge correspondence.

notation.meaning: Cycle matroid of the plane graph

knowledge_statements.scope_note: Plane-graph form of graphic-cographic duality.

source_refs.locator: Section 13. Duality Theory p. 53

knowledge_statements.statement_latex: Identify each edge \(e\in E(G)\) with the dual edge \(e^*\in E(G^*)\). For every \(B\subseteq E(G)\), \(B\) is a spanning-tree edge set of \(G\) if and only if \(\{e^*:e\in E(G)\setminus B\}\) is a spanning-tree edge set of \(G^*\). Hence the bases of \(M(G)^*\) and \(M(G^*)\) coincide under this correspondence, so \(M(G)^*=M(G^*)\). Thus every planar graphic matroid has a graphic dual, represented by a plane dual graph.
knowledge_statements.statement_plain: For a connected plane graph, complements of spanning trees correspond to spanning trees of the geometric dual, so the dual cycle matroid is again graphic.

children.title: Graph-Derived Class Boundaries
children.top_down_role: Containment and separation among the principal graph-derived matroid classes.

assumptions_latex: \(G\) is the multigraph with two vertices joined by four parallel edges.
knowledge_statements.conclusion_latex: \(B(G)\cong U_{2,4}\), while \(U_{2,4}\) is neither graphic nor cographic.

notation.meaning: Bicircular matroid represented by the graph
Uniform rank-two matroid on four elements

knowledge_statements.scope_note: Concrete separation of bicircular matroids from graphic and cographic classes.
knowledge_statements.statement_latex: Every edge subset of \(G\) having at most two elements induces at most one cycle, whereas every three-edge subset induces two cycles. Therefore \(B(G)\cong U_{2,4}\). The matroid \(U_{2,4}\) is not representable over \(\mathbb F_2\), since a rank-two binary vector space has only three nonzero one-dimensional subspaces. Every graphic and every cographic matroid is binary. Consequently, \(B(G)\) is neither graphic nor cographic, so graph-derived matroid constructions do not define a single matroid class.
knowledge_statements.statement_plain: Four parallel edges yield the bicircular matroid U(2,4), which is nonbinary and therefore neither graphic nor cographic, separating these graph-derived classes.

knowledge_statements.statement_title: Deltoid matroids and their dual and minor characterizations
knowledge_statements.scope_note: Defines deltoids from bipartite graphs and records their self-duality and relationships to transversal matroids and strict gammoids.
knowledge_statements.statement_latex: Let $G=(V,E)$ be bipartite with color classes $U,W$, and let $M$ be the transversal matroid on $V$ induced by the family $(\{u\}\cup N(u):u\in U)$. A set $B\subseteq V$ is a base of $M$ if and only if $(U\setminus B)\cup(W\cap B)$ is matchable in $G$. Such an $M$ is called the deltoid induced by $(G,U,W)$. Its dual is the deltoid induced by $(G,W,U)$. Moreover, transversal matroids are exactly restrictions of deltoids, and strict gammoids are exactly contractions of deltoids.

Its bases have the stated matching characterization. Swapping the color classes gives the dual deltoid. Every transversal matroid is a restriction of a deltoid, and every strict gammoid is a contraction of one, with both converses holding.

knowledge_statements.statement_title: Affine-Simplex Characterization of Transversal Matroids
knowledge_statements.scope_note: Geometric characterization of loopless rank-$r$ transversal matroids.
knowledge_statements.statement_latex: For $r\geq1$, a loopless rank-$r$ matroid $M$ is transversal if and only if there are disjoint finite subsets $J,S\subseteq\mathbb R^{r-1}$ such that: (i) $|J|=r$ and the elements of $J$ form a simplex; (ii) $M$ is isomorphic to the affine matroid $N$ on $S$; and (iii) every $e\in S$ is freely added to a face $F_e$ of the simplex $J$ such that, for every flat $X$ of $N$ containing $e$, the closure of $X$ in the affine matroid on $S\cup J$ contains $F_e$.
knowledge_statements.statement_plain: A loopless rank-r matroid is transversal exactly when it admits the stated finite affine realization together with an r-element simplex, with each represented element freely added to a suitable face satisfying the specified closure condition for every flat containing it.
assumptions_latex: M\text{ is a loopless matroid of rank }r.
knowledge_statements.conclusion_latex: M\text{ is transversal if and only if there exist disjoint finite }J,S\subseteq\mathbb R^{r-1}\text{ satisfying conditions (i)--(iii).}

knowledge_statements.statement_title: Transversal Matroids and Their Rank Formula
knowledge_statements.scope_note: Defines transversal matroids from partial transversals and records their bases, rank formula, field representability, and principal subclasses.
knowledge_statements.statement_latex: Let \(\mathcal X=(X_1,\ldots,X_n)\) be a family of subsets of a finite set \(S\). The partial transversals of \(\mathcal X\) form the independent sets of a matroid on \(S\), called the transversal matroid induced by \(\mathcal X\). It has an inducing subfamily possessing a transversal, so its bases can be represented as full transversals. For every \(U\subseteq S\), \[r(U)=\min_{T\subseteq U}\left(|U\setminus T|+|\{i:X_i\cap T\ne\varnothing\}|\right)=\min_{I\subseteq\{1,\ldots,n\}}\left(n-|I|+\left|\bigcup_{i\in I}(X_i\cap U)\right|\right).\] Every transversal matroid is representable over all fields except possibly finitely many finite fields. Partition matroids and uniform matroids are special cases of transversal matroids; partition matroids are graphic and cographic.
knowledge_statements.statement_plain: Partial transversals of a finite family of sets form a transversal matroid. Its bases can be represented as full transversals of a suitable inducing subfamily, and its rank has two equivalent matching-deficiency minimum formulas. Each transversal matroid is representable over all but possibly finitely many finite fields. Partition and uniform matroids are transversal, and partition matroids are graphic and cographic.
assumptions_latex: \mathcal X=(X_1,\ldots,X_n)\text{ is a family of subsets of a finite set }S
knowledge_statements.conclusion_latex: (S,\{I\subseteq S:I\text{ is a partial transversal of }\mathcal X\})\text{ is a matroid with the stated rank formula}

knowledge_statements.statement_title: Transversals and partial transversals
knowledge_statements.scope_note: Defines transversals and partial transversals of a finite indexed set family and gives the equivalent bipartite-matching representation.
knowledge_statements.statement_latex: Let \(S\) be finite and let \(\mathcal A=(A_j:j\in J)\) be a finite indexed family of subsets of \(S\), with repetitions allowed. A transversal is a set \(T\subseteq S\) for which there exists a bijection \(\psi:J\to T\) satisfying \(\psi(j)\in A_j\) for every \(j\in J\). A subset \(X\subseteq S\) is a partial transversal if, for some \(K\subseteq J\), it is a transversal of \((A_j:j\in K)\). Define the bipartite graph \(\Delta[\mathcal A]\) with vertex classes \(S\) and \(J\), where \(xj\) is an edge exactly when \(x\in A_j\). Then \(X\) is a partial transversal if and only if \(\Delta[\mathcal A]\) has a matching that saturates \(X\).
knowledge_statements.statement_plain: A transversal chooses a distinct representative from every member of an indexed set family. A partial transversal does so for some subfamily. Equivalently, a subset is a partial transversal exactly when it can be matched injectively to family indices in the associated incidence bipartite graph.
knowledge_statements.conclusion_latex: X\text{ is a partial transversal of }\mathcal A\iff\Delta[\mathcal A]\text{ has a matching saturating }X.

knowledge_statements.statement_title: Transversal matroids and deltoids
knowledge_statements.scope_note: Bipartite-matching and set-system presentations of transversal matroids, their rank, and the associated deltoid construction.
knowledge_statements.statement_latex: For a bipartite graph \(G=(S,T;E)\), the subsets \(I\subseteq S\) coverable by a matching are the independent sets of a transversal matroid, with \(r(S')=\min_{X\subseteq S'}\{|S'\setminus X|+|\Gamma(X)|\}\). Equivalently, its independent sets are subtransversals of a family \(\{A_1,\ldots,A_t\}\), or systems of distinct representatives viewed on the hyperedge ground set. The circuit matroid of \(K_4\) is not transversal, while every rank-\(r\) transversal matroid has a bipartite presentation whose opposite vertex class has size \(r\). For the same bipartite graph, the \(|S|\)-element symmetric differences of \(S\) with matching-covered vertex sets form the bases of the deltoid of base \(S\); the deltoids of bases \(S\) and \(T\) are dual, the transversal matroid on \(S\) is a restriction of the deltoid of base \(T\), and every deltoid of base \(S\) is transversal via \(\{\Gamma_G(s)\cup\{s\}:s\in S\}\).
knowledge_statements.statement_plain: In a bipartite graph, the subsets of one side that can be covered by a matching form a transversal matroid. Its rank is the minimum of the uncovered-element count plus the neighborhood size. Equivalent descriptions use subtransversals or systems of distinct representatives. The circuit matroid of K4 is not transversal, and every rank-r transversal matroid has a presentation with r vertices on the opposite side. Matching-covered vertex sets also define deltoids; the two base-side constructions are dual, transversal matroids occur as restrictions of deltoids, and deltoids are themselves transversal matroids.
knowledge_statements.conclusion_latex: \mathcal I=\{I\subseteq S:I\text{ is covered by a matching}\}\text{ defines a transversal matroid, with the stated equivalent representations, rank formula, boundary, and deltoid relations.}

knowledge_statements.statement_title: Transversal matroids and their presentations
knowledge_statements.scope_note: Defines the matroid presented by a set family and records the stated uniform-matroid and large-field representability properties.
knowledge_statements.statement_latex: For a finite family \(\mathcal A\) of subsets of a finite set \(S\), let \(M[\mathcal A]\) denote the matroid on \(S\) whose independent sets are the partial transversals of \(\mathcal A\). A matroid \(M\) is a transversal matroid if \(M\cong M[\mathcal A]\) for some such family \(\mathcal A\); in that case, \(\mathcal A\) is a presentation of \(M\). Every uniform matroid is transversal, and every transversal matroid is representable over every sufficiently large field.

A matroid is transversal if it is isomorphic to M[A] for some A, which is then called a presentation. Uniform matroids are transversal, and transversal matroids are representable over all sufficiently large fields.

knowledge_statements.statement_title: Equivalence of matroid base and rank axioms
knowledge_statements.scope_note: Makes the referenced base-exchange and rank axioms explicit.
knowledge_statements.statement_latex: For a finite set V, nonempty families \mathcal B\subseteq2^V satisfying simultaneous exchange are in one-to-one correspondence with functions \rho:2^V\to\mathbb Z satisfying 0\leq\rho(X)\leq|X|, monotonicity, and submodularity. knowledge_statements.statement_title: Gammoids, strict gammoids, and the linkage rank formula
knowledge_statements.scope_note: Defines gammoids by vertex-disjoint directed linkage and records their strict representation, bases, and rank formula.
knowledge_statements.statement_latex: Let $D=(V,A)$ be a directed graph and let $U,S\subseteq V$. Sets $X,Y\subseteq V$ are linked if $|X|=|Y|$ and there are $|X|$ pairwise vertex-disjoint directed paths with initial-vertex set $X$ and terminal-vertex set $Y$. Set $\mathcal I=\{I\subseteq S:\text{some }U'\subseteq U\text{ is linked to }I\}$. Then $M=(S,\mathcal I)$ is a matroid, called a gammoid. If $S=V$, it is a strict gammoid. Gammoids are exactly restrictions of strict gammoids. In the strict gammoid induced by $(D,U)$, the bases are precisely the sets $B\subseteq V$ such that $U$ is linked to $B$. For every $X\subseteq S$, $$r_M(X)=\min\{|Y|:Y\subseteq V\text{ intersects every directed }U\text{-}X\text{ path}\}.$$
knowledge_statements.statement_plain: Vertex sets linkable from subsets of U by pairwise vertex-disjoint directed paths form the independent sets of a gammoid. Strict gammoids use the whole vertex set as ground set, and every gammoid is a restriction of one. Strict-gammoid bases are exactly the sets linked from U, while rank is the minimum size of a vertex set meeting every U-to-X path.
knowledge_statements.conclusion_latex: M=(S,\mathcal I)\text{ is a gammoid; gammoids are exactly restrictions of strict gammoids, with the stated base and rank characterizations.}

assumptions_latex: \(D\) has four source vertices \(S=\{s_1,s_2,s_3,s_4\}\), two targets \(T=\{t_1,t_2\}\), and every arc \(s_i t_j\).

notation.meaning: Uniform rank-two matroid on four elements

knowledge_statements.scope_note: Concrete boundary showing that gammoid status does not imply binary representability.
knowledge_statements.statement_latex: A subset \(I\subseteq S\) links to \(T\) exactly when \(|I|\le 2\), because each source reaches either target directly and the paths must have distinct endpoints. Thus \(L(D,T)|S\cong U_{2,4}\). If \(U_{2,4}\) had a rank-two representation over \(\mathbb F_2\), its four nonparallel elements would require four distinct one-dimensional subspaces of \(\mathbb F_2^2\), but only three exist. Hence this gammoid is not binary. Directed-linkage representability therefore does not imply representability over every field.
knowledge_statements.statement_plain: A complete four-source, two-target linkage presentation gives U(2,4), a gammoid that is not binary, so gammoid representation does not ensure every-field linear representability.

knowledge_statements.statement_title: Nonrepresentability and structural properties of AG(3,2)'
knowledge_statements.scope_note: Catalog characterization of the unique relaxation of the binary affine cube.
knowledge_statements.statement_latex: The matroid AG(3,2)' has as its 4-point planes the six cube faces, the six diagonal planes (including \{1,2,7,8\}), and the single twisted plane \{1,8,3,6\}. It is the unique relaxation of AG(3,2) and is a tipless 4-spike. It is a smallest nonrepresentable matroid, but for no field \mathbb F is it a minimal excluded minor for \mathbb F-representability. It is neither graphic, cographic, regular, near-regular, transversal, a strict gammoid, nor a gammoid. It is self-dual but not identically self-dual, and its automorphism group is not transitive. Every single-element deletion is isomorphic to F_7^* or (F_7^-)^*, and every single-element contraction is isomorphic to F_7 or F_7^-. It is nonalgebraic.
knowledge_statements.statement_plain: AG(3,2)' has the specified six face planes, six diagonal planes, and one twisted plane. It is the unique relaxation of AG(3,2), a tipless 4-spike, and a smallest nonrepresentable matroid, although it is not a minimal excluded minor for representability over any field. It is not graphic, cographic, regular, near-regular, transversal, a strict gammoid, or a gammoid. It is self-dual but not identically so, has a nontransitive automorphism group, has only the stated Fano and non-Fano deletion and contraction types, and is nonalgebraic.
knowledge_statements.conclusion_latex: M\text{ has the stated relaxation, minimal nonrepresentability, class-exclusion, duality, minor, and nonalgebraicity properties.}

knowledge_statements.statement_title: Equivalence and projective equivalence of matroid matrix representations
knowledge_statements.scope_note: Defines equivalence notions for labeled matrix representations over a fixed field.
knowledge_statements.statement_latex: Let M have rank r\ge 1 on E=\{e_1,\ldots,e_n\}. For i\in\{1,2\}, let A_i be a nonzero matrix over \mathbb F with n columns labeled by E, and suppose the identity on E is an isomorphism M\cong M[A_i]. The representations A_1 and A_2 are equivalent if A_2 is obtainable from A_1 using row interchange, nonzero row scaling, row addition, adjoining or removing a zero row, interchange of labeled columns, nonzero column scaling, and entrywise application of a field automorphism. They are projectively equivalent if such a sequence exists without a field-automorphism operation; otherwise they are projectively inequivalent.
knowledge_statements.statement_plain: Two labeled matrices representing the same positive-rank matroid are equivalent when connected by the seven listed operations. They are projectively equivalent when no field automorphism is used.
assumptions_latex: M\cong M[A_i]\text{ via the identity on }E\quad(i=1,2)
A_1,A_2\text{ are nonzero matrices over }\mathbb F\text{ with columns labeled by }E
knowledge_statements.conclusion_latex: A_1\sim A_2\iff A_2\text{ is obtainable from }A_1\text{ by operations 6.3.1--6.3.7},\qquad A_1\sim_{\mathrm{proj}}A_2\iff\text{such a sequence uses no field automorphism}.

knowledge_statements.statement_title: Sharp size bounds for three partial-field matroid classes
knowledge_statements.scope_note: Applies to simple rank-r matroids and characterizes every equality case.
knowledge_statements.statement_latex: Let \(M\) be a simple rank-\(r\) matroid. If \(M\) is dyadic, then \(|E(M)|\le r^2\), with equality iff \(M\cong Q_r(GF(3)^\times)\). If \(M\) is a \(\sqrt[6]{1}\)-matroid, then \(|E(M)|\le\binom{r+2}{2}-2\) for \(r\ne3\) and \(|E(M)|\le9\) for \(r=3\); equality holds iff \(M\cong T_r\) when \(r\ne3\), or \(M\cong AG(2,3)\) when \(r=3\). If \(M\) is near-regular, then \(|E(M)|\le\binom{r+2}{2}-2\), with equality iff \(M\cong T_r\).
knowledge_statements.statement_plain: A simple rank-r dyadic matroid has at most r squared elements, with equality exactly for the ternary Dowling geometry. A simple sixth-root-of-unity matroid has at most binomial(r+2,2)−2 elements except in rank three, where the bound is nine; equality occurs exactly for T_r outside rank three and AG(2,3) in rank three. A simple near-regular matroid has the same binomial bound, with equality exactly for T_r.
assumptions_latex: M\text{ is a simple rank-}r\text{ matroid}
knowledge_statements.conclusion_latex: \begin{aligned}&M\text{ dyadic}\Rightarrow |E(M)|\le r^2,\text{ equality iff }M\cong Q_r(GF(3)^\times);\\&M\text{ a }\sqrt[6]{1}\text{-matroid}\Rightarrow |E(M)|\le\begin{cases}\binom{r+2}{2}-2,&r\ne3,\\9,&r=3,\end{cases}\text{ with the stated equality cases};\\&M\text{ near-regular}\Rightarrow |E(M)|\le\binom{r+2}{2}-2,\text{ equality iff }M\cong T_r.\end{aligned}

knowledge_statements.statement_title: Pivoting on a nonzero matrix entry
knowledge_statements.scope_note: General matrix row operation defining a pivot, independent of a particular combinatorial model.
knowledge_statements.statement_latex: Let \(X=(x_{ij})\in\mathbb F^{m\times n}\) and let \(x_{st}\ne0\). A pivot on \(x_{st}\) first replaces each row \(i\ne s\) by \(\operatorname{row}_i-(x_{it}/x_{st})\operatorname{row}_s\), and then replaces row \(s\) by \((1/x_{st})\operatorname{row}_s\). The resulting \(t\)-th column is the standard basis vector \(e_s\), and the pivot entry equals \(1\).
knowledge_statements.statement_plain: To pivot on a nonzero entry x_st, eliminate every other entry in column t using row s and then scale row s by 1/x_st. This transforms column t into the s-th standard basis vector and makes the pivot entry one.
knowledge_statements.conclusion_latex: X'_{\cdot t}=e_s\quad\text{and}\quad x'_{st}=1.

knowledge_statements.statement_title: Fundamental-Circuit Incidence Matrix and Partial Representation
knowledge_statements.scope_note: Defines the support matrix associated with a standard matroid representation and chosen basis.
knowledge_statements.statement_latex: Let M be a rank-r matroid with r\ge 1, represented over a field by [I_r\mid D], with columns labelled e_1,\ldots,e_n, and let B=\{e_1,\ldots,e_r\}. knowledge_statements.statement_title: Pivot Closure of Signed Binary-Matroid Representations
knowledge_statements.scope_note: Preservation of signed entries and agreement between field and real pivot computations.
knowledge_statements.statement_latex: Let \(D_1=[d_{ij}]\) have entries in \(\{0,1,-1\}\), and suppose \([I_r\mid D_1]\) is an \(\mathbb F\)-representation of a binary matroid \(M\), where \(\operatorname{char}(\mathbb F)\ne2\). If \([I_r\mid D_2]\) is obtained by pivoting on a nonzero entry \(d_{st}\) of \(D_1\), then every entry of \(D_2\) lies in \(\{0,1,-1\}\). Moreover, the same matrix \([I_r\mid D_2]\) is obtained by viewing \([I_r\mid D_1]\) as a real \((0,\pm1)\)-matrix and performing the pivot over \(\mathbb R\).
knowledge_statements.statement_plain: Pivoting on a nonzero entry of a signed representation of a binary matroid over a field of characteristic other than two preserves signed entries, and the result agrees with the corresponding real pivot.
assumptions_latex: \([I_r\mid D_1]\) is an \(\mathbb F\)-representation of a binary matroid \(M\).
knowledge_statements.conclusion_latex: D_2\in\{0,1,-1\}^{r\times m}\quad\text{and the pivot over }\mathbb F\text{ agrees with the pivot over }\mathbb R.

knowledge_statements.statement_title: Matrix representations of matroids
knowledge_statements.scope_note: Column-independence representations, induced rank functions, and closure of fixed-field representability under duals and minors.
knowledge_statements.statement_latex: Let \(A\in\mathbb F^{m\times n}\), let \(S=\{1,\ldots,n\}\), and define \(\mathcal I=\{I\subseteq S:\operatorname{rank}(A_I)=|I|\}\). Then \((S,\mathcal I)\) is a matroid represented by the columns of \(A\), and \(r_M(U)=\operatorname{rank}(A_U)\) for every \(U\subseteq S\). A matroid is representable over \(\mathbb F\) when it is isomorphic to one obtained this way. If \(M\) is representable over \(\mathbb F\), then \(M^*\) and every minor of \(M\) are also representable over \(\mathbb F\). Not every matroid is representable over a field.
knowledge_statements.statement_plain: The linearly independent column subsets of a matrix form a matroid, and the rank of each subset equals the rank of its corresponding submatrix. This defines representability over a field. Representability over a fixed field is preserved by duality and minors, but nonrepresentable matroids exist.
knowledge_statements.conclusion_latex: \left(S,\{I\subseteq S:\operatorname{rank}(A_I)=|I|\}\right)\text{ is a matroid},\qquad r_M(U)=\operatorname{rank}(A_U),\qquad M\text{ representable over }\mathbb F\Rightarrow M^*\text{ and every minor of }M\text{ are representable over }\mathbb F.

knowledge_statements.statement_title: Rational and Affine Representation of the Non-Fano Matroid
knowledge_statements.scope_note: Construction of the non-Fano matroid by interpreting the Fano array over the rationals.
knowledge_statements.statement_latex: The non-Fano matroid is obtained by interpreting the entries of the \(\operatorname{GF}(2)\) representation of the Fano matroid over \(\mathbf Q\). This representation is projectively equivalent over \(\mathbf Q\) to \[F_- = \begin{pmatrix}1&0&0&0&1/2&1/2&1/3\\0&1&0&1/2&0&1/2&1/3\\1&1&1&1&1&1&1\end{pmatrix}.\] If \(F_-'\) is obtained by deleting the final all-ones row, then the linear dependencies among the columns of \(F_-\) are exactly the affine dependencies among the corresponding columns of \(F_-'\). Thus the independent sets are the affinely independent point sets; in the plane, independent pairs are distinct and independent triples are noncollinear.
knowledge_statements.statement_plain: The non-Fano matroid is obtained by reading the Fano representation over the rational numbers. It is projectively equivalent to the stated rational matrix. Deleting its final row of ones gives planar points whose affine dependencies correspond exactly to the linear dependencies of the original columns.
assumptions_latex: F_-'\text{ is obtained from }F_-\text{ by deleting its final all-ones row}
knowledge_statements.conclusion_latex: X\text{ is linearly dependent in }F_-\iff X\text{ is affinely dependent in }F_-';\qquad \mathcal I=\{X:X\text{ is affinely independent in }F_- '\}.

knowledge_statements.statement_title: Basis for planar rigid motions
knowledge_statements.scope_note: For a framework whose vertices are points of the plane.
knowledge_statements.statement_latex: Every planar framework has a three-dimensional space of trivial infinitesimal motions induced by rigid motions of \(\mathbb{R}^2\). For each vertex \(v=(v_1,v_2)\), a basis is given by the velocity assignments \(m^v=(1,0)^\top\), \(m^v=(0,1)^\top\), and \(m^v=(v_2,-v_1)^\top\), representing horizontal translation, vertical translation, and clockwise rotation about the origin, respectively.
knowledge_statements.statement_plain: The trivial infinitesimal motions of a planar framework form a three-dimensional space. Horizontal translation, vertical translation, and clockwise rotation about the origin give a basis, with vertex velocities (1,0), (0,1), and (v2,-v1), respectively.
knowledge_statements.conclusion_latex: \dim \mathcal{T}=3,\qquad \mathcal{T}=\operatorname{span}\{(m^v)_v:m^v=(1,0)^\top,\ (0,1)^\top,\ (v_2,-v_1)^\top\}.

knowledge_statements.statement_title: Equivalent forms of an invertible row transformation
knowledge_statements.scope_note: Characterizes elementary row equivalence algebraically and by a common linear action on columns.
knowledge_statements.statement_latex: For r\times n matrices A,A' over a field \mathbb F, the following are equivalent: (i) A' is obtained from A by elementary row operations; (ii) A'=XA for some nonsingular r\times r matrix X; (iii) there exists a nonsingular linear transformation \tau:V(r,\mathbb F)\to V(r,\mathbb F) such that the ith column of A' is \tau applied to the ith column of A for every i\in\{1,\ldots,n\}.
knowledge_statements.statement_plain: Elementary row operations, left multiplication by an invertible matrix, and applying one invertible linear transformation to every column describe the same transformation.
knowledge_statements.conclusion_latex: \text{(i)}\iff\text{(ii)}\iff\text{(iii)}.

knowledge_statements.statement_title: Standard representative matrices of a vector matroid
knowledge_statements.scope_note: Representation-preserving matrix operations and standard forms relative to a chosen basis.
knowledge_statements.statement_latex: Let \(A\in\mathbb F^{m\times n}\) have labelled columns and let \(M=M[A]\). The matroid is unchanged by elementary row operations, adjoining or deleting a zero row, permuting columns together with their labels, multiplying a column by a nonzero field element, or applying one automorphism of \(\mathbb F\) entrywise. If \(A\ne0\), operations of the first four kinds, including labelled column permutations, can put the representation in the form \([I_r\mid D]\), where \(r=r(M)\). The identity-column labels form a basis \(B\); \([I_r\mid D]\) is a standard representative matrix with respect to \(B\), and the correspondingly labelled \(D\) is a reduced standard representative matrix.
knowledge_statements.statement_plain: The listed row, zero-row, labelled-column, scaling, and field-automorphism operations preserve a vector matroid. A nonzero representation can be put in standard form [I_r | D], where r is the matroid rank and the identity-column labels form a basis; D is the associated reduced standard representative.
knowledge_statements.conclusion_latex: M[A]\text{ is invariant under the listed operations, and }M=M[I_r\mid D]\text{ with }r=r(M)\text{ and the identity-column labels forming a basis.}

children.title: Projective Equivalence
children.top_down_role: Equivalence of matrix presentations under projective transformations.

assumptions_latex: \(\mathbb F\) is a field and \(E\) is a finite labeled set.
\(A,B\in\mathbb F^{r\times E}\) have full row rank and represent matroids on \(E\).
knowledge_statements.conclusion_latex: \(A\sim_{\mathrm{proj}}B\iff (\exists P\in\operatorname{GL}_r(\mathbb F))(\exists D\in\mathbb F^{E\times E}\text{ invertible diagonal})\;B=PAD\).

notation.meaning: projective equivalence over the fixed field with labeled columns
group of invertible rank-by-rank matrices over the field

knowledge_statements.statement_latex: Let \(A\) and \(B\) be full-row-rank matrices over \(\mathbb F\), with columns indexed by the same labeled set \(E\). They are projectively equivalent if there exist an invertible matrix \(P\in\operatorname{GL}_r(\mathbb F)\) and an invertible diagonal matrix \(D\in\mathbb F^{E\times E}\) such that \(B=PAD\). Thus projective equivalence permits elementary changes of coordinates in the ambient vector space and independent nonzero rescaling of columns, while preserving column labels. Projectively equivalent matrices represent the same matroid on \(E\).
knowledge_statements.statement_plain: Two labeled matrix representations are projectively equivalent when one is obtained from the other by invertible row operations and independent nonzero column scalings.

knowledge_statements.statement_title: Minimal Representations and Projective Equivalence
knowledge_statements.scope_note: Minimality and projective comparison of matrix representations of linear matroids.
knowledge_statements.statement_latex: A representation of a linear matroid is minimal if its rows are linearly independent. For full-row-rank matrices \(A,A'\in K^{r\times n}\), projective equivalence means that there exist \(B\in\operatorname{GL}_r(K)\) and a nonsingular diagonal matrix \(D\in K^{n\times n}\) such that \(A'=BAD\). This is an equivalence relation. Projectively equivalent matrices represent the same matroid, but matrices representing the same matroid need not be projectively equivalent.
knowledge_statements.statement_plain: A representation is minimal when its rows are linearly independent. Two full-row-rank matrices over the same field are projectively equivalent if one is obtained from the other by an invertible row transformation and nonzero column scalings. Projective equivalence preserves the represented matroid, but the converse fails in general.
knowledge_statements.conclusion_latex: A\sim_{\mathrm{proj}}A'\implies M(A)=M(A'),\qquad M(A)=M(A')\centernot\implies A\sim_{\mathrm{proj}}A'\text{ in general.}

Projective equivalence restricts to an equivalence relation on this set. Its equivalence classes are \([A]_{\mathrm{proj}}=\{PAD:P\in\operatorname{GL}_r(\mathbb F),\ D\text{ invertible diagonal}\}\), intersected with \(\operatorname{Rep}_{\mathbb F}(M)\). The representation-equivalence space is the quotient \(\operatorname{Rep}_{\mathbb F}(M)/{\sim_{\mathrm{proj}}}\).

knowledge_statements.statement_latex: A matroid \(M\) on a fixed labeled ground set \(E\) is uniquely representable over \(\mathbb F\) if it is \(\mathbb F\)-representable and any two full-row-rank \(\mathbb F\)-matrices \(A\) and \(B\) representing \(M\) are projectively equivalent. Equivalently, for every such pair there are \(P\in\operatorname{GL}_{r(M)}(\mathbb F)\) and an invertible diagonal matrix \(D\in\mathbb F^{E\times E}\) satisfying \(B=PAD\). Hence unique representability is exactly the condition that \(\operatorname{Rep}_{\mathbb F}(M)/{\sim_{\mathrm{proj}}}\) has one element.
knowledge_statements.statement_plain: A matroid is uniquely representable over a fixed field when all its labeled representations belong to one projective-equivalence class.

Choose a matrix \(B\in\mathbb F^{(|E|-r)\times E}\) whose rows form a basis of \(\ker A\), so \(AB^{\mathsf T}=0\). Then the column matroid of \(B\) is the dual matroid \(M^*\). knowledge_statements.statement_title: Representations and structural properties of AG(3,2)
knowledge_statements.scope_note: Extraction-grounded catalog characterization of the binary affine cube.
knowledge_statements.statement_latex: The matroid AG(3,2) has as its 4-point planes the six cube faces, six diagonal planes, and the two twisted planes \{1,8,3,6\} and \{2,7,4,5\}. It is the binary affine cube, isomorphic to the unique S(3,4,8), the unique tipless binary 4-spike, and F_7\oplus_3F_7. It is representable over a field \mathbb F if and only if \operatorname{char}(\mathbb F)=2, and over GF(2) it is represented by [I_4\mid J_4-I_4]. It is not graphic, cographic, regular, transversal, a strict gammoid, or a gammoid. It is identically self-dual; its automorphism group is 3-transitive on points and transitive on hyperplanes; and its circuits and hyperplanes coincide, each having four elements. For every element e, AG(3,2)\setminus e\cong F_7^* and AG(3,2)/e\cong F_7. Together with S_8 it comprises the 8-element 3-connected binary nonregular matroids. It is the unique splitter for binary paving matroids, is the complement of F_7 in PG(3,2), and is algebraic over \mathbb F if and only if \operatorname{char}(\mathbb F)=2.
knowledge_statements.statement_plain: AG(3,2) is the binary affine cube, with six face planes, six diagonal planes, and two twisted planes. It has the stated isomorphisms, is linearly representable and algebraic exactly in characteristic two, and has binary representation [I4 | J4−I4]. It has the stated class exclusions, self-duality, automorphisms, circuit-hyperplane structure, single-element minors, uniqueness properties, and projective-complement description.
knowledge_statements.conclusion_latex: M\text{ has the representation, exclusion, duality, automorphism, circuit-hyperplane, minor, and uniqueness properties stated above.}

knowledge_statements.statement_latex: For X\subseteq E(M), write M.X=M/(E(M)-X); analogously, for X\subseteq E(G), write G.X=G/(E(G)-X). If C^* is a cocircuit of M, a bridge of C^* is the ground set of a component of M\setminus C^*. Distinct bridges Y_1,Y_2 overlap if there do not exist parallel classes Z_i of M.(C^*\cup Y_i), i=1,2, such that C^*\subseteq Z_1\cup Z_2.
knowledge_statements.statement_plain: The restriction-like notation M.X denotes contraction of every element outside X, with the analogous notation for graphs. A bridge of a cocircuit is the ground set of a component left after deleting that cocircuit. Two distinct bridges overlap when no choice of one parallel class from each associated contraction covers the cocircuit.
assumptions_latex: Y_1,Y_2\text{ are distinct component ground sets of }M\setminus C^*
knowledge_statements.conclusion_latex: Y\text{ is a bridge of }C^*\iff Y=E(K)\text{ for a component }K\text{ of }M\setminus C^*;\quad Y_1,Y_2\text{ overlap}\iff\nexists Z_i\text{ parallel in }M.(C^*\cup Y_i)\text{ with }C^*\subseteq Z_1\cup Z_2.

knowledge_statements.statement_title: GF(4)-Flows and Circuit Decomposition
knowledge_statements.scope_note: Definition of GF(4)-flows and nowhere-zero flows on a binary matroid, together with their circuit-vector representation.
knowledge_statements.statement_latex: Let \(M=(E,\mathcal I)\) be a binary matroid. A flow over \(\mathrm{GF}(4)\) is a function \(f:E\to\mathrm{GF}(4)\) satisfying \(f(D)=0\) for every cocircuit \(D\) of \(M\). It is nowhere-zero if \(f(e)\ne0\) for every \(e\in E\). Every flow over \(\mathrm{GF}(4)\) is a sum of vectors \(\alpha\chi^C\), where \(\alpha\in\mathrm{GF}(4)\) and \(C\) is a circuit of \(M\).
knowledge_statements.statement_plain: A GF(4)-flow on a binary matroid vanishes on every cocircuit and is nowhere-zero when every element receives a nonzero value. Every such flow is a sum of scalar multiples of circuit incidence vectors.
assumptions_latex: M=(E,\mathcal I)\text{ is a binary matroid}
knowledge_statements.conclusion_latex: f=\sum_i\alpha_i\chi^{C_i}\quad(\alpha_i\in\mathrm{GF}(4),\ C_i\text{ circuits}),\qquad f\text{ is nowhere-zero}\iff \forall e\in E,\ f(e)\ne0
