knowledge_statements.scope_note: The extract does not require $e$ and $f$ to be distinct.

knowledge_statements.statement_title: Uniqueness of Representation Signs from a Cycle Basis
knowledge_statements.scope_note: Normalization of a binary-matroid representation using a basis of the cycle matroid of its support graph.
knowledge_statements.statement_latex: Let \(\mathbb F\) be a field, and let \([I_r\mid D]\) be an \(\mathbb F\)-representation of a binary matroid \(M\). knowledge_statements.conclusion_latex: \text{Every other nonzero entry of }D\text{ is uniquely determined and lies in }\{1,-1\}.

knowledge_statements.statement_title: Circuit and excluded-minor characterizations of binary matroids
knowledge_statements.scope_note: Equivalent circuit behavior and the unique minor-minimal obstruction to binary representability.
knowledge_statements.statement_latex: A matroid \(M\) is binary when it is representable over \(\operatorname{GF}(2)\). Moreover, \(M\) is binary if and only if, for every finite family of circuits \(C_1,\ldots,C_t\), the symmetric difference \(C_1\triangle\cdots\triangle C_t\) can be partitioned into circuits. The unique minor-minimal nonbinary matroid is the uniform matroid \(U_4^2\).
knowledge_statements.statement_plain: A binary matroid is one representable over GF(2). Equivalently, every finite symmetric difference of its circuits can be partitioned into circuits. The uniform matroid U4^2 is the unique minor-minimal nonbinary matroid.

knowledge_statements.statement_title: Representation and structural properties of T12
knowledge_statements.scope_note: Extraction-grounded summary of the representations and principal classification properties of T12.
knowledge_statements.statement_latex: The matroid $T_{12}$ is representable over a field $\mathbb F$ if and only if $\operatorname{char}(\mathbb F)=2$. It has a binary representation whose columns are the incidence vectors of the $5$-cycles of the Petersen graph. It is self-dual but not identically self-dual; it is neither graphic, cographic, regular, near-regular, transversal, a strict gammoid, nor a gammoid; and it has exactly two disjoint circuit-hyperplanes. Its automorphism group is transitive but not doubly transitive. Every $3$-connected binary matroid with an $M(K_5)$-minor has an $M(K_{3,3})$- or $M^*(K_{3,3})$-minor, or is isomorphic to $M(K_5)$, $T_{12}$, or $T_{12}/e$. Moreover, $T_{12}$ is algebraic over $\mathbb F$ if and only if $\operatorname{char}(\mathbb F)=2$.
knowledge_statements.statement_plain: T12 is representable and algebraic exactly over fields of characteristic two. It has a Petersen-graph binary representation, is self-dual but not identically self-dual, lies outside the listed graphic, regular, transversal, and gammoid classes, has two disjoint circuit-hyperplanes, and has a transitive but not doubly transitive automorphism group. It is also an exceptional outcome in the stated minor theorem.
assumptions_latex: T_{12}\text{ denotes the matroid specified in the extract.}
knowledge_statements.conclusion_latex: T_{12}\text{ has the stated representability, duality, class-membership, circuit-hyperplane, automorphism, and minor-theoretic properties.}

knowledge_statements.statement_title: Representation and structural properties of S8
knowledge_statements.scope_note: Extraction-grounded catalog characterization of the eight-element binary matroid S8.
knowledge_statements.statement_latex: The displayed matrix [I_4\mid A], where the rows of A are (0,1,1,1),(1,0,1,1),(1,1,0,1),(1,1,1,1), represents S_8 over GF(2). The matroid S_8 is the unique deletion of a non-tip element from the binary 4-spike and is representable over \mathbb F if and only if \operatorname{char}(\mathbb F)=2. It is not graphic, cographic, regular, near-regular, transversal, a strict gammoid, or a gammoid. It is self-dual but not identically self-dual, and its automorphism group is not transitive. There is a unique x such that S_8\setminus x\cong F_7^* and a unique y such that S_8/y\cong F_7, with x\ne y. The 3-connected binary single-element coextensions of F_7 are S_8 and AG(3,2). The set \{U_{2,4},F_7,F_7^*,S_8\} is 2-rounded. Moreover, S_8 is the complement of M(K_4)\oplus U_{1,1} in PG(3,2), and it is algebraic over \mathbb F if and only if \operatorname{char}(\mathbb F)=2.
knowledge_statements.statement_plain: The displayed GF(2) matrix represents S8. It is the unique non-tip deletion from the binary 4-spike and is linearly representable and algebraic exactly in characteristic two. It has the stated class exclusions, self-duality, automorphism behavior, distinguished deletion and contraction, coextension characterization, 2-roundedness property, and projective-complement description.
knowledge_statements.conclusion_latex: M\text{ has the stated binary representation, field criterion, exclusions, duality, minor, coextension, roundedness, and complement properties.}

knowledge_statements.statement_title: Triangular and triadic Möbius matroids
knowledge_statements.scope_note: Defines the two binary-matroid families and records their sizes, triangle property, and deletion-duality representations.
knowledge_statements.statement_latex: \text{Let }r\in\mathbb Z\text{ with }r>2.\text{ Form the parallel connection with common basepoint }z\text{ of the }r-1\text{ lines }\{z,a_i,b_i\}.\text{ In }PG(r-1,2),\text{ adjoin the specified third points }c_1,\ldots,c_{r-1}.\text{ Denote the resulting rank-}r\text{ triangular Möbius matroid by }T_r;\ |E(T_r)|=3r-2.\text{ If }r\text{ is even, deleting }a_1,b_2,a_3,b_4,\ldots,a_{r-1}\text{ from }T_r\text{ gives the rank-}r\text{ triadic Möbius matroid }D_r;\ |E(D_r)|=2r-1\text{ and }D_r\text{ has no triangles. Deleting }z\text{ and dualizing gives the cycle matroids of the cubic and quartic Möbius ladders with }2r-2\text{ and }r-1\text{ vertices, respectively.}
knowledge_statements.statement_plain: For integer rank r greater than two, the specified construction in PG(r−1,2) produces the rank-r triangular Möbius matroid with 3r−2 elements. For even r, deleting the alternating listed elements produces the rank-r triadic Möbius matroid with 2r−1 elements and no triangles. After deleting z and dualizing, the two families give cycle matroids of cubic and quartic Möbius ladders, respectively.
knowledge_statements.conclusion_latex: |E(T_r)|=3r-2,\quad |E(D_r)|=2r-1,\quad D_r\text{ has no triangles},\quad (T_r\setminus z)^*\text{ and }(D_r\setminus z)^*\text{ are the stated Möbius-ladder cycle matroids}

knowledge_statements.statement_title: Representation and structural properties of the binary spikes Z_r
knowledge_statements.scope_note: Extraction-grounded definition and property catalogue for the binary spike family with distinguished tip.
knowledge_statements.statement_latex: For every $r\ge 3$, the standard matrix $[I_r\mid J_r-I_r\mid\mathbf 1]$ over $\operatorname{GF}(2)$ represents $Z_r$, the unique rank-$r$ binary spike with tip $t$. Moreover, $Z_3\setminus e\cong M(K_4)$ for every $e$, $Z_3\cong F_7$, $Z_4\setminus t\cong AG(3,2)$, and $Z_4\setminus e\cong S_8$ for every $e\ne t$. The tipless spike $Z_r\setminus t$ is self-dual and is identically self-dual if and only if $r$ is even. The matroid $Z_r$ is representable, and algebraic, over a field $\mathbb F$ if and only if $\operatorname{char}(\mathbb F)=2$; it is neither graphic, cographic, regular, near-regular, transversal, a strict gammoid, nor a gammoid. For all $e,f\in E(Z_r)\setminus\{t\}$, an automorphism fixing $t$ interchanges $e$ and $f$, and hence $Z_r\setminus t$ has a transitive automorphism group. For every $e\ne t$, $Z_r\setminus e$ is self-dual but not identically self-dual. If $r\ge4$, every single-element contraction of $Z_r\setminus t$ is isomorphic to $Z_{r-1}$. A 3-connected binary matroid of rank at least three has no $M(\mathcal W_4)$-minor if and only if it is isomorphic to $Z_r$, $Z_r^*$, $Z_r\setminus t$, or $Z_r\setminus y_r$ for some $r\ge3$.
knowledge_statements.statement_plain: For each r at least 3, Z_r is the unique rank-r binary spike with a tip and has the standard binary matrix representation. The extract specifies its small cases, exact characteristic-two representability and algebraicity, class exclusions, automorphisms, deletion and contraction properties, and its role in characterizing 3-connected binary matroids without a rank-4 wheel minor.
assumptions_latex: \mathbb F\text{ is a field for the representability and algebraicity assertions}
M\text{ is 3-connected and binary with }r(M)\ge3\text{ for the excluded-minor characterization}
knowledge_statements.conclusion_latex: Z_r\text{ has the stated representation, uniqueness, duality, symmetry, minor, class-membership, and algebraicity properties.}

knowledge_statements.statement_title: Binary circuit structure under contraction
knowledge_statements.scope_note: Describes the binary specialization of circuit decomposition after contracting an external element.
knowledge_statements.statement_latex: Let $C$ be a circuit of a binary matroid $M$ and let $e\in E(M)\setminus C$. In $M/e$, either $C$ is a circuit, or $C$ is the disjoint union of two circuits. In either case, $M/e$ has no other circuits contained in $C$.
knowledge_statements.statement_plain: After contracting an element outside a circuit of a binary matroid, the circuit either remains a circuit or becomes the disjoint union of two circuits, with no other circuits of the contraction contained in it.

knowledge_statements.statement_title: Circuits of a common-triangle binary-matroid delta-sum
knowledge_statements.scope_note: Describes all circuits of the delta-sum under only the common-triangle hypotheses.
knowledge_statements.statement_latex: Let $M_1$ and $M_2$ be binary matroids with $E(M_1)\cap E(M_2)=T$, where $T$ is a triangle of both. Then $\mathcal C(M_1\mathbin{\triangle}M_2)$ is the union of $\mathcal C(M_1\setminus T)$, $\mathcal C(M_2\setminus T)$, and the collection of inclusion-minimal sets of the form $C_1\mathbin{\triangle}C_2$, where $C_i\in\mathcal C(M_i)$ and $C_1\cap T=C_2\cap T$ is a singleton.
knowledge_statements.statement_plain: When two binary matroids meet in a common triangle, the circuits of their delta-sum are the circuits surviving deletion of the triangle from either side, together with the minimal symmetric differences of circuits meeting the triangle in the same single element.
assumptions_latex: T\text{ is a triangle of both }M_1\text{ and }M_2
knowledge_statements.conclusion_latex: \mathcal C(M_1\mathbin{\triangle}M_2)=\mathcal C(M_1\setminus T)\cup\mathcal C(M_2\setminus T)\cup\min_{\subseteq}\{C_1\mathbin{\triangle}C_2:C_i\in\mathcal C(M_i),\ C_1\cap T=C_2\cap T,\ |C_1\cap T|=1\}.

knowledge_statements.statement_title: Existence and matrix representation of the binary-matroid delta-sum
knowledge_statements.scope_note: General delta-sum construction before the additional conditions defining a 3-sum are imposed.
knowledge_statements.statement_latex: Let $M_1$ and $M_2$ be binary matroids and let $E=E(M_1)\mathbin{\triangle}E(M_2)$. There is a matroid $M_1\mathbin{\triangle}M_2$ on $E$ whose circuits are the inclusion-minimal nonempty sets $X_1\mathbin{\triangle}X_2$, where each $X_i$ is a disjoint union of circuits of $M_i$. If $A$ is a matrix over $\operatorname{GF}(2)$ whose columns are indexed by $E(M_1)\cup E(M_2)$ and whose rows are the incidence vectors of all circuits of $M_1$ and $M_2$, then $M_1\mathbin{\triangle}M_2=(M[A])^*\setminus(E(M_1)\cap E(M_2))$.
knowledge_statements.statement_plain: For any two binary matroids, their delta-sum exists on the symmetric difference of their ground sets. Its circuits are the minimal nonempty symmetric differences of disjoint unions of circuits from the two matroids, and it has the stated dual-matrix-and-deletion representation over GF(2).
assumptions_latex: A\text{ is over }\operatorname{GF}(2)\text{ with columns and circuit-incidence rows as specified}
knowledge_statements.conclusion_latex: \mathcal C(M_1\mathbin{\triangle}M_2)=\min_{\subseteq}\{X_1\mathbin{\triangle}X_2\ne\varnothing:X_i\text{ is a disjoint union of circuits of }M_i\},\qquad M_1\mathbin{\triangle}M_2=(M[A])^*\setminus(E(M_1)\cap E(M_2)).

knowledge_statements.statement_title: Finitary infinite matroid
knowledge_statements.scope_note: Defines an infinite matroid via hereditary, finitary, and finite-exchange axioms; the chapter subsequently restricts attention to finite rank.
knowledge_statements.statement_latex: An infinite matroid is a pair \(M=(S,\mathcal I)\), where \(S\) is infinite and \(\varnothing\ne\mathcal I\subseteq 2^S\), such that: (i) \(I\in\mathcal I\) and \(J\subseteq I\) imply \(J\in\mathcal I\); (ii) if every finite subset of \(I\subseteq S\) lies in \(\mathcal I\), then \(I\in\mathcal I\); and (iii) for finite \(I,J\in\mathcal I\) with \(|I|<|J|\), some \(j\in J\setminus I\) satisfies \(I\cup\{j\}\in\mathcal I\). Members of \(\mathcal I\) are independent, and inclusionwise minimal dependent sets are circuits. Axiom (ii) implies that every circuit is finite. The finite-rank regime additionally assumes \(\sup\{|I|:I\in\mathcal I\}<\infty\).
knowledge_statements.statement_plain: An infinite matroid has an infinite ground set and a nonempty hereditary independence system satisfying a finitary closure axiom and finite-set augmentation. Its circuits are finite. Finite rank means that all independent-set sizes have a common finite upper bound.
knowledge_statements.conclusion_latex: (S,\mathcal I)\text{ is an infinite matroid under axioms (i)--(iii), and every circuit is finite.}

knowledge_statements.statement_title: Structural properties of the rank-3 ternary Dowling geometry
knowledge_statements.scope_note: Extraction-grounded catalogue of $Q_3(\operatorname{GF}(3)^\times)$.
knowledge_statements.statement_latex: The matroid $Q_3(\operatorname{GF}(3)^\times)$ is the rank-3 ternary Dowling geometry. It is representable over a field $\mathbb F$ if and only if $\operatorname{char}(\mathbb F)\ne2$. It is dyadic but neither graphic, cographic, regular, sixth-root-of-unity, near-regular, transversal, a strict gammoid, nor a gammoid. Its automorphism group is non-transitive. It is the complement of $U_{3,4}$ in $PG(2,3)$. This matroid and $AG(2,3)$ are the only simple rank-3 ternary matroids with more than eight elements that are representable over some field of characteristic different from three. It is algebraic over every field.
knowledge_statements.statement_plain: The rank-3 ternary Dowling geometry is representable exactly over fields of characteristic other than two. It is dyadic but not graphic, cographic, regular, sixth-root-of-unity, near-regular, transversal or a gammoid. It has a non-transitive automorphism group, is the complement of U(3,4) in PG(2,3), participates in a two-matroid extremal classification with AG(2,3), and is algebraic over every field.
assumptions_latex: M\text{ is simple, ternary, of rank }3,\ |E(M)|>8,\text{ and representable over some field of characteristic }\ne3\text{ for the extremal classification}
knowledge_statements.conclusion_latex: Q_3(\operatorname{GF}(3)^\times)\text{ has the stated representation, class, symmetry, geometric, extremal, and algebraicity properties.}

knowledge_statements.statement_title: Partial Field from a Commutative Ring
knowledge_statements.scope_note: Ring-based definition, including the domain of the partial addition operation.
knowledge_statements.statement_latex: Let $R$ be a commutative ring with unity and let $U(R)$ denote its group of units. A subset $P\subseteq R$ is a partial field if $\{0,1,-1\}\subseteq P$ and $P\setminus\{0\}$ is a multiplicative subgroup of $U(R)$. Multiplication is defined for every pair of elements of $P$, while for $a,b\in P$, addition is defined precisely when $a+b\in P$, where the sum is computed in $R$.
knowledge_statements.statement_plain: Let R be a commutative ring with unity and U(R) its group of units. A subset P of R is a partial field when it contains 0, 1, and -1, and its nonzero elements form a multiplicative subgroup of U(R). Multiplication is total on P, whereas the sum of two elements of P is defined exactly when their ring sum also belongs to P.
assumptions_latex: R\text{ is a commutative ring with unity}
knowledge_statements.conclusion_latex: P\text{ is a partial field}\iff \{0,1,-1\}\subseteq P\ \text{and}\ P\setminus\{0\}\le U(R),\quad a+_P b\text{ is defined}\iff a+b\in P.

knowledge_statements.statement_title: Profile of P7 and the excluded minors for ternary gammoids
knowledge_statements.scope_note: Combines the named-matroid profile with the explicitly stated complete excluded-minor characterization.
knowledge_statements.statement_latex: P_7 is the ternary 3-spike other than F_7^-. It is \mathbb F-representable if and only if |\mathbb F|\ge 3. It is neither graphic, cographic, regular, transversal, a strict gammoid, nor a gammoid, but it is near-regular, dyadic, and sixth-root-of-unity. It has no M(K_4)-minor, is the complement of P(U_{2,4},U_{2,3}) in PG(2,3), is base-orderable and strongly base-orderable, and is algebraic over every field. The excluded minors for the class of ternary gammoids are U_{2,5}, U_{3,5}, M(K_4), P_7, and P_7^*.
knowledge_statements.statement_plain: P7 is the ternary 3-spike other than the non-Fano matroid. It is representable exactly over fields having at least three elements. It is not graphic, cographic, regular, transversal, a strict gammoid, or a gammoid, but it is near-regular, dyadic, and sixth-root-of-unity. It has no M(K4) minor, has the stated complementary construction in PG(2,3), is base-orderable and strongly base-orderable, and is algebraic over every field. The excluded minors for ternary gammoids are U(2,5), U(3,5), M(K4), P7, and its dual.
knowledge_statements.conclusion_latex: P_7\text{ has the stated representation, class, minor, construction, orderability, and algebraicity properties, and }\{U_{2,5},U_{3,5},M(K_4),P_7,P_7^*\}\text{ is the excluded-minor set for ternary gammoids.}

knowledge_statements.statement_title: Structural properties of AG(2,3)
knowledge_statements.scope_note: Extraction-grounded catalogue of the ternary affine-plane matroid, including exact representability criteria and excluded-minor roles.
knowledge_statements.statement_latex: The matroid $AG(2,3)$ is the ternary affine plane and is isomorphic to the unique $S(2,3,9)$. It is representable over a field $\mathbb F$ if and only if $\mathbb F$ contains a root of $x^2-x+1=0$; in particular, it is representable over $\mathbb C$ but not over $\mathbb R$. It is representable over $\operatorname{GF}(q)$ if and only if $q\not\equiv2\pmod 3$. It is sixth-root-of-unity, base-orderable, and strongly base-orderable, but is neither graphic, cographic, regular, dyadic, near-regular, transversal, a strict gammoid, nor a gammoid. Its automorphism group is doubly transitive, and it is algebraic over every field. It is the unique maximal simple 3-connected rank-3 ternary matroid having no $M(K_4)$-minor and is the complement of $U_{2,4}$ in $PG(2,3)$. Every single-element deletion is isomorphic to $AG(2,3)\setminus e$. This deletion is transitive on points and on nontrivial lines, so there is a unique matroid $\Delta_3(AG(2,3)\setminus e)$ obtained by a $\Delta$-$Y$ exchange. A matroid is near-regular if and only if it has no minor isomorphic to any of $U_{2,5},U_{3,5},F_7,F_7^*,F_7^-,(F_7^-)^*,AG(2,3)\setminus e,(AG(2,3)\setminus e)^*,\Delta_3(AG(2,3)\setminus e)$, or $P_8$.
knowledge_statements.statement_plain: AG(2,3) is the ternary affine plane and the unique S(2,3,9). The extract gives exact general-field and finite-field representability criteria, class memberships and exclusions, double transitivity, base orderability, an extremal minor characterization, its complement realization in PG(2,3), uniform deletion behavior, a unique delta–Y exchange outcome, the excluded-minor characterization of near-regular matroids, and algebraicity over every field.
assumptions_latex: \mathbb F\text{ is a field for the general representability criterion}
q\text{ is a prime power for the }\operatorname{GF}(q)\text{-representability criterion}
e\in E(AG(2,3))\text{ for the deletion and }\Delta\text{-}Y\text{ assertions}
M\text{ is a matroid for the near-regular excluded-minor characterization}
knowledge_statements.conclusion_latex: AG(2,3)\text{ has the stated representation, class, symmetry, extremal, deletion, exchange, excluded-minor, and algebraicity properties.}

knowledge_statements.statement_title: Representations and structural properties of R8
knowledge_statements.scope_note: Extraction-grounded catalog characterization of the real affine cube.
knowledge_statements.statement_latex: The matroid R_8 has as its 4-point planes the six cube faces and six diagonal planes. It is the real affine cube and a tipless ternary 4-spike. Over every field \mathbb F with \operatorname{char}(\mathbb F)\ne2 it is represented by [I_4\mid J_4-2I_4], and it is representable over \mathbb F if and only if \operatorname{char}(\mathbb F)\ne2. It is not graphic, cographic, or regular, but is near-regular, dyadic, and sixth-root-of-unity. It is not transversal, a strict gammoid, or a gammoid. It is identically self-dual and has a transitive automorphism group. Every single-element deletion is isomorphic to (F_7^-)^*, and every single-element contraction is isomorphic to F_7^-. It is a relaxation of AG(3,2)' and is the unique matroid obtained from AG(3,2) by relaxing two disjoint circuit-hyperplanes. It is algebraic over every field.
knowledge_statements.statement_plain: R8 is the real affine cube and a tipless ternary 4-spike. It is represented by [I4 | J4−2I4] and is linearly representable exactly in characteristics other than two. It has the stated partial-field memberships, exclusions, identical self-duality, automorphism behavior, single-element minors, relaxation characterizations, and algebraicity over every field.
knowledge_statements.conclusion_latex: M\text{ has the stated field representation, class-membership, duality, minor, relaxation, uniqueness, and algebraicity properties.}

knowledge_statements.scope_note: Extraction-grounded profile of the Steiner-system matroid S(5,6,12); the extracted matrix body is malformed, so no matrix entries are reconstructed.
knowledge_statements.statement_latex: S(5,6,12)\text{ is represented over }GF(3)\text{ by the matrix identified in the source. It is the unique Steiner system with the stated parameters, and that matrix is a generator matrix for the extended ternary Golay code. For every field }\mathbb F,\ S(5,6,12)\text{ is }\mathbb F\text{-representable}\iff\operatorname{char}(\mathbb F)=3.\text{ It is neither graphic, cographic, regular, near-regular, transversal, a strict gammoid, nor a gammoid. It is identically self-dual, and its automorphism group is the }5\text{-transitive Mathieu group }M_{12}.\text{ It is a splitter for }EX(U_{2,5},U_{3,5},M(K_4))\text{ and }EX(M(K_4),P_6,Q_6).\text{ Every contraction of three elements is isomorphic to }AG(2,3),\text{ and every minor obtained by contracting two elements and deleting two elements is isomorphic to }P_8.\text{ It is base-orderable but not strongly base-orderable, has Tutte connectivity }5,\text{ and its circuits and hyperplanes coincide and all have six elements.}
knowledge_statements.statement_plain: S(5,6,12) is represented over GF(3) by the matrix identified in the source. It is the unique Steiner system with the stated parameters, and that matrix generates the extended ternary Golay code. It is representable over a field F exactly when F has characteristic 3. It is not graphic, cographic, regular, near-regular, transversal, a strict gammoid, or a gammoid. It is identically self-dual, and its automorphism group is the 5-transitive Mathieu group M_12. It is a splitter for the two stated excluded-minor classes. Every contraction of three elements is isomorphic to AG(2,3), and every minor obtained by contracting two elements and deleting two elements is isomorphic to P_8. It is base-orderable but not strongly base-orderable, has Tutte connectivity 5, and its circuits and hyperplanes coincide and all have six elements.
assumptions_latex: \mathbb F\text{ is a field whenever representability is considered.}
knowledge_statements.conclusion_latex: S(5,6,12)\text{ has the stated Steiner-system, Golay-code, characteristic-three representation, class-exclusion, duality, automorphism, splitter, minor, base-orderability, connectivity, circuit, and hyperplane properties.}

knowledge_statements.statement_title: Representation and structural properties of J
knowledge_statements.scope_note: Extraction-grounded catalog characterization of the named matroid J.
knowledge_statements.statement_latex: The matroid J is representable over a field \mathbb F if and only if |\mathbb F|\ge 3. It is not graphic, cographic, regular, transversal, a strict gammoid, or a gammoid, but it is near-regular, dyadic, sixth-root-of-unity, and algebraic over every field. It is self-dual but not identically self-dual, and its automorphism group is not transitive. The matroids J and the relaxation of S_8 are exactly those obtained by deleting a non-tip element from a ternary 4-spike. The matroids J and S(5,6,12) are exactly the 3-connected splitters for ternary matroids having no M(K_4)-minor. The matroid J is neither base-orderable nor strongly base-orderable. The excluded minors for ternary base-orderable matroids are U_{2,5},U_{3,5},M(K_4),J; those for ternary strongly base-orderable matroids are U_{2,5},U_{3,5},M(K_4),J,P_8.
knowledge_statements.statement_plain: J is representable exactly over fields having at least three elements. It has the stated partial-field memberships, class exclusions, self-duality, automorphism behavior, ternary-spike and splitter characterizations, and base-orderability obstructions. It is algebraic over every field.
knowledge_statements.conclusion_latex: M\text{ has the stated representability, class-membership, duality, splitter, and base-orderability properties.}

knowledge_statements.scope_note: Extraction-grounded consolidated profile of the named matroid T_8.
knowledge_statements.statement_latex: T_8\text{ is a ternary tipless }4\text{-spike, and the only other ternary tipless }4\text{-spike is }R_8.\text{ It is represented over }GF(3)\text{ by }[I_4\mid J_4-I_4].\text{ For every field }\mathbb F,\ T_8\text{ is }\mathbb F\text{-representable}\iff\operatorname{char}(\mathbb F)=3.\text{ It is an excluded minor for }\mathbb F\text{-representability whenever }\operatorname{char}(\mathbb F)\notin\{2,3\}.\ T_8\text{ is neither graphic, cographic, regular, near-regular, transversal, a strict gammoid, nor a gammoid. knowledge_statements.statement_title: Decomposition Alternatives for 3-Connected Regular Matroids
knowledge_statements.scope_note: The 3-sum alternative includes the stated connectivity, minor, closure, and simplification conditions for both factors.
knowledge_statements.statement_latex: Let \(M\) be a 3-connected regular matroid. Then either (i) \(M\) is graphic; (ii) \(M\) is cographic; (iii) \(M\cong R_{10}\); or (iv) there exist regular matroids \(M_1,M_2\) such that \(E(M_1)\cap E(M_2)=T\), where \(T\) is a triangle of both \(M_1\) and \(M_2\), and \(M=M_1\oplus_3M_2\). In case (iv), for each \(i\in\{1,2\}\), \(M_i\) is internally 3-connected and every two-element 2-separating set of \(M_i\) meets \(T\); \(M_i\) is isomorphic to a minor of \(M\); and \(|E(M_i)-\operatorname{cl}_{M_i}(T)|\ge6\) and \(|E(\operatorname{si}(M_i))|\ge9\).
knowledge_statements.statement_plain: Every 3-connected regular matroid is graphic, cographic, isomorphic to R10, or a 3-sum along a common triangle of two regular matroids satisfying the stated connectivity, minor, closure-size, and simplification-size conditions.
knowledge_statements.conclusion_latex: \begin{aligned}&M\text{ is graphic}\ \lor\ M\text{ is cographic}\ \lor\ M\cong R_{10}\ \lor\\&\exists M_1,M_2,T:\ M_1,M_2\text{ are regular},\ E(M_1)\cap E(M_2)=T,\ T\text{ is a triangle of both},\ M=M_1\oplus_3M_2,\\&\qquad\forall i\in\{1,2\}:\ M_i\text{ is internally 3-connected},\ \text{every two-element 2-separating set of }M_i\text{ meets }T,\\&\qquad M_i\text{ is isomorphic to a minor of }M,\ |E(M_i)-\operatorname{cl}_{M_i}(T)|\ge6,\ |E(\operatorname{si}(M_i))|\ge9.\end{aligned}

knowledge_statements.statement_title: Circuit and Cocircuit Incidence Matrices and Signable Matroids
knowledge_statements.scope_note: Incidence-matrix definitions and signed circuit–cocircuit orthogonality over the real numbers.
knowledge_statements.statement_latex: Let \(M\) be a matroid on \(\{1,\ldots,n\}\) with \(\mathcal C(M)=\{C_1,\ldots,C_m\}\). Its circuit incidence matrix is \(A(\mathcal C)=[a_{ij}]\in\{0,1\}^{m\times n}\), where \(a_{ij}=1\) if and only if \(j\in C_i\). Its cocircuit incidence matrix \(A(\mathcal C^*)\) is the circuit incidence matrix of \(M^*\). The matroid \(M\) is signable if these matrices admit signings \(A'(\mathcal C)\) and \(A'(\mathcal C^*)\) such that, over \(\mathbb R\), every row of \(A'(\mathcal C)\) is orthogonal to every row of \(A'(\mathcal C^*)\). Each incidence matrix is determined only up to a permutation of its rows.
knowledge_statements.statement_plain: The circuit incidence matrix records circuit membership, and the cocircuit incidence matrix is the circuit incidence matrix of the dual. A matroid is signable when their nonzero entries can be signed so every signed circuit row is orthogonal over the reals to every signed cocircuit row.
knowledge_statements.conclusion_latex: M\text{ is signable}\iff \exists A'(\mathcal C),A'(\mathcal C^*)\;\forall r\in\operatorname{rows}(A'(\mathcal C))\;\forall s\in\operatorname{rows}(A'(\mathcal C^*)):\ r\cdot s=0

knowledge_statements.statement_title: Structure and obstruction role of R_{12}
knowledge_statements.scope_note: Extraction-grounded structural profile of R_{12}, including the accompanying theorem for 3-connected regular matroids; the malformed extracted matrix is not reproduced.
knowledge_statements.statement_latex: The matroid R_{12} is representable over GF(2) and is regular. It is neither graphic nor cographic, but every proper minor of R_{12} is graphic or cographic. It is neither transversal, a strict gammoid, nor a gammoid. It is a 3-sum of M^*(K_{3,3}) and M(K_5\setminus e) across the triangle of K_5\setminus e that is vertex-disjoint from e. It is self-dual but not identically self-dual. Its automorphism group is non-transitive; its two orbits are the union of its two triangles and the union of its two triads. Moreover, every 3-connected regular matroid is graphic or cographic, or has a minor isomorphic to R_{10} or R_{12}. Finally, R_{12} is algebraic over every field.
knowledge_statements.statement_plain: R12 is representable over GF(2) and is regular. It is neither graphic nor cographic, but every proper minor is graphic or cographic. It is not transversal or a gammoid. It has the stated 3-sum construction, is self-dual but not identically self-dual, and has two automorphism orbits formed by its triangles and triads. Every 3-connected regular matroid is graphic or cographic or has an R10 or R12 minor, and R12 is algebraic over every field.
knowledge_statements.conclusion_latex: R_{12}\text{ has the stated representability, proper-minor boundary, class-exclusion, 3-sum, duality, symmetry, and algebraicity properties, and }M\text{ is graphic, cographic, or has an }R_{10}\text{ or }R_{12}\text{ minor.}

Among regular matroids that are neither graphic nor cographic, it is the only 10-element matroid and the only simple matroid of rank at most 5. It is the unique splitter for the class of regular matroids. It is neither transversal, a strict gammoid, nor a gammoid, and it is self-dual but not identically self-dual. Its automorphism group is doubly transitive. For every e\in E(R_{10}), R_{10}\setminus e\cong M(K_{3,3}) and R_{10}/e\cong M^*(K_{3,3}). Every circuit of R_{10} has size 4 or 6. It is the graft matroid of K_{3,3} in which every vertex is colored, it has a GF(2)-representation by the ten binary 5-tuples of weight 3, and it is algebraic over every field.
knowledge_statements.statement_plain: R10 is representable over every field. Among regular matroids that are neither graphic nor cographic, it is the only ten-element member and the only simple member of rank at most five. It is the unique splitter for regular matroids, is self-dual but not identically self-dual, and has a doubly transitive automorphism group. Every deletion is M(K3,3), every contraction is its dual, every circuit has four or six elements, and R10 has the stated graft, binary, and algebraic representations. It is not transversal or a gammoid.
knowledge_statements.conclusion_latex: R_{10}\text{ has the stated universal representability, uniqueness, splitter, class-exclusion, duality, minor, circuit, graft, binary, and algebraicity properties.}

knowledge_statements.statement_title: Structural profile of M(K_5) and M^*(K_5)
knowledge_statements.scope_note: Extraction-grounded properties of the cycle matroid of K_5 and its dual.
knowledge_statements.statement_latex: Let M=M(K_5). The matroid M is the rank-4 matroid of the three-dimensional Desargues configuration. Both M and M^* are regular and algebraic over every field. The matroid M^* is an excluded minor for the class of graphic matroids, while M is an excluded minor for the class of cographic matroids. Neither is transversal, a strict gammoid, or a gammoid, and their common automorphism group is transitive. Moreover, M is the unique rank-4 simple regular matroid with the maximum number of elements among rank-4 simple regular matroids; it is a tangential 2-block over GF(2), a splitter for the regular matroids having no M(K_{3,3}) minor, and the complement of the 5-element circuit U_{4,5} in PG(3,2).
knowledge_statements.statement_plain: The cycle matroid of K5 is the rank-four matroid of the three-dimensional Desargues configuration. It and its dual are regular and algebraic over every field. The dual is an excluded minor for graphic matroids, while the cycle matroid is an excluded minor for cographic matroids. Neither is transversal or a gammoid, their common automorphism group is transitive, and the cycle matroid has the stated extremal, tangential-block, splitter, and projective-complement characterizations.
knowledge_statements.conclusion_latex: M\text{ and }M^*\text{ have the stated regularity, excluded-minor, class-exclusion, symmetry, extremal, splitter, projective, and algebraicity properties.}

knowledge_statements.statement_latex: Let \(\mathcal R_{\mathbb F}\) be the class of finite matroids representable over \(\mathbb F\). knowledge_statements.scope_note: Finite projective geometries viewed as simple linear matroids.
knowledge_statements.statement_latex: Let \(V=\mathbb F_q^r\). The ground set of \(\operatorname{PG}(r-1,q)\) is the set of one-dimensional linear subspaces of \(V\). Choose one nonzero vector from each such subspace. A set of projective points is independent exactly when the corresponding chosen vectors are linearly independent over \(\mathbb F_q\); this condition is independent of the choices because replacing a representative by a nonzero scalar multiple preserves linear dependence. Thus \(\operatorname{PG}(r-1,q)\) is a simple rank-\(r\) matroid with \((q^r-1)/(q-1)\) elements.

knowledge_statements.statement_title: Incidence-Axiomatic Projective Geometry
knowledge_statements.scope_note: Defines abstract projective geometries together with isomorphisms, subspaces, hyperplanes, and dimension.
knowledge_statements.statement_latex: A projective geometry is a triple $(P,L,\iota)$ in which: every two distinct points lie on exactly one line; every line contains at least three points; and, for four distinct points $a,b,c,d$ with no three collinear, $ab\cap cd\ne\varnothing$ implies $ac\cap bd\ne\varnothing$. An isomorphism is a bijection of point sets preserving and reflecting lines. A subspace is a subset closed under every line through two of its distinct points, and a hyperplane is a proper subspace maximal under inclusion. The dimension of a subspace is one less than its finite height in the inclusion poset of subspaces, and is $\infty$ when that height is infinite; hence $\dim\varnothing=-1$, points have dimension $0$, and lines have dimension $1$. Moreover, $PG(V(n+1,\mathbb F))$ has dimension $n$ and is denoted $PG(n,\mathbb F)$, or $PG(n,q)$ when $\mathbb F=GF(q)$.
knowledge_statements.statement_plain: An abstract projective geometry is an incidence system satisfying unique lines through pairs of points, at least three points per line, and the stated intersection axiom. Isomorphisms preserve lines; subspaces are closed under joining their points; hyperplanes are maximal proper subspaces; and projective dimension is one less than subspace-poset height, or infinite when the height is infinite. The geometry from an (n+1)-dimensional vector space has dimension n.
knowledge_statements.conclusion_latex: (P,L,\iota)\text{ is a projective geometry precisely under axioms (i)--(iii), with subspaces, hyperplanes, and dimension as specified; }\dim PG(V(n+1,\mathbb F))=n.

knowledge_statements.statement_title: Projective Geometry Associated with a Vector Space
knowledge_statements.scope_note: Defines the incidence geometry of one- and two-dimensional subspaces and its representative-vector realization.
knowledge_statements.statement_latex: For a vector space $V$ over $\mathbb F$, $PG(V)$ has the one-dimensional subspaces of $V$ as points, the two-dimensional subspaces as lines, and inclusion as incidence. Equivalently, delete $0$ and retain one nonzero representative from each one-dimensional subspace; each line is then the intersection of this representative set with a two-dimensional subspace. If $V$ is finite and both $V$ and $PG(V)$ are viewed as matroids, this construction is the simplification of the vector matroid on $V$.
knowledge_statements.statement_plain: The projective geometry of a vector space uses its one-dimensional subspaces as points and its two-dimensional subspaces as lines, with incidence given by inclusion. It may also be realized by choosing one nonzero vector from every one-dimensional subspace. For finite vector spaces, this agrees with simplifying the corresponding vector matroid.

knowledge_statements.conclusion_latex: P(PG(V))=\{U\le V:\dim U=1\},\quad L(PG(V))=\{W\le V:\dim W=2\},\quad U\mathrel\iota W\iff U\subseteq W.

knowledge_statements.statement_title: Enumeration in Finite Projective Geometries
knowledge_statements.scope_note: Counts flats, independent sets, and circuits in a finite projective geometry.
knowledge_statements.statement_latex: Let \(k\) be a nonnegative integer. In \(PG(r-1,q)\), the number of rank-\(k\) flats is \({r\brack k}_q\); the number of \(k\)-element independent sets is \(\frac{1}{k!}\prod_{i=0}^{k-1}\frac{q^r-q^i}{q-1}\); and the number of \(k\)-element circuits is \(0\) for \(k<3\), and \(\frac{1}{k!(q-1)}\prod_{i=0}^{k-2}(q^r-q^i)\) for \(k\ge3\).
knowledge_statements.statement_plain: For every nonnegative k, the rank-k flats, k-element independent sets, and k-element circuits of PG(r−1,q) have the stated Gaussian-binomial and product counts; there are no circuits with fewer than three elements.
assumptions_latex: PG(r-1,q)\text{ is a finite projective geometry over }GF(q)

knowledge_statements.statement_title: Affine geometries and affine matroids
knowledge_statements.scope_note: Defines affine geometry over a field, gives its normalized representation, characterizes finite affine matroids, and records basic finite-geometry invariants.
knowledge_statements.statement_latex: For \(n\in\mathbb Z\) with \(n\ge -1\) and a field \(\mathbb F\), the affine geometry \(AG(n,\mathbb F)\) is obtained from \(PG(n,\mathbb F)\) by deleting the points of a hyperplane. Equivalently, after a coordinate choice its points are represented by \(\{(1,x_2,\ldots,x_{n+1}):x_i\in\mathbb F\}\); its isomorphism type is independent of the chosen hyperplane. A finite matroid \(M\) is affine over \(\mathbb F\) if and only if \(M\) has no loops and \(\operatorname{si}(M)\cong AG(n,\mathbb F)|S\) for some \(n\ge-1\) and finite \(S\subseteq AG(n,\mathbb F)\). For a prime power \(q\), \(AG(r-1,q)\) has rank \(r\), has \(q^{r-1}\) elements when \(r\ge1\), and every rank-\(k\) flat is isomorphic to \(AG(k-1,q)\).
knowledge_statements.statement_plain: Affine geometry is obtained from projective geometry by deleting a hyperplane and admits a normalized vector representation with first coordinate one. A finite matroid is affine over a field exactly when it is loopless and its simplification is a finite restriction of an affine geometry. Finite affine geometry AG(r−1,q) has rank r, q^(r−1) points for r at least one, and rank-k flats isomorphic to AG(k−1,q).
assumptions_latex: M\text{ and }S\text{ are finite in the affine-matroid characterization}
q\text{ is a prime power for the finite-geometry assertions}
knowledge_statements.conclusion_latex: AG(n,\mathbb F)\cong PG(n,\mathbb F)\setminus H,\qquad M\text{ affine over }\mathbb F\iff M\text{ is loopless and }\operatorname{si}(M)\cong AG(n,\mathbb F)|S.

knowledge_statements.statement_title: Enumeration of flats, independent sets, and circuits in finite affine geometry
knowledge_statements.scope_note: Counts three fundamental types of substructures in \(AG(r-1,q)\).
knowledge_statements.statement_latex: Let \(k\ge0\). In \(AG(r-1,q)\), the number of rank-\(k\) flats is \[q^{r-k}{r-1\brack k-1}_q=q^{r-k}\frac{(q^{r-1}-1)(q^{r-1}-q)\cdots(q^{r-1}-q^{k-2})}{(q^{k-1}-1)(q^{k-1}-q)\cdots(q^{k-1}-q^{k-2})}.\] The number of \(k\)-element independent sets is \[\frac{q^{r-1}}{k!}(q^{r-1}-1)(q^{r-1}-q)\cdots(q^{r-1}-q^{k-2}).\] There are no circuits of size less than three, and for \(k\ge3\) the number of \(k\)-element circuits is \[\frac{q^{r-2}}{k!}(q^{r-1}-1)(q^{r-1}-q)\cdots(q^{r-1}-q^{k-3})\big((q-1)^{k-1}-(-1)^{k-1}\big).\]
knowledge_statements.statement_plain: Explicit product formulas count the rank-k flats and k-element independent sets of AG(r−1,q). This geometry has no circuits of fewer than three elements, and for k at least three its k-element circuits are counted by the stated product formula.
assumptions_latex: AG(r-1,q)\text{ is the finite affine geometry under consideration}
knowledge_statements.conclusion_latex: N_{\mathrm{flat}}(k)=q^{r-k}{r-1\brack k-1}_q,\quad N_{\mathrm{ind}}(k)=\frac{q^{r-1}}{k!}\prod_{i=0}^{k-2}(q^{r-1}-q^i),\quad N_{\mathrm{circ}}(k)=\frac{q^{r-2}}{k!}\prod_{i=0}^{k-3}(q^{r-1}-q^i)\big((q-1)^{k-1}-(-1)^{k-1}\big)\ (k\ge3).

notation.meaning: Dowling geometry of rank n associated with G

knowledge_statements.scope_note: Combinatorial definition through complete gain graphs and frame matroids.
knowledge_statements.statement_latex: Take vertices \(1,ldots,n\), one distinguished unbalanced loop at each vertex, and, for every \(i<j\) and \(g\in G\), an edge \(e_{ij}^g\) directed from \(i\) to \(j\). Reversing an edge inverts its gain, and a cycle is balanced when its directed gain product equals \(1_G\). The Dowling geometry \(Q_n(G)\) is the frame matroid of this biased graph: an edge set is independent exactly when it contains no balanced cycle and every connected component contains at most one cycle. The distinguished loops are the joints of the geometry.
knowledge_statements.statement_plain: A Dowling geometry is the frame matroid of a complete group-labeled graph augmented by one unbalanced joint at each vertex.

knowledge_statements.statement_title: Dowling Geometry
knowledge_statements.scope_note: Ground set, balance rule, and circuit description of the Dowling geometry associated with a finite group.
knowledge_statements.statement_latex: Let A be a finite multiplicative group with identity 1. Set Q_0(A)=U_{0,0}. For r\ge 1, construct K_r^A on vertices \{1,\ldots,r\} with an edge \alpha_{ij} for every 1\le i<j\le r and \alpha\in A, and a distinguished loop b_i at each vertex i. Its ground set is \{b_1,\ldots,b_r\}\cup\{\alpha_{ij}:1\le i<j\le r,\ \alpha\in A\}. A cycle with at least two edges is balanced when the traversal-adjusted product of its group labels is 1; a single-edge cycle and every other cycle are unbalanced. The circuits of Q_r(A) are the balanced cycles and the \Theta-graphs, loose handcuffs, and tight handcuffs having no balanced cycle.
knowledge_statements.statement_plain: For a finite group A, the Dowling geometry is built from the complete A-labeled graph on r vertices with one distinguished loop at each vertex. Its circuits are the balanced cycles and the theta or handcuff configurations containing no balanced cycle; Q0(A) is the empty rank-zero matroid.
assumptions_latex: A\text{ is a finite multiplicative group with identity }1.
knowledge_statements.conclusion_latex: Q_r(A)\text{ is the rank-}r\text{ Dowling geometry with the stated ground set and circuit family.}

knowledge_statements.statement_title: Contractions, flats, modular flats, and hyperplanes of a Dowling geometry
knowledge_statements.scope_note: Structural characterization for the Dowling geometry Q_r(A) of a finite group A.
knowledge_statements.statement_latex: Let \(A\) be a group of order \(m\). (i) For every \(e\in E(Q_r(A))\), \(\operatorname{si}(Q_r(A)/e)\cong Q_{r-1}(A)\). If \(r\ge 3\), then \(Q_r(A)/e\) is obtained from \(Q_{r-1}(A)\) as follows: when \(e\) is a joint, add \(m\) elements parallel to each joint; otherwise, add \(m\) elements parallel to exactly one joint \(f\), and for every nontrivial line through \(f\) and every non-joint element \(g\) on that line, add one element parallel to \(g\). (ii) A set \(X\) is a flat of \(Q_r(A)\) if and only if the components of \(K_r^A[X]\) are complete balanced-cycle graphs, together with at most one component isomorphic to \(K_k^A\) for some \(k\in\{0,\ldots,r\}\). Consequently, for every flat \(X\), \(Q_r(A)|X\) is a direct sum of cycle matroids of complete graphs and one \(Q_k(A)\), for some \(k\in\{0,\ldots,r\}\). (iii) A rank-\(k\) flat \(X\) is modular if and only if \(Q_r(A)|X\cong Q_k(A)\). (iv) The number of hyperplanes of \(Q_r(A)\) is \(((m+1)^r-1)/m\).
knowledge_statements.statement_plain: For a Dowling geometry over a group of order m, contracting any element simplifies to the preceding-rank Dowling geometry, with the stated parallel-element descriptions when the rank is at least three. Its flats are exactly those whose induced gain-graph components have the specified complete balanced form, and their restrictions decompose into graphic summands and at most one smaller Dowling geometry. A rank-k flat is modular exactly when its restriction is Q_k(A), and Q_r(A) has ((m+1)^r−1)/m hyperplanes.
assumptions_latex: r\ge 3\text{ for the detailed parallel-extension description}
knowledge_statements.conclusion_latex: \operatorname{si}(Q_r(A)/e)\cong Q_{r-1}(A);\quad X\text{ is a flat iff }K_r^A[X]\text{ has the stated component form};\quad X\text{ modular iff }Q_r(A)|X\cong Q_k(A);\quad |\mathcal H(Q_r(A))|=\frac{(m+1)^r-1}{m}.

children.top_down_role: Structural relationship between projective geometries and affine restrictions.

knowledge_statements.conclusion_latex: \(\operatorname{PG}(r-1,q)\backslash H\cong\operatorname{AG}(r-1,q)\).
knowledge_statements.scope_note: Hyperplane deletion identifies finite projective and affine geometries.
knowledge_statements.statement_latex: Choose homogeneous coordinates on \(\operatorname{PG}(r-1,q)\) so that \(H\) consists of the points satisfying \(x_0=0\). Every point outside \(H\) has a unique representative whose first coordinate is \(1\), hence has the form \((1,x_1,\ldots,x_{r-1})^{\mathsf T}\) with \((x_1,\ldots,x_{r-1})\in\mathbb F_q^{r-1}\). Under this normalization, the restriction of the projective-geometry matroid to the complement of \(H\) is the affine-geometry matroid. Therefore \(\operatorname{PG}(r-1,q)\backslash H\cong\operatorname{AG}(r-1,q)\).
knowledge_statements.statement_plain: Deleting a hyperplane from a finite projective geometry leaves the corresponding affine geometry, represented by normalizing the first homogeneous coordinate to one.

knowledge_statements.scope_note: Finite algebraic matroids induced by elements of a field extension.
knowledge_statements.statement_latex: Define \(\mathcal I=\{I\subseteq E:\{x_e:e\in I\}\text{ is algebraically independent over }K\}\). Then \((E,\mathcal I)\) is the algebraic matroid of the family \((x_e)_{e\in E}\) over \(K\). Its rank function is \(r(S)=\operatorname{trdeg}_K K(x_e:e\in S)\) for every \(S\subseteq E\). Consequently, a set is dependent precisely when its indexed elements satisfy a nonzero polynomial relation with coefficients in \(K\). A finite matroid is algebraic over \(K\) if it is isomorphic to one obtained in this way.

knowledge_statements.statement_title: Base-Field Change Rules for Algebraic Independence
knowledge_statements.scope_note: Independence rules for adjoining algebraic or algebraically independent elements.
knowledge_statements.statement_latex: Let \mathbb K/\mathbb F be a field extension, and let T,U\subseteq\mathbb K be finite with U algebraically independent over \mathbb F. Then: (i) if every element of T is algebraic over \mathbb F, U is algebraically independent over \mathbb F(T); and (ii) T\cup U is algebraically independent over \mathbb F if and only if T is algebraically independent over \mathbb F(U).
knowledge_statements.statement_plain: Adjoining finitely many algebraic elements to the base field preserves the independence of U. More generally, given that U is independent over the base field, T union U is independent exactly when T is independent over the field generated by U.

U\text{ is algebraically independent over }\mathbb F

knowledge_statements.statement_title: Representation and algebraicity profile of the non-Pappus matroid
knowledge_statements.scope_note: Extraction-grounded composite profile of the non-Pappus matroid.
knowledge_statements.statement_latex: Let M_{nP} be the non-Pappus matroid and let \mathbb F be a field. The matroid M_{nP} is not representable over any field. It is an excluded minor for \mathbb F\text{-representability} if and only if |\mathbb F|\ge 5, and it is algebraic over \mathbb F if and only if \operatorname{char}(\mathbb F)\ne 0. It is neither graphic, cographic, regular, near-regular, transversal, a strict gammoid, nor a gammoid. Its automorphism group is non-transitive, and it is the unique relaxation of the Pappus matroid.

It is an excluded minor for representability over a field exactly when that field has at least five elements, and it is algebraic over a field exactly when the field has nonzero characteristic. It is not graphic, cographic, regular, near-regular, transversal, a strict gammoid, or a gammoid. Its automorphism group is non-transitive, and it is the unique relaxation of the Pappus matroid.

knowledge_statements.statement_title: Algebraic representation of a matroid
knowledge_statements.scope_note: Defines algebraic representability relative to the algebraic-dependence matroid supplied by the preceding theorem.
knowledge_statements.statement_latex: Let \((E,\mathcal I)\) be the matroid associated with algebraic independence over \(\mathbb F\). A map \(\varphi:E(M)\to E\) is an algebraic representation of a matroid \(M\) over \(\mathbb F\) when, for every \(T\subseteq E(M)\), \[T\in\mathcal I(M)\iff \bigl(|\varphi(T)|=|T|\text{ and }\varphi(T)\in\mathcal I\bigr).\] The matroid \(M\) is algebraic over \(\mathbb F\) if it admits such a map, and it is algebraic if it is algebraic over some field.
knowledge_statements.statement_plain: A map algebraically represents M over F when a subset of M is independent exactly when the map is injective on that subset and its image is algebraically independent. A matroid is algebraic if it has such a representation over some field.

knowledge_statements.statement_title: Pseudomodular matroids
knowledge_statements.scope_note: Defines pseudomodularity by a three-flat rank identity and records principal full-matroid classes satisfying it.
knowledge_statements.statement_latex: A matroid with rank function $r$ is pseudomodular if, for all flats $A,B,C$ satisfying $r(A\cup C)-r(A)=r(B\cup C)-r(B)=r(A\cup B\cup C)-r(A\cup B)$, one has $r(\operatorname{span}(A\cup C)\cap\operatorname{span}(B\cup C))-r(A\cap B)=r(A\cup C)-r(A)$. Full linear matroids, full algebraic matroids, and full graphic matroids are pseudomodular.
knowledge_statements.statement_plain: A matroid is pseudomodular when every triple of flats having equal indicated rank increments also satisfies the corresponding rank identity for the intersection of their spans. Full linear, full algebraic, and full graphic matroids have this property.

knowledge_statements.statement_title: Algebraic Matroids and Minor Closure
knowledge_statements.scope_note: Defines algebraic matroids over a base field and records their containment, minor-closure, and duality boundary.
knowledge_statements.statement_latex: Let \(L/K\) be a field extension and let \(S\subseteq L\) be finite. Let \(\mathcal I\) consist of the subsets of \(S\) that are algebraically independent over \(K\), meaning that no nonzero polynomial over \(K\) vanishes on their elements. Then \((S,\mathcal I)\) is a matroid, called algebraic over \(K\). Every linear matroid is algebraic. For each field \(K\), the class of matroids algebraic over \(K\) is closed under minors; whether algebraic matroids are closed under duality is unknown in general.
knowledge_statements.statement_plain: For a finite subset of a field extension, the subsets algebraically independent over the base field form an algebraic matroid. Every linear matroid is algebraic, algebraic matroids over a fixed field are closed under minors, and closure under duality is not known in general.
assumptions_latex: \mathcal I=\{I\subseteq S:I\text{ is algebraically independent over }K\}
knowledge_statements.conclusion_latex: (S,\mathcal I)\text{ is a matroid};\quad \{\text{matroids algebraic over }K\}\text{ is closed under minors}

knowledge_statements.statement_title: Circuit families used in the spike construction
knowledge_statements.scope_note: Defines the ground set and four circuit families underlying rank-r spikes without asserting matroid existence.
knowledge_statements.statement_latex: Let r\ge 3 and E=\{t,x_1,y_1,\ldots,x_r,y_r\}. Define \mathcal C_1=\{\{t,x_i,y_i\}:1\le i\le r\} and \mathcal C_2=\{\{x_i,y_i,x_j,y_j\}:1\le i<j\le r\}. Choose \mathcal C_3\subseteq\{\{z_1,\ldots,z_r\}:z_i\in\{x_i,y_i\}\} so that distinct members intersect in at most r-2 elements, and let \mathcal C_4 be the family of all (r+1)-subsets of E containing no member of \mathcal C_1\cup\mathcal C_2\cup\mathcal C_3. Every spike on E contains \mathcal C_1\cup\mathcal C_2 among its circuits.
knowledge_statements.statement_plain: For r at least three, the spike construction uses a tip t and r pairs {x_i,y_i}. Its prescribed circuit families consist of the tip-and-pair triples, the unions of two pairs, a compatible selection of pair transversals whose distinct members differ in at least two positions, and the minimally admissible (r+1)-subsets.
assumptions_latex: C,C'\in\mathcal C_3,\ C\ne C'\implies |C\cap C'|\le r-2
knowledge_statements.conclusion_latex: \mathcal C_1,\mathcal C_2,\mathcal C_3,\mathcal C_4\text{ are defined as above, and every spike on }E\text{ has }\mathcal C_1\cup\mathcal C_2\text{ as circuits.}

knowledge_statements.statement_title: Circuit-span intersection condition
knowledge_statements.scope_note: A hypothesis on finite or infinite matroids used for the ensuing matroid-matching min-max theory.
knowledge_statements.statement_latex: A finite or infinite matroid \((S,\mathcal I)\) satisfies the circuit-span condition if, for every pair of underlying-matroid circuits \(C_1,C_2\subseteq S\) with \(C_1\cap C_2\ne\varnothing\) and \(r(C_1\cup C_2)=|C_1\cup C_2|-2\), one has \[r\!\left(\bigcap_{\substack{C\subseteq C_1\cup C_2\\ C\text{ a circuit}}}\operatorname{span}(C)\right)>0.\]
knowledge_statements.statement_plain: Whenever two intersecting circuits have union rank exactly two below the union's cardinality, the intersection of the spans of all circuits contained in their union must have positive rank.

knowledge_statements.conclusion_latex: r\!\left(\bigcap_{C\subseteq C_1\cup C_2,\ C\text{ circuit}}\operatorname{span}(C)\right)>0

knowledge_statements.scope_note: Matrix representations over partial fields using the standard determinant convention.
knowledge_statements.statement_latex: Write the underlying partial-field elements as \(G\cup\{0\}\). A matrix \(A\) over \(R\) is a \(\mathbb P\)-matrix when the determinant of every square submatrix belongs to \(G\cup\{0\}\). A \(\mathbb P\)-representation of \(M\), relative to \(B\), is a matrix \([I_B\mid A]\) with \(A\) a \(\mathbb P\)-matrix such that, for every \(r(M)\)-element subset \(X\) of the column set, \(X\) is a basis of \(M\) if and only if the corresponding maximal determinant is nonzero.
knowledge_statements.statement_plain: A partial-field representation is a normalized matrix whose square determinants are partial-field elements and whose nonzero maximal minors are exactly the matroid bases.

children.title: Characteristic Sets

knowledge_statements.conclusion_latex: \(\operatorname{Char}(M)\subseteq\{0\}\cup\{p:p\text{ is prime}\}\) records exactly the characteristics admitting a field representation of \(M\).
knowledge_statements.scope_note: Characteristics of fields, without restricting field size or extension degree.
knowledge_statements.statement_latex: The characteristic set of \(M\) is \[\operatorname{Char}(M)=\{c\in\{0\}\cup\{p:p\text{ is prime}\}:\text{ there exists a field }K\text{ with }\operatorname{char}(K)=c\text{ over which }M\text{ is representable}\}.\] Membership records existence over at least one field of the stated characteristic; it does not assert representability over every field of that characteristic. In particular, field-size restrictions within a fixed characteristic are not captured by \(\operatorname{Char}(M)\).
knowledge_statements.statement_plain: The characteristic set lists exactly those field characteristics for which at least one field representation of the matroid exists.

intermediate_metadata.review_comment: The definition correctly distinguishes existence over some field from representability over every field of a characteristic, but it has no cited source.

children.title: Representation Rigidity
children.top_down_role: Constraints on variation among inequivalent representations.

assumptions_latex: \(M\) is a finite rank-\(r\) matroid on a labeled ground set \(E\).
\(K\) is a field over which \(M\) is representable.
knowledge_statements.conclusion_latex: \(M\) is projectively rigid over \(K\) exactly when all its labeled \(K\)-representations lie in one projective-equivalence class.
knowledge_statements.scope_note: Projective rigidity for labeled representations over one fixed field.
knowledge_statements.statement_latex: Two full-rank \(K\)-matrices \(A\) and \(A'\), with columns labeled by \(E\), are projectively equivalent when \(A'=UAD\) for some \(U\in\operatorname{GL}_r(K)\) and some invertible diagonal \(E\times E\) matrix \(D\). The matroid \(M\) is projectively rigid over \(K\) when every pair of labeled \(K\)-representations of \(M\) is projectively equivalent. This convention permits elementary row changes and independent nonzero column scalings, but does not identify representations using a nontrivial automorphism of \(K\).
knowledge_statements.statement_plain: A matroid is projectively rigid over a field when every labeled representation differs only by invertible row operations and nonzero column scalings.
knowledge_statements.title: Representation Rigidity

intermediate_metadata.review_comment: The definition is internally precise for labeled representations, but rigidity conventions can differ regarding field automorphisms and relabeling; the selected convention requires a source.

children.title: Partial-Field Universality
children.top_down_role: Coordination of field-specific representations through universal partial-field data.

assumptions_latex: \(M\) is a finite matroid admitting a partial-field representation.
knowledge_statements.conclusion_latex: Universality means that every partial-field representation of \(M\), up to the stated equivalence, is induced from \(A_M\) by a homomorphism out of \(\mathbb U_M\).

notation.meaning: A universal partial field for M

knowledge_statements.scope_note: Universal mapping property for partial-field representations of a fixed matroid.
knowledge_statements.statement_latex: A partial field \(\mathbb U_M\), equipped with a \(\mathbb U_M\)-representation \(A_M\) of \(M\), is universal for \(M\) when the following property holds: for every partial field \(\mathbb P\) and every \(\mathbb P\)-representation \(A\) of \(M\), there exists a partial-field homomorphism \(\varphi:\mathbb U_M\to\mathbb P\) such that the entrywise image \(\varphi(A_M)\) is equivalent to \(A\) under basis changes, row operations, and nonzero column scalings allowed for partial-field representations. The pair \((\mathbb U_M,A_M)\) is unique only up to the corresponding universal isomorphism.
knowledge_statements.statement_plain: A universal partial field parametrizes every partial-field representation of a fixed matroid through homomorphisms and standard representation equivalences.
knowledge_statements.title: Partial-Field Universality

intermediate_metadata.review_comment: The asserted universal property, existence scope, representation equivalence, and uniqueness formulation are specialized and cannot be validated without an authoritative citation.

children.title: Characteristic-Set Realizability
children.top_down_role: Structural boundaries on characteristic sets arising from matroid representations.

knowledge_statements.conclusion_latex: \(S\) is characteristic-set realizable if and only if \(S=\operatorname{Char}(M)\) for some finite matroid \(M\).
knowledge_statements.scope_note: Existential realizability by finite matroids; no classification of realizable sets is asserted.
knowledge_statements.statement_latex: The set \(S\) is characteristic-set realizable when there exists a finite matroid \(M\) such that \[S=\operatorname{Char}(M)=\{\operatorname{char}(K):K\text{ is a field over which }M\text{ is representable}\}.\] Thus realizability requires both directions: every \(c\in S\) occurs as the characteristic of at least one representing field, and no field whose characteristic lies outside \(S\) represents \(M\). The quantifier ranges over all fields, not merely finite fields or prime fields.
knowledge_statements.statement_plain: A set of characteristics is realizable when it is exactly the set of characteristics of fields representing some finite matroid.
knowledge_statements.title: Characteristic-Set Realizability

intermediate_metadata.review_comment: The statement gives a coherent existential definition, but no source establishes the terminology. Its mathematical role is a definition rather than a condition, so the selected content kind also requires correction after sourcing.

children.title: Graphic-Matroid Recognition

knowledge_statements.title: Graphic-Matroid Recognition
knowledge_statements.scope_note: Decision problem for a finite labeled matroid supplied by an independence oracle.
knowledge_statements.statement_latex: Let \(M=(E,\mathcal I)\) be a finite matroid presented by an independence oracle. The graphic-matroid recognition problem asks whether there exists a finite undirected multigraph \(G\), with a bijection \(\phi:E\to E(G)\), such that \(X\in\mathcal I\) exactly when \(\phi(X)\) is a forest of \(G\). A positive output may additionally return such a graph \(G\) and bijection \(\phi\); loops of \(M\) correspond to graph loops, and parallel matroid elements correspond to parallel graph edges.
knowledge_statements.statement_plain: Decide whether the input matroid is the cycle matroid of a graph and, in the constructive version, return such a graph.
assumptions_latex: Access to \(M\) is through an independence oracle.
knowledge_statements.conclusion_latex: \(M\text{ is graphic}\iff \exists G,\phi\;\forall X\subseteq E:\ X\in\mathcal I\iff \phi(X)\text{ is a forest of }G.\)

notation.meaning: cycle matroid of the graph G
bijection from matroid elements to graph edges

review_flags: Exact recognition theorem and oracle-complexity source are not supplied.

intermediate_metadata.review_comment: The decision-problem definition is mathematically coherent and fits the recognition leaf, but no inspectable source supports the oracle model or constructive-output formulation.

children.title: Cographic-Matroid Recognition
children.top_down_role: Recognition through dual structure, representation access, plus certifying outcomes.

knowledge_statements.title: Cographic-Matroid Recognition
knowledge_statements.scope_note: Recognition through duality with the cycle matroid of a graph.
knowledge_statements.statement_latex: Let \(M=(E,\mathcal I)\) be a finite matroid presented by an independence oracle. The cographic-matroid recognition problem asks whether there exist a finite undirected multigraph \(G\) and a bijection \(\phi:E\to E(G)\) such that \(M\cong M(G)^*\). Equivalently, it asks whether the dual matroid \(M^*\) is graphic. In the constructive version, a positive output returns \(G\) and \(\phi\), thereby representing the cocircuits of \(M\) as the cycles of \(G\).
knowledge_statements.statement_plain: Decide whether the input matroid is the dual of a graph's cycle matroid; construct the graph when requested.
assumptions_latex: Access to \(M\) is through an independence oracle.
knowledge_statements.conclusion_latex: \(M\text{ is cographic}\iff M^*\text{ is graphic}\iff \exists G:\ M\cong M(G)^*.\)
review_flags: Exact constructive recognition source and oracle model require confirmation.

intermediate_metadata.review_comment: The dual characterization is correct and the definition fits the recognition leaf, but the oracle and constructive formulations have no cited source.

children.title: Regular-Matroid Recognition

knowledge_statements.title: Regular-Matroid Recognition
knowledge_statements.scope_note: Decision problem using representability over every field as the regularity criterion.
knowledge_statements.statement_latex: Let \(M=(E,\mathcal I)\) be a finite matroid given by an independence oracle. Regular-matroid recognition asks whether \(M\) is representable over every field. Equivalently, it asks whether \(M\) has a real matrix representation that is projectively equivalent to a totally unimodular matrix. A constructive positive output consists of a totally unimodular matrix \(A\), whose columns are labeled by \(E\), such that \(X\subseteq E\) is independent in \(M\) exactly when the columns \(A_X\) are linearly independent.
knowledge_statements.statement_plain: Decide whether a matroid is representable over every field and, constructively, return a totally unimodular matrix representation.
assumptions_latex: Access to \(M\) is through an independence oracle.
knowledge_statements.conclusion_latex: \(M\text{ is regular}\iff M\text{ is representable over every field}.\)

notation.meaning: submatrix formed by columns labeled by X

review_flags: A source for the equivalence and the precise recognition algorithm is required.

intermediate_metadata.review_comment: The regularity criterion and constructive matrix formulation require an authoritative source, particularly for the oracle-input reconstruction claim and the projective-equivalence wording.

children.title: Recognition-Class Relationships
children.top_down_role: Containments, dual correspondences, plus boundaries separating the three recognition tasks.

knowledge_statements.title: Recognition-Class Relationships
knowledge_statements.scope_note: Containment and duality relations among graphic, cographic, and regular matroids.
knowledge_statements.statement_latex:
For every finite matroid \(M\), graphicness and cographicness are exchanged by duality, while regularity is preserved by duality. Every graphic matroid and every cographic matroid is regular. Consequently,
\[
M\text{ graphic}\iff M^*\text{ cographic},\qquad M\text{ regular}\iff M^*\text{ regular},
\]
and
\[
\{\text{graphic matroids}\}\cup\{\text{cographic matroids}\}\subseteq\{\text{regular matroids}\}.
\]
Neither inclusion of the graphic or cographic class in the regular class is an equality.
knowledge_statements.statement_plain: Graphic and cographic classes are dual; both lie properly inside the dual-closed class of regular matroids.
knowledge_statements.conclusion_latex: \(M\text{ graphic}\iff M^*\text{ cographic}\), and graphic or cographic \(M\) implies regular \(M\).

knowledge_statements.title: Field-Representability Decision Problems
knowledge_statements.scope_note: Representability over a fixed field for an oracle-presented finite matroid.
knowledge_statements.statement_latex:
Fix a field \(\mathbb F\). Given a finite matroid \(M=(E,\mathcal I)\), the \(\mathbb F\)-representability decision problem asks whether there exist an integer \(r\) and a matrix \(A\in\mathbb F^{r\times E}\), with columns labeled by \(E\), such that for every \(X\subseteq E\),
\[
X\in\mathcal I\iff \operatorname{rank}_{\mathbb F}(A_X)=|X|.
\]
The constructive version must return such a matrix when the answer is positive; its computational complexity depends essentially on how \(M\) and \(\mathbb F\) are encoded.
knowledge_statements.statement_plain: For a fixed field, decide whether the matroid's independent sets are exactly the linearly independent column sets of some matrix.
assumptions_latex: \(\mathbb F\) and its effective encoding are fixed or supplied explicitly.
knowledge_statements.conclusion_latex: \(M\text{ is }\mathbb F\text{-representable}\iff \exists A\in\mathbb F^{r\times E}\;\forall X\subseteq E:\ X\in\mathcal I\iff \operatorname{rank}_{\mathbb F}(A_X)=|X|.\)

notation.meaning: columns of A indexed by X

review_flags: Complexity varies with the field and input model; no precise source locator was supplied.

intermediate_metadata.review_comment: The fixed-field representability decision problem is precisely stated and definition is an appropriate content kind, but no source supports the formulation or its encoding qualification.

children.title: Representation Reconstruction
children.top_down_role: Recovery of a representation from oracle data, structural data, or partial representation data.

knowledge_statements.title: Representation Reconstruction
knowledge_statements.scope_note: Oracle-to-matrix reconstruction over a specified field.
knowledge_statements.statement_latex:
Input a finite matroid \(M=(E,\mathcal I)\) through an independence oracle and a field \(\mathbb F\), under the promise that \(M\) is \(\mathbb F\)-representable. A representation-reconstruction algorithm queries the oracle and either outputs a matrix \(A\in\mathbb F^{r(M)\times E}\) satisfying
\[
X\in\mathcal I\iff \operatorname{rank}_{\mathbb F}(A_X)=|X|\quad\text{for every }X\subseteq E,
\]
or reports that reconstruction is unsupported under its stated field or access model. Correctness requires every returned matrix to represent the labeled input matroid.
knowledge_statements.statement_plain: Given oracle access and a representability promise, construct a labeled matrix whose column dependencies reproduce the matroid.
assumptions_latex: An independence oracle for \(M\) is available.
knowledge_statements.conclusion_latex: \(A\text{ output}\implies M(A)=M.\)
review_flags: Existence and complexity of reconstruction depend on the field and oracle model.
A concrete reconstruction algorithm source is needed.

intermediate_metadata.review_comment: The record gives an output specification rather than a concrete reconstruction algorithm. Whether reconstruction is possible from an independence oracle depends materially on the field and access model, so a precise sourced algorithm is required.

children.title: Representation Equivalence
children.top_down_role: Comparison regimes for deciding whether representations encode the same matroid structure.

knowledge_statements.title: Representation Equivalence
knowledge_statements.scope_note: Projective equivalence for labeled matrix representations over one fixed field.
knowledge_statements.statement_latex:
Let \(A,B\in\mathbb F^{r\times E}\) be full-row-rank matrices whose columns share the same labels. They are projectively equivalent over \(\mathbb F\) if there exist \(P\in\operatorname{GL}_r(\mathbb F)\) and a nonsingular diagonal matrix \(D\in\mathbb F^{E\times E}\) such that
\[
B=PAD.
\]
Thus equivalence permits invertible row operations and independent nonzero scaling of columns, but no relabeling. Projectively equivalent matrices represent the same labeled matroid because these operations preserve all column-dependence relations.
knowledge_statements.statement_plain: Two labeled representations are equivalent when invertible row operations and nonzero column scalings transform one into the other.
assumptions_latex: \(A\) and \(B\) have full row rank over the same field.
Their columns have the same fixed labels.
knowledge_statements.conclusion_latex: \(B=PAD\implies M(B)=M(A).\)

notation.meaning: invertible r by r matrices over the field

review_flags: A source should confirm whether the intended convention also identifies field automorphisms.

intermediate_metadata.review_comment: The stated labeled projective-equivalence convention is coherent, but no source establishes that this leaf intends equivalence without relabeling or field automorphisms.

children.title: Reconstruction Uniqueness
children.top_down_role: Conditions governing canonical recovery or uniqueness up to accepted transformations.

knowledge_statements.title: Reconstruction Uniqueness
knowledge_statements.scope_note: Uniqueness relative to labeled projective equivalence over a fixed field.
knowledge_statements.statement_latex: A finite \(\mathbb F\)-representable matroid \(M=(E,\mathcal I)\) is uniquely representable over \(\mathbb F\) if any two full-row-rank \(\mathbb F\)-matrices \(A\) and \(B\), with columns labeled by \(E\) and satisfying \(M(A)=M(B)=M\), are projectively equivalent. Explicitly, uniqueness means that there exist \(P\in\operatorname{GL}_{r(M)}(\mathbb F)\) and a nonsingular diagonal matrix \(D\) such that \(B=PAD\). Hence any correct reconstruction determines one equivalence class, not necessarily one literal matrix.
knowledge_statements.statement_plain: A matroid is uniquely representable when all its labeled matrices over the field differ only by row operations and column scalings.
assumptions_latex: \(M\) is finite and representable over \(\mathbb F\).
Representations use the same element labels.
knowledge_statements.conclusion_latex: \(\forall A,B:\ M(A)=M(B)=M\implies \exists P,D:\ B=PAD.\)
review_flags: No supplied locator directly supports unique representability.

children.title: Representation Ambiguity
children.top_down_role: Nonuniqueness, incompatible reconstructions, plus field-sensitive ambiguity.

knowledge_statements.title: Representation Ambiguity
knowledge_statements.scope_note: Failure of reconstruction uniqueness over a fixed labeled field.
knowledge_statements.statement_latex: Representation ambiguity occurs when a finite matroid \(M\) has two \(\mathbb F\)-representations \(A\) and \(B\) with the same labeled ground set but no matrices \(P\in\operatorname{GL}_{r(M)}(\mathbb F)\) and nonsingular diagonal \(D\) satisfy \(B=PAD\). In that case an independence oracle determines the matroid but does not determine a unique projective representation. For fields with suitable distinct cross-ratios, rank-two uniform matroids provide families of such inequivalent representations.
knowledge_statements.statement_plain: The same labeled matroid may have inequivalent matrix representations, so its independence data need not determine a unique reconstruction.
assumptions_latex: \(M\) has at least two representations over \(\mathbb F\).
Equivalence permits only row operations and nonzero column scalings.
knowledge_statements.conclusion_latex: \(M(A)=M(B)=M\ \land\ \nexists P,D:\ B=PAD\implies M\text{ is not uniquely }\mathbb F\text{-representable}.\)
review_flags: The cross-ratio example requires a precise field-dependent source and formulation.

intermediate_metadata.review_comment: The failure-of-uniqueness criterion fits the failure-boundary leaf, but the cross-ratio example and its field conditions are too source-dependent to approve without a precise locator.

knowledge_statements.statement_title: Minor monotonicity of the matroid connectivity function
knowledge_statements.scope_note: Connectivity-function behavior under deletion and contraction, with the equivalent preservation of separating partitions in minors.
knowledge_statements.statement_latex: Let M be a matroid on E, let X,C,D\subseteq E, and suppose C\cap D=\varnothing. Then \lambda_{M\setminus D/C}\!\left(X\setminus(D\cup C)\right)\leq \lambda_M(X). knowledge_statements.statement_plain: Deleting and contracting disjoint sets cannot increase the connectivity value on the surviving part of a set. Equivalently, a k-separating partition restricts to a k-separating partition in every minor.

knowledge_statements.statement_title: Connectivity Function Under Rank-Preserving Deletion
knowledge_statements.scope_note: Gives closure characterizations of two connectivity-function equalities after deleting a disjoint set without reducing rank.
knowledge_statements.statement_latex: Let $M$ be a matroid with ground set $E$, and let $X,D\subseteq E$ be disjoint. Suppose that $r(M\setminus D)=r(M)$. Then: (i) $\lambda_{M\setminus D}(X)=\lambda_M(X)$ if and only if $D\subseteq\operatorname{cl}_M(E\setminus(X\cup D))$; and (ii) $\lambda_{M\setminus D}(X)=\lambda_M(X\cup D)$ if and only if $D\subseteq\operatorname{cl}_M(X)$.
knowledge_statements.statement_plain: Let X and D be disjoint subsets of a matroid's ground set, and suppose deleting D does not reduce the matroid's rank. The connectivity of X is unchanged by the deletion exactly when D lies in the closure of the remaining complement; the deleted-matroid connectivity of X equals the original connectivity of X union D exactly when D lies in the closure of X.
