knowledge_statements.statement_title: Exact connectivity changes under one-element deletion and contraction
knowledge_statements.scope_note: One-element minor operations change connectivity by zero or one, with exact closure, coclosure, loop, and coloop characterizations.
knowledge_statements.statement_latex:
Let z\in E(M), and let (X,Y) partition E(M)\setminus\{z\}, allowing empty parts. Then \lambda_M(X)-1\leq\lambda_{M\setminus z}(X)\leq\lambda_M(X) and \lambda_M(X)-1\leq\lambda_{M/z}(X)\leq\lambda_M(X). Moreover: \lambda_{M\setminus z}(X)=\lambda_M(X) iff z\in\operatorname{cl}_M(Y) or z is a coloop, iff z
otin\operatorname{cl}_M^*(X) or z is a coloop; \lambda_{M\setminus z}(X)=\lambda_M(X)-1 iff z
otin\operatorname{cl}_M(Y) and z is not a coloop, iff z\in\operatorname{cl}_M^*(X) and z is not a coloop; \lambda_{M/z}(X)=\lambda_M(X) iff z\in\operatorname{cl}_M^*(Y) or z is a loop, iff z
otin\operatorname{cl}_M(X) or z is a loop; and \lambda_{M/z}(X)=\lambda_M(X)-1 iff z
otin\operatorname{cl}_M^*(Y) and z is not a loop, iff z\in\operatorname{cl}_M(X) and z is not a loop.
knowledge_statements.statement_plain: Deleting or contracting one element lowers the connectivity value by either zero or one. The two cases are characterized exactly by closure or coclosure membership, with coloops exceptional for deletion and loops exceptional for contraction.
knowledge_statements.conclusion_latex: \lambda_M(X)-1\leq\lambda_{M\setminus z}(X)\leq\lambda_M(X)\quad\text{and}\quad\lambda_M(X)-1\leq\lambda_{M/z}(X)\leq\lambda_M(X),\text{ with the stated equivalences}

knowledge_statements.statement_title: Size bounds for minor-minimal bridges of exact 1- and 2-separations

Let $(X,Y)$ be an exact $k$-separation of a matroid $N$, and let $M$ be a minor-minimal matroid that bridges $(X,Y)$. Then
\[
k=1\implies |E(M)|\le |E(N)|+2,

k=2\implies |E(M)|\le |E(N)|+5.
\]

knowledge_statements.conclusion_latex: (k=1\Rightarrow |E(M)|\le |E(N)|+2)\land(k=2\Rightarrow |E(M)|\le |E(N)|+5)

knowledge_statements.statement_title: Equivalent base-exchange axioms
knowledge_statements.scope_note: Characterizes nonempty collections that are the bases of a matroid.
knowledge_statements.statement_latex: Let $S$ be a set and let $\mathcal B\subseteq 2^S$ be nonempty. The following are equivalent: (i) $\mathcal B$ is the collection of bases of a matroid on $S$; (ii) for all $B,B'\in\mathcal B$ and every $x\in B'\setminus B$, there exists $y\in B\setminus B'$ such that $B'-x+y\in\mathcal B$; (iii) for all $B,B'\in\mathcal B$ and every $x\in B'\setminus B$, there exists $y\in B\setminus B'$ such that $B-y+x\in\mathcal B$.
knowledge_statements.statement_plain: A nonempty family of subsets is the base family of a matroid exactly when it satisfies either of two equivalent one-element exchange formulations: an element of one base absent from another can be exchanged into the second base, or symmetrically an element can be exchanged out of the first base.
knowledge_statements.conclusion_latex: \mathcal B\text{ is a matroid base family}\iff\text{condition (ii)}\iff\text{condition (iii)}.

knowledge_statements.title: Connected Matroids
knowledge_statements.scope_note: Connectivity defined by absence of a nontrivial direct-sum separation.
knowledge_statements.statement_latex:
Let \(M=(E,r)\) be a finite matroid with \(|E|\ge 2\), and define
\[
\lambda_M(X)=r(X)+r(E\setminus X)-r(E).
\]
The matroid \(M\) is connected if \(\lambda_M(X)>0\) for every nonempty proper subset \(X\subset E\). Equivalently, \(M\) admits no partition \(E=X\mathbin{\dot\cup}Y\) into nonempty sets with \(r(X)+r(Y)=r(E)\); equivalently, every pair of distinct elements belongs to a common circuit.
knowledge_statements.statement_plain: A matroid is connected when no nonempty partition separates its rank additively; equivalently, every two elements share a circuit.
knowledge_statements.conclusion_latex: \(M\text{ connected}\iff \forall\varnothing\ne X\subsetneq E:\ \lambda_M(X)>0.\)

knowledge_statements.statement_title: Two-cocircuit forced by deletion-critical elements of a circuit
knowledge_statements.scope_note: Relates disconnection after deleting specified circuit elements to the existence of a two-element cocircuit among those elements.
knowledge_statements.statement_latex: Let \(M\) be a connected matroid with at least two elements, and let \(\{e_1,e_2,\ldots,e_m\}\) be a circuit of \(M\). If \(M\setminus e_i\) is disconnected for every \(i\in\{1,\ldots,m-1\}\), then \(\{e_1,e_2,\ldots,e_{m-1}\}\) contains a two-element cocircuit of \(M\).

knowledge_statements.statement_title: Partition displayed by a circuit- or cocircuit-labelled vertex
knowledge_statements.scope_note: Defines vertex display for a partition of the ground set in a canonical tree decomposition.
knowledge_statements.statement_latex: Let $T$ be the canonical tree decomposition of a 2-connected matroid $M$, and let $v$ be a vertex of $T$ labelled by a circuit or a cocircuit. Let $G_1,\ldots,G_k$ be the components of $T-v$, and let $Z_i\subseteq E(M)$ correspond to $G_i$. A partition $(X,Y)$ of $E(M)$ with $|X|,|Y|\ge 2$ is displayed by $v$ if, for every $i$, either $Z_i\subseteq X$ or $Z_i\subseteq Y$.
knowledge_statements.statement_plain: Delete a circuit- or cocircuit-labelled vertex v from the canonical tree decomposition. A ground-set partition with both parts containing at least two elements is displayed by v when each set corresponding to a resulting tree component lies wholly in one part of the partition.
assumptions_latex: $T$ is the canonical tree decomposition of $M$.
$v\in V(T)$ is labelled by a circuit or a cocircuit.
$G_1,\ldots,G_k$ are the components of $T-v$, with corresponding subsets $Z_i\subseteq E(M)$.
knowledge_statements.conclusion_latex: (X,Y)\text{ is displayed by }v\iff \forall i\in\{1,\ldots,k\},\; Z_i\subseteq X\text{ or }Z_i\subseteq Y.

knowledge_statements.statement_latex: Let $\mathcal M$ be closed under isomorphism and minors. Let $M\in\mathcal M$ be a smallest minor-minimal bridge for $(X,Y)$, write $N=M\setminus D/C$, and order $E(M)\setminus E(N)$ as $(v_1,\ldots,v_t)$ so that $\lambda_M(X\cup\{v_1,\ldots,v_i\})=k$ for every $i\in\{0,,,,,,,, ,	,,,,,,,,,,,,,,,,\ldots,t\}$. Y\text{ is closed and coclosed in }N
M\in\mathcal M\text{ is a smallest minor-minimal bridge for }(X,Y)
knowledge_statements.conclusion_latex: \forall i\in\{0,1,\ldots,t\},\ M[D,C;\{v_1,\ldots,v_i\}]\text{ is 3-connected}

knowledge_statements.statement_title: Structure and representability of R_6
knowledge_statements.scope_note: Extraction-grounded profile of R_6.
knowledge_statements.statement_latex: R_6\cong U_{2,4}\oplus_2U_{2,4}. It is connected but not 3-connected and is \mathbb F-representable if and only if |\mathbb F|\ge3. It is near-regular but neither graphic, cographic, nor regular. It is transversal, a strict gammoid, and a gammoid; it is identically self-dual and has a transitive automorphism group. It has P_6 as a relaxation. A connected GF(4)-representable matroid M is uniquely GF(4)-representable if and only if it has no 2-separation induced by the unique 2-separation of an R_6-minor. The matroid R_6 is algebraic over every field.
knowledge_statements.statement_plain: R_6 is the 2-sum of two copies of U_{2,4}. It has the stated connectivity, representation, class, duality, symmetry, relaxation, unique-GF(4)-representability, and algebraicity properties.
assumptions_latex: \mathbb F\text{ is a field for the field-representability assertion}
M\text{ is connected and GF}(4)\text{-representable for the uniqueness characterization}
knowledge_statements.conclusion_latex: R_6\text{ has the stated properties, and }M\text{ is uniquely GF}(4)\text{-representable exactly under the stated absence condition.}

knowledge_statements.statement_title: Unique decomposition into connected components
knowledge_statements.scope_note: Existence and uniqueness up to permutation of the direct-sum decomposition into nonempty connected matroids.
knowledge_statements.statement_latex: If \(T_1,\ldots,T_k\) are the connected components of a matroid \(M\), then \[M=(M|T_1)\oplus\cdots\oplus(M|T_k).\] Moreover, if \[M_1\oplus\cdots\oplus M_n=N_1\oplus\cdots\oplus N_m,\] where every \(M_i\) and \(N_j\) is connected and nonempty, then \(m=n\) and there is a permutation \(\sigma\in S_n\) such that \(M_i=N_{\sigma(i)}\) for every \(i\).
knowledge_statements.statement_plain: Every matroid is the direct sum of its restrictions to its connected components, and any decomposition into nonempty connected summands is unique up to reordering.
assumptions_latex: T_1,\ldots,T_k\text{ are the connected components of }M
M_i\text{ and }N_j\text{ are connected and nonempty in the uniqueness assertion}

knowledge_statements.statement_title: Element-Preserving Splitter Classification
knowledge_statements.scope_note: Classification up to simultaneous dualization of a minimal 3-connected extension retaining a specified element and minor.
knowledge_statements.statement_latex: Let \(N\) be a 3-connected minor of a 3-connected matroid \(M\), with \(|E(N)|\ge 4\), and let \(e\in E(M)\setminus E(N)\). Suppose no 3-connected proper minor of \(M\) both uses \(e\) and has \(N\) as a minor. Put \(n=|E(M)\setminus E(N)|\). For some \((N_1,M_1)\in\{(N,M),(N^*,M^*)\}\), exactly one of the following alternatives holds: (i) \(n=1\) and \(N_1=M_1\setminus e\); (ii) \(n=2\), \(N_1=M_1\setminus e/f\), and some \(x\in E(N_1)\) makes \(\{e,f,x\}\) a triangle of \(M_1\); (iii) \(n=3\), \(N_1=M_1\setminus e,g/f\), some \(x\in E(N_1)\) makes \(\{e,f,x\}\) a triangle and \(\{f,g,x\}\) a triad of \(M_1\), and \(M_1\setminus e\) is 3-connected; (iv) \(n=3\), \(\{e,f,g\}\) is a triad of \(M_1\), \(N_1=M_1\setminus e,f,g\), and distinct \(x,y\in E(N_1)\) make \(\{e,g,x\}\) and \(\{e,f,y\}\) triangles of \(M_1\); or (v) \(n=4\), \(N_1=M_1\setminus e,g/f,h\), some \(x\in E(N_1)\) makes \(\{e,f,x\}\) and \(\{g,h,x\}\) triangles and \(\{f,g,x\}\) a triad of \(M_1\), while \(M_1\setminus e\) and \(M_1\setminus e/f\) are 3-connected.
knowledge_statements.statement_plain: If a 3-connected matroid M is minimal among its proper 3-connected minors that retain a designated element e and a prescribed 3-connected minor N of at least four elements, then, after possibly dualizing M and N, their ground-set difference has size one through four and one of five specified deletion-contraction configurations occurs, with the stated triangle, triad, and residual 3-connectivity conditions.
assumptions_latex: N\text{ is a 3-connected minor of the 3-connected matroid }M
\nexists\,M'\text{ a 3-connected proper minor of }M\text{ that uses }e\text{ and has an }N\text{-minor}
knowledge_statements.conclusion_latex: \exists (N_1,M_1)\in\{(N,M),(N^*,M^*)\}\text{ satisfying one of alternatives (i)--(v).}

knowledge_statements.statement_title: Displayed partitions and subgraph-associated element sets
knowledge_statements.scope_note: Ground-set information represented by edges and connected subgraphs of a matroid tree decomposition.
knowledge_statements.statement_latex: Let $T$ be a tree decomposition of a matroid $M$. Every $x\in E(M)$ lies in the ground set of the label of a unique vertex of $T$. Consequently, every edge $e_i$ of $T$ induces a partition $(X_i,Y_i)$ of $E(M)$, which is said to be displayed by $e_i$. If $G$ is a connected subgraph of $T$, the subset of $E(M)$ corresponding to $G$ consists of the elements lying in the ground set of some vertex label in $G$.
knowledge_statements.statement_plain: Each original matroid element belongs to exactly one vertex label in a tree decomposition. An edge displays the ground-set partition induced by the two sides of the tree, and a connected subgraph corresponds to the original elements appearing in its vertex labels.
assumptions_latex: $T$ is a tree decomposition of a matroid $M$.
knowledge_statements.conclusion_latex: Every edge of $T$ displays a well-defined partition of $E(M)$, and every connected subgraph of $T$ determines a well-defined corresponding subset of $E(M)$.

knowledge_statements.scope_note: Characterizes modularity through restriction components and derives connectedness in the connected case.
knowledge_statements.statement_latex: Let \(M\) be a simple matroid, let \(X\) be a flat of \(M\), and let \(X_1,\ldots,X_k\) be the components of \(M|X\). Then \(X\) is modular if and only if \(M\) has distinct components \(M_1,\ldots,M_k\) such that \(X_i\) is a modular flat of \(M_i\) for every \(i\). knowledge_statements.conclusion_latex: The asserted reduced decomposition is called the canonical tree decomposition of $M$, and $M$ can be reconstructed from its pieces using 2-sums along the indicated common elements.

knowledge_statements.statement_title: Every tree-decomposition vertex label is realized as a minor
knowledge_statements.scope_note: Minor realization of a vertex label in a tree decomposition of a 2-connected matroid.
knowledge_statements.statement_latex: Let a matroid $N$ label a vertex $v$ of a tree decomposition $T$ of a 2-connected matroid $M$. Let $f_1,\ldots,f_m$ be the edges of $T$ incident with $v$, and let $G_i$ be the component of $T-v$ containing the other endpoint of $f_i$. For each $i$, choose $x_i$ in the subset of $E(M)$ corresponding to $G_i$. Then there exist subsets $U,V\subseteq E(M)\setminus\{x_1,\ldots,x_m\}$ such that $N$ is obtained from $M\setminus U/V$ by relabelling each $x_i$ as $f_i$. In particular, $M$ has a minor isomorphic to $N$.
knowledge_statements.statement_plain: Every matroid labelling a vertex of a tree decomposition of a 2-connected matroid is isomorphic to a minor of the original matroid. One representative element can be retained from each incident branch and relabelled as the corresponding decomposition edge.
assumptions_latex: The edges incident with $v$ are $f_1,\ldots,f_m$, and $G_i$ is the associated component of $T-v$.
For every $i$, $x_i$ lies in the subset of $E(M)$ corresponding to $G_i$.
knowledge_statements.conclusion_latex: There exist $U,V\subseteq E(M)\setminus\{x_1,\ldots,x_m\}$ such that relabelling each $x_i$ as $f_i$ in $M\setminus U/V$ yields $N$; hence $M$ has a minor isomorphic to $N$.

knowledge_statements.statement_title: Tree decomposition of a 2-connected matroid
knowledge_statements.scope_note: Defines a matroid-labelled tree whose edge interfaces encode iterated 2-sums reconstructing the matroid.
knowledge_statements.statement_latex: A tree decomposition of a 2-connected matroid \(M\) is a matroid-labelled tree \(T\) with \(V(T)=\{M_1,\ldots,M_k\}\) and \(E(T)=\{e_1,\ldots,e_{k-1}\}\) such that: (i) \(E(M)=\left(\bigcup_{i=1}^kE(M_i)\right)-\{e_1,\ldots,e_{k-1}\}\); (ii) \(|E(M_i)|\geq3\) for every \(i\), unless \(|E(M)|<3\), in which case \(k=1\) and \(M_1=M\); and (iii) \(M\) labels the single vertex of \(T/e_1,\ldots,e_{k-1}\).
knowledge_statements.statement_plain: A tree decomposition of a 2-connected matroid is a matroid-labelled tree whose pieces cover the original ground set apart from their interface labels, satisfy the stated minimum-size condition and small-matroid exception, and reconstruct the matroid after all tree edges are contracted by 2-sums.
knowledge_statements.conclusion_latex: E(M)=\left(\bigcup_{i=1}^kE(M_i)\right)-E(T),\quad |E(M_i)|\geq3\text{ subject to the stated exception, and }T/e_1,\ldots,e_{k-1}\text{ has sole label }M.

knowledge_statements.statement_title: Blocks and circuit characterizations of connected matroids
knowledge_statements.scope_note: Defines matroid blocks through circuit-hypergraph components and records associated connectivity characterizations, including the graphic specialization.
knowledge_statements.statement_latex: If the circuit hypergraph \(\mathcal C_M\) of a matroid \(M\) on \(S\) is disconnected with components inducing \(S=S_1\dot\cup\cdots\dot\cup S_k\), \(k\ge2\), then \(M=\bigoplus_{i=1}^k M|S_i\); the connected matroids \(M|S_i\) are the blocks of \(M\). Moreover, \(M\) is connected if and only if every two distinct elements of \(S\) lie in a common circuit. Consequently, for a graph \(G\) with at least two edges, its circuit matroid is connected if and only if \(G\) is 2-connected.
knowledge_statements.statement_plain: The components of a disconnected circuit hypergraph partition the ground set and yield a direct-sum decomposition into connected restrictions called blocks. A matroid is connected exactly when every pair of distinct elements lies in a common circuit; for a graph with at least two edges, this is equivalent to 2-connectivity of the graph.
assumptions_latex: \mathcal C_M\text{ is the hypergraph whose hyperedges are the circuits of }M.
\text{For the block decomposition, }\mathcal C_M\text{ is disconnected and has }k\ge2\text{ components}.
\text{For the graphic specialization, }G\text{ has at least two edges}.
knowledge_statements.conclusion_latex: M=\bigoplus_{i=1}^k M|S_i,\quad M|S_i\text{ are the blocks of }M;\qquad M\text{ connected}\iff \forall e\ne f\in S\,\exists C\in\mathcal C_M:\{e,f\}\subseteq C;\qquad M(G)\text{ connected}\iff G\text{ is 2-connected}.

knowledge_statements.statement_title: Internal 3-connectivity and 3-connectivity up to series or parallel couples
knowledge_statements.scope_note: Defines refined connectivity regimes through the allowable sides of their 2-separations.
knowledge_statements.statement_latex: A matroid is internally 3-connected precisely when it is 2-connected and has no non-minimal 2-separations; consequently, every 2-separation corresponds to a 2-circuit or a 2-cocircuit. A series couple is a series class containing exactly two elements. A matroid \(N\) is 3-connected up to series couples when it is 2-connected, has at least six elements, and every 2-separation \((X,Y)\) has \(X\) or \(Y\) equal to a series couple. A parallel couple is a parallel class containing exactly two elements, and \(N\) is 3-connected up to parallel couples when \(N^*\) is 3-connected up to series couples. Either couple condition implies that \(N\) has no non-minimal 2-separations.
knowledge_statements.statement_plain: Internal 3-connectivity means 2-connectivity without non-minimal 2-separations. A series or parallel couple is a corresponding class of exactly two elements. A matroid is 3-connected up to series couples when it is 2-connected, has at least six elements, and one side of every 2-separation is a series couple; the parallel-couple version is defined by duality. Either condition excludes non-minimal 2-separations.
knowledge_statements.conclusion_latex: N\text{ satisfies the stated refined connectivity definition, and either couple regime implies that }N\text{ has no non-minimal 2-separations}

knowledge_statements.statement_title: Characterizations and dual invariance of connected matroids
knowledge_statements.scope_note: Equivalent rank and circuit criteria for matroid connectedness, together with invariance under duality.
knowledge_statements.statement_latex: Let \(M=(S,\mathcal I)\) be a matroid. Then \(M\) is connected if and only if \(r_M(U)+r_M(S\setminus U)>r_M(S)\) for every nonempty proper subset \(U\subset S\). Equivalently, for every \(s,t\in S\), there is a circuit \(C\) of \(M\) containing both \(s\) and \(t\). Moreover, \(M\) is connected if and only if \(M^*\) is connected.
knowledge_statements.statement_plain: A matroid is connected exactly when every nontrivial partition of its ground set has rank sum strictly greater than the total rank. Equivalently, every two elements lie in a common circuit. Connectedness is invariant under matroid duality.
knowledge_statements.conclusion_latex: M\text{ is connected}\iff \forall\,\varnothing\ne U\subsetneq S,\ r_M(U)+r_M(S\setminus U)>r_M(S)\iff \forall s,t\in S\ \exists C\in\mathcal C(M):\{s,t\}\subseteq C,\qquad M\text{ is connected}\iff M^*\text{ is connected}.

knowledge_statements.title: Two-Separations
knowledge_statements.scope_note: Standard exact two-separation defined by the matroid connectivity function.
knowledge_statements.statement_latex:
Let \(M=(E,r)\) be a finite matroid. A two-separation of \(M\) is a partition \((X,E\setminus X)\) such that
\[
|X|\ge 2,\qquad |E\setminus X|\ge 2,\qquad \lambda_M(X)=1,
\]
where \(\lambda_M(X)=r(X)+r(E\setminus X)-r(E)\).
knowledge_statements.statement_plain: A two-separation partitions the ground set into two sides of size at least two whose ranks exceed the total rank by exactly one.
knowledge_statements.conclusion_latex: \((X,E\setminus X)\text{ is a two-separation}\iff |X|,|E\setminus X|\ge 2\ \land\ \lambda_M(X)=1.\)

knowledge_statements.title: One-Sum versus Two-Sum Boundaries
knowledge_statements.scope_note: Rank-connectivity boundary distinguishing direct-sum separations from two-separations.
knowledge_statements.statement_latex:
Let \(M=(E,r)\) be finite and let \(E=X\mathbin{\dot\cup}Y\) with \(X,Y\ne\varnothing\). The partition is a one-sum boundary exactly when
\[
\lambda_M(X)=0,
\]
in which case \(M=M|X\oplus M|Y\). If instead \(|X|,|Y|\ge2\) and \(\lambda_M(X)=1\), the partition is a two-separation. Thus connectivity excludes one-sum boundaries but does not exclude two-separations.
knowledge_statements.statement_plain: Connectivity value zero gives a direct-sum split, whereas value one with both sides of size at least two defines a two-separation.
knowledge_statements.conclusion_latex: \(\lambda_M(X)=0\iff M=M|X\oplus M|Y\), while \(|X|,|Y|\ge2\land\lambda_M(X)=1\) defines a two-separation.

knowledge_statements.statement_title: Trichotomy for maximal fans in 3-connected matroids
knowledge_statements.scope_note: Classifies maximal fans and identifies the non-essential elements in the long-fan case; the subsequent figure discussion is an example and is excluded.
knowledge_statements.statement_latex: Let M be a 3-connected matroid with |E(M)|\ge 4, and let S be a maximal fan in M. Exactly one of the following holds: (i) M is a wheel or a whirl; (ii) S is a triangle or triad containing at least two non-essential elements; (iii) |S|>3 and S contains exactly two non-essential elements, which are the first and last elements in every fan ordering of S.
knowledge_statements.statement_plain: Exactly one of three alternatives holds for a maximal fan in a 3-connected matroid with at least four elements: the matroid is a wheel or whirl; the fan is a triangle or triad with at least two non-essential elements; or the fan has more than three elements and exactly two non-essential elements, located at its two ends in every fan ordering.
assumptions_latex: S\text{ is a maximal fan in }M
knowledge_statements.conclusion_latex: \text{Exactly one of (i)--(iii) holds; in case (iii), the two non-essential elements are the first and last elements in every fan ordering of }S.

knowledge_statements.statement_title: Maximal-fan existence and uniqueness for essential elements
knowledge_statements.scope_note: Preserves the one-way uniqueness guarantee and all listed exceptional configurations.
knowledge_statements.statement_latex: Let M be a 3-connected matroid and let e be an essential element of M. Then e lies in a maximal fan S in M. Moreover, S is unique unless one of the following holds: (i) every maximal fan containing e is a triangle and every two such triangles meet in \{e\}; (ii) every maximal fan containing e is a triad and every two such triads meet in \{e\}; or (iii) e lies in exactly three maximal fans, each having exactly five elements, their union X has exactly six elements, and the restriction or contraction of M to X is isomorphic to M(K_4).
knowledge_statements.statement_plain: Every essential element of a 3-connected matroid lies in a maximal fan. The maximal fan is unique unless one of three stated configurations occurs: triangular fans meeting pairwise only at the element, triadic fans meeting pairwise only there, or a specified six-element K4-type configuration of three five-element maximal fans.
knowledge_statements.conclusion_latex: e\text{ lies in a maximal fan }S;\quad S\text{ is unique unless exception (i), (ii), or (iii) holds}.

knowledge_statements.statement_title: Single-element change in the matroid connectivity function
knowledge_statements.scope_note: Gives the sharp one-step bound and closure–coclosure characterizations for adjoining an element to one side of a partition.
knowledge_statements.statement_latex: Let \(z\in E(M)\), and let \((X,Y)\) partition \(E(M)\setminus\{z\}\), with possibly empty parts. Then \[\lambda_M(X)-1\leq\lambda_M(X\cup\{z\})\leq\lambda_M(X)+1.\] Moreover, within each line the conditions are equivalent: \[\lambda_M(X\cup\{z\})=\lambda_M(X)\iff z\text{ is in exactly one of }\operatorname{cl}_M(X),\operatorname{cl}_M^*(X)\] \[\iff z\text{ is in exactly one of }\operatorname{cl}_M(X)\cap\operatorname{cl}_M(Y),\ \operatorname{cl}_M^*(X)\cap\operatorname{cl}_M^*(Y);\] \[\lambda_M(X\cup\{z\})=\lambda_M(X)-1\iff z\in\operatorname{cl}_M(X)\cap\operatorname{cl}_M^*(X)\iff z\notin\operatorname{cl}_M(Y)\cup\operatorname{cl}_M^*(Y);\] \[\lambda_M(X\cup\{z\})=\lambda_M(X)+1\iff z\notin\operatorname{cl}_M(X)\cup\operatorname{cl}_M^*(X)\iff z\in\operatorname{cl}_M(Y)\cap\operatorname{cl}_M^*(Y).\]
knowledge_statements.statement_plain: Adjoining one element changes connectivity by at most one. No change, a decrease by one, and an increase by one have the stated equivalent closure and coclosure characterizations relative to both sides.
knowledge_statements.conclusion_latex: \lambda_M(X)-1\leq\lambda_M(X\cup\{z\})\leq\lambda_M(X)+1,\text{ with the three possible changes characterized by the stated equivalences}

knowledge_statements.statement_title: Deletion–Contraction Connectivity Inequality
knowledge_statements.scope_note: Connectivity-function inequality coupling deletion and contraction at one matroid element.
knowledge_statements.statement_latex: Let \(e\in E(M)\) and let \(X,Y\subseteq E(M)\setminus\{e\}\). Then \[\lambda_{M\setminus e}(X)+\lambda_{M/e}(Y)\geq \lambda_M(X\cap Y)+\lambda_M(X\cup Y\cup\{e\})-1.\]
knowledge_statements.statement_plain: For an element e of a matroid and subsets X and Y avoiding e, the sum of the deletion connectivity of X and contraction connectivity of Y is at least the sum of the original connectivities of their intersection and their union with e, minus one.
knowledge_statements.conclusion_latex: \lambda_{M\setminus e}(X)+\lambda_{M/e}(Y)\geq \lambda_M(X\cap Y)+\lambda_M(X\cup Y\cup\{e\})-1

knowledge_statements.statement_title: Internal matroid connectivity
knowledge_statements.scope_note: Defines internal $(k+1)$-connectivity and records the stated internal three- and four-connectivity consequences.
knowledge_statements.statement_latex: For $k\geq2$, a $k$-connected matroid is internally $(k+1)$-connected if it has no non-minimal $k$-separations. For every $e$ in a $3$-connected matroid $M$, either $M\setminus e$ or $M/e$ is internally $3$-connected. An internally $4$-connected matroid is a $3$-connected matroid whose only $3$-separations have a triangle or a triad as one side.
knowledge_statements.statement_plain: A k-connected matroid is internally (k+1)-connected when it has no non-minimal k-separations. For each element of a 3-connected matroid, either deletion or contraction is internally 3-connected. Internal 4-connectivity means being 3-connected with a triangle or triad on one side of every 3-separation.
assumptions_latex: M\text{ is }k\text{-connected for the general definition}
M\text{ is }3\text{-connected and }e\in E(M)\text{ for the deletion-contraction consequence}
knowledge_statements.conclusion_latex: \begin{aligned}&M\text{ is internally }(k+1)\text{-connected}\iff M\text{ has no non-minimal }k\text{-separations};\\&M\setminus e\text{ is internally }3\text{-connected}\ \lor\ M/e\text{ is internally }3\text{-connected};\\&M\text{ is internally }4\text{-connected}\iff M\text{ is }3\text{-connected and every }3\text{-separation has a triangle or triad as one side}.\end{aligned}

knowledge_statements.statement_title: k-Separations and n-Connected Matroids
knowledge_statements.scope_note: Defines Tutte's hierarchy of matroid separations and connectivity levels.
knowledge_statements.statement_latex: Let $M$ be a matroid with ground set $E$, let $X\subseteq E$, and let $k$ be a positive integer. The set $X$ and the pair $(X,E\setminus X)$ are called $k$-separating when $\lambda_M(X)<k$. A $k$-separating pair is a $k$-separation when $\min\{|X|,|E\setminus X|\}\ge k$. A $1$-separating set is a separator. The matroid $M$ is $2$-connected if and only if it has no $1$-separation. More generally, for $n\ge2$, $M$ is $n$-connected if and only if it has no $k$-separation for every $k\in\{1,\ldots,n-1\}$.
knowledge_statements.statement_plain: A subset and its complementary bipartition are k-separating when the subset has connectivity less than k. The pair is a k-separation when each side has at least k elements. A matroid is n-connected exactly when it has no k-separation for any positive k below n.
assumptions_latex: M\text{ is a matroid with ground set }E
knowledge_statements.conclusion_latex: (X,E\setminus X)\text{ is }k\text{-separating}\iff\lambda_M(X)<k;\quad (X,E\setminus X)\text{ is a }k\text{-separation}\iff\lambda_M(X)<k\ \land\ \min\{|X|,|E\setminus X|\}\ge k;\quad M\text{ is }n\text{-connected}\iff M\text{ has no }k\text{-separation for every }k\in\{1,\ldots,n-1\}

knowledge_statements.statement_title: Fan and fan ordering in a matroid
knowledge_statements.scope_note: Defines fans without combining the definition with later proposition-dependent structural and representability results.
knowledge_statements.statement_latex: Let \(M\) be a simple, cosimple matroid. A subset \(S\subseteq E(M)\) with \(|S|\ge 3\) is a fan if it has an ordering \((s_1,\ldots,s_n)\) such that each consecutive triple \(\{s_i,s_{i+1},s_{i+2}\}\) is a triangle or a triad and successive consecutive triples alternate between triangles and triads. Such an ordering is called a fan ordering of \(S\).
knowledge_statements.statement_plain: In a simple, cosimple matroid, a fan is a set of at least three elements admitting an ordering whose consecutive triples are alternately triangles and triads. The ordering is called a fan ordering.
assumptions_latex: M\text{ is a simple, cosimple matroid}
knowledge_statements.conclusion_latex: S\text{ is a fan precisely when it admits the stated alternating triangle--triad ordering.}

knowledge_statements.statement_title: Graphical Representation of Cycle-Matroid Connectivity
knowledge_statements.scope_note: Expresses cycle-matroid connectivity through shared incident vertices and component counts, with a sharp bound for connected graphs.
knowledge_statements.statement_latex: Let $G$ be a graph without isolated vertices. For every $X\subseteq E(G)$, writing $\omega(H)$ for the number of connected components of $H$, $$\lambda_{M(G)}(X)=|V(G[X])\cap V(G[E(G)\setminus X])|-\omega(G[X])-\omega(G[E(G)\setminus X])+\omega(G).$$ If $G$ is connected and both $X$ and $E(G)\setminus X$ are nonempty, then $$\lambda_{M(G)}(X)\le |V(G[X])\cap V(G[E(G)\setminus X])|-1,$$ with equality if and only if both $G[X]$ and $G[E(G)\setminus X]$ are connected.
knowledge_statements.statement_plain: For a graph without isolated vertices, the connectivity of an edge set in its cycle matroid equals the number of vertices incident with edges on both sides, minus the component counts of the two edge-induced subgraphs, plus the component count of the whole graph. If the graph is connected and both sides are nonempty, this is at most the number of shared vertices minus one, with equality exactly when both side subgraphs are connected.
assumptions_latex: G\text{ is a graph without isolated vertices}
\text{for the bound: }G\text{ is connected and }X\ne\varnothing\text{ and }E(G)\setminus X\ne\varnothing
knowledge_statements.conclusion_latex: \lambda_{M(G)}(X)=|V(G[X])\cap V(G[E(G)\setminus X])|-\omega(G[X])-\omega(G[E(G)\setminus X])+\omega(G);\quad \lambda_{M(G)}(X)\le |V(G[X])\cap V(G[E(G)\setminus X])|-1,\text{ with equality}\iff G[X]\text{ and }G[E(G)\setminus X]\text{ are connected}

knowledge_statements.statement_title: Bixby's lemma
knowledge_statements.scope_note: A deletion-contraction alternative for recovering a three-connected minor after removing series or parallel redundancy.
knowledge_statements.statement_latex: Let $M$ be a $3$-connected matroid and let $e\in E(M)$. Either $M\setminus e$ has no non-minimal $2$-separations and $\operatorname{co}(M\setminus e)$ is $3$-connected, or $M/e$ has no non-minimal $2$-separations and $\operatorname{si}(M/e)$ is $3$-connected.
knowledge_statements.statement_plain: For any element of a 3-connected matroid, either its deletion has no non-minimal 2-separations and becomes 3-connected after cosimplification, or its contraction has no non-minimal 2-separations and becomes 3-connected after simplification.
knowledge_statements.conclusion_latex: \begin{aligned}&\bigl[M\setminus e\text{ has no non-minimal }2\text{-separations and }\operatorname{co}(M\setminus e)\text{ is }3\text{-connected}\bigr]\\&\quad\lor\bigl[M/e\text{ has no non-minimal }2\text{-separations and }\operatorname{si}(M/e)\text{ is }3\text{-connected}\bigr].\end{aligned}

knowledge_statements.statement_title: Fan closure and wheel–whirl recognition
knowledge_statements.scope_note: Gives closure and global-structure consequences for the specified cyclic triangle–triad configuration.
knowledge_statements.statement_latex: Let n\ge 2, let M be connected, and let X=\{x_1,\ldots,x_n\} and Y=\{y_1,\ldots,y_n\} be disjoint subsets of E(M), with subscripts interpreted modulo n. Suppose \{x_i,y_i,x_{i+1}\} is a triangle for 1\le i<n and \{y_j,x_{j+1},y_{j+1}\} is a triad for 1\le j\le n. Then (i) if M is 3-connected, \{x_n,y_n,x_1\} is a triangle; and (ii) if \{x_n,y_n,x_1\} is a triangle, then E(M)=X\cup Y and M is isomorphic to M(\mathcal W_n) or \mathcal W^n, with X as its spokes and Y as its rim.
knowledge_statements.statement_plain: For the specified cyclic sequence of triangles and triads in a connected matroid, 3-connectivity forces the missing final triangle. If that final triangle is present, the configuration exhausts the ground set and the matroid is a wheel or whirl, with X as the spokes and Y as the rim.
assumptions_latex: X=\{x_1,\ldots,x_n\},\quad Y=\{y_1,\ldots,y_n\},\quad X,Y\subseteq E(M),\quad X\cap Y=\varnothing
\{y_j,x_{j+1},y_{j+1}\}\text{ is a triad for }1\le j\le n
knowledge_statements.conclusion_latex: M\text{ 3-connected}\Rightarrow\{x_n,y_n,x_1\}\text{ is a triangle};\quad \{x_n,y_n,x_1\}\text{ a triangle}\Rightarrow E(M)=X\cup Y\text{ and }M\cong M(\mathcal W_n)\text{ or }\mathcal W^n,\text{ with }X\text{ the spokes and }Y\text{ the rim}.

knowledge_statements.title: Three-Connected Matroids
knowledge_statements.scope_note: Finite matroids, using the standard separation definition of 3-connectivity.
knowledge_statements.statement_latex: Let \(M\) be a finite matroid on a ground set \(E\) with rank function \(r\), and define \(\lambda_M(X)=r(X)+r(E\setminus X)-r(E)\). The matroid \(M\) is three-connected if \(|E|\ge 4\) and there is no partition \((X,E\setminus X)\) for which either \(|X|,|E\setminus X|\ge 1\) and \(\lambda_M(X)=0\), or \(|X|,|E\setminus X|\ge 2\) and \(\lambda_M(X)\le 1\). Thus a three-connected matroid has neither a 1-separation nor a 2-separation.
knowledge_statements.statement_plain: A matroid is three-connected when it has at least four elements and admits neither a 1-separation nor a 2-separation.
knowledge_statements.conclusion_latex: \(M\text{ is three-connected}\iff M\text{ has no 1-separation or 2-separation}.\)

knowledge_statements.title: Higher-Order Connectivity
knowledge_statements.scope_note: Finite matroid \(k\)-connectivity defined by exclusion of all lower-order separations.
knowledge_statements.statement_latex: Let \(k\ge 2\), and let \(M\) be a finite matroid on \(E\) with \(|E|\ge 2(k-1)\). For \(1\le j<k\), a \(j\)-separation is a partition \((X,E\setminus X)\) satisfying \(|X|,|E\setminus X|\ge j\) and \(\lambda_M(X)\le j-1\). The matroid \(M\) is \(k\)-connected if it has no \(j\)-separation for any \(j<k\). Equivalently, every \(X\subseteq E\) with \(|X|,|E\setminus X|\ge j\) satisfies \(\lambda_M(X)\ge j\) for each \(1\le j<k\).
knowledge_statements.statement_plain: A finite matroid is k-connected when every separation of order below k is excluded, subject to the usual side-size requirements.
knowledge_statements.conclusion_latex: \(M\text{ is }k\text{-connected}\iff M\text{ has no }j\text{-separation for }1\le j<k.\)

knowledge_statements.title: Connectivity-Level Transitions
knowledge_statements.scope_note: Monotonicity of the finite matroid connectivity hierarchy.
knowledge_statements.statement_latex: Let \(k\ge 2\), and let \(M\) be a finite matroid. Under the convention that \(q\)-connectivity excludes every \(j\)-separation with \(1\le j<q\), \((k+1)\)-connectivity implies \(k\)-connectivity. Thus the connectivity classes form a nested hierarchy. The reverse implication fails in general: a \(k\)-connected matroid possessing a \(k\)-separation is not \((k+1)\)-connected.
knowledge_statements.statement_plain: Every (k+1)-connected matroid is k-connected, while a k-connected matroid with a k-separation is not (k+1)-connected.
knowledge_statements.conclusion_latex: \(M\text{ is }(k+1)\text{-connected}\Longrightarrow M\text{ is }k\text{-connected}.\)

knowledge_statements.statement_title: Tutte's Triangle Lemma
knowledge_statements.scope_note: Derives a triad from the failure of two specified triangle-element deletions to preserve 3-connectivity.
knowledge_statements.statement_latex: Let $M$ be a $3$-connected matroid with $|E(M)|\ge 4$, and suppose that $\{e,f,g\}$ is a triangle of $M$. If neither $M\setminus e$ nor $M\setminus f$ is $3$-connected, then $M$ has a triad containing $e$ and exactly one of $f$ and $g$.
knowledge_statements.statement_plain: In a 3-connected matroid with at least four elements, if deleting either of two specified elements e and f of a triangle destroys 3-connectivity, then a triad contains e and exactly one of f and g.
knowledge_statements.conclusion_latex: \exists T^*\text{ a triad of }M:\ e\in T^*\text{ and }|T^*\cap\{f,g\}|=1

knowledge_statements.statement_title: Criterion for placing one element on either side of an exact separation
knowledge_statements.scope_note: Characterizes when adjoining one element to either side of a partition yields exactly k-separating bipartitions for one common integer k.
knowledge_statements.statement_latex: Let \(z\in E(M)\), and let \((X,Y)\) be a partition of \(E(M)\setminus\{z\}\), where either part may be empty. There exists an integer \(k\) such that both \((X\cup\{z\},Y)\) and \((X,Y\cup\{z\})\) are exactly \(k\)-separating if and only if \[z\in\operatorname{cl}_M(X)\cap\operatorname{cl}_M(Y)\quad\text{or}\quad z\in\operatorname{cl}_M^*(X)\cap\operatorname{cl}_M^*(Y).\]
knowledge_statements.statement_plain: Assigning z to either side produces exactly k-separating bipartitions of one common order precisely when z lies in the closures of both sides or in the coclosures of both sides.
knowledge_statements.conclusion_latex: \exists k\in\mathbb Z:\ (X\cup\{z\},Y)\text{ and }(X,Y\cup\{z\})\text{ are exactly }k\text{-separating}\iff z\in\operatorname{cl}_M(X)\cap\operatorname{cl}_M(Y)\ \lor\ z\in\operatorname{cl}_M^*(X)\cap\operatorname{cl}_M^*(Y)

knowledge_statements.title: Vertical Connectivity
knowledge_statements.scope_note: Rank-based vertical connectivity for finite matroids.
knowledge_statements.statement_latex: Let \(M\) be a finite matroid on \(E\). For an integer \(j\ge 1\), a vertical \(j\)-separation is a partition \((X,E\setminus X)\) such that \(\lambda_M(X)\le j-1\) and \(r(X),r(E\setminus X)\ge j\). For \(k\ge 2\), the matroid \(M\) is vertically \(k\)-connected if it has no vertical \(j\)-separation for any \(1\le j<k\). Unlike ordinary connectivity, the side constraints use rank rather than cardinality, so low-rank sides do not witness failure.
knowledge_statements.statement_plain: Vertical k-connectivity excludes lower-order separations whose two sides both have sufficiently large rank.
knowledge_statements.conclusion_latex: \(M\text{ is vertically }k\text{-connected}\iff M\text{ has no vertical }j\text{-separation for }1\le j<k.\)

intermediate_metadata.review_comment: The rank-based definition is plausible, but vertical-connectivity indexing and side-rank conventions vary. An authoritative source with a definition-level locator is required.

knowledge_statements.statement_title: Vertical Separations and Vertical Connectivity
knowledge_statements.scope_note: Defines vertical separations, vertical connectivity, and vertical connectedness, with their stated cocircuit consequences and uniform-matroid values.
knowledge_statements.statement_latex: For a matroid $M$ and a positive integer $k$, a partition $(X,Y)$ of $E(M)$ is a vertical $k$-separation if $\lambda_M(X)<k$ and $\min\{r(X),r(Y)\}\ge k$. Any such separation satisfies $2k-r(M)\le r(X)+r(Y)-r(M)\le k-1$; consequently $k\le r(M)-1$, $\max\{r(X),r(Y)\}\le r(M)-1$, and each of $X$ and $Y$ contains a cocircuit. Conversely, two disjoint cocircuits imply a vertical $k$-separation for some positive integer $k\le r(M)-1$. If $M$ has two disjoint cocircuits, $\kappa(M)$ is the least positive integer $j$ for which $M$ has a vertical $j$-separation; otherwise $\kappa(M)=r(M)$. Hence $\kappa(M)=r(M)$ if and only if $M$ has no two disjoint cocircuits. Moreover, $\kappa(U_{r,n})=n-r+1$ when $n\le 2r-2$, and $\kappa(U_{r,n})=r$ otherwise. A matroid $M$ is vertically $q$-connected when $2\le q\le\kappa(M)$.
knowledge_statements.statement_plain: A vertical k-separation has connectivity value below k while both sides have rank at least k. Vertical connectivity is the least order of such a separation when two disjoint cocircuits exist, and otherwise equals the matroid rank. The extract also gives cocircuit consequences, uniform-matroid values, and the definition of vertical connectedness.
knowledge_statements.conclusion_latex: \kappa(M)=\begin{cases}\min\{j\in\mathbb Z_{>0}:M\text{ has a vertical }j\text{-separation}\},&M\text{ has two disjoint cocircuits},\\r(M),&\text{otherwise.}\end{cases}

knowledge_statements.title: Cyclic Connectivity
knowledge_statements.scope_note: Dual-rank version of vertical connectivity for finite matroids.
knowledge_statements.statement_latex: Let \(M\) be a finite matroid on \(E\), with dual rank function \(r^*\). For \(j\ge 1\), a cyclic \(j\)-separation is a partition \((X,E\setminus X)\) satisfying \(\lambda_M(X)\le j-1\) and \(r^*(X),r^*(E\setminus X)\ge j\). For \(k\ge 2\), the matroid \(M\) is cyclically \(k\)-connected if no cyclic \(j\)-separation exists for \(1\le j<k\). Equivalently, \(M\) is cyclically \(k\)-connected exactly when its dual \(M^*\) is vertically \(k\)-connected.
knowledge_statements.statement_plain: Cyclic k-connectivity is vertical k-connectivity in the dual matroid and uses dual ranks on both sides of a separation.
knowledge_statements.conclusion_latex: \(M\text{ is cyclically }k\text{-connected}\iff M^*\text{ is vertically }k\text{-connected}.\)

notation.meaning: rank function of the dual matroid

intermediate_metadata.review_comment: The proposed dual-rank definition is plausible, but the precise cyclic-connectivity convention and its equivalence with vertical connectivity of the dual require an authoritative source.

knowledge_statements.statement_title: Cyclic Separations and Cyclic Connectivity
knowledge_statements.scope_note: Defines cyclic separation, the exceptional circuit-disjointness case, the dual identity, and cyclic n-connectivity.
knowledge_statements.statement_latex: Let \(M\) be a matroid, let \(k\in\mathbb Z_{>0}\), and let \((X,Y)\) partition \(E(M)\). The partition is a cyclic \(k\)-separation if \(\lambda_M(X)<k\) and both \(X\) and \(Y\) contain circuits of \(M\). If \(M\) has a pair of disjoint circuits, \(\kappa^*(M)\) is the least positive integer \(j\) for which \(M\) has a cyclic \(j\)-separation; otherwise, \(\kappa^*(M)=r^*(M)\). For every matroid, \(\kappa^*(M)=\kappa(M^*)\). The matroid \(M\) is cyclically \(n\)-connected when \(n\in\mathbb Z\) and \(2\le n\le\kappa^*(M)\).
knowledge_statements.statement_plain: A cyclic k-separation is a partition with connectivity value below k whose two sides both contain circuits. Cyclic connectivity is the least order of such a separation when a pair of disjoint circuits exists, and otherwise equals the dual rank. It equals the vertical connectivity of the dual. A matroid is cyclically n-connected when 2 ≤ n ≤ its cyclic connectivity.
knowledge_statements.conclusion_latex: (X,Y)\text{ is a cyclic }k\text{-separation}\iff\lambda_M(X)<k\text{ and both }X,Y\text{ contain circuits of }M;\quad \kappa^*(M)=\begin{cases}\min\{j\in\mathbb Z_{>0}:M\text{ has a cyclic }j\text{-separation}\},&M\text{ has a pair of disjoint circuits},\\r^*(M),&\text{otherwise},\end{cases}\quad \kappa^*(M)=\kappa(M^*)

knowledge_statements.title: Local Connectivity
knowledge_statements.scope_note: Rank-theoretic local connectivity between two subsets of a matroid.
knowledge_statements.statement_latex:
Let \(M\) be a finite matroid with rank function \(r\), and let \(X,Y\subseteq E(M)\). The local connectivity of \(X\) and \(Y\) is
\[\sqcap_M(X,Y)=r(X)+r(Y)-r(X\cup Y).\]
It is symmetric and satisfies \(0\le \sqcap_M(X,Y)\le \min\{r(X),r(Y)\}\). If \(X\cap Y=\varnothing\), then \(\sqcap_M(X,Y)\) measures the rank lost when the two restrictions are combined; in particular, it is zero exactly when \(r(X\cup Y)=r(X)+r(Y)\).
knowledge_statements.statement_plain: Local connectivity is the rank overlap between two subsets, computed as the sum of their ranks minus the rank of their union.
knowledge_statements.conclusion_latex: \(\sqcap_M(X,Y)=r(X)+r(Y)-r(X\cup Y).\)

notation.meaning: local connectivity of X and Y in M

knowledge_statements.statement_title: Local Connectivity and Skew Sets
knowledge_statements.scope_note: Rank definition of local connectivity, its basic identities, its representable interpretation, and the induced notion of skewness.
knowledge_statements.statement_latex: For $X,Y\subseteq E(M)$, define $\sqcap_M(X,Y)=r_M(X)+r_M(Y)-r_M(X\cup Y)$. Then $\sqcap_M(X,Y)=\sqcap_M(Y,X)$ and $\sqcap_M(X,E(M)\setminus X)=\lambda_M(X)$. If $X\cap Y=\varnothing$, then $\sqcap_M(X,Y)=r_M(X)-r_{M/Y}(X)$. If $M$ is represented by vectors in a vector space $V$, then $\sqcap_M(X,Y)$ is the dimension of the intersection of the subspaces spanned by $X$ and $Y$. Sets $X$ and $Y$ are skew if and only if $r_M(X\cup Y)=r_M(X)+r_M(Y)$, equivalently $\sqcap_M(X,Y)=0$.
knowledge_statements.statement_plain: Local connectivity is the sum of the ranks of two sets minus the rank of their union. It is symmetric, equals the connectivity function across a set and its complement, has a contraction identity for disjoint sets, and in a vector representation measures the dimension of the intersection of their spans. Two sets are skew exactly when their local connectivity is zero.
knowledge_statements.conclusion_latex: \sqcap_M(X,Y):=r_M(X)+r_M(Y)-r_M(X\cup Y)

children.title: Connectivity-Variant Comparisons
children.top_down_role: Implications, separations, plus dual correspondences among the named variants.

knowledge_statements.title: Connectivity-Variant Comparisons
knowledge_statements.scope_note: Duality comparison among ordinary, vertical, and cyclic connectivity.
knowledge_statements.statement_latex: For every finite matroid \(M\) and every \(X\subseteq E(M)\), duality preserves the connectivity function: \(\lambda_{M^*}(X)=\lambda_M(X)\). Consequently ordinary \(k\)-connectivity is self-dual. Because vertical separations impose rank constraints while cyclic separations impose the corresponding dual-rank constraints, a partition is a cyclic \(j\)-separation of \(M\) exactly when it is a vertical \(j\)-separation of \(M^*\). Therefore \(M\) is cyclically \(k\)-connected if and only if \(M^*\) is vertically \(k\)-connected, and conversely.
knowledge_statements.statement_plain: Ordinary connectivity is invariant under duality, while vertical and cyclic connectivity are exchanged by matroid duality.
knowledge_statements.conclusion_latex: \(\lambda_{M^*}=\lambda_M,\qquad M\text{ cyclically }k\text{-connected}\iff M^*\text{ vertically }k\text{-connected}.\)

intermediate_metadata.review_comment: The self-duality of the connectivity function and exchange of vertical and cyclic connectivity are standard-looking, but the exact convention-dependent claims have no cited source.

children.title: Matroid Connectivity Functions
children.top_down_role: Connectivity-function viewpoints used to organize separations across subsets.

knowledge_statements.title: Matroid Connectivity Functions
knowledge_statements.scope_note: Standard normalized connectivity function of a finite matroid.
knowledge_statements.statement_latex:
Let \(M=(E,r)\) be a finite matroid. Its connectivity function is the integer-valued set function
\[\lambda_M(X)=r(X)+r(E\setminus X)-r(E),\qquad X\subseteq E.\]
It is normalized, symmetric, and submodular: \(\lambda_M(\varnothing)=0\), \(\lambda_M(X)=\lambda_M(E\setminus X)\), and
\[\lambda_M(X)+\lambda_M(Y)\ge \lambda_M(X\cap Y)+\lambda_M(X\cup Y)\]
for all \(X,Y\subseteq E\). Moreover, \(\lambda_M(X)\ge 0\), and its small values identify low-order separations of \(M\).
knowledge_statements.statement_plain: The matroid connectivity function measures rank interaction across a bipartition and is nonnegative, symmetric, normalized, and submodular.
knowledge_statements.conclusion_latex: \(\lambda_M(X)=r(X)+r(E\setminus X)-r(E)\) is a normalized symmetric submodular function.

knowledge_statements.statement_title: Connectivity Function Under Deletion and Contraction
knowledge_statements.scope_note: Bounds on connectivity after taking a minor, including the exact equality criteria.
knowledge_statements.statement_latex: Let $X,C,D$ be pairwise disjoint subsets of $E(M)$. Then $\lambda_{M\setminus D/C}(X)\le \lambda_M(X)$, with equality if and only if $r_M(X\cup C)=r_M(X)+r_M(C)$ and $r_M(E(M)\setminus X)+r_M(E(M)\setminus D)=r_M(E(M))+r_M(E(M)\setminus(X\cup D))$. If, in addition, $C$ is independent and $D$ is coindependent, then $\lambda_{M\setminus D/C}(X)\ge \lambda_M(X)-|C|-|D|$, with equality if and only if $C\subseteq\operatorname{cl}_M(X)$ and $D\subseteq\operatorname{cl}_M^*(X)$.
knowledge_statements.statement_plain: Deleting D and contracting C cannot increase the connectivity of a disjoint set X, with equality characterized by two rank identities. If C is independent and D is coindependent, the decrease is at most |C|+|D|, with maximum decrease exactly when C lies in the closure of X and D lies in its coclosure.
knowledge_statements.conclusion_latex: \lambda_{M\setminus D/C}(X)\le\lambda_M(X);\quad C\text{ independent and }D\text{ coindependent}\Rightarrow\lambda_{M\setminus D/C}(X)\ge\lambda_M(X)-|C|-|D|

children.title: Matroid Branch-Width
children.top_down_role: Branch decompositions, width regimes, plus structural interpretations of bounded width.

knowledge_statements.title: Matroid Branch-Width
knowledge_statements.scope_note: Branch-width with edge width normalized as \(\lambda_M+1\).
knowledge_statements.statement_latex: Let \(M\) be a finite matroid on \(E\) with \(|E|\ge 2\). A branch-decomposition is a pair \((T,\tau)\), where \(T\) is a tree whose internal vertices have degree three and \(\tau:E\to L(T)\) is a bijection. Each edge \(e\in E(T)\) determines a bipartition \((A_e,E\setminus A_e)\) from the two components of \(T-e\). Its width is \(\lambda_M(A_e)+1\). The width of \((T,\tau)\) is the maximum edge width, and the branch-width \(\operatorname{bw}(M)\) is the minimum such width over all branch-decompositions.
knowledge_statements.statement_plain: Matroid branch-width minimizes the largest connectivity value, plus one, displayed by an edge of a subcubic leaf-labeled tree.
knowledge_statements.conclusion_latex: \(\operatorname{bw}(M)=\min_{(T,\tau)}\max_{e\in E(T)}\bigl(\lambda_M(A_e)+1\bigr).\)

notation.meaning: one side of the bipartition displayed by tree edge e

intermediate_metadata.review_comment: The definition is coherent, but matroid branch-width conventions differ by a plus-one shift. The selected normalization requires an authoritative definition-level citation.

knowledge_statements.statement_title: Duality and Minor Behavior of Matroid Branch-Width
knowledge_statements.scope_note: States dual invariance, minor monotonicity, and the one-step deletion and contraction bounds.
knowledge_statements.statement_latex: For every matroid \(M\), \(\operatorname{bw}(M^*)=\operatorname{bw}(M)\). For every minor \(N\) of \(M\), \(\operatorname{bw}(N)\le \operatorname{bw}(M)\). For every \(e\in E(M)\), both \(\operatorname{bw}(M\setminus e)\) and \(\operatorname{bw}(M/e)\) belong to \(\{\operatorname{bw}(M)-1,\operatorname{bw}(M)\}\).
knowledge_statements.statement_plain: Branch-width is invariant under duality and cannot increase upon taking a minor. Deleting or contracting one element preserves branch-width or decreases it by one.
knowledge_statements.conclusion_latex: \operatorname{bw}(M^*)=\operatorname{bw}(M),\quad \forall N\preceq M:\operatorname{bw}(N)\le\operatorname{bw}(M),\quad \forall e\in E(M):\operatorname{bw}(M\setminus e),\operatorname{bw}(M/e)\in\{\operatorname{bw}(M)-1,\operatorname{bw}(M)\}

knowledge_statements.statement_title: Branch-Decomposition and Branch-Width of a Matroid
knowledge_statements.scope_note: Defines displayed bipartitions, edge width, decomposition width, and branch-width under the convention permitting unlabelled leaves.
knowledge_statements.statement_latex: A branch-decomposition of a matroid \(M\) consists of a cubic tree \(T\), meaning that every nonleaf vertex has degree three, with at least \(|E(M)|\) leaves and an injective labelling of exactly \(|E(M)|\) leaves by \(E(M)\); additional leaves may be unlabelled. Each edge \(e\in E(T)\) displays the bipartition \((X,E(M)\setminus X)\) induced by the components of \(T\setminus e\). Its width is \(w(e)=\lambda_M(X)+1=r(X)+r(E(M)\setminus X)-r(M)+1\). Define \(w(T)=\max_{e\in E(T)}w(e)\) and \(\operatorname{bw}(M)=\min_T w(T)\), where the minimum is over all such branch-decompositions. Under this convention, \(\operatorname{bw}(M)\ge 1\) for every matroid, including matroids with at most one element.
knowledge_statements.statement_plain: A branch-decomposition labels one leaf for each matroid element in a cubic tree and may have additional unlabelled leaves. Each edge displays a ground-set bipartition and has width equal to its connectivity value plus one. The tree width is the maximum edge width, and branch-width is the minimum tree width. Under this convention every matroid has branch-width at least one.
assumptions_latex: T\text{ is a tree whose nonleaf vertices all have degree three, with at least }|E(M)|\text{ leaves and an injective labelling of }|E(M)|\text{ leaves by }E(M)
knowledge_statements.conclusion_latex: \operatorname{bw}(M)=\min_T\max_{e\in E(T)}\bigl(\lambda_M(X_e)+1\bigr)\ge 1

knowledge_statements.statement_title: Linked edge pairs and linked branch-decompositions
knowledge_statements.scope_note: Defines linkedness using local connectivity between the ground-set portions beyond two decomposition edges.
knowledge_statements.statement_latex: Let \(f\neq g\) be edges of a branch-decomposition \(T\) of a matroid \(M\). Let \(F\) be the subset of \(E(M)\) displayed by the component of \(T\setminus f\) not containing \(g\), let \(G\) be the subset displayed by the component of \(T\setminus g\) not containing \(f\), and let \(P\) be the shortest path in \(T\) containing \(f\) and \(g\). Define \[\kappa_M(F,G)=\min\{\lambda_M(S):F\subseteq S\subseteq E(M)\setminus G\}.\] Every edge of \(P\) has width at least \(\kappa_M(F,G)+1\). The pair \(f,g\) is linked if the minimum edge width on \(P\) equals \(\kappa_M(F,G)+1\), and \(T\) is linked if every pair of distinct edges is linked.
knowledge_statements.statement_plain: For two distinct edges of a matroid branch-decomposition, form the ground-set portions lying beyond them and the path joining them. The pair is linked when the smallest width on that path attains the local-connectivity lower bound plus one. The decomposition is linked when every distinct edge pair is linked.
assumptions_latex: T\text{ is a branch-decomposition of a matroid }M
F,G\subseteq E(M)\text{ and }P\text{ are defined from }T,f,g\text{ as stated}
knowledge_statements.conclusion_latex: f\text{ and }g\text{ are linked}\iff\min_{e\in E(P)}\operatorname{width}(e)=\kappa_M(F,G)+1;\qquad T\text{ is linked}\iff\text{every distinct edge pair is linked}

knowledge_statements.title: Branch-Width via Connectivity Functions
knowledge_statements.scope_note: Branch-width as the decomposition width induced by a connectivity function.
knowledge_statements.statement_latex:
Let \(E\) be finite and let \(f:2^E\to\mathbb{R}_{\ge0}\) be symmetric. For a branch-decomposition \((T,\tau)\), define
\[w_f(T,\tau)=\max_{e\in E(T)} f(A_e),\qquad \operatorname{bw}(f)=\min_{(T,\tau)}w_f(T,\tau).\]
For a matroid \(M	o E\), use the shifted connectivity function \(f_M(X)=\lambda_M(X)+1\). Then matroid branch-width is exactly the branch-width of this connectivity system:
\[\operatorname{bw}(M)=\operatorname{bw}(f_M)=\min_{(T,\tau)}\max_{e\in E(T)}\bigl(\lambda_M(A_e)+1\bigr).\]
knowledge_statements.statement_plain: Matroid branch-width is precisely the branch-decomposition width of its connectivity function under the stated plus-one normalization.
knowledge_statements.conclusion_latex: \(\operatorname{bw}(M)=\operatorname{bw}(\lambda_M+1).\)

notation.meaning: shifted connectivity function defined by lambda plus one
side displayed by a decomposition-tree edge
branch-width induced by symmetric function f

intermediate_metadata.review_comment: The connectivity-function representation and plus-one normalization require a source. In addition, “M\to E” is malformed and should read that M is a matroid on E once the sourced convention is established.

knowledge_statements.statement_title: Graph branch-width and its cycle-matroid bound
knowledge_statements.scope_note: Defines graph branch-width and records the component-corrected connectivity identity and resulting bound.
knowledge_statements.statement_latex: For a branch-decomposition \(T\) of a graph \(G\), if an edge displays \((X,E(G)\setminus X)\), its width is \(\eta_G(X)=|V(G[X])\cap V(G[E(G)\setminus X])|\). The width of \(T\) is the maximum of its edge widths, and \(\beta(G)\) is the minimum such width over all labelled cubic branch-decomposition trees. If \(G\) has no isolated vertices, then \[\lambda_{M(G)}(X)=\eta_G(X)+\omega(G)-\omega(G[X])-\omega(G[E(G)\setminus X]).\] If, moreover, \(G\) is connected and has at least two edges, then \(\operatorname{bw}(M(G))\leq\beta(G)\).
knowledge_statements.statement_plain: Graph branch-width minimizes the maximum vertex-boundary size over labelled cubic branch-decomposition trees. For a graph without isolated vertices, cycle-matroid connectivity equals this boundary size plus a component-count correction. A connected graph with at least two edges therefore has cycle-matroid branch-width no greater than its graph branch-width.
assumptions_latex: T\text{ is a labelled cubic branch-decomposition of }G
G\text{ has no isolated vertices for the connectivity identity}
G\text{ is connected and }|E(G)|\geq2\text{ for the branch-width inequality}
knowledge_statements.conclusion_latex: \lambda_{M(G)}(X)=\eta_G(X)+\omega(G)-\omega(G[X])-\omega(G[E(G)\setminus X]),\qquad \operatorname{bw}(M(G))\leq\beta(G)\text{ under the respective assumptions}

knowledge_statements.title: Bounded-Width Structural Regimes
knowledge_statements.scope_note: A branch-decomposition as a certificate of bounded matroid branch-width.
knowledge_statements.statement_latex:
Let \(M=(E,r)\) be a finite matroid and let \(b\ge 1\). A branch-decomposition \((T,\tau)\) certifies \(\operatorname{bw}(M)\le b\) if every edge \(e\in E(T)\), displaying \((A_e,E\setminus A_e)\), satisfies
\[r(A_e)+r(E\setminus A_e)-r(E)+1\le b.\]
The certificate is checked by verifying that \(T\) is subcubic, \(\tau\) bijects \(E\) with its leaves, and the displayed inequality holds for every tree edge. Existence of such a certificate is equivalent to membership in the branch-width-at-most-\(b\) regime.
knowledge_statements.statement_plain: A subcubic leaf-labeled tree certifies branch-width at most b when every displayed matroid separation has width at most b.
assumptions_latex: Rank values for displayed subsets are available for verification.
knowledge_statements.conclusion_latex: \(\operatorname{bw}(M)\le b\iff \exists(T,\tau)\ \forall e\in E(T):\lambda_M(A_e)+1\le b.\)

notation.meaning: side displayed by tree edge e

intermediate_metadata.review_comment: A displayed branch-decomposition is a suitable certificate for the bounded-width leaf, but the normalization and rank-access verification model depend on the unsourced branch-width convention.

knowledge_statements.title: Tutte Linking Theory
knowledge_statements.scope_note: Finite-matroid linking theorem for two disjoint terminal sets.
knowledge_statements.statement_latex:
Let \(M\) be a finite matroid on \(E\), and let \(S,T\subseteq E\) be disjoint. Define
\[\kappa_M(S,T)=\min\{\lambda_M(X):S\subseteq X\subseteq E\setminus T\}.\]
There is a partition \((C,D)\) of \(E\setminus(S\cup T)\) such that the minor \(N=M/C\setminus D\), whose ground set is \(S\cup T\), satisfies \(N|S=M|S\), \(N|T=M|T\), and
\[\kappa_N(S,T)=\kappa_M(S,T).\]
Thus all nonterminal elements can be contracted or deleted while preserving both terminal restrictions and their minimum separation order.
knowledge_statements.statement_plain: Tutte's linking theorem produces a minor on two terminal sets that preserves their restrictions and minimum connectivity.
knowledge_statements.conclusion_latex: \(\exists C\mathbin{\dot\cup}D=E\setminus(S\cup T):\ N=M/C\setminus D,\ \kappa_N(S,T)=\kappa_M(S,T),\ N|S=M|S,\ N|T=M|T.\)

notation.meaning: minimum connectivity separating S from T
minor formed by contracting C and deleting D

intermediate_metadata.review_comment: This is an appropriate theorem for Tutte linking theory, but the exact minor conclusion, preservation of both terminal restrictions, and connectivity normalization require an authoritative theorem-level citation.

knowledge_statements.statement_title: Linking Minor Preserving Terminal Restrictions
knowledge_statements.scope_note: Existence of a linking minor that preserves local connectivity and the restrictions on both terminal sets.
knowledge_statements.statement_latex: Let \(X\) and \(Y\) be disjoint subsets of \(E(M)\). Then \(M\) has a minor \(N\) such that \[E(N)=X\cup Y,\qquad \kappa_N(X,Y)=\kappa_M(X,Y),\qquad N|X=M|X,\qquad N|Y=M|Y.\]
knowledge_statements.statement_plain: For disjoint sets X and Y in a matroid M, there is a minor on exactly X union Y that preserves their local connectivity and agrees with M when restricted separately to X and to Y.
knowledge_statements.conclusion_latex: \exists N\preccurlyeq M:\ E(N)=X\cup Y,\ \kappa_N(X,Y)=\kappa_M(X,Y),\ N|X=M|X,\ N|Y=M|Y

knowledge_statements.title: Wheel Matroids
knowledge_statements.scope_note: Defines the finite rank-wheel matroid as the cycle matroid of a wheel graph.
knowledge_statements.statement_latex: For an integer \(r\ge 3\), let \(W_r\) be the graph obtained from a cycle \(v_1v_2\cdots v_rv_1\) by adjoining a hub \(h\) and the spokes \(hv_i\) for \(1\le i\le r\). The rank-\(r\) wheel matroid is the cycle matroid \(M(W_r)\). Its ground set comprises the \(r\) rim edges and \(r\) spokes, and its bases are precisely the edge sets of spanning trees of \(W_r\).
knowledge_statements.statement_plain: A wheel matroid is the cycle matroid of a cycle joined to a central hub; its bases are the wheel graph's spanning trees.
knowledge_statements.conclusion_latex: \(M(W_r)\) is a rank-\(r\) graphic matroid on \(2r\) elements.

notation.meaning: wheel graph with r rim vertices and one hub
cycle matroid of a graph G

review_flags: Exact supporting definition locator is absent from the supplied source inventory.

intermediate_metadata.review_comment: The definition, content kind, notation, and rank/ground-set claims are mathematically standard and fit the Wheel Matroids leaf, but no citation or inspectable locator supports the record. A source specifically defining wheel matroids is required.

knowledge_statements.statement_title: Structural profile of rank-r wheels and whirls
knowledge_statements.scope_note: Comparative profile for ranks r≥2, with additional conclusions and exceptions at r≥3 and r=2.
knowledge_statements.statement_latex: For r\ge 2, \mathcal W^r is the unique relaxation of M(\mathcal W_r). The wheel M(\mathcal W_r) is graphic, cographic, and regular, whereas \mathcal W^r is neither graphic, cographic, nor regular and is \mathbb F-representable if and only if |\mathbb F|\ge 3. For r\ge 3, M(\mathcal W_r) is neither transversal, a strict gammoid, nor a gammoid, while \mathcal W^r is transversal, a strict gammoid, and a gammoid. Both are self-dual but not identically self-dual and are algebraic over every field. Except for \mathcal W^2\cong U_{2,4}, their automorphism groups are nontransitive. For r\ge 3, M(\mathcal W_r) and \mathcal W^r are exactly the 3-connected matroids for which no single-element deletion and no single-element contraction is 3-connected. Moreover, \mathcal W^2 is 3-connected, whereas M(\mathcal W_2) is not.
knowledge_statements.statement_plain: For rank at least two, the whirl is the wheel's unique relaxation. Wheels are graphic, cographic, and regular; whirls are none of these and are representable exactly over fields having at least three elements. From rank three onward, wheels are neither transversal nor gammoids, whereas whirls are transversal matroids, strict gammoids, and gammoids. Both families are self-dual but not identically self-dual and are algebraic over every field. Their automorphism groups are nontransitive except for the rank-two whirl U(2,4). At rank at least three, wheels and whirls are precisely the 3-connected matroids having no 3-connected single-element deletion or contraction. The rank-two whirl is 3-connected, but the rank-two wheel is not.
knowledge_statements.conclusion_latex: \mathcal W^r\text{ and }M(\mathcal W_r)\text{ have the stated relaxation, class-membership, duality, automorphism, connectivity, and algebraicity properties.}

knowledge_statements.statement_title: Structural properties of M(K_4)
knowledge_statements.scope_note: Class, obstruction, minor-universality, series-parallel, and fragility properties of the rank-three wheel matroid.
knowledge_statements.statement_latex: The cycle matroid $M(K_4)$ is isomorphic to $M(\mathcal W_3)$, the rank-three wheel, and to the tipless binary 3-spike. It is regular, graphic, cographic, self-dual but not identically self-dual, algebraic over every field, and has a transitive automorphism group. It is minor-minimal among non-transversal matroids, among matroids that are not strict gammoids, and among non-gammoids. It is neither base-orderable nor strongly base-orderable. Every three-connected binary matroid with at least four elements has an $M(K_4)$ minor. A connected nonempty binary matroid is a series-parallel network if and only if it has no $M(K_4)$ minor. For every $e\in E(M(K_4))$, neither $M(K_4)\setminus e$ nor $M(K_4)/e$ is three-connected.
knowledge_statements.statement_plain: M(K4) is the rank-three wheel and the tipless binary 3-spike. It has the stated class, obstruction, minor-universality, series-parallel, base-orderability, and connectivity-fragility properties.

e\in E(M(K_4))\text{ for the deletion-contraction assertion.}

knowledge_statements.title: Whirl Matroids
knowledge_statements.scope_note: Uses the standard relaxation definition of a finite whirl.
knowledge_statements.statement_latex: Let \(M(W_r)\) be the rank-\(r\) wheel matroid for \(r\ge 3\), and let \(R\) be its set of rim edges. The set \(R\) is a circuit-hyperplane of \(M(W_r)\). knowledge_statements.title: Deletion–Contraction Fragility
knowledge_statements.scope_note: Defines fragility relative to a fixed minor in finite matroids.
knowledge_statements.statement_latex: Let \(M\) and \(N\) be finite matroids. The matroid \(M\) is \(N\)-fragile if \(N\) is a minor of \(M\) and, for every \(e\in E(M)\), at most one of \(M\backslash e\) and \(M/e\) has an \(N\)-minor. Equivalently, no element is simultaneously deletable and contractible while preserving an \(N\)-minor. An element may nevertheless be essential, meaning that neither operation preserves such a minor.
knowledge_statements.statement_plain: A matroid is N-fragile when it has an N-minor but no element can be both deleted and contracted while retaining an N-minor.
knowledge_statements.conclusion_latex: \(M\text{ is }N\text{-fragile}\iff N\preccurlyeq M\text{ and }\forall e\in E(M),\;\neg(N\preccurlyeq M\backslash e\text{ and }N\preccurlyeq M/e)\).

notation.meaning: N is isomorphic to a minor of M

review_flags: Terminology varies between fragile and strictly fragile; an exact source is required to certify this convention.

intermediate_metadata.review_comment: The statement coherently defines fragility as absence of N-flexible elements and correctly distinguishes essential elements, but published conventions differ between N-fragile and strictly N-fragile. An exact definition locator is required before selecting this convention.

knowledge_statements.title: Wheel–Whirl Exceptional Regimes
knowledge_statements.scope_note: Records why wheels and whirls require exceptions in literal splitter statements.
knowledge_statements.statement_latex: For \(r\ge 3\), let \(M\) be the wheel \(M(W_r)\) or the whirl \(\mathcal W^r\). For every \(e\in E(M)\), neither \(M\backslash e\) nor \(M/e\) is 3-connected: one operation exposes a series class and the dual operation exposes a parallel class. Consequently, a splitter assertion demanding a proper 3-connected single-element deletion or contraction cannot be applied literally within a wheel or whirl chain.
knowledge_statements.statement_plain: Every single deletion or contraction of a wheel or whirl destroys 3-connectivity, so literal one-element splitter conclusions need an exceptional clause.

knowledge_statements.statement_title: Tutte's Wheels-and-Whirls Theorem
knowledge_statements.scope_note: Characterizes the 3-connected matroids for which neither deletion nor contraction of any element preserves 3-connectivity.
knowledge_statements.statement_latex: Let \(M\) be a 3-connected matroid with \(|E(M)|\ge 1\). The following are equivalent: (i) for every \(e\in E(M)\), neither \(M\setminus e\) nor \(M/e\) is 3-connected; (ii) \(r(M)\ge 3\) and \(M\) is isomorphic to a wheel or a whirl.
knowledge_statements.statement_plain: A nonempty 3-connected matroid loses 3-connectivity under both deletion and contraction of every element exactly when it has rank at least three and is a wheel or whirl.
knowledge_statements.conclusion_latex: \left[\forall e\in E(M),\ M\setminus e\text{ is not 3-connected and }M/e\text{ is not 3-connected}\right]\iff\left[r(M)\ge 3\text{ and }M\text{ is isomorphic to a wheel or a whirl}\right].

knowledge_statements.statement_title: t-Rounded Class of Matroids
knowledge_statements.scope_note: Class-level connectivity and prescribed-subset minor property, explicitly distinct from the unrelated property of a matroid being round.
knowledge_statements.statement_latex: Let \(t\in\mathbb Z_{>0}\). A class \(\mathcal N\) of matroids is \(t\)-rounded if every member of \(\mathcal N\) is \((t+1)\)-connected and, whenever a \((t+1)\)-connected matroid \(M\) has an \(\mathcal N\)-minor and \(X\subseteq E(M)\) with \(|X|\le t\), the matroid \(M\) has an \(\mathcal N\)-minor using \(X\). This property is unrelated to a matroid being round, which means that every cocircuit of the matroid is spanning.
knowledge_statements.statement_plain: For a positive integer t, a class is t-rounded when all its members are (t+1)-connected and every set of at most t elements in any (t+1)-connected matroid having a class minor is contained in some class minor. This is unrelated to a matroid being round, meaning that every cocircuit is spanning.
assumptions_latex: \mathcal N\text{ is a class of matroids}
knowledge_statements.conclusion_latex: \mathcal N\text{ is }t\text{-rounded}\iff\left[\forall N\in\mathcal N,\ N\text{ is }(t+1)\text{-connected, and the prescribed-subset minor condition holds}\right].

knowledge_statements.scope_note: For \(t=1\) or \(2\), characterization of roundedness through ambient matroids differing by one ground-set element from a specified class minor.

knowledge_statements.scope_note: Definition and equivalent characterization in terms of 3-connected class members.
knowledge_statements.statement_latex: Let \mathcal N be a class of matroids closed under minors and isomorphism, and let N\in\mathcal N. knowledge_statements.title: Classical Splitter Regime
knowledge_statements.scope_note: Finite-matroid form of the classical Splitter Theorem with the wheel–whirl proviso.
knowledge_statements.statement_latex: Let \(M\) and \(N\) be 3-connected finite matroids such that \(N\) is a proper minor of \(M\) and \(|E(N)|\ge 4\). If \(N\) is a wheel or whirl, additionally suppose that \(M\) has no wheel or whirl minor, respectively, with more elements than \(N\). Then some \(e\in E(M)\) satisfies one of the following: \(M\backslash e\) is 3-connected and has an \(N\)-minor, or \(M/e\) is 3-connected and has an \(N\)-minor.
knowledge_statements.statement_plain: Outside the stated wheel–whirl obstruction, a proper 3-connected minor can be retained after a deletion or contraction that preserves 3-connectivity.
assumptions_latex: \(N\) is a proper minor of \(M\) and \(|E(N)|\ge 4\)
The wheel–whirl maximality proviso holds when applicable
knowledge_statements.conclusion_latex: \(\exists e\in E(M)\) such that \((N\preccurlyeq M\backslash e\text{ and }M\backslash e\text{ is 3-connected})\) or \((N\preccurlyeq M/e\text{ and }M/e\text{ is 3-connected})\).

notation.meaning: N is isomorphic to a minor of M

knowledge_statements.statement_title: Splitter-Based Decomposition of a Minor-Closed Matroid Class
knowledge_statements.scope_note: Decomposition under a one-element 3-connected extension gap and wheel–whirl maximality assumptions.
knowledge_statements.statement_latex: Let \(\mathcal N\) be closed under isomorphism and minors, and let \(N\in\mathcal N\) be 3-connected with \(|E(N)|\ge 4\). Assume that no 3-connected member of \(\mathcal N\) with an \(N\)-minor has exactly \(|E(N)|+1\) elements. If \(N\) is a wheel, assume that \(\mathcal N\) contains no larger wheel; if \(N\) is a whirl, assume that \(\mathcal N\) contains no larger whirl. Then every matroid in \(\mathcal N\) can be obtained by a sequence of direct sums and 2-sums from copies of \(N\) and members of \(\mathcal N\) having no \(N\)-minor.
knowledge_statements.statement_plain: Under the stated extension-gap and wheel–whirl maximality assumptions, every member of the minor-closed class decomposes through direct sums and 2-sums into copies of N and class members without an N-minor.
assumptions_latex: \mathcal N\text{ is closed under isomorphism and minors}
\nexists M\in\mathcal N:\ M\text{ is 3-connected, has an }N\text{-minor, and }|E(M)|=|E(N)|+1
N\text{ is a wheel}\Rightarrow\mathcal N\text{ contains no larger wheel}
N\text{ is a whirl}\Rightarrow\mathcal N\text{ contains no larger whirl}
knowledge_statements.conclusion_latex: \forall M\in\mathcal N,\ M\text{ is obtainable by a sequence of direct sums and 2-sums from copies of }N\text{ and members of }\mathcal N\text{ having no }N\text{-minor}.

knowledge_statements.statement_title: Graphical one-edge splitter criterion
knowledge_statements.scope_note: Graph specialization of the classical splitter criterion.
knowledge_statements.statement_latex: Let \mathcal G be a class of graphs closed under minors and isomorphism, and let H be a simple 3-connected graph. If H is a wheel, assume it is the largest wheel in \mathcal G. Suppose no simple 3-connected graph G'\in\mathcal G has a single-edge deletion or contraction isomorphic to H. Then every simple 3-connected G\in\mathcal G satisfies H\not\preccurlyeq G or G\cong H.
knowledge_statements.statement_plain: Let G be a minor- and isomorphism-closed graph class and H a simple 3-connected graph, maximal among wheels in the class when H is a wheel. If no simple 3-connected class member becomes H after deleting or contracting one edge, then any simple 3-connected graph in the class either has no H minor or is isomorphic to H.
assumptions_latex: \mathcal G\text{ is closed under graph minors and isomorphism}
H\text{ wheel}\Rightarrow H\text{ is the largest wheel in }\mathcal G
\nexists G'\in\mathcal G\ \exists e\in E(G'):\ G'\text{ is simple and 3-connected and }(G'\setminus e\cong H\ \lor\ G'/e\cong H)
knowledge_statements.conclusion_latex: \forall G\in\mathcal G,\quad G\text{ simple and 3-connected}\Rightarrow(H\not\preccurlyeq G\ \lor\ G\cong H)

knowledge_statements.statement_title: Exception-Qualified Single-Step Splitter Proposition
knowledge_statements.scope_note: A single-element splitter conclusion under explicit wheel and whirl exclusions.
knowledge_statements.statement_latex: Let \(N\) be a 3-connected proper minor of a 3-connected matroid \(M\), where \(|E(N)|\ge 4\), and suppose that \(M\) is neither a wheel nor a whirl. Suppose also that if \(N\cong\mathcal W^2\), then \(M\) has no \(\mathcal W^3\)-minor, while if \(N\cong M(\mathcal W_3)\), then \(M\) has no \(M(\mathcal W_4)\)-minor. Then \(M\) has a 3-connected minor \(M_1\) and an element \(e\in E(M_1)\) such that \(M_1\setminus e\cong N\) or \(M_1/e\cong N\).
knowledge_statements.statement_plain: Under the stated connectivity, size, wheel, whirl, and exceptional-minor hypotheses, M has a 3-connected minor from which one deletion or contraction yields N.
assumptions_latex: N\text{ is a 3-connected proper minor of the 3-connected matroid }M
M\text{ is neither a wheel nor a whirl}
N\cong\mathcal W^2\Rightarrow M\text{ has no }\mathcal W^3\text{-minor}
N\cong M(\mathcal W_3)\Rightarrow M\text{ has no }M(\mathcal W_4)\text{-minor}
knowledge_statements.conclusion_latex: \exists\,M_1\preceq M\text{ 3-connected}\;\exists e\in E(M_1):\ M_1\setminus e\cong N\ \lor\ M_1/e\cong N
