knowledge_statements.statement_title: Geometric rank characterization of a tipped spike
knowledge_statements.scope_note: An if-and-only-if characterization using concurrent three-element circuits and ranks of their unions.
knowledge_statements.statement_latex: Let r>2 be an integer. A matroid M is a rank-r spike with tip t if and only if there are 3-element circuits L_1,\ldots,L_r, each containing t, such that E(M)=\bigcup_{i=1}^rL_i; for every k\in\{1,\ldots,r-1\}, the union of any k distinct L_i has rank k+1; and r_M\!\left(\bigcup_{i=1}^rL_i\right)=r.
knowledge_statements.statement_plain: For integer r greater than two, a matroid is a rank-r spike with tip t exactly when its ground set is the union of r three-point lines through t, every union of k fewer than r legs has rank k+1, and the union of all legs has rank r.
assumptions_latex: M\text{ is a matroid and }t\in E(M)
knowledge_statements.conclusion_latex: M\text{ is a rank-}r\text{ spike with tip }t\iff\begin{cases}E(M)=\bigcup_{i=1}^rL_i,\quad t\in L_i,\quad |L_i|=3,\quad L_i\in\mathcal C(M),\\r_M(\bigcup_{i\in I}L_i)=|I|+1\quad(1\le |I|\le r-1),\\r_M(\bigcup_{i=1}^rL_i)=r.\end{cases}

knowledge_statements.statement_title: Reducible and irreducible matroids
knowledge_statements.scope_note: A decomposition is nontrivial only when neither union factor equals the resulting matroid.
knowledge_statements.statement_latex: A matroid \(M\) is reducible if there exist matroids \(M_1\) and \(M_2\) on \(E(M)\) such that \(M=M_1\vee M_2\), \(M_1\ne M\), and \(M_2\ne M\). knowledge_statements.statement_title: Strongly Base-Orderable Matroid

knowledge_statements.statement_title: Minimum independent-set decomposition of an integral multiplicity vector
knowledge_statements.scope_note: Matroid-union min-max formula for representing a nonnegative integral vector by incidence vectors of independent sets.
knowledge_statements.statement_latex:
Let \(M=(S,\mathcal I)\) be a matroid with rank function \(r\), and let \(c:S\to\mathbb Z_+\). Then

knowledge_statements.statement_plain: The minimum number, counted with multiplicity, of independent sets whose incidence vectors sum to c equals the maximum of the ceiling of c(U)/r(U) over subsets U of positive rank.
assumptions_latex: M=(S,\mathcal I)\text{ is a matroid with rank function }r

knowledge_statements.title: Matroid Union Theorem Family
knowledge_statements.scope_note: Finite matroid-union theorem in rank and independence forms.
knowledge_statements.statement_latex:
Let \(M_i=(E,\mathcal I_i)\), \(i=1,\ldots,k\), be finite matroids with rank functions \(r_i\). The family \(\mathcal I=\{I_1\cup\cdots\cup I_k:I_i\in\mathcal I_i\}\) is the independent-set family of a matroid \(M_1\vee\cdots\vee M_k\). Its rank function satisfies
\[
r_{\vee}(X)=\min_{T\subseteq X}\left(|X\setminus T|+\sum_{i=1}^k r_i(T)\right)\qquad(X\subseteq E).
\]
Consequently, \(X\subseteq E\) belongs to \(\mathcal I\) exactly when \(|A|\le\sum_{i=1}^k r_i(A)\) for every \(A\subseteq X\).
knowledge_statements.statement_plain: Unions of independent sets form a matroid whose rank has a min-formula; subset rank inequalities exactly characterize union independence.
assumptions_latex: \(M_1,\ldots,M_k\) are finite matroids on a common ground set \(E\).
knowledge_statements.conclusion_latex: \(\mathcal I\) is matroidal and \(r_{\vee}(X)=\min_{T\subseteq X}(|X\setminus T|+\sum_i r_i(T))\).

knowledge_statements.statement_title: Edmonds–Fulkerson Matroid Partition Criterion
knowledge_statements.scope_note: Rank-inequality characterization of subsets partitionable into independent sets of prescribed matroids.

knowledge_statements.statement_title: Partitionable Sets and Matroid Union
knowledge_statements.scope_note: Defines the union, also called the sum, of finitely many matroids on the same ground set.
knowledge_statements.statement_latex: Let $(E,\mathcal F_1),\ldots,(E,\mathcal F_k)$ be matroids. A set $X\subseteq E$ is partitionable if there is a partition $X=X_1\cup\cdots\cup X_k$ such that $X_i\in\mathcal F_i$ for every $i\in\{1,\ldots,k\}$. If $\mathcal F$ is the family of all partitionable subsets of $E$, then $(E,\mathcal F)$ is called the union or sum of these matroids.
knowledge_statements.statement_plain: For matroids on a common ground set, a subset is partitionable when it can be partitioned into sets independently feasible in the respective matroids. The family of all such subsets defines their union, or sum.
assumptions_latex: (E,\mathcal F_i)\text{ is a matroid for each }i=1,\ldots,k
knowledge_statements.conclusion_latex: \mathcal F=\{X\subseteq E:\exists\text{ a partition }X=X_1\cup\cdots\cup X_k\text{ with }X_i\in\mathcal F_i\ \forall i\},\quad (E,\mathcal F)\text{ is the union (sum).}

knowledge_statements.statement_title: Hall's Transversal Theorem
knowledge_statements.scope_note: Necessary and sufficient condition for a finite family of sets to admit a system of distinct representatives.
knowledge_statements.statement_latex: Let Q=\{q_1,\ldots,q_m\} be a finite family of sets. A system of distinct representatives exists if and only if, for every J\subseteq\{1,\ldots,m\}, \[\left|\bigcup_{j\in J}q_j\right|\geq |J|.\] Equivalently, for each r=1,\ldots,m, the union of any r members of Q contains at least r distinct elements.
knowledge_statements.statement_plain: A finite family of sets has a system of distinct representatives exactly when the union of every chosen subfamily contains at least as many distinct elements as the subfamily has sets.
assumptions_latex: Q=\{q_1,\ldots,q_m\}\text{ is a finite family of sets}.
knowledge_statements.conclusion_latex: Q\text{ has an SDR}\iff\forall J\subseteq\{1,\ldots,m\},\ \left|\bigcup_{j\in J}q_j\right|\geq |J|.

knowledge_statements.statement_title: Matroid Union Theorem and Rank Formula
knowledge_statements.scope_note: Closure under matroid union and the associated rank min-formula for matroids on a common ground set.
knowledge_statements.statement_latex:
Let $(E,\mathcal F_1),\ldots,(E,\mathcal F_k)$ be matroids with rank functions $r_1,\ldots,r_k$, and let $(E,\mathcal F)$ be their union. Then $(E,\mathcal F)$ is a matroid, and for every $X\subseteq E$,
\[
r(X)=\min_{A\subseteq X}\left(|X\setminus A|+\sum_{i=1}^k r_i(A)\right).
\]
knowledge_statements.statement_plain: The union of matroids on a common ground set is itself a matroid. For every subset X, its union-matroid rank is the minimum over subsets A of X of the number of elements in X outside A plus the sum of the component ranks of A.
assumptions_latex: (E,\mathcal F_i)\text{ is a matroid with rank function }r_i\text{ for each }i=1,\ldots,k
knowledge_statements.conclusion_latex: (E,\mathcal F)\text{ is a matroid, and }\forall X\subseteq E,\quad r(X)=\min_{A\subseteq X}\left(|X\setminus A|+\sum_{i=1}^k r_i(A)\right).

knowledge_statements.statement_title: Matroid Union on Distinct Ground Sets
knowledge_statements.scope_note: Loop-extension definition and rank formula for a finite family of matroids with possibly different ground sets.
knowledge_statements.statement_latex: Let $M_1,\ldots,M_n$ be matroids on ground sets $E_1,\ldots,E_n$, let $E=\bigcup_{i=1}^nE_i$, and let $M_i^+$ be the matroid on $E$ obtained from $M_i$ by adjoining every element of $E\setminus E_i$ as a loop. Define $\bigvee_{i=1}^nM_i:=\bigvee_{i=1}^nM_i^+$. If $r_i$ is the rank function of $M_i$, then for every $X\subseteq E$, $r_{\bigvee_iM_i}(X)=\min_{Y\subseteq X}\left(|X\setminus Y|+\sum_{i=1}^n r_i(Y\cap E_i)\right)$.

assumptions_latex: M_i\text{ is a matroid on }E_i\text{ with rank function }r_i\quad(1\le i\le n).
M_i^+\text{ is obtained from }M_i\text{ by adjoining }E\setminus E_i\text{ as loops}.
knowledge_statements.conclusion_latex: \bigvee_{i=1}^nM_i:=\bigvee_{i=1}^nM_i^+,\qquad r_{\bigvee_iM_i}(X)=\min_{Y\subseteq X}\left\{|X\setminus Y|+\sum_{i=1}^nr_i(Y\cap E_i)\right\}\quad(X\subseteq E).

knowledge_statements.statement_title: Feasibility Criterion for Representatives with Bounded Repetitions

children.title: Union Rank Evaluation
children.top_down_role: Structural evaluation of rank in a matroid union.

knowledge_statements.title: Union Rank Evaluation
knowledge_statements.scope_note: Minimization representation for evaluating the rank of a matroid union.
knowledge_statements.statement_latex:
For finite matroids \(M_i=(E,\mathcal I_i)\) with rank functions \(r_i\), the rank of their union on any \(X\subseteq E\) is
\[
r_{\vee}(X)=\min_{T\subseteq X}\left(|X|-|T|+\sum_{i=1}^k r_i(T)\right).
\]
Equivalently, evaluating \(r_{\vee}(X)\) reduces to minimizing the integer-valued submodular function \(T\mapsto |X|-|T|+\sum_i r_i(T)\) over subsets of \(X\). Any minimizing set \(T\) certifies the returned rank value by attaining the displayed minimum.
knowledge_statements.statement_plain: Union rank equals the minimum of a rank-sum plus the number of elements excluded from a chosen subset.
knowledge_statements.conclusion_latex: \(r_{\vee}(X)=\min_{T\subseteq X}(|X|-|T|+\sum_i r_i(T))\).

notation.meaning: Subset used in the rank minimization.

knowledge_statements.statement_title: Matroid union rank formula
knowledge_statements.scope_note: Matroid closure and rank formula for the union of finitely many matroids with possibly overlapping ground sets.
knowledge_statements.statement_latex: Let M_i=(S_i,\mathcal I_i) be matroids with rank functions r_i for i=1,\ldots,k. Then M_1\vee\cdots\vee M_k is a matroid on S_1\cup\cdots\cup S_k, and for every U\subseteq S_1\cup\cdots\cup S_k,\quad r(U)=\min_{T\subseteq U}\left(|U\setminus T|+\sum_{i=1}^k r_i(T\cap S_i)\right).
knowledge_statements.statement_plain: The union of finitely many matroids is again a matroid. Its rank on U equals the minimum, over subsets T of U, of the number of elements outside T plus the sum of the component ranks of T restricted to their respective ground sets.
assumptions_latex: M_i=(S_i,\mathcal I_i)\text{ is a matroid with rank function }r_i\text{ for }i=1,\ldots,k.
knowledge_statements.conclusion_latex: M_1\vee\cdots\vee M_k\text{ is a matroid and }r(U)=\min_{T\subseteq U}\left(|U\setminus T|+\sum_{i=1}^k r_i(T\cap S_i)\right).

knowledge_statements.statement_title: Direct sum of matroids and its rank
knowledge_statements.scope_note: Defines the direct sum on two disjoint ground sets and states its rank formula.
knowledge_statements.statement_latex: Let M_1=(S_1,\mathcal I_1) and M_2=(S_2,\mathcal I_2) be matroids with S_1\cap S_2=\varnothing. Their direct sum is M_1\oplus M_2=(S_1\cup S_2,\mathcal I), where \mathcal I=\{J_1\cup J_2:J_i\in\mathcal I_i\}. This is a matroid, and for every A\subseteq S_1\cup S_2, r(A)=r_1(A\cap S_1)+r_2(A\cap S_2).
knowledge_statements.statement_plain: For matroids on disjoint ground sets, the independent sets of their direct sum are unions of one independent set from each component. The result is a matroid whose rank on any subset is the sum of the component ranks on the corresponding intersections.
assumptions_latex: M_i=(S_i,\mathcal I_i)\text{ is a matroid for }i=1,2
knowledge_statements.conclusion_latex: M_1\oplus M_2\text{ is a matroid and }r(A)=r_1(A\cap S_1)+r_2(A\cap S_2)\quad\forall A\subseteq S_1\cup S_2.

knowledge_statements.title: Union Feasibility Certificates
knowledge_statements.scope_note: Subset certificates for feasible and infeasible matroid-union decompositions.
knowledge_statements.statement_latex: Let \(M_i=(E,\mathcal I_i)\), \(i=1,\ldots,k\), be finite matroids with rank functions \(r_i\), and let \(X\subseteq E\). Exactly one of the following alternatives holds: (i) there are sets \(I_i\in\mathcal I_i\) such that \(X=I_1\cup\cdots\cup I_k\), which may be chosen pairwise disjoint; or (ii) there is a set \(A\subseteq X\) such that \(|A|>\sum_{i=1}^k r_i(A)\). The data in (i) certify feasibility, while the set in (ii) certifies infeasibility.
knowledge_statements.statement_plain: A valid independent-set decomposition certifies feasibility; otherwise, a subset whose size exceeds the sum of its ranks certifies infeasibility.
knowledge_statements.conclusion_latex: Either \(X=\bigcup_i I_i\) with \(I_i\in\mathcal I_i\), or \(\exists A\subseteq X:\ |A|>\sum_i r_i(A)\), but not both.

notation.meaning: Independent part assigned to matroid i.

knowledge_statements.title: Rank-Based Feasibility Tests
knowledge_statements.scope_note: Necessary and sufficient rank inequalities for covering a prescribed set.
knowledge_statements.statement_latex:
Let \(M_i=(E,\mathcal I_i)\), \(i=1,\ldots,k\), be finite matroids with rank functions \(r_i\). For a prescribed set \(X\subseteq E\), there exist sets \(I_i\in\mathcal I_i\) satisfying \(X=I_1\cup\cdots\cup I_k\) if and only if
\[
|A|\le \sum_{i=1}^k r_i(A)\qquad\text{for every }A\subseteq X.
\]
It is sufficient to test subsets of \(X\); elements outside \(X\) play no role in the feasibility predicate.
knowledge_statements.statement_plain: A set is decomposable among the matroids exactly when every one of its subsets has size at most the corresponding rank sum.
assumptions_latex: \(M_1,\ldots,M_k\) are finite matroids on the same ground set \(E\).
knowledge_statements.conclusion_latex: \(X\in\mathcal I(M_1\vee\cdots\vee M_k)\iff \forall A\subseteq X,\ |A|\le\sum_i r_i(A)\).

notation.meaning: Rank of A in matroid i.

knowledge_statements.title: Matroid-Union Polyhedra
knowledge_statements.scope_note: Independence polytope of the finite matroid union.
knowledge_statements.statement_latex:
Let \(M=M_1\vee\cdots\vee M_k\) be the union matroid on finite ground set \(E\), with union rank function \(r_{\vee}\). Its independence polytope is
\[
P(M)=\left\{x\in\mathbb R^E_{\ge0}:x(A)\le r_{\vee}(A)\text{ for every }A\subseteq E\right\}.
\]
Using the union-rank formula, the right-hand sides may equivalently be written as \(r_{\vee}(A)=\min_{T\subseteq A}(|A\setminus T|+\sum_i r_i(T))\).
knowledge_statements.statement_plain: The matroid-union polyhedron is the nonnegative rank-inequality polytope determined by the union matroid's rank function.
assumptions_latex: \(r_{\vee}\) is the rank function of their union.
knowledge_statements.conclusion_latex: \(P(M)=\{x\in\mathbb R^E_{\ge0}:x(A)\le r_{\vee}(A)\ \forall A\subseteq E\}\).

notation.meaning: The sum of coordinates indexed by A.

knowledge_statements.title: Union Polytope Integrality
knowledge_statements.scope_note: Integrality of the finite matroid-union independence polytope.
knowledge_statements.statement_latex:
For finite matroids \(M_1,\ldots,M_k\) on \(E\), let \(M=M_1\vee\cdots\vee M_k\). The polytope
\[
P(M)=\left\{x\in\mathbb R^E_{\ge0}:x(A)\le r_{\vee}(A)\text{ for all }A\subseteq E\right\}
\]
is integral: every vertex belongs to \(\{0,1\}^E\). Moreover, its integral points are exactly the incidence vectors of independent sets of the union matroid, equivalently of sets expressible as unions \(I_1\cup\cdots\cup I_k\) with \(I_i\in\mathcal I_i\).
knowledge_statements.statement_plain: Every vertex of the union independence polytope is integral and represents a set decomposable into independent sets of the input matroids.
assumptions_latex: \(M_1,\ldots,M_k\) are finite matroids on the same ground set \(E\).
knowledge_statements.conclusion_latex: \(\operatorname{vert}(P(M))\subseteq\{0,1\}^E\), and \(P(M)\cap\mathbb Z^E=\{\chi^I:I\in\mathcal I(M)\}\).

knowledge_statements.title: Integral Hull Descriptions
knowledge_statements.scope_note: Convex-hull description for incidence vectors of union-independent sets.
knowledge_statements.statement_latex:
Let \(M=M_1\vee\cdots\vee M_k\) be a finite matroid union with rank function \(r_{\vee}\). Then
\[
\operatorname{conv}\{\chi^I:I\in\mathcal I(M)\}
=
\left\{x\in\mathbb R^E:x\ge0,\ x(A)\le r_{\vee}(A)\text{ for every }A\subseteq E\right\}.
\]
Equivalently, substituting the union-rank formula gives the valid right-hand side \(x(A)\le\min_{T\subseteq A}(|A\setminus T|+\sum_i r_i(T))\) for every \(A\subseteq E\).
knowledge_statements.statement_plain: Rank inequalities give the exact convex hull of incidence vectors of sets decomposable among the input matroids.
knowledge_statements.conclusion_latex: \(\operatorname{conv}\{\chi^I:I\in\mathcal I(M)\}=\{x\ge0:x(A)\le r_{\vee}(A)\ \forall A\subseteq E\}\).

knowledge_statements.title: Augmenting Union Algorithms
knowledge_statements.scope_note: Exchange-path augmentation for maximum-cardinality matroid union.
knowledge_statements.statement_latex: Input finite matroids \(M_i=(E,\mathcal I_i)\) through independence oracles. Initialize pairwise disjoint \(I_i=\varnothing\). For an uncovered element, construct the exchange graph whose labeled move \(e\to f\) in class \(i\) is allowed when \((I_i\setminus\{f\})\cup\{e\}\in\mathcal I_i\); a path terminates when its current element can be inserted into some class without displacement. Apply the exchanges backward to increase \(|\bigcup_i I_i|\) by one. Repeat until no augmenting path exists, then output \(\bigcup_i I_i\), which has maximum cardinality in \(M_1\vee\cdots\vee M_k\).
knowledge_statements.statement_plain: Repeatedly route an uncovered element through valid exchanges; each augmenting path increases the covered set, and absence of one proves optimality.
assumptions_latex: Each \(M_i\) is a finite matroid on \(E\) with an independence oracle.
The maintained sets \(I_i\) are pairwise disjoint and independent in their respective matroids.
knowledge_statements.conclusion_latex: The output \(I=\bigcup_i I_i\) satisfies \(|I|=r_{\vee}(E)\).

notation.meaning: Current elements assigned to matroid i.

knowledge_statements.title: Matroid Partition Algorithms
knowledge_statements.scope_note: Constructive feasibility algorithm for partitioning a ground set among matroids.
knowledge_statements.statement_latex: Input finite matroids \(M_i=(E,\mathcal I_i)\) through independence oracles and initialize \(I_i=\varnothing\). Process elements by attempting to insert each uncovered \(e\) into a class; if direct insertion fails, search the labeled exchange graph for a sequence of displacements ending at a class admitting insertion. Apply such a sequence and continue. If every element is assigned, output the partition \(E=I_1\mathbin{\dot\cup}\cdots\mathbin{\dot\cup}I_k\). If augmentation fails, output a reachable-set obstruction \(A\subseteq E\) satisfying \(|A|>\sum_i r_i(A)\), which certifies that no feasible partition exists.
knowledge_statements.statement_plain: Exchange-path augmentation either partitions all elements into appropriate independent sets or returns a subset violating the rank-sum condition.
assumptions_latex: \(M_1,\ldots,M_k\) are finite matroids on \(E\) with independence oracles.
Each maintained part \(I_i\) is independent in \(M_i\).
knowledge_statements.conclusion_latex: The algorithm returns either \(E=\mathbin{\dot\bigcup}_i I_i\) with \(I_i\in\mathcal I_i\), or \(A\subseteq E\) with \(|A|>\sum_i r_i(A)\).

knowledge_statements.statement_title: Strongly polynomial minimum fractional independent-set decomposition
knowledge_statements.scope_note: Fractional matroid-partition algorithm for a nonnegative rational multiplicity vector.
knowledge_statements.statement_latex: Given a matroid $M=(S,\mathcal I)$ through an independence-testing oracle and $y\in\mathbb Q_+^S$, one can find independent sets $I_1,\ldots,I_k$ and coefficients $\lambda_1,\ldots,\lambda_k\in\mathbb Q_+$ such that $y=\sum_{i=1}^k\lambda_i\chi^{I_i}$ and $\sum_{i=1}^k\lambda_i$ is minimum, in strongly polynomial time.
knowledge_statements.statement_plain: For an oracle-presented matroid and a nonnegative rational vector, a minimum-total-coefficient decomposition into independent-set incidence vectors can be found in strongly polynomial time.
assumptions_latex: M=(S,\mathcal I)\text{ is given by an independence-testing oracle}
knowledge_statements.conclusion_latex: \text{A decomposition }y=\sum_{i=1}^k\lambda_i\chi^{I_i},\ I_i\in\mathcal I,\ \lambda_i\in\mathbb Q_+,\text{ minimizing }\sum_{i=1}^k\lambda_i\text{ is computable in strongly polynomial time.}

knowledge_statements.statement_title: Matroid Partition Rank Formula
knowledge_statements.scope_note: Rank characterization for the sum of finitely many matroids on a common ground set.
knowledge_statements.statement_latex: Let M_i=(S,r_i), i=1,\ldots,k, be matroids on the same finite ground set, and let M_{\sum} be their matroid sum. For every Z\subseteq S,\qquad r_{\sum}(Z)=\min_{X\subseteq Z}\left(|Z\setminus X|+\sum_{i=1}^k r_i(X)\right). Consequently, the maximum cardinality of a subset of S that can be partitioned into M_i-independent sets equals \min_{X\subseteq S}\left(|S\setminus X|+\sum_{i=1}^k r_i(X)\right).
knowledge_statements.statement_plain: For matroids on a common finite ground set, the rank of their sum on any subset Z is the minimum, over subsets X of Z, of the number of elements outside X plus the sum of the component ranks on X. At Z=S, this is the maximum size of a subset partitionable into one independent set from each matroid.
knowledge_statements.conclusion_latex: r_{\sum}(Z)=\min_{X\subseteq Z}\left\{|Z\setminus X|+\sum_{i=1}^k r_i(X)\right\}

knowledge_statements.statement_title: Edmonds Matroid Partitioning Algorithm
knowledge_statements.scope_note: Constructive partition of a common ground set among multiple matroids, with lexicographic maximality or detection of nonpartitionability.
knowledge_statements.statement_latex: Let M_i=(E,\mathcal I_i),\ i=1,\ldots,k, be matroids with rank functions r_i. Initialize I_i=\varnothing and U=E. Repeatedly construct sets S_j using rank and span tests. When an unassigned element e lies outside the current S_j, insert it into I_{\ell(j)} and, if a circuit is created, continue an exchange chain by removing an element of that circuit outside S_{j-1}. If no eligible block exists, declare E nonpartitionable. If U becomes empty, return (I_1,\ldots,I_k). When a partition exists, the returned partition lexicographically maximizes (|I_1|,\ldots,|I_k|).
knowledge_statements.statement_plain: Edmonds' algorithm uses rank, span, and circuit exchanges to partition a common ground set into independent sets of the given matroids. It either correctly reports nonpartitionability or returns a lexicographically maximum partition.
assumptions_latex: M_i=(E,\mathcal I_i)\text{ is a matroid for each }i=1,\ldots,k.
r_i\text{ and }\operatorname{sp}_i\text{ denote the rank and span operators of }M_i.
knowledge_statements.conclusion_latex: E=\biguplus_{i=1}^k I_i,\quad I_i\in\mathcal I_i,\quad (|I_1|,\ldots,|I_k|)\text{ is lexicographically maximum},\text{ or }E\text{ is correctly declared nonpartitionable.}

knowledge_statements.statement_title: Auxiliary Digraph and Terminal Certificate for Matroid Partitioning
knowledge_statements.scope_note: This extract specifies the auxiliary-digraph representation and its terminal optimality certificate, not the complete augmentation procedure. The current partitioning may be taken pairwise disjoint.
knowledge_statements.statement_latex: Let \(M_i=(S,\mathcal I_i)\), \(1\le i\le k\), and let \(J=\mathbin{\dot\bigcup}_{i=1}^k J_i\) with \(J_i\in\mathcal I_i\). Construct a digraph on \(S\cup\{r,s\}\) containing \(r\to e\) for every \(e\in S\setminus J\); \(e\to s\) whenever \(J_i\cup\{e\}\in\mathcal I_i\) for some \(i\); and \(e\to f\) whenever, for some \(i\), \(f\in J_i\), \(J_i\cup\{e\}\notin\mathcal I_i\), and \(J_i\triangle\{e,f\}\in\mathcal I_i\). At termination, if \(A\subseteq S\) satisfies \(\delta(A\cup\{s\})=\varnothing\), then \(J_i\cap A\) spans \(A\) in \(M_i\) for every \(i\), and \[|J|=|S\setminus A|+\sum_{i=1}^k r_i(A).\]
knowledge_statements.statement_plain: For a disjoint matroid partition, the auxiliary digraph has source arcs to unused elements, sink arcs for feasible insertions, and exchange arcs for feasible replacements. At termination, any set satisfying the stated empty-cut condition yields spanning conditions in every matroid and a rank equality certifying optimality.
assumptions_latex: M_i=(S,\mathcal I_i)\text{ is a matroid with rank function }r_i\text{ for }1\le i\le k
knowledge_statements.conclusion_latex: (J_i\cap A)\text{ spans }A\text{ in }M_i\text{ for every }i,\qquad |J|=|S\setminus A|+\sum_{i=1}^k r_i(A).

knowledge_statements.statement_title: Lattice Closure of Matroid-Partition Minimizers
knowledge_statements.scope_note: Closure and extremal elements of the minimizers of the matroid-union rank expression.
knowledge_statements.statement_latex: For matroids M_i=(S,r_i), i=1,\ldots,k, define \mathcal{X}=\operatorname*{argmin}_{X\subseteq S}\left(\sum_{i=1}^k r_i(X)+|S\setminus X|\right). If X,Y\in\mathcal{X}, then X\cap Y\in\mathcal{X} and X\cup Y\in\mathcal{X}. Hence \mathcal{X} has a unique inclusion-minimal member and a unique inclusion-maximal member.
knowledge_statements.statement_plain: The minimizers in the matroid-partition rank formula are closed under intersection and union. Therefore there is a unique smallest minimizer and a unique largest minimizer.
knowledge_statements.conclusion_latex: X,Y\in\mathcal{X}\Longrightarrow X\cap Y,X\cup Y\in\mathcal{X},\quad\text{and }\mathcal{X}\text{ has unique least and greatest members}

knowledge_statements.statement_title: Characterization of Matroid-Partition Minimizers
knowledge_statements.scope_note: Necessary and sufficient optimality conditions associated with a maximum family of disjoint independent sets.
knowledge_statements.statement_latex: Let M_i=(S,r_i), i=1,\ldots,k, and let F_1,\ldots,F_k\subseteq S be pairwise disjoint, with each F_i independent in M_i, such that |F_1\cup\cdots\cup F_k| is maximum. A set X\subseteq S minimizes \sum_{i=1}^k r_i(X)+|S\setminus X| if and only if |X\cap F_i|=r_i(X) for every i and X\cup F_1\cup\cdots\cup F_k=S.
knowledge_statements.statement_plain: Given a maximum collection of pairwise disjoint component-independent sets, X minimizes the matroid-partition rank expression exactly when each intersection X∩Fi has full rank on X in its component matroid and X together with all Fi covers the ground set.
knowledge_statements.conclusion_latex: X\in\operatorname*{argmin}_{Y\subseteq S}\left(\sum_{i=1}^k r_i(Y)+|S\setminus Y|\right)\iff\left[\forall i,\ |X\cap F_i|=r_i(X)\right]\land\left[X\cup\bigcup_{i=1}^kF_i=S\right]

knowledge_statements.statement_title: Edmonds Matroid Partition Augmentation Algorithm
knowledge_statements.scope_note: Exchange-digraph augmentation algorithm producing a maximum family of disjoint independent sets and an optimality certificate.
knowledge_statements.statement_latex: Let M_i=(S,r_i), i=1,\ldots,k, be matroids on a finite common ground set, and start with pairwise disjoint M_i-independent sets F_i. Put R=S\setminus\bigcup_iF_i and form the exchange digraph with terminal t_i, arcs xt_i when F_i+x is independent, and arcs xy for y in the fundamental M_i-circuit of F_i+x. If no path from R to the terminals exists, the vertices X reachable from R satisfy S=X\cup\bigcup_iF_i and |X\cap F_i|=r_i(X) for every i, certifying optimality. Otherwise, augment along a shortest R-to-terminal path by the prescribed exchanges; the resulting F_i remain independent and their union grows by one. Thus after at most |S| augmentations the procedure terminates with a maximum partitionable subset and a minimizing certificate X.
knowledge_statements.statement_plain: Starting from any disjoint independent sets, build an exchange digraph. A shortest path from an uncovered element to a component terminal yields exchanges that increase the covered union by one. If no such path exists, the reachable set supplies the rank-equality and coverage conditions certifying optimality. At most |S| augmentations occur.
assumptions_latex: F_1,\ldots,F_k\text{ are pairwise disjoint and each }F_i\text{ is }M_i\text{-independent}
knowledge_statements.conclusion_latex: \text{The algorithm returns maximum disjoint independent sets }F_i\text{ and }X\subseteq S\text{ with }S=X\cup\bigcup_iF_i,\ |X\cap F_i|=r_i(X),\text{ after at most }|S|\text{ augmentations}

children.top_down_role: Matroid-union problems with element-weight objectives.

knowledge_statements.title: Weighted Matroid-Union Variants
knowledge_statements.scope_note: Common element-weight version of finite matroid union.
knowledge_statements.statement_latex:
Let \(M_i=(E,\mathcal I_i)\), for \(i=1,\ldots,k\), be matroids with rank functions \(r_i\), and let \(w:E\to\mathbb R\). A set \(I\subseteq E\) is union-independent exactly when it can be partitioned as \(I=I_1\mathbin{\dot\cup}\cdots\mathbin{\dot\cup}I_k\) with \(I_i\in\mathcal I_i\). Consequently, the weighted matroid-union problem has the representation
\[\max\left\{\sum_{e\in E}w(e)x_e:x\in\{0,1\}^{E},\ \sum_{e\in F}x_e\leq\sum_{i=1}^{k}r_i(F)\ \text{for every }F\subseteq E\right\}.\]
An optimal support is a maximum-weight independent set of the union matroid.
knowledge_statements.statement_plain: Weighted matroid union maximizes element weight over sets partitionable into one independent set from each constituent matroid, equivalently over the displayed rank-inequality system.
knowledge_statements.conclusion_latex: \(\operatorname{supp}(x)\in\mathcal I_1\vee\cdots\vee\mathcal I_k\), and the displayed maximum is the weighted union optimum.

notation.meaning: Rank function of the matroid M_i.
Independent-set family of the union matroid.

knowledge_statements.title: Capacitated Matroid-Union Variants
knowledge_statements.scope_note: Assignment-capacity extension allowing an element in several constituent independent sets.
knowledge_statements.statement_latex:
Let \(M_i=(E,\mathcal I_i)\), for \(i=1,\ldots,k\), be matroids, and let \(b\in\mathbb Z_+^E\). A capacitated union assignment is a tuple \((I_1,\ldots,I_k)\) satisfying
\[I_i\in\mathcal I_i\quad(i=1,\ldots,k),\qquad \left|\{i:e\in I_i\}\right|\leq b_e\quad(e\in E).\]
Equivalently, its binary incidence vectors satisfy \(y^i\in\{0,1\}^E\), \(\operatorname{supp}(y^i)\in\mathcal I_i\), and \(\sum_{i=1}^k y^i_e\leq b_e\) for every \(e\in E\). The usual disjoint matroid union is recovered when \(b_e=1\) for every \(e\in E\).
knowledge_statements.statement_plain: A capacitated union assignment selects one independent set per matroid while limiting how many selected sets may use each ground element.
assumptions_latex: \(b_e\) is a nonnegative integer for every \(e\in E\).
knowledge_statements.conclusion_latex: \((I_1,\ldots,I_k)\) is feasible exactly when all constituent-independence and element-load constraints hold.

notation.meaning: Maximum permitted number of constituent sets using element e.
Indicator that element e is assigned to the i-th independent set.

knowledge_statements.title: Weighted Capacitated Union
knowledge_statements.scope_note: Assignment-weighted optimization over capacitated matroid-union selections.
knowledge_statements.statement_latex:
For matroids \(M_i=(E,\mathcal I_i)\), capacities \(b\in\mathbb Z_+^E\), and assignment weights \(w_{i,e}\in\mathbb R\), weighted capacitated union is
\[\max\left\{\sum_{i=1}^{k}\sum_{e\in E}w_{i,e}y^i_e:\ y^i\in\{0,1\}^{E},\ \operatorname{supp}(y^i)\in\mathcal I_i,\ \sum_{i=1}^{k}y^i_e\leq b_e\ \text{for every }e\in E\right\}.\]
The formulation permits different rewards for assigning the same element to different matroids. With \(b_e=1\) and \(w_{i,e}=w_e\), it specializes to common-weight matroid union.
knowledge_statements.statement_plain: Weighted capacitated union chooses independent assignments of maximum total reward subject to a usage capacity for every element.
knowledge_statements.conclusion_latex: The displayed integer program is the weighted capacitated-union optimum.

notation.meaning: Reward for assigning element e to matroid i.

knowledge_statements.statement_title: Matroid via base exchange or rank axioms
knowledge_statements.scope_note: Defines a matroid in either of its equivalent base-family and rank-function forms.
knowledge_statements.statement_latex: A matroid may be specified as (V,\mathcal B), where V is finite, \mathcal B\subseteq2^V is nonempty, and for all J,J'\in\mathcal B and i\in J\setminus J' there exists j\in J'\setminus J with J-i+j,J'+i-j\in\mathcal B. Equivalently, it may be specified as (V,\rho), where \rho:2^V\to\mathbb Z satisfies 0\leq\rho(X)\leq|X|, X\subseteq Y\Rightarrow\rho(X)\leq\rho(Y), and \rho(X)+\rho(Y)\geq\rho(X\cup Y)+\rho(X\cap Y). Here V is the ground set, \mathcal B is the base family, members of \mathcal B are bases, and subsets of bases are independent sets.
knowledge_statements.statement_plain: A matroid on a finite ground set is equivalently a nonempty base family satisfying simultaneous exchange or an integer-valued rank function satisfying boundedness, monotonicity, and submodularity. Bases are members of the base family, and their subsets are independent.
knowledge_statements.conclusion_latex: (V,\mathcal B)\text{ satisfying base exchange and }(V,\rho)\text{ satisfying the rank axioms are equivalent descriptions of a matroid.}

knowledge_statements.title: Fractional Base Packing
knowledge_statements.scope_note: Capacity-weighted fractional packing in the base hypergraph of a matroid.
knowledge_statements.statement_latex:
Let \(M=(E,\mathcal I)\) have base family \(\mathcal B\), and let \(c\in\mathbb R_+^E\) be element capacities. A fractional base packing is a vector \(\lambda\in\mathbb R_+^{\mathcal B}\) satisfying
\[\sum_{B\in\mathcal B:e\in B}\lambda_B\leq c_e\qquad(e\in E).\]
Its value is \(\sum_{B\in\mathcal B}\lambda_B\), and the fractional base-packing number is
\[\nu_f(M,c)=\max\left\{\sum_{B\in\mathcal B}\lambda_B:\lambda\geq0,\ \sum_{B\ni e}\lambda_B\leq c_e\ \text{for every }e\in E\right\}.\]
knowledge_statements.statement_plain: A fractional base packing assigns nonnegative weights to bases so that the total weight using each element does not exceed its capacity.
assumptions_latex: \(M\) is a finite matroid with at least one base.
knowledge_statements.conclusion_latex: \(\nu_f(M,c)\) is the maximum total feasible base weight.

notation.meaning: Fractional multiplicity assigned to base B.

children.title: Fractional Base Covering
children.top_down_role: Fractional allocation regimes for covering elements with matroid bases.

knowledge_statements.title: Fractional Base Covering
knowledge_statements.scope_note: Demand-weighted fractional covering by matroid bases.
knowledge_statements.statement_latex:
Let \(M=(E,\mathcal I)\) have base family \(\mathcal B\), and let \(d\in\mathbb R_+^E\) be element demands. A fractional base covering is a vector \(\mu\in\mathbb R_+^{\mathcal B}\) satisfying
\[\sum_{B\in\mathcal B:e\in B}\mu_B\geq d_e\qquad(e\in E).\]
Its cost under unit base costs is \(\sum_{B\in\mathcal B}\mu_B\), and the fractional covering number is
\[\tau_f(M,d)=\min\left\{\sum_{B\in\mathcal B}\mu_B:\mu\geq0,\ \sum_{B\ni e}\mu_B\geq d_e\ \text{for every }e\in E\right\}.\]
knowledge_statements.statement_plain: A fractional base covering weights bases so that their total weight through every element meets that element's demand.
knowledge_statements.conclusion_latex: \(\tau_f(M,d)\) is the minimum total base weight satisfying all demands.

notation.meaning: Fractional multiplicity assigned to base B.

children.title: Fractional Packing–Covering Duality
children.top_down_role: Dual relationship between fractional base packing and covering parameters.

knowledge_statements.title: Fractional Packing–Covering Duality
knowledge_statements.scope_note: LP duality for capacity packing and demand covering over the base-incidence matrix.
knowledge_statements.statement_latex:
For a finite matroid with base family \(\mathcal B\), linear-programming duality gives
\[\nu_f(M,c)=\min\left\{\sum_{e\in E}c_e y_e:y\in\mathbb R_+^E,\ \sum_{e\in B}y_e\geq1\ \text{for every }B\in\mathcal B\right\},\]
and
\[\tau_f(M,d)=\max\left\{\sum_{e\in E}d_e z_e:z\in\mathbb R_+^E,\ \sum_{e\in B}z_e\leq1\ \text{for every }B\in\mathcal B\right\}.\]
Thus fractional base packing is dual to an element cover of all bases, while fractional base covering is dual to an element packing constrained on every base.
knowledge_statements.statement_plain: LP duality converts base weights into element prices: packing yields base-covering inequalities, while covering yields base-packing inequalities.
assumptions_latex: \(M\) is finite and has at least one base.
\(c,d\in\mathbb R_+^E\), and the relevant primal optimum is finite.
knowledge_statements.conclusion_latex: The two displayed primal-dual optimum equalities hold.

notation.meaning: Dual price for packing capacity at element e.
Dual weight associated with covering element e.

children.title: Integer Base Packing

knowledge_statements.title: Integer Base Packing
knowledge_statements.scope_note: Edmonds' finite base-packing criterion and min-max formula.
knowledge_statements.statement_latex:
Let \(M=(E,\mathcal I)\) be a finite matroid of positive rank \(r(E)\). There exist \(k\) pairwise disjoint bases if and only if
\[|E\setminus X|\geq k\bigl(r(E)-r(X)\bigr)\qquad\text{for every }X\subseteq E.\]
Consequently, the maximum number of pairwise disjoint bases is
\[\nu(M)=\min_{\substack{X\subseteq E\\r(X)<r(E)}}\left\lfloor\frac{|E\setminus X|}{r(E)-r(X)}\right\rfloor.\]
The minimum is taken only over subsets with positive denominator.
knowledge_statements.statement_plain: A matroid contains k disjoint bases exactly when every subset leaves enough outside elements to supply k copies of its rank deficit.
knowledge_statements.conclusion_latex: \(\nu(M)=\min_{X:r(X)<r(E)}\left\lfloor |E\setminus X|/(r(E)-r(X))\right\rfloor\).

notation.meaning: Maximum number of pairwise disjoint bases.

knowledge_statements.statement_title: Rank and co-rank criteria for bounded element multiplicities in selected matroid bases
knowledge_statements.scope_note: Necessary and sufficient subset inequalities for selecting one basis from each of several matroids with prescribed element-occurrence bounds.
knowledge_statements.statement_latex: Let $M_i$ be matroids on $S$ with rank functions $r_i$ and co-rank functions $t_i$, $i=1,\ldots,k$, and write $\widetilde f(X)=\sum_{s\in X}f(s)$ and $\widetilde g(X)=\sum_{s\in X}g(s)$. Bases $B_i$ of $M_i$ can be selected so that every $s\in S$ belongs to at least $f(s)$ of them if and only if $\sum_{i=1}^k r_i(X)\ge\widetilde f(X)$ for every $X\subseteq S$. They can be selected so that every $s$ belongs to at most $g(s)$ of them if and only if $\sum_{i=1}^k t_i(X)\le\widetilde g(X)$ for every $X\subseteq S$. Bases satisfying both bounds simultaneously exist if and only if both families of inequalities hold.
knowledge_statements.statement_plain: For several matroids on the same ground set, selected bases meet prescribed lower element-occurrence bounds exactly when all rank-sum inequalities hold, and meet prescribed upper bounds exactly when all co-rank-sum inequalities hold. Both kinds of bounds can be met simultaneously exactly when the two one-sided criteria both hold.
assumptions_latex: M_i\text{ is a matroid on the common ground set }S\text{ for }i=1,\ldots,k
r_i\text{ and }t_i\text{ are respectively the rank and co-rank functions of }M_i
knowledge_statements.conclusion_latex: \begin{aligned}&\exists(B_i)_{i=1}^k\ \forall s:\ \sum_i\mathbf1_{s\in B_i}\ge f(s)\iff \forall X\subseteq S:\ \sum_i r_i(X)\ge\widetilde f(X),\\&\exists(B_i)_{i=1}^k\ \forall s:\ \sum_i\mathbf1_{s\in B_i}\le g(s)\iff \forall X\subseteq S:\ \sum_i t_i(X)\le\widetilde g(X),\\&\exists(B_i)_{i=1}^k\ \forall s:\ f(s)\le\sum_i\mathbf1_{s\in B_i}\le g(s)\iff\text{ both inequality systems hold.}\end{aligned}

knowledge_statements.statement_title: Matroid base packing theorem
knowledge_statements.scope_note: Rank-inequality characterization of the existence of k pairwise disjoint bases.
knowledge_statements.statement_latex: Let M=(S,\mathcal I) be a matroid with rank function r, and let k\in\mathbb Z_{+}. Then M\text{ has }k\text{ pairwise disjoint bases}\iff k\bigl(r(S)-r(U)\bigr)\le |S\setminus U|\quad\text{for every }U\subseteq S.
knowledge_statements.statement_plain: A matroid has k pairwise disjoint bases if and only if, for every subset U, the elements outside U are numerous enough to supply k copies of the rank deficit from U to the whole ground set.

knowledge_statements.conclusion_latex: M\text{ has }k\text{ pairwise disjoint bases}\iff (\forall U\subseteq S)\;k\left(r(S)-r(U)\right)\le |S\setminus U|.

children.title: Integer Base Covering

knowledge_statements.title: Integer Base Covering
knowledge_statements.scope_note: Finite matroid-union criterion for covering the ground set by bases.
knowledge_statements.statement_latex:
Let \(M=(E,\mathcal I)\) be a finite loopless matroid with rank function \(r\), and let \(k\) be a positive integer. The ground set \(E\) can be covered by \(k\) bases, with overlaps allowed, if and only if
\[|X|\leq k\,r(X)\qquad\text{for every }X\subseteq E.\]
Consequently, the minimum number of bases covering \(E\) is
\[\tau(M)=\max_{\varnothing\neq X\subseteq E}\left\lceil\frac{|X|}{r(X)}\right\rceil.\]
knowledge_statements.statement_plain: A finite loopless matroid can be covered by k bases exactly when every subset has cardinality at most k times its rank; hence its minimum base-covering number is the displayed maximum of rounded-up cardinality-to-rank ratios.
knowledge_statements.conclusion_latex: \(\tau(M)=\max_{\varnothing\neq X\subseteq E}\left\lceil |X|/r(X)\right\rceil\).

notation.meaning: Minimum number of bases whose union is E.

knowledge_statements.statement_title: Rank Criterion for Covering by Matroid Bases
knowledge_statements.scope_note: Covering a common ground set by one base from each of several matroids; the bases are not required to be disjoint.
knowledge_statements.statement_latex: Let \mathbf M_i=(E,\mathcal I_i) have rank function \rho_i for i=1,\ldots,k. There exist bases B_i of \mathbf M_i such that \bigcup_{i=1}^k B_i=E if and only if \[\forall X\subseteq E,\qquad \sum_{i=1}^k\rho_i(X)\ge |X|.\]

children.title: Integer Packing–Covering Gap
children.top_down_role: Structural differences between integral packing and covering parameters.

knowledge_statements.title: Integer Packing–Covering Gap
knowledge_statements.scope_note: Unbounded separation between integer base-packing and base-covering numbers.
knowledge_statements.statement_latex: For each integer \(m\geq1\), let \(M_m\) be the partition matroid on two nonempty blocks \(P_1,P_2\) with \(|P_1|=1\), \(|P_2|=m\), and capacity one on each block. Every base contains one element from each block. Therefore any two bases intersect in the unique element of \(P_1\), so \(\nu(M_m)=1\). Covering every element of \(P_2\) requires at least \(m\) bases and is achievable with \(m\) bases, so \(\tau(M_m)=m\). Thus \(\tau(M_m)-\nu(M_m)=m-1\), showing that no universal additive packing-covering bound exists.
knowledge_statements.statement_plain: A two-block partition matroid with block sizes one and m has packing number one and covering number m, producing an unbounded additive gap.
assumptions_latex: Each base of \(M_m\) selects exactly one element from each block.

children.title: Blocking-Polyhedron View
children.top_down_role: Blocking geometry associated with base-covering structures.

knowledge_statements.title: Blocking-Polyhedron View
knowledge_statements.scope_note: Upward-closed polyhedral representation of covering constraints.
knowledge_statements.statement_latex:
A blocking polyhedron is a nonempty polyhedron \(P\subseteq\mathbb R_+^E\) satisfying \(P+\mathbb R_+^E=P\). For a finite nonempty family \(\mathcal S\subseteq2^E\), its incidence-vector dominant
\[P_{\mathcal S}=\operatorname{conv}\{\chi^S:S\in\mathcal S\}+\mathbb R_+^E\]
is a blocking polyhedron. Its blocker is
\[b(P_{\mathcal S})=\{y\in\mathbb R_+^E:\langle y,x\rangle\geq1\ \text{for every }x\in P_{\mathcal S}\}=\{y\in\mathbb R_+^E:y(S)\geq1\ \text{for every }S\in\mathcal S\}.\]
Thus the nonnegative vectors covering every member of \(\mathcal S\) are precisely the members of \(b(P_{\mathcal S})\).
knowledge_statements.statement_plain: A blocking polyhedron is a nonempty upward-closed nonnegative polyhedron. The blocker of a set-family incidence dominant consists exactly of the nonnegative vectors assigning weight at least one to every represented set.
knowledge_statements.conclusion_latex: \(b(P_{\mathcal S})=\{y\in\mathbb R_+^E:y(S)\geq1\text{ for every }S\in\mathcal S\}\).

notation.meaning: Dominant of the incidence vectors of the set family.
Blocker of a nonnegative blocking polyhedron.

children.title: Antiblocking-Polyhedron View
children.top_down_role: Antiblocking geometry associated with base-packing structures.

knowledge_statements.title: Antiblocking-Polyhedron View
knowledge_statements.scope_note: Downward-closed convex representation of packing constraints.
knowledge_statements.statement_latex:
A convex corner is a nonempty compact convex set \(Q\subseteq\mathbb R_+^E\) that is lower-comprehensive: if \(x\in Q\) and \(0\leq x'\leq x\), then \(x'\in Q\). Its antiblocker is
\[\operatorname{abl}(Q)=\{y\in\mathbb R_+^E:\langle y,x\rangle\leq1\ \text{for every }x\in Q\}.\]
The set \(\operatorname{abl}(Q)\) is again a convex corner. If \(D\subseteq\mathbb R_+^E\) is finite and \(Q=\operatorname{conv}(D)\) is a convex corner, then
\[\operatorname{abl}(Q)=\{y\in\mathbb R_+^E:\langle y,d\rangle\leq1\ \text{for every }d\in D\},\]
which is a packing-inequality representation indexed by \(D\).
knowledge_statements.statement_plain: Antiblocking maps a compact downward-closed nonnegative convex set to the nonnegative vectors whose scalar product with every feasible vector is at most one; for a finite generating set, it suffices to impose the inequalities on the generators.
assumptions_latex: \(Q\) is a convex corner in \(\mathbb R_+^E\).
When a generating set is used, \(D\subseteq\mathbb R_+^E\) is finite and \(Q=\operatorname{conv}(D)\).
knowledge_statements.conclusion_latex: \(\operatorname{abl}(Q)\) is a convex corner, with the displayed finite inequality description when \(Q=\operatorname{conv}(D)\).

notation.meaning: Antiblocker of the convex corner Q.
Finite generating set whose convex hull is Q.

children.title: Blocking–Antiblocking Polarity
children.top_down_role: Polar relationship connecting the two geometric viewpoints.

knowledge_statements.title: Blocking–Antiblocking Polarity
knowledge_statements.scope_note: Involutive polarity for nonnegative blocking polyhedra and convex corners.
knowledge_statements.statement_latex:
Let \(P\subseteq\mathbb R_+^E\) be a nonempty closed convex blocking polyhedron with \(0\notin P\), and let \(Q\subseteq\mathbb R_+^E\) be a convex corner. Define
\[b(P)=\{y\geq0:\langle y,x\rangle\geq1\ \text{for every }x\in P\},\qquad \operatorname{abl}(Q)=\{y\geq0:\langle y,x\rangle\leq1\ \text{for every }x\in Q\}.\]
Nonnegative separation yields the involutions
\[b(b(P))=P,\qquad \operatorname{abl}(\operatorname{abl}(Q))=Q.\]
Accordingly, either member of a blocking or antiblocking polar pair determines the other uniquely.
knowledge_statements.statement_plain: Taking the blocker twice recovers a closed blocking polyhedron, and taking the antiblocker twice recovers a convex corner.
assumptions_latex: \(P\) is nonempty, closed, convex, blocking, and excludes the origin.
\(Q\) is nonempty, compact, convex, and lower-comprehensive.
knowledge_statements.conclusion_latex: \(b(b(P))=P\) and \(\operatorname{abl}(\operatorname{abl}(Q))=Q\).

notation.meaning: Blocking polar defined by scalar products at least one.
Antiblocking polar defined by scalar products at most one.

children.title: Graph Arboricity
children.top_down_role: Arboricity viewed through graphic-matroid union.

knowledge_statements.title: Graph Arboricity
knowledge_statements.scope_note: Defines arboricity for finite loopless multigraphs.
knowledge_statements.statement_latex:
For a finite loopless multigraph \(G=(V,E)\), its arboricity is
\[
a(G):=\min\bigl\{k\in\mathbb{Z}_{\ge 0}:E=F_1\mathbin{\dot\cup}\cdots\mathbin{\dot\cup}F_k,\ (V,F_i)\text{ is a forest for every }i\bigr\}.
\]
The empty graph has \(a(G)=0\). Parallel edges are permitted, but no forest may contain two parallel edges joining the same vertices.
knowledge_statements.statement_plain: The arboricity of a finite loopless multigraph is the minimum number of forests whose edge sets partition all its edges.
knowledge_statements.conclusion_latex: \(a(G)\) is the minimum size of a partition of \(E\) into forests.

children.title: Forest Partition

knowledge_statements.title: Forest Partition
knowledge_statements.scope_note: Defines a fixed-size forest partition of a graph.
knowledge_statements.statement_latex:
Let \(G=(V,E)\) be a finite loopless multigraph and let \(k\in\mathbb{Z}_{\ge 0}\). A \(k\)-forest partition of \(G\) is an ordered family \((F_1,\ldots,F_k)\) of pairwise disjoint subsets of \(E\) such that
\[
E=\bigcup_{i=1}^{k}F_i
\quad\text{and}\quad
(V,F_i)\text{ is acyclic for every }i\in\{1,\ldots,k\}.
\]
Empty parts are allowed.
knowledge_statements.statement_plain: A k-forest partition assigns every edge to one of k parts so that each part induces an acyclic spanning subgraph.
knowledge_statements.conclusion_latex: \((F_1,\ldots,F_k)\) partitions \(E\) and every \((V,F_i)\) is a forest.

notation.meaning: the edge set of forest part i

knowledge_statements.statement_title: Finest and coarsest k-rich/k-sparse decompositions
knowledge_statements.scope_note: Existence and extremal uniqueness of a vertex partition separating rich induced pieces from a sparse contraction.
knowledge_statements.statement_latex: For every undirected graph G=(V,E) and positive integer k, there exists a partition \mathcal P=\{V_1,\ldots,V_q\} of V, q\ge 1, such that every induced graph G[V_i] is k\text{-rich} and the graph obtained by contracting each V_i to one vertex is k\text{-sparse}. Among all such partitions there are a finest partition \mathcal P_0 and a coarsest partition \mathcal P_1. Every member of \mathcal P_0 induces a strictly k\text{-rich} graph, and contracting every member of \mathcal P_1 produces a strictly k\text{-sparse} graph.

children.title: Arboricity–Partition Correspondence
children.top_down_role: Structural correspondence between arboricity bounds and forest partitions.

knowledge_statements.title: Arboricity–Partition Correspondence
knowledge_statements.scope_note: Nash-Williams arboricity formula in graphic-matroid form.
knowledge_statements.statement_latex:
Let \(G=(V,E)\) be a finite loopless multigraph. For nonempty \(F\subseteq E\), let \(V(F)\) be the vertices incident with \(F\), and let \(c(F)\) be the number of connected components of \((V(F),F)\). Then \(E\) can be partitioned into \(k\) forests if and only if
\[
|F|\le k\bigl(|V(F)|-c(F)\bigr)
\quad\text{for every nonempty }F\subseteq E.
\]
Consequently,
\[
a(G)=\max_{\varnothing\ne F\subseteq E}\left\lceil\frac{|F|}{|V(F)|-c(F)}\right\rceil,
\]
with \(a(G)=0\) when \(E=\varnothing\).
knowledge_statements.statement_plain: A graph decomposes into k forests exactly when every edge subset has size at most k times its graphic rank; the maximum density ceiling equals arboricity.
knowledge_statements.conclusion_latex: \(E\) is partitionable into \(k\) forests exactly under the displayed subset inequalities, and their least feasible \(k\) equals \(a(G)\).

notation.meaning: vertices incident with edges in F
number of components of the edge-induced subgraph on V(F)

children.title: Matroid Coloring
children.top_down_role: Partition-based coloring of a matroid ground set.

knowledge_statements.title: Matroid Coloring
knowledge_statements.scope_note: Defines the chromatic number of a finite matroid.
knowledge_statements.statement_latex:
Let \(M=(E,\mathcal I)\) be a finite matroid. A proper \(k\)-coloring is a map \(\varphi:E\to\{1,
\ldots,k\}\) such that every color class \(\varphi^{-1}(i)\) belongs to \(\mathcal I\). The matroid chromatic number is
\[
\chi(M):=\min\bigl\{k\in\mathbb Z_{\ge 0}:E\text{ is the union of }k\text{ independent sets}\bigr\}.
\]
Set \(\chi(M)=\infty\) if \(M\) has a loop, and \(\chi(M)=0\) if \(E=\varnothing\).
knowledge_statements.statement_plain: The chromatic number of a finite matroid is the minimum number of independent color classes covering its ground set; a loop makes it infinite.
knowledge_statements.conclusion_latex: \(\chi(M)\) is the least number of independent sets whose union is \(E\).

notation.meaning: family of independent sets of M

children.title: Matroid List Coloring

knowledge_statements.title: Matroid List Coloring
knowledge_statements.scope_note: Defines list colorability and list chromatic number for finite matroids.
knowledge_statements.statement_latex: Let \(M=(E,\mathcal I)\) be a finite matroid. Given finite color lists \(L(e)\) for \(e\in E\), an \(L\)-coloring is a map \(\varphi:E\to\bigcup_{e\in E}L(e)\) such that \(\varphi(e)\in L(e)\) for every \(e\), and each color class \(\varphi^{-1}(c)\) is independent. The list chromatic number \(\chi_\ell(M)\) is the least \(k\) such that an \(L\)-coloring exists whenever \(|L(e)|\ge k\) for all \(e\). It is \(\infty\) when \(M\) has a loop.
knowledge_statements.statement_plain: The list chromatic number is the least k guaranteeing an independent-class coloring from every assignment of at least k allowed colors per element.
assumptions_latex: Each \(L(e)\) is a finite set of colors.
knowledge_statements.conclusion_latex: \(\chi_\ell(M)\) is the universal list-size threshold for a proper matroid coloring.

children.title: Coloring-to-List-Coloring Transfer
children.top_down_role: Structural relationships between ordinary and list-constrained matroid coloring.

knowledge_statements.title: Coloring-to-List-Coloring Transfer
knowledge_statements.scope_note: Seymour's list-coloring theorem for finite matroids.
knowledge_statements.statement_latex:
For every finite matroid \(M=(E,\mathcal I)\),
\[
\chi_\ell(M)=\chi(M).
\]
Equivalently, if \(E\) can be partitioned into \(k\) independent sets and every element \(e\in E\) is assigned a list \(L(e)\) with \(|L(e)|\ge k\), then there exists a choice \(\varphi(e)\in L(e)\) such that every color class \(\varphi^{-1}(c)\) is independent. The equality uses the convention that both parameters are \(\infty\) when \(M\) has a loop.
knowledge_statements.statement_plain: Every finite matroid has equal ordinary and list chromatic numbers: any feasible k-coloring transfers to every assignment of lists having at least k colors per element.
assumptions_latex: \(k\in\mathbb Z_{\ge 0}\), and \(|L(e)|\ge k\) for every \(e\in E\) in the equivalent formulation.
knowledge_statements.conclusion_latex: \(\chi_\ell(M)=\chi(M)\).

children.title: Matroid Density Parameters
children.top_down_role: Rank-normalized density measures relevant to union applications.

knowledge_statements.title: Matroid Density Parameters
knowledge_statements.scope_note: Defines maximum rank density for a finite matroid.
knowledge_statements.statement_latex:
Let \(M=(E,r)\) be a finite matroid. Its maximum rank density is
\[
\gamma(M):=\max_{\varnothing\ne A\subseteq E}\frac{|A|}{r(A)},
\]
where a quotient with \(r(A)=0\) is interpreted as \(\infty\). Thus \(\gamma(M)=\infty\) exactly when \(M\) has a loop. For \(E=\varnothing\), set \(\gamma(M)=0\). The integral density parameter is \(d(M):=\lceil\gamma(M)\rceil\).
knowledge_statements.statement_plain: Maximum matroid density is the largest ratio of a nonempty subset's size to its rank; its ceiling is the integral density parameter.
knowledge_statements.conclusion_latex: \(\gamma(M)=\max_{\varnothing\ne A\subseteq E}|A|/r(A)\) and \(d(M)=\lceil\gamma(M)\rceil\).

knowledge_statements.title: Matroid Covering Parameters
knowledge_statements.scope_note: Defines independent-set covering and partition parameters.
knowledge_statements.statement_latex:
For a finite matroid \(M=(E,\mathcal I)\), define
\[
\kappa(M):=\min\bigl\{k\in\mathbb Z_{\ge0}:E=I_1\cup\cdots\cup I_k,\ I_i\in\mathcal I\text{ for every }i\bigr\}.
\]
Equivalently, \(\kappa(M)\) is the minimum number of independent sets whose pairwise-disjoint union is \(E\). Set \(\kappa(M)=\infty\) if \(M\) has a loop and \(\kappa(M)=0\) when \(E=\varnothing\).
knowledge_statements.statement_plain: The covering parameter is the least number of independent sets covering the ground set, equivalently the least number of independent sets partitioning it.
knowledge_statements.conclusion_latex: \(\kappa(M)\) is both the minimum independent-cover size and the minimum independent-partition size.

knowledge_statements.statement_title: Balanced Distribution of a Prescribed Set
knowledge_statements.scope_note: Loop-free matroid refinement for independent-set partitions and disjoint-base packings.
knowledge_statements.statement_latex: Let \(M=(S,r)\) be loop-free, let \(k\in\mathbf Z_{+}\), and let \(J\subseteq S\) satisfy \(|J|\le k\). (A) If \(S\) can be partitioned into \(k\) independent sets, then it has such a partition in which every part contains at most one element of \(J\). (B) If \(M\) has \(k\) pairwise disjoint bases, then it has \(k\) pairwise disjoint bases whose union contains \(J\) and each of which contains at most one element of \(J\).
knowledge_statements.statement_plain: In a loop-free matroid, any distinguished set of at most k elements can be spread one per member across a feasible k-part independent-set partition; likewise it can be covered and spread one per base across a packing of k disjoint bases.
knowledge_statements.conclusion_latex: \(\bigl[S\text{ partitions into }k\text{ independent sets}\bigr]\Rightarrow\bigl[\exists(S_1,\ldots,S_k):S=\dot\bigcup_jS_j,\ S_j\text{ independent},\ |S_j\cap J|\le1\bigr]\), and \(\bigl[M\text{ has }k\text{ disjoint bases}\bigr]\Rightarrow\bigl[\exists\text{ disjoint bases }B_1,\ldots,B_k:\ J\subseteq\bigcup_jB_j,\ |B_j\cap J|\le1\bigr]\)

children.title: Density–Covering Correspondence
children.top_down_role: Structural links between density thresholds and covering requirements.

knowledge_statements.title: Density–Covering Correspondence
knowledge_statements.scope_note: Matroid-union characterization of independent-set covering.
knowledge_statements.statement_latex:
Let \(M=(E,r)\) be a finite matroid and let \(k\in\mathbb Z_{\ge0}\). The ground set \(E\) can be covered, equivalently partitioned, by \(k\) independent sets if and only if
\[
|A|\le k\,r(A)
\quad\text{for every }A\subseteq E.
\]
Consequently,
\[
\kappa(M)=\max_{\varnothing\ne A\subseteq E}\left\lceil\frac{|A|}{r(A)}\right\rceil
=\lceil\gamma(M)\rceil,
\]
with the conventions \(\kappa(M)=\gamma(M)=\infty\) when \(M\) has a loop and both equal \(0\) when \(E=\varnothing\).
knowledge_statements.statement_plain: A matroid is coverable by k independent sets exactly when every subset has size at most k times its rank; the covering number is ceiling density.
knowledge_statements.conclusion_latex: \(E\) is coverable by \(k\) independent sets iff \(|A|\le kr(A)\) for all \(A\subseteq E\), and \(\kappa(M)=\lceil\gamma(M)\rceil\).

knowledge_statements.statement_title: Rado’s Matroidal Matching Theorem
knowledge_statements.scope_note: Characterizes when a bipartite graph admits a matroid-independent matching covering one vertex class.
knowledge_statements.statement_latex: Let \(M=(S,r)\) be a matroid and \(G=(S,T;E)\) a bipartite graph. Then \(G\) has an \(M_E\)-independent matching covering \(T\) if and only if \[r(\Gamma_G(X))\ge |X|\qquad\text{for every }X\subseteq T.\]
knowledge_statements.statement_plain: A bipartite graph has a matroid-independent matching covering T exactly when the matroid rank of the neighborhood of every subset X of T is at least the size of X.
knowledge_statements.conclusion_latex: G\text{ has an }M_E\text{-independent matching covering }T\iff (\forall X\subseteq T)\ r(\Gamma_G(X))\ge |X|

knowledge_statements.statement_title: Rank formula for a homomorphic image
knowledge_statements.scope_note: Defines the homomorphic-image matroid and gives its rank on every subset of the target set.

knowledge_statements.scope_note: Equivalent union, induced-edge, and orientation conditions for a hypergraph to admit distinct representatives.

knowledge_statements.title: Matroidal Systems of Representatives
knowledge_statements.scope_note: Rado's independent-transversal theorem for finite set families.
knowledge_statements.statement_latex:
Let \(M=(E,r)\) be a finite matroid and let \((A_i)_{i\in I}\) be a finite family of subsets of \(E\). There exist pairwise distinct representatives \(x_i\in A_i\) for all \(i\in I\) such that \(\{x_i:i\in I\}\) is independent in \(M\) if and only if
\[
r\left(\bigcup_{i\in J}A_i\right)\ge |J|
\quad\text{for every }J\subseteq I.
\]

knowledge_statements.conclusion_latex: An independent system of distinct representatives exists iff \(r(\bigcup_{i\in J}A_i)\ge |J|\) for every \(J\subseteq I\).

knowledge_statements.statement_title: Criterion for a Common System of Restricted Representatives
knowledge_statements.scope_note: For U\subseteq S, write a(U)=\sum_{s\in U}a(s) and b(U)=\sum_{s\in U}b(s). A common SRR is a bounded-multiplicity representative multiset realizable for each family, not necessarily through identical indexwise assignments.
knowledge_statements.statement_latex:
Let \mathcal A=(A_1,\ldots,A_n) and \mathcal B=(B_1,\ldots,B_n) be families of subsets of S, and let a,b\in\mathbb Z_+^S with a\le b. Then \mathcal A and \mathcal B have a common system of restricted representatives if and only if, for all I,J\subseteq[n],
\[
b(A_I\cap B_J)\ge |I|+|J|-n+a\bigl(S\setminus(A_I\cup B_J)\bigr),
\]
where A_I=\bigcup_{i\in I}A_i and B_J=\bigcup_{j\in J}B_j.
knowledge_statements.statement_plain: The two families admit a common bounded-multiplicity representative multiset exactly when the displayed inequality holds for every pair of index subsets. Its realizations for the two families need not use the same indexwise assignments.
knowledge_statements.conclusion_latex: \mathcal A,\mathcal B\text{ have a common SRR}\iff \forall I,J\subseteq[n],\ b(A_I\cap B_J)\ge |I|+|J|-n+a(S\setminus(A_I\cup B_J))

knowledge_statements.title: Transversal Rank
knowledge_statements.scope_note: Rado's min-max formula for maximum partial independent transversals.
knowledge_statements.statement_latex:
Let \(M=(E,r)\) be a finite matroid and let \((A_i)_{i\in I}\) be a finite family of subsets of \(E\). Let \(\nu_M(A)\) be the largest cardinality of a set \(K\subseteq I\) for which there are pairwise distinct elements \(x_i\in A_i\), indexed by \(i\in K\), with \(\{x_i:i\in K\}\) independent in \(M\). Then
\[
\nu_M(A)=\min_{J\subseteq I}\left(|I\setminus J|+r\left(\bigcup_{i\in J}A_i\right)\right).
\]
knowledge_statements.statement_plain: The maximum size of a partial independent transversal equals a minimum combining omitted indices with the rank of a selected subfamily's union.
assumptions_latex: \((A_i)_{i\in I}\) is a finite family of subsets of \(E\).
knowledge_statements.conclusion_latex: \(\nu_M(A)=\min_{J\subseteq I}(|I\setminus J|+r(\bigcup_{i\in J}A_i))\).

knowledge_statements.title: Transversal Deficiency Certificates
knowledge_statements.scope_note: Rank-deficient subfamilies certify missing independent representatives.
knowledge_statements.statement_latex:
For a finite matroid \(M=(E,r)\) and family \((A_i)_{i\in I}\), define the deficiency of \(J\subseteq I\) by
\[
\delta(J):=|J|-r\left(\bigcup_{i\in J}A_i\right).
\]
If \(\delta(J)=d>0\), then every partial independent transversal omits at least \(d\) indices, so \(J\) is a verifiable deficiency certificate. Moreover, if \(\nu_M(A)\) is the maximum partial independent-transversal size, then
\[
|I|-\nu_M(A)=\max_{J\subseteq I}\delta(J).
\]
Thus a maximizing \(J\) certifies the exact optimum deficit.
knowledge_statements.statement_plain: A subfamily whose size exceeds the rank of its union certifies unavoidable omissions; maximum such deficiency equals the exact transversal deficit.
assumptions_latex: \((A_i)_{i\in I}\) is a finite family of subsets of \(E\).
knowledge_statements.conclusion_latex: Every \(J\subseteq I\) certifies deficit \(\delta(J)\), and \(|I|-\nu_M(A)=\max_{J\subseteq I}\delta(J)\).

A parity solution is a subfamily \(P\subseteq\Pi\) for which the union of its pairs is independent, namely

knowledge_statements.statement_title: Polymatroids and matchings in 2-polymatroids
knowledge_statements.scope_note: Foundational definitions, representations, specializations, and parameters for 2-polymatroid matching.
knowledge_statements.statement_latex: For a finite set $S$, a function $f:2^S\to\mathbb R$ is submodular if $f(X\cap Y)+f(X\cup Y)\le f(X)+f(Y)$ for all $X,Y\subseteq S$. A normalized, nondecreasing, integer-valued submodular function is a polymatroid rank function. It defines a $k$-polymatroid when $f(\{s\})\le k$ for every $s\in S$; $1$-polymatroids are matroids. If $(U,r)$ is a matroid and $(A_i)_{i\in T}$ is a family of subsets of $U$, then $f(X)=r(\bigcup_{i\in X}A_i)$ defines a polymatroid on $T$, and every polymatroid admits a representation of this form. For a family of linear subspaces, $f(X)$ may be taken as the dimension of their joint span; families of two-dimensional subspaces give $2$-polymatroids. For a hypergraph, $f(X)=|\bigcup_{i\in X}A_i|$ is a polymatroid rank function, with graphs giving $2$-polymatroids. In a $2$-polymatroid $(S,f)$, a set $X$ is a matching when $f(X)=2|X|$. This specializes to ordinary graph matchings, to graph $b$-matchings for $f(X)=\sum_{v\in V}\min\{b(v),\deg_X(v)\}$, and to common independent sets of two matroids for $f=r_1+r_2$. Every subset of a matching is a matching. The span of $X$ is the unique largest $Y\supseteq X$ satisfying $f(Y)=f(X)$; $X$ is spanning exactly when $f(X)=f(S)$. Let $\nu(S,f)$ be the maximum matching cardinality and $\rho(S,f)$ the minimum cardinality of a spanning set.
knowledge_statements.statement_plain: A polymatroid has a normalized, monotone, integer-valued submodular rank function, and it is a k-polymatroid when singleton ranks are at most k. Polymatroids have matroid-induced representations, including linear-subspace and hypergraph constructions. A matching in a 2-polymatroid is a set whose rank is twice its size; this includes graph matchings, b-matchings, and common independent sets of two matroids. Matchings are hereditary, while nu and rho denote maximum matching size and minimum spanning-set size.
assumptions_latex: f:2^S\to\mathbb Z_+\text{ is normalized, nondecreasing, and submodular whenever }(S,f)\text{ is a polymatroid}
knowledge_statements.conclusion_latex: \text{The stated constructions define polymatroids, and the stated matching, span, and parameter definitions and specializations hold.}

A fractional matroid-matching cover is a finite family \((z_X)_{X\subseteq V}\) satisfying \(z_X\geq0\) and
\[\sum_{X\subseteq V}|e\cap X|z_X\geq1\qquad(e\in E_G).\]
Its cost is \(c(z)=\sum_{X\subseteq V}r_M(X)z_X\). For every matroid matching \(F\), independence of \(V(F)\) gives \(|V(F)\cap X|\leq r_M(X)\); consequently the displayed edge-cover conditions certify
\[|F|\leq c(z).\]
Thus any cover of cost \(k\) is an explicitly checkable upper-bound certificate \(\nu(G,M)\leq k\).
knowledge_statements.statement_plain: Nonnegative weights on vertex subsets cover every edge by endpoint incidence; their rank-weighted cost is a verifiable upper bound on every matroid matching.
knowledge_statements.title: Matroid Matching Covers

intermediate_metadata.review_comment: The displayed fractional rank-cover inequalities do yield the stated upper bound, but this nonstandard cover terminology and formulation lack a source. The statement also includes derivational proof text that should be removed after sourcing.

knowledge_statements.statement_title: Algebraically Independent Pair Selection Min–Max Formula
knowledge_statements.scope_note: Algebraic-matroid matching over a field extension; \(\operatorname{tr}\) denotes the source's transcendence-rank quantity.
knowledge_statements.statement_latex:
Let \(L/K\) be a field extension and let \(E\) be a finite set of pairs from \(L\). The maximum number of disjoint pairs from \(E\) whose union is algebraically independent over \(K\) equals
\[
\min_{F,\,E_1\dot\cup\cdots\dot\cup E_k=E}\left[\operatorname{tr}_K(F)+\sum_{i=1}^k\left\lfloor\frac{\operatorname{tr}_F(E_i)}2\right\rfloor\right],
\]
where \(F\) ranges over the intermediate fields \(K\subseteq F\subseteq L\) and \((E_1,\ldots,E_k)\) ranges over all partitions of \(E\).
knowledge_statements.statement_plain: For pairs in a field extension, the largest disjoint subfamily with algebraically independent union equals a minimum over intermediate fields and partitions of the pair family, expressed through transcendence ranks.
assumptions_latex: K\subseteq L\text{ is a field extension.}
E\text{ is a finite set of pairs from }L.
knowledge_statements.conclusion_latex: \max\{|\mathcal M|:\mathcal M\subseteq E\text{ consists of disjoint pairs and }\bigcup\mathcal M\text{ is algebraically independent over }K\}=\min_{K\subseteq F\subseteq L,\ E=\dot\bigcup_{i=1}^kE_i}\left(\operatorname{tr}_K(F)+\sum_{i=1}^k\left\lfloor\frac{\operatorname{tr}_F(E_i)}2\right\rfloor\right).

assumptions_latex: \(G=(V,E_G)\) is finite and \(M\) is a matroid on \(V\).
The rank-inequality linear programs below are feasible and bounded.
knowledge_statements.conclusion_latex: \[\nu(G,M)\leq\nu_f(G,M)=\tau_f(G,M),\] with equality on the left exactly when the relaxation has an integral optimum.

notation.meaning: Optimum of the fractional matching relaxation.

review_flags: standard_field_rationale: finite linear-programming duality applied to matroid rank inequalities

knowledge_statements.statement_latex:
Define \(\nu_f(G,M)\) by maximizing \(\sum_{e\in E_G}x_e\) subject to \(x_e\geq0\) and
\[\sum_{e\in E_G}|e\cap X|x_e\leq r_M(X)\qquad(X\subseteq V).\]
Its linear-programming dual is the minimum-cost fractional cover of the preceding record, so
\[\nu(G,M)\leq\nu_f(G,M)=\tau_f(G,M).\]
Moreover, \(\nu(G,M)=\tau_f(G,M)\) holds exactly when the relaxation admits an optimal incidence vector of a matroid matching. Thus strong fractional duality is unconditional, while integral matching-covering equality is an additional structural property.
knowledge_statements.statement_plain: The rank-constrained fractional matching program and fractional cover program are LP duals; an integral min-max equality holds precisely when the relaxation is exact.

notation.meaning: Symmetric difference of two pair families.

knowledge_statements.scope_note: Abstract augmentation framework; concrete admissible sequences depend on the represented matroid class.
knowledge_statements.statement_latex:
Input \((M,\Pi)\), initialize \(P=\varnothing\), and repeatedly search for an ordered family \(Q=(q_1,\ldots,q_t)\) of distinct pairs such that
\[P'=P\mathbin{\triangle}\{q_1,\ldots,q_t\},\qquad |P'|=|P|+1,\qquad \bigcup_{p\in P'}p\in\mathcal I.\]
When such an augmenting sequence is found, replace \(P\) by \(P'\). Stop when the class-specific completeness criterion certifies that no augmenting sequence exists, and output \(P\). Cardinality increases at every update, so termination occurs after at most \(|\Pi|\) augmentations; correctness requires the cited completeness property for the chosen sequence system.
knowledge_statements.statement_plain: Starting from no pairs, repeatedly toggle an admissible alternating sequence that increases the feasible family by one; a complete sequence system certifies optimality at termination.
knowledge_statements.title: Augmenting-Sequence Methods

intermediate_metadata.review_comment: The record does not specify an admissible augmenting-sequence system or a search procedure. It defines augmentation as finding any larger feasible solution and assumes a class-specific completeness criterion, so it is not a substantive algorithm for the terminal container.

assumptions_latex: \(M\) is represented over a field \(\mathbb F\) of characteristic different from \(2\).
Each pair \(p_i\) is represented by columns \(a_i,b_i\in\mathbb F^r\).
knowledge_statements.conclusion_latex: \[\nu(M,\Pi)=\frac12\operatorname{rank}_{\mathbb F(y_1,\ldots,y_m)}\left(\sum_{i=1}^m y_i(a_ib_i^{\mathsf T}-b_ia_i^{\mathsf T})\right).\]

notation.meaning: Algebraically independent indeterminates, one per pair.

review_flags: standard_field_rationale: classical symbolic skew-matrix formulation of linear matroid parity
knowledge_statements.scope_note: Linear matroid parity over fields of characteristic other than two.
knowledge_statements.statement_latex:
Let \(p_i=\{a_i,b_i\}\) for \(1\leq i\leq m\), and introduce algebraically independent indeterminates \(y_1,\ldots,y_m\). Form the skew-symmetric symbolic matrix
\[A(y)=\sum_{i=1}^m y_i\bigl(a_ib_i^{\mathsf T}-b_ia_i^{\mathsf T}\bigr).\]
Then its rank over the rational-function field records the optimum parity size:
\[\operatorname{rank}_{\mathbb F(y_1,\ldots,y_m)}A(y)=2\nu(M,\Pi).\]
Consequently, symbolic elimination, randomized specialization over sufficiently large fields, or exact polynomial-identity methods can determine the linear matroid-parity value through matrix rank.
knowledge_statements.statement_plain: For a linear matroid, twice the maximum number of feasible pairs equals the generic rank of a symbolic skew-symmetric matrix built from the pair columns.
knowledge_statements.title: Linear-Algebraic Matroid-Parity Methods

intermediate_metadata.review_comment: The symbolic skew-matrix rank correspondence is a specialized theorem central to the record and requires an authoritative source with an exact theorem or section locator.

children.title: Combinatorial Methods for Special Matroid Classes

assumptions_latex: A matroid class supplies an independence oracle and a complete, terminating combinatorial augmentation routine for parity instances in that class.
knowledge_statements.conclusion_latex: The routine returns a maximum-cardinality parity family after at most \(|\Pi|\) successful augmentations.
review_flags: standard_field_rationale: oracle-level specialization of augmenting-sequence methods
knowledge_statements.scope_note: Oracle template for classes admitting complete combinatorial augmentation; no universal complexity bound is asserted.
knowledge_statements.statement_latex:
Given \((M,\Pi)\), set \(P=\varnothing\). Invoke the class-specific combinatorial search routine on \(P\). If it returns a feasible augmentation \(P'\subseteq\Pi\) with
\[|P'|=|P|+1\quad\text{and}\quad\bigcup_{p\in P'}p\in\mathcal I,\]
replace \(P\) by \(P'\) and repeat. If it returns its prescribed no-augmentation certificate, output \(P\). Under the assumed completeness property, the certificate implies that no larger feasible parity family exists. Since every successful iteration increases \(|P|\), at most \(|\Pi|\) successful augmentations occur; the total running time is determined by the class-specific search routine.
knowledge_statements.statement_plain: For a special matroid class with complete combinatorial augmentation, repeatedly enlarge the feasible pair family; the class-specific no-augmentation certificate establishes optimality.
knowledge_statements.title: Combinatorial Methods for Special Matroid Classes

intermediate_metadata.review_comment: The record assumes the complete class-specific routine that the leaf is supposed to describe. It names no special matroid class, augmentation rule, or implementable combinatorial method, so it does not fill the exact container.

knowledge_statements.statement_title: Alternating and augmenting sequences for matroid parity
knowledge_statements.scope_note: Defines the sequence conditions and records their immediate independence, cardinality, and span consequences.
knowledge_statements.statement_latex: Let \(M=(E,\mathcal I)\) be a matroid whose elements are paired, and let \(I\) be an independent parity set. For a sequence of distinct elements \(S=(e_1,\bar e_1,\ldots,e_s,\bar e_s)\), require \(e_i,\bar e_i\in E\setminus I\) for odd \(i\) and \(e_i,\bar e_i\in I\) for even \(i\). Define \(S_i=(e_1,\bar e_1,\ldots,e_{i-1},\bar e_{i-1},e_i)\). The sequence is alternating with respect to \(I\) if \(I+e_1\in\mathcal I\) and, for every \(i\le s\), \(\operatorname{sp}(I\mathbin\triangle S_i)=\operatorname{sp}(I+e_1)\). Consequently, \(|I\mathbin\triangle S_i|=|I|+1\) and \(I\mathbin\triangle S_i\in\mathcal I\) for every \(i\le s\), while \(I\mathbin\triangle(S_i+\bar e_i)\notin\mathcal I\) for odd \(i<s\). An alternating sequence is augmenting if additionally \(s\) is odd and \(I\mathbin\triangle S\in\mathcal I\); then \(|I\mathbin\triangle S|=|I|+2\) and \(\operatorname{sp}(I\mathbin\triangle S)\supseteq\operatorname{sp}(I)\).
knowledge_statements.statement_plain: In a matroid with paired elements, an alternating sequence switches between pairs outside and inside an independent parity set while all prescribed prefixes have the same span as the first one-element extension. These prefixes remain independent and gain one element. If the sequence has odd length and switching the entire sequence also remains independent, it is augmenting; the resulting parity set gains two elements and its span contains the original span.
assumptions_latex: M=(E,\mathcal I)\text{ is a matroid with paired elements}
I\text{ is an independent parity set}
S=(e_1,\bar e_1,\ldots,e_s,\bar e_s)\text{ consists of distinct elements}
e_i,\bar e_i\in E\setminus I\text{ for odd }i,\quad e_i,\bar e_i\in I\text{ for even }i
knowledge_statements.conclusion_latex: S\text{ is alternating exactly under the stated prefix conditions; if also }s\text{ is odd and }I\mathbin\triangle S\in\mathcal I,\text{ then }|I\mathbin\triangle S|=|I|+2\text{ and }\operatorname{sp}(I\mathbin\triangle S)\supseteq\operatorname{sp}(I).
